title: Reconciler gives up a RE-ANCHORED old anchor row at its first pass: the 24 h test reads created_at, not the new submission's age
description:
**BLUF:** On demo, an anchor row created on 2026-09-30 received a new transaction on 2026-10-29 at 05:53Z. The node refused it, so nothing was on chain, and the reconciler marked the row `failed` at its first pass, 06:07:07Z, about 14 minutes later, with the message "transaction never appeared on chain within 24h (reconciler)". The give-up test measures the row's age from `created_at`, which a re-anchor does not change, so an old row that is re-anchored is eligible for the 24 hour give-up as soon as the reconciler next scans it.

**Source** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`): `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/reconciler.ts:98` reads `now() - new Date(row.created_at).getTime() > config.giveUpMs` and then writes `status: 'failed'` with "transaction never appeared on chain within Nh (reconciler)". The reconciler scans rows with `status IN ('pending', 'submitted', 'submitting')`, a non-null `transaction_hash`, `simulated = FALSE` and `updated_at` older than `minAgeMs` (`reconciler.ts:73-76`). `created_at` is selected but is not in that WHERE clause; it is read only by the give-up test.

**Measured on demo** (Seat D 42nd, read-only, host `secuura02-demo-vm`, 2026-10-29 06:16Z and 06:17Z; files `moved_C.txt`, `attrib_C.txt` and `moved_logs.txt`):

* The row: `created=2026-09-30 04:20:54.978+00` (unchanged by the 29 Oct submissions), `updated=2026-10-29 06:07:07.096+00`, `status=failed`, `retries=0`, `confirmed_at=null`, error "transaction never appeared on chain within 24h (reconciler)".
* Anchoring log lines that name the row, 05:10Z to 06:10Z: 05:52:41Z "Anchor created"; 05:52:44Z a transaction submitted (`e563c41d…`); 05:53:11Z "Anchor created" again; 05:53:13Z that transaction confirmed on Cardano (block 4804058), together with the warning "KS-1385: declined to record a transaction against an anchor whose metadata changed under it"; 05:53:13Z a second submission, "Node REFUSED the written-ahead transaction — the reply arrived, nothing is on chain" (`c8fe9420…`); then "Anchor already submitted — re-polling the known transaction"; 06:07:07Z "Reconciler: stale anchor marked failed — tx never appeared (KS-584)" naming `c8fe9420…`, pass summary `scanned 1, confirmed 0, failed 1`.
* In the same read, by status: confirmed 249, failed 93; 3 failed rows carry a `confirmed_at` (they were confirmed once). That count is as read; I did not analyse its cause.

**Evidence:** `5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatD-42nd/evidence/demo/moved_C.txt`, `attrib_C.txt`, `moved_logs.txt`. Seat D 42nd reported the finding to Wednesday in its STATUS C mail (2026-10-29 06:22Z).

**Searched** (issues filter over title, description and comments, archived included; positive control `parseScopeString` 9 hits, a random token 0 hits): `reconciler.ts:98` 0 hits; `giveUpMs` 1 hit (KS-726, archived, the write-ahead of the transaction hash); "never appeared on chain within" 1 hit (KS-772, comments only); "re-anchored" 1 hit (KS-963, archived, unrelated); `created_at` 28 hits, read by title (KS-1630 concerns which clock sets `created_at`, a different defect).

**Not measured:** why the row received a second submission (the repeat-POST reset of an existing row is described in KS-1384; I did not verify it here), and whether any chain state exists for `c8fe9420…`.

**Related:** KS-1384 (a repeat `POST /api/anchors` resets the existing row), KS-1171.

title: Please bring the platform-k docs up to date with current behaviour, so systemTest can be written to the docs rather than to the source
description:
## BLUF

Kamil, when you have the capacity, could you please update the platform-k documentation so that it describes how the platform is meant to behave today? The systemTest suites take their expected results from the docs, not from the platform-k source code, so up-to-date docs are what let the tests check the platform against its intended behaviour.

## Why this matters

* **The tests are written to the docs, on purpose.** A test whose expectation comes from the source can only confirm that the code does what the code does. It cannot catch a bug. When the expectation comes from the docs, a difference between the two is a real finding.
* **This follows the ruling already recorded under** [KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or)**:** the docs lead and the code aligns to the docs. That ticket added your Linear rulings to the docs. This one asks for the wider pass that only you can do, because you know the intended behaviour best.
* **Where the docs are silent or out of date**, the test has no source for its expectation. It then either goes unwritten, or it is written against the code, which is the habit we are trying to avoid.

## What would help most

* Endpoint behaviour as it is meant to be: status codes, error bodies, auth and role requirements, and tenancy and ownership rules.
* Flows across services, such as originate, anchoring, certification, transfer and S↔K, including what happens when a step fails.
* Removing or marking anything retired, so a test does not keep asserting behaviour that is gone.
* Where the intended behaviour is not yet decided, a short line saying so is very useful. It tells us to wait rather than guess.

The order and the split into smaller pieces are entirely up to you. Child tickets per area are welcome if that suits you better.

## Done when

The platform-k docs describe current intended behaviour for the areas above, and anything still undecided is marked as such.

Thank you very much, Kamil. It makes a real difference to how much we can trust the test results.

title: KS-1709 follow-ups: non-JSON 2xx reads 'failed'; recertify unpublished with no fetch timeout; no re-anchor for a kept certification
description:
**BLUF:** Four loose ends from KS-1709, none introduced by it. QA gate 15 (1806-2, 1806-3) and Seat U 6th listed them in comments on KS-1709, and none has a ticket of its own: (1) an accepted 2xx from the anchoring service whose body is not JSON is reported as `failed`; (2) `POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify` is not in the published spec; (3) its anchoring `fetch` has no timeout; (4) Platform K has no re-anchor for a kept certification.

**1. A non-JSON 2xx reads** `failed` (gate 15, 1806-2, measured at runtime). `upstream.json()` throws inside the `try` before `anchoringStatus = 'submitted'` is set (`certifications.ts:619-621` on the issue route; the same shape at `:1393-1395` on recertify, read only). On the issue route a 202 with an empty body gives 201 with `anchoringStatus: "failed"`, and a 200 with the text `ok` gives the same. In production the 202-empty case gives 503 with the provisional row deleted although anchoring had accepted the request (an orphan anchor; the gate records the production part as pre-existing). A 202 or 299 with a JSON id, and a 202 without `data.id`, give no key and `submitted`; a 409 gives `failed`. The published description says "a 4xx, a 5xx, an unreachable service or a timeout" and omits this case. The gate's likelihood note: low, since anchoring always answers JSON. The gate's fix-shape (not ruled): set `submitted` on `upstream.ok` before parsing (anchorId null when unreadable), or add "or an unreadable acceptance" to the description.

**2. Recertify is not published** (gate 15, 1806-3, read). `originate.openapi.ts:27` lists `/:id/recertify` among the endpoints not yet registered, and `secuura-api.yaml` has 0 matches for `recertify` (counted at develop `6d41673e0f79`). title: A kept (refused-anchor) certification reads anchored: true on GET /api/documents/{id}, and POST /anchor 400s "already anchored"
description:
**BLUF:** A certification whose anchor was refused is now kept and marked unanchored (KS-1709, Kam's 2026-10-23 ruling b: "keep it, but mark it unanchored"). Its blob carries `blockchain.status` `failed`. The documents surface still reads that blob as anchored: `GET /api/documents/{id}` answers `blockchain.anchored: true`, and `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor` answers 400 "Document is already anchored", so the documents retry route cannot re-anchor it. The comparison dates from KS-1124 F4 (2026-09-28); the ruling turns it into a contradiction on a second read surface.

**What was measured** (QA gate 15, finding 1806-1, on the KS-1709 pull request head; documentRepo mocked, the real `documentsRouter`):

* A certification is a row in `documents`, so `GET /api/documents/{certUuid}` serves it. With the blob the KS-1709 cells assert (`status: 'failed'`, `anchoringStatus: 'failed'`, `anchorId: null`), GET answers `blockchain.anchored: true` and `POST /api/documents/{id}/anchor` answers 400 "Document is already anchored".
* Controls in the same probe: a blob with `status: 'anchor_failed'` gives `anchored: false` and POST 202; a null blob gives `anchored: false` and POST 202.
* `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` returns early on `anchorId: null`, so nothing heals it.

**Where** (read at develop `6d41673e0f79`):

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1200`: `anchored: !!document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed'`.
* `documents.ts:1458`: `if (document.blockchain && document.blockchain.status !== 'anchor_failed')` then 400 "Document is already anchored".
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:99-100`: `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES` is `['failed', 'anchor_failed']`, so the verify surfaces already read `failed` as failed.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:1204`: `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` builds `checks.blockchainAnchored` as `!!certification.blockchain`, which is true for a kept failed certification (Seat U 6th recorded this in its KS-1709 wrap; I read the line and did not run it).

**The gate's fix-shape (not ruled):** use one set, for example `FAILED_ANCHOR_STATUSES`, at both `documents.ts` sites. The regression test the gate proposed: the kept-certification blob gives GET `anchored: false` and POST `/anchor` 202.

**Evidence:**

* `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate15-1805-1806/verdict.md`, finding 1806-1
* the probe it names, in the same folder: `evidence/probe/_quarantine_2026-10-29/gate15-probe-docs.test.ts` and `evidence/probe/probe_docs.out`

None of these describes this defect.

**Not measured:** I read the lines above at develop `6d41673e0f79` and did not re-run the gate's probe.

title: Security (nit): decideMint's toUpperCase admits a dotless-i, a long-s and an array role as a key admin; plus the role-comparison sweep
description:
**BLUF:** `decideMint` (`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:96-97`, the `POST /api/keys` admission test) still compares `String(caller?.role ?? '').toUpperCase()` against the key-admin set, so a role spelled with U+0131 (dotless i) or U+017F (long s), or an array role, can be read as an admin role. KS-1591 fixed the same shape in `isPlatformRole` and `requireKeyAdmin` and deliberately left this site; this ticket tracks it, and the sweep of other role comparisons that KS-1591's description asks for, so that KS-1591 can close. Reachability is not established.

## Where

`services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts` at develop `5dccdcb29ec20393e80cbdb1e359a49caa633165` (the build on both boxes), read with `git show`:

* line 96: `const role = String(caller?.role ?? '');`
* line 97: `if (KEY_ADMIN_ROLES.has(role.toUpperCase())) {`

## What is measured and what is not

* Measured by the tier-2 gate on 2026-10-28 (the batch covering PRs 1775, 1776 and 1780, GO WITH NOTES): `decideMint` admits a role spelled with U+0131 or U+017F, and an array role, at PR 1776's head `8b92887a6fac`. The gate's note was filed on KS-1591 as a comment (`42e97e12`).
* Read by me, not run: lines 96 and 97 are unchanged at the deployed build. I ran no test of `decideMint` with those roles.
* Not established: whether any issuer, user-management path or seed can store or sign a token with such a role. That needs a token the auth service signs. KS-1591 said the same. Until someone measures it this is a nit; if any path can, it is a privilege escalation (admission to mint API keys) and should be re-rated at once.

## Recommendation

Not built. Apply the KS-1591 remedy here: fold ASCII letters only (`replace(/[a-z]/g, ...)`, as `isPlatformRole` now does) and refuse a role that is not a string, in the one shared definition so every caller inherits it. Cells: a dotless-i spelling, a long-s spelling and an array role each refused by `decideMint`; a control that every ASCII spelling admitted today is still admitted.

## Sweep candidates (not findings)

Method: `git grep -n -I "toUpperCase()"` at `5dccdcb29ec2` over `Blockchain/Dev/services` and `Blockchain/Dev/packages`, tests, `dist` and `node_modules` excluded, keeping lines that also contain "role" (case-insensitive). 14 lines. Controls: the `decideMint` line is in the result (1 line from `provisioningPolicy.ts`); a nonsense token over the same paths matches 0 files. Of the 14: 2 are comments, 2 are the sites KS-1591 fixed (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:144`, `security/src/index.ts:1104`), 1 is `decideMint`, and 9 are other candidates:

* `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:85` and `:102` (`ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`, `SCOPED_ADMIN_ROLES`; the same file KS-1591 changed at `:144`)
* `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:288`
* `services/auth/src/routes/issuerCerts.ts:71`
* `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:285` and `:377`
* `services/auth/src/services/password.ts:234` (whether it is a role comparison is unread)
* `services/originate/src/middleware/rbac.ts:56` and `:58`

I read none of these beyond the matching line. The census misses a comparison split across lines or through another variable name. KS-1601 tracks the SQL counterpart (`upper(role) = $3` in the admin-scope route).

## Board search (before filing)

Issues filter with `includeArchived: true`, title or description (comments excluded), read 2026-10-29: tickets whose title contains `decideMint`: 0. Tickets naming `decideMint` together with "dotless", "0131" or "017F": 0. Controls: `isPlatformRole` finds 7 tickets (KS-1701, KS-1601, KS-1591, KS-1536, KS-1535, KS-976, KS-743); a random nonsense token finds 0. The only place the gap is recorded is the gate's note on KS-1591 (a comment, which this search excludes). Tickets that mention `decideMint` for other reasons, none with this fold as its subject: KS-1594, KS-1584, KS-1570, KS-1536, KS-1535, KS-1533, KS-742 and KS-486.

## Source

KS-1591 (the tier-2 gate's note, comment `42e97e12`, and its description's request for a sweep); the MERGE GO for PR 1775 recorded the narrowing: PR 1776 says `Refs KS-1591`, not `Closes`.

title: m365 ks1670 source-text pin: a raw connectionId by concatenation survives (gate 7 N6)
description:
**BLUF:** the source-text pin that PR 1791 added for KS-1670 (`ks1670-the-success-redirect-encodes-the-connection-id.test.ts`) has blind spots that gate 7 found with mutants N3, N4 and N6 (finding 1791-1, Low, a disclosed test gap). It is not a defect in the product line. Low. Related to KS-1670. I read the file at develop and did not re-run the gate's mutants.

**What the pin is, read at develop** `5dccdcb29ec2`**:** it reads `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts` as text and boots nothing. Its needle is the string `connectionId=${` (line 10 of the test). R1 (line 32) requires every interpolation that follows that needle to be wrapped in `encodeURIComponent`. R2 (line 37) requires the exact success-redirect text `m365=success&connectionId=${encodeURIComponent(connectionId)}&tenant=${encodeURIComponent(connection.tenantName`. C1 (line 41) requires that the instrument finds exactly one such interpolation.

**The gaps, from gate 7 (tested there by mutants):**

1. N6: a raw id added by string concatenation survives. R1's needle sees only template interpolations, so a redirect built by concatenation is invisible to it by construction (the needle is the literal `connectionId=${`).
2. N4: a wrapped-then-unwrapped expression passes R1; only R2's exact text catches it, and only on the success line.
3. N3: an equivalent rewrite of the success line (same behaviour, different text) turns R2 red for no behavioural reason.
   The gate's own HTTP probe showed the behaviour the pin cannot, and it suggested lifting its cells A1, A3 and A7 into the PR as wire cells.

**What has changed since:** PR 1791 merged with an added behaviour cell, `ks1670-the-success-redirect-keeps-a-hostile-connection-id-intact.test.ts`, added on gate 7's note (it also answers the gate's finding 1791-2, the missing non-ASCII cell). Seat R 6th measured it on the PR: three of its six cells were red against the pin, and it kills the raw, `encodeURI` and double-encode mutants; N3 remains. I did not re-run that. Gate 7's finding 1791-3 (a lone surrogate makes `encodeURIComponent` throw; unreachable because ids are `conn_` plus a uuid) is not part of this ticket.

**So what is left:** the pin can still go red for an equivalent rewrite (N3), and a redirect added elsewhere by concatenation is outside R1. Whether that is worth a change, or the behaviour cell is enough and this can be closed with a note, is a decision for whoever picks it up.

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** make R2 assert the behaviour (the encoded id reaches the wire) instead of the exact text; or lift the gate's A1, A3 and A7 as wire cells; or close it with a note that the behaviour cell is the real guard.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 22:3xZ): `ks1670` 0 hits; `source-text pin` 5 hits, read by title (KS-1670 itself, and KS 1602, KS 1521, KS 1328, KS 1187, which are other tests' pins); KS-1670's own text says only that the test "is a source-text pin … proves the text of the template, not the redirect on the wire" and does not name these mutants (`concatenat` 0 matches, `blind` 0); `connectionId=` 3 hits (KS-1670, KS 1641 Done, KS 423 Done), none is this. The positive control `parseScopeString` found 4; a nonsense token generated at run time found 0 and was not recorded in this ticket.

title: OAuth /authorize: a repeated state or code_challenge answers 500, and POST accepts arrays
description:
**BLUF:** `GET /api/oauth/authorize` answers **500** `server_error` when `state` or `code_challenge` arrives as a repeated query parameter, the same class as the `scope` crash KS-1219 fixes. On POST, JSON arrays for the same two fields do not crash: an array `state` is coerced to a comma-joined string and echoed in the redirect, and an array `code_challenge` reaches `createAuthorizationCode` as an array. Low. Related to KS-1219, whose own recommendation ("by the same shape, any other non-string authorize parameter") PR 1797 closes for `scope` only. Raised on the tier-1 gate's note 1797-2 (gate 9, 2026-10-28), then measured here; the gate's wording ("repeated `state` / `code_challenge` still 500") holds for GET only.

Every figure below is from a loopback listener driving the real router with its collaborators mocked (the same harness as the ks1219 test), on PR 1797's branch with develop `92a02a356139` merged in. `oauth.ts` is blob `91aa664ac910`, which develop did not change; the lines involved are not touched by PR 1797. Nothing was run against a live box.

**Measured, GET** (client `client-1`, a confidential app, otherwise valid request):

1. `&state=xyz&state=second` answers **500** `server_error`; a single `state=xyz` answers 200 and serves the consent page.
2. `&code_challenge=aaa&code_challenge=bbb` answers **500** `server_error`; a single `code_challenge=aaa` answers 200.
3. `&code_challenge_method=S256&code_challenge_method=plain` answers 400 `invalid_request`. It is already refused, but by accident: the check at lines 361 to 367 is `PKCE_METHODS.has(codeChallengeMethod)`, which is false for an array.
4. `&scope=openid&scope=profile` answers 400 `invalid_request` (the KS-1219 fix, as the control).

**Cause, read from the file:** `generateConsentPage` calls `escapeHtml(params.state)` and `escapeHtml(params.codeChallenge || '')` (lines 1522 and 1523), and `escapeHtml(s: string)` is `s.replace(...)` (lines 1582 to 1584). An array has no `replace`, so the call throws and the handler's catch answers 500. The `as Record<string, string>` cast on `req.query` (line 492) does nothing at run time.

**Measured, POST with JSON arrays** (none of these is a 500):

1. `action: deny` with `state: ["a","b"]` answers 302 to `...?error=access_denied&state=a%2Cb`. The client's `state` comes back altered.
2. `action: approve` with `state: ["a","b"]` mints a code and answers 302 to `...?code=...&state=a%2Cb`.
3. `action: approve` with `code_challenge: ["x","y"]` answers 302, and `createAuthorizationCode` was called with `codeChallenge` equal to the array `["x","y"]` (`Array.isArray` true). **Not measured:** what the real pg driver and the column do with it, because the repository is mocked. It may store text, or it may fail.

**Scope is neither deduplicated nor bounded** (the gate's note 1797-3, pre-existing, measured here for a string scope, repository mocked): `openid openid profile openid` is stored as sent, 28 characters with the repeats; `openid,profile` is stored as `openid profile`; a 14,000-character scope made of one repeated token is stored as a 13,999-character string. Real column limits not measured.

**Not probed:** the other authorize parameters as arrays (`client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `response_type`, `email`, `password`, `action`, `mfaCode`).

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** one check ahead of the resolver on both GET and POST that every authorize parameter is a string or absent, answering 400 `invalid_request` (the existing message, so no published message changes), as KS-1219's recommendation already describes; or per-field guards in the two handlers. A decision for whoever takes it: whether POST should refuse an array `state` or coerce it, and whether `scope` should be deduplicated and capped.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 21:2xZ): `repeated state` 0 hits, `repeated code_challenge` 0, `?state=` 0; `escapeHtml` 5 hits, read by title (KS 841, KS 799 and KS 798 are the consent page posting its own form, KS 488 a review stream, KS 163 a connector XSS), none is this; `code_challenge` 13 hits, read by title (PKCE, token-exchange and consent-page work, mostly Done, plus KS 836 and KS 782 in Backlog and KS 1677, the m365 callback), none is this; `array-valued` 5 hits (KS-1219 itself; KS 1671, the same species in the m365 callback, a different service; KS 839; KS 677; KS 256). The positive control `parseScopeString` found 3 (KS 1220, KS-1219, KS 839); a nonsense token generated at run time found 0 and was not recorded in this ticket.

title: change-password publishes no 422: a weak new password is documented under 400 while the route answers 422
description:
**BLUF:** the published contract for `POST /api/users/me/change-password` lists **no 422** and documents a too-weak new password under **400** ("Wrong current password or new password too weak"), while the route answers **422** for a weak password. This is a pre-existing contract gap, found by the tier-1 gate on the KS-1467 services/auth change (finding 1799-7); KS-1467 was ruled to change no OpenAPI, so it did not touch it. Low. Related to KS-1467.

**What I read, at develop** `802eb2b8ecaf`**:**

1. `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`, operation `/api/users/me/change-password`, response codes: 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 415, 429, 500, 502, 503. There is no 422. The 400 description reads "Wrong current password or new password too weak".
2. The source of that text is `services/auth/src/auth.openapi.ts` line 1012: `400: { ...commonErrorResponses[400], description: 'Wrong current password or new password too weak' }`, and that operation's `responses` has no 422 entry.
3. The two sibling routes do publish it: reset-password has `422: ... 'New password too weak'` (a comment at `auth.openapi.ts` line 813 cites KS 255), and register has a 422 described "Weak password, or client-supplied `role` field (not permitted)".
4. The route throws `new ValidationError('New password is too weak', ...)` (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts`, around line 993 at the pin), and `ValidationError` answers 422. The route-level cell for change-password in the KS-1467 PR drives the real route and reads status 422 for weak candidates.

**Not claimed:** I ran no schema-conformance tool against the yaml for this; the gate measured it on the wire (finding 1799-7). A wrong *current* password is a 400 and stays one.

**Fix shapes, not chosen here:** add `422: { ...commonErrorResponses[422], description: 'New password too weak' }` to the change-password operation and take "or new password too weak" out of the 400 text, then regenerate the yaml (`generate-openapi`, `check:openapi`). That changes the published contract, so it wants its own ruling; the KS-1467 ruling was no OpenAPI change. Since KS-1467 round 2 the 422 `details` is the published ZodIssue-compatible array, so documenting the 422 matches what the route sends.

**Searched before filing** (Linear `issues` filter over title, description and comments, archived included, team KS, 2026-10-28 15:5xZ): `new password too weak` 0 hits; `publishes no 422` 0; `no 422` with `change-password` 0; `change-password` with `422` 7 hits (KS-1467, KS-1005, KS-732, KS-501, KS-486, KS-485, KS-480), read: none records this gap; `too weak` with `yaml` 2 hits (KS 255, KS 141), neither covers change-password; the zero control `zzqq-no-such-token-r6c` 0 hits; the positive control (title `AppError resets`) found KS-1467.

title: ks597 integration guard (KS-1340): 127.0.0.1:6433, the shared stack's pgbouncer, is accepted, and the hostaddr refusal is case- and percent-encoding-literal
description:
**BLUF:** the guard that pull request 1790 gives the ks597 integration file (KS-1340) refuses the shared stack's Postgres ports 5432 and 6432 but not **6433**, the port docker-compose publishes for the shared stack's pgbouncer, which fronts the same shared database. `postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:6433/db` is accepted, and so is `...:55412/db?port=6433`. Separately, its `hostaddr` refusal matches the lower-case key literally, so `?HOSTADDR=` and `?host%61ddr=` pass it. One guard and one logical path, so one ticket. Neither is a change to pull request 1790, which merges as gated (gate 8, 2026-10-29: #1790 GO). Filed on Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-10-28 13:38:21Z; gate 8 findings 1790-1 and 1790-2.

## Where

`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks597-issuer-organization-id.integration.test.ts`: the `SHARED_STACK_PORTS` list (the port `5432` plus the `POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT` default read from docker-compose.yml) and the `hostaddr` test in `disposableDsnTarget()`, at the head of pull request 1790 (`3a9b1c121f6d`). The port list is pre-existing (KS-1306); the pull request did not change it.

## 1. Port 6433

docker-compose.yml publishes the shared stack's Postgres on `127.0.0.1:${POSTGRES_EXTERNAL_PORT:-6432}` (line 156) and its pgbouncer on `127.0.0.1:${PGBOUNCER_PORT:-6433}` (line 262, container port 6432), the pooler every service connects through. The guard's list is `["5432","6432"]` (printed by the probe below). KS-296 records the labels (6432 = direct Postgres, 6433 = pgbouncer) and the compose stack-safety script's list in KS-1558's description already includes 6433.

Measured by running the pull request's own guard function, extracted from the file at its head and transpiled, beside the pg client (pg 8.20.0; no database and no socket: 0 connect calls, with a control reading 1):

```
DSN                                    guard                       pg dials
control: clean loopback, free port     ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:55412    127.0.0.1:55412
control: shared postgres port 5432     REFUSED                     127.0.0.1:5432
control: shared published port 6432    REFUSED                     127.0.0.1:6432
pgbouncer published port 6433          ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:6433     127.0.0.1:6433
6433 named only in the query string    ACCEPTED 127.0.0.1:6433     127.0.0.1:6433
```

Nothing was run against a pooler. Gate 8 found the same independently. Not measured: a stack started on another slot publishes pgbouncer and Postgres on other ports (KS-390's table lists 6533, 6633 and so on), and the list reads only the default; whether it should cover slot ports is a decision for whoever fixes this.

## 2. The hostaddr refusal is literal

The test is `/[?&]hostaddr(=|&|$)/`: lower case, not percent-decoded. Measured with the same probe: `?HOSTADDR=203.0.113.7` and `?host%61ddr=203.0.113.7` are accepted, and the pg client dials the authority (`127.0.0.1:55412`) for both. There is **no measured bypass**: pg ignores `hostaddr` in every spelling, and no consumer of the DSN in this file is libpq. The rule's stated reason is that libpq honours `hostaddr`; the gate states that libpq also decodes percent-escapes in a key, so the rule only partly meets that reason. I did not run libpq here.

## Fix shape (not chosen here)

Read the pgbouncer default from the compose file the way the Postgres one is read (`PGBOUNCER_PORT:-(\d+)\}:6432`), so the list cannot drift; and either decode and lower-case the query's keys before the `hostaddr` test, or refuse any query key outside a short allow-list.

## Also noted by the gate, not measured

Finding 1790-3: the same DSN is handed to the product as `DATABASE_URL` (Prisma), whose parser may read a duplicate or overriding query key differently from the pg client. Checking that needs a connection attempt.

## Board search before filing

Issues filter over title, description and comment bodies, archived included, run immediately before filing. `SHARED_STACK_PORTS`: 0 hits. `hostaddr` and `HOSTADDR`: only KS-1340 and KS-1793 (both mine; neither covers the spelling). `PGBOUNCER_PORT`: 3 hits (KS-1166, KS-390, KS-614) and `6433`: 6 hits (KS-1236, KS-1558, KS-296, KS-390, KS-490, KS-614); I read them: they concern slot ports, the VM firewall, a docs label fix and the compose stack-safety script's list, and none covers the ks597 guard's port list. Positive control `disposable`: 20 hits. Zero control: a fresh token never written to the board returned 0; the token is not recorded here so that it stays a control.

## Related

KS-1340 (pull request 1790, the guard). KS-1793 (the ks1263 guard with the same hole; unfixed). KS-1558 and KS-296 (where the role of 6433 is recorded).

## Provenance

Gate 8, findings 1790-1 and 1790-2 (`0_Brain/reference/2026-10-29_gate8-batch/verdict.md`), reproduced by running the pull request's own function on 2026-10-29. Probe: `5_Project_History/2026-10-28_seatT-5th/tools/guard_probe_followup_t5.js` in the project record.

title: smoke-test.sh is not remote-clean: 12 localhost:60xx checks, RUNBOOK 2.2's remote full run, and URL credentials echoed in "Smoke target:"
description:
**BLUF:** `scripts/smoke-test.sh` is still not remote-clean after PR 1793 made its `GATEWAY` honour `SMOKE_BASE_URL` (KS-1250). One remote full run would show all three problems below at once, which is why they are one ticket. Low. Related to KS-1250. Filed on the tier-2 gate's note (gate 8, 2026-10-28), after a search of the board (quoted at the end).

**Nobody runs this script against kintsugi, demo or any live box to reproduce or check any of this.** A full run anchors a real document, and that run is held for Kam (the KS-1250 hold). Everything below was read from the script or measured with a stub `curl` on a private PATH against a `.invalid` host.

1. **12 hard-coded** `http://localhost:60xx` **service-port checks remain in the full run** (sections 7 onward): lines 259, 263, 267, 275, 283, 292, 305, 307, 317, 319, 327 and 329 of `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/smoke-test.sh` at PR 1793's head `29989b01ab05`. PR 1793 moves only `GATEWAY`, so with `SMOKE_BASE_URL` set to a remote gateway those 12 checks still hit localhost, and the run mixes two environments while reading as a result for one.
2. **RUNBOOK section 2.2 still tells an operator to do a remote full run.** `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/RUNBOOK.md` lines 139 to 143: `SMOKE_BASE_URL=https://<prod-gateway-fqdn> ../../scripts/smoke-test.sh`, under the heading "Bash smoke against production gateway", with no `--quick`.
3. **The** `Smoke target:` **line echoes credentials embedded in the URL verbatim.** Measured with a stub `curl` and `--quick`: `SMOKE_BASE_URL='https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999'` (a fake credential) prints, as line 1 of the output, `Smoke target: https://alice:s3cr3t-token@smoke-target.invalid:9999`. A base URL carrying a token or basic-auth would be written to the terminal and to any CI log. The stub recorded 9 requests, all to `smoke-target.invalid`.

Also on this ticket: **no test cell uses an** `https://` **base** (the new suite uses `http://smoke-target.invalid:9999`), so the gate's mutant M11 survives.

Fix shapes, not chosen here: route the 12 service-port checks through a base the way `GATEWAY` is, or skip them with a printed line when the base is not localhost; make section 2.2 say `--quick` or say what a remote full run does not cover; print the target as scheme, host and port only.
