It reuses the **first** cached account whose key merely *starts with* the id of the account now signing in. `result.account` is then that other account. `refreshTokenForAccount` (`token-manager.ts`) matches `e.home_account_id === result.account.homeAccountId` exactly, so it selects the **other** account's refresh token.

**Reproduced on the sign-in path** by Seat R 59th, 2026-10-20, at PR #1664's head `efd79bc87b36` (a scratch cell, not committed), using the repo's real `@azure/msal-node` over a fake in-process transport (nothing reached Microsoft). In this file's terms `exchangeAuthCode`'s call into the selector is byte-for-byte what develop has:

```
X signs in (id uida.tidax)                          -> exchangeAuthCode returns "RT-X-1"
P signs in (id uida.tida), a strict prefix of X's   -> exchangeAuthCode returns "RT-X-1"
msal's raw result.account for P's sign-in           : uida.tidax
cache RT entries                                    : ["uida.tidax:RT-X-1","uida.tida:RT-P-1"]
P received its OWN token: false      P received X's token: true
```

P's own token is in the cache, under P's id. It is not returned, and X's is. **Gate CB1 measured the same on both trees (its cell GC7);** I reproduced it on the sign-in path myself and did not run it on develop directly.

**Other shapes the gate found (refresh path, same msal lookup):** an id differing only by a trailing space, and an **empty** home account id (`startsWith('')` matches every cached account). Case-only twins do **not** leak: msal lower-cases the cache *key* but not `home_account_id`, so a twin overwrites the entry and the selector fails closed.

## Why it was not fixed with KS-1687

The coordinator scoped KS-1687's round 2 to the refresh path. The sign-in path's fix is a different surface: the new token is also "the entry that changed", so the same before/after snapshot would apply, but a fail-closed sign-in stores `refreshToken = ''` and still writes `status = 'connected'` (KS-1689's open product question), so the user-visible consequence needs that ruling first.

## Suggested direction (no design built, nothing changed)

Apply the snapshot guard to `exchangeAuthCode` so only an entry msal wrote during the call can be returned; sequence it with KS-1689's ruling on how a fail-closed exchange should surface.

## Board search

Over all KS issues, archived included — **1686 issues, 7 pages, pagination exhausted, measured 2026-10-20T02:53Z** — exact substring over title + description: `buildAccountToCache` **0**, `startsWith(homeAccountId` **0**, `startsWith(refreshingId` **0**, `prefix collision` **0**, `ResponseHandler.mjs:326` **0**. The only `GC7` hit is KS-1599, an unrelated incidental string. KS-1682 and KS-1687 were read for the lookup/prefix/`sign-in path` wording: neither mentions it.
**Controls, same corpus and moment:** `exchangeAuthCode` **4** hits and `m365-integration` **36** hits, so the instrument finds text when it is there. (`homeAccountId` returned 0 as well: no ticket names that identifier at all. I had expected KS-1682 to and mis-labelled it a control; it is a data fact, not a control.)

## How it was found

Gate CB1 on PR #1664 (KS-1687 round 1), note N1 and cell GC7, 2026-10-20; reproduced independently by Seat R 59th on the sign-in path. Filed as its own ticket on the coordinator's ruling that it is pre-existing and not fixed in #1664.

title: A transferee cannot read the certification by id: the transfer flow never rewrites the record's issuer or holder, and the E2E spec that asserts it fails three steps earlier
description:
## BLUF

**The E2E spec** `full-certification-flow.api.spec.ts` **asserts that a transferee can read a certification by id after an accepted ownership transfer. Nothing in the product makes that true, and the spec cannot reach that assertion anyway — it fails three steps earlier.** Filed as facts only, during the KS-1695 gap-1 build, because the gap-1 bound (issuer / holder / platform admin) makes the question explicit rather than creating it. No remedy is proposed here: whether a transferee reads a certification by id is a product decision nobody has made.

Refs [KS-1695](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1695).

## The three facts, each with its instrument

**1. An accepted transfer never rewrites the record's issuer or holder.**
The transfer lifecycle lives in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/index.ts` — the endpoints are defined directly on `app`, not under `src/routes/`: `POST /api/transfers/initiate` at `:596`, `/:id/approve` at `:666`, `/:id/execute` at `:795`. `approve` (`:666-733`) mutates only the in-memory `memTransfers` map and `dbSaveTransfer`; `execute` (`:795-857`) sets the transfer's own status, mints a `mock_tx_` hash and writes notifications. **No write to** `documents.owner_user_id` **or** `documents.issuer_user_id` **exists in the service.**
*Instrument:* read of those three handlers at develop `7e3b9362e08b`, plus `/usr/bin/grep -rn "owner_user_id|issuer_user_id|UPDATE documents" services/transfer/src` → **0 hits**. Control: the same grep over `services/originate/src` matches **25 files**, so it discriminates.
*Consequence:* under any issuer/holder bound on `GET /api/certifications/:id`, a transferee reads **404**. This is not specific to KS-1695's shape — it follows from the record never naming the transferee.

**2. The E2E spec fails at STEP 3, two steps before the read.**
`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/tests/integration/full-certification-flow.api.spec.ts`:

* STEP 3 (`:140-150`) posts `{ action, comment, signature }` to `/:id/approve`, but `approveTransferSchema` (`transfer/src/index.ts:395`) **requires** `approverId: z.string().uuid()` and `approverRole: z.string()`. Neither is sent, so zod answers **400** and `expect(response.ok()).toBeTruthy()` fails there.
* STEP 4 (`:157-170`) then asserts `result.status` matches `/completed|accepted/`, while the handler answers `{ success, data: { approval, transfer, fullyApproved } }` — `result.status` is `undefined`.
* `execute` is never called by the spec, so no transfer ever reaches `completed`.
* STEP 5 (`:178-183`) is the `GET /api/certifications/${certificationId}` as the verifier that expects `ok()`.
  *Instrument:* read of `:110-190` of the spec and of the schema at `:395`, both at develop `7e3b9362e08b`.

**3. No push gate runs this suite.**
Nothing in `.githooks/pre-push` or `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/` runs `tests/e2e`. It is a standalone Playwright package (`tests/e2e/package.json`, `"test": "playwright test"`) that needs the full stack.
*Instrument:* `/usr/bin/grep -rn "tests/e2e" .githooks/pre-push scripts/preflight/` → the only two hits are prose comments inside `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh` (`:36`, `:69`), not an invocation. Control: the same hook names other test paths **13** times.

## What was NOT run or measured

* **The spec was never executed.** There is no Docker on this machine, so the stack could not come up. Facts 1–3 are source reads and greps at one sha, not a run. The STEP 3 → 400 claim is therefore a read of the schema against the body, not an observed response.
* Whether any environment outside the push gate (a person's machine, a formal test pass) runs this suite, and whether it has ever passed, is unknown — I did not search CI history or ask anyone.
* Whether a transferee is *expected* to read the certification by id. The spec's own comment says "The verifier should now have access", which is an aspiration in a test, not a ruling.
* Whether `/api/documents/:id/transfer-custody` in originate (a different mechanism, see [KS-1651](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1651)) rewrites the owner. I did not read it; it is not the route the spec calls.

title: Security: GET /api/gdpr/deletion-log with no userId reads every tenant's deletion log — unfiltered SELECT on a table with no tenant_id, admitted to ORG_ADMIN
description:
**BLUF —** `GET /api/gdpr/deletion-log` **called with no** `userId` **runs an unfiltered** `SELECT` **over** `data_deletion_log`**, a table with no** `tenant_id` **column and no RLS policy, and the route admits** `ORG_ADMIN`**. So one organisation's admin can read the newest 100 deletion-log rows of every tenant on the deployment. Source-read on develop** `3a6f1810981e`**; NOT driven on a real Postgres as a second tenant's** `ORG_ADMIN` **— see Not measured.**

### The chain, with the instrument named for each count

| \# | fact | instrument |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | the route is `gdprRouter.get('/deletion-log', requireRole('SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'ORG_ADMIN'), …)` and passes `req.query.userId` straight through | `routes/gdpr.ts:623-626`, read at develop `3a6f1810981e` |
| 2 | with no `userId`, the service runs `SELECT * FROM data_deletion_log ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 100` — **no** `WHERE` **of any kind** | `services/gdprService.ts:1022-1034` |
| 3 | `data_deletion_log` has **no** `tenant_id` **column**: `id, user_id, dsr_id, data_type, records_affected, deletion_method, reason, performed_by, created_at` | `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:473-483` |
| 4 | **no migration attaches an RLS policy to it** | `grep -rn "data_deletion_log" migrations/*.sql \| grep -iE "rls\|policy\|row level"` → 0 lines; the same grep without the second filter returns the two migrations that do touch it (`001`, `036`), so the instrument discriminates |
| 5 | the row reaches HTTP verbatim: `mapDeletionLogRow` copies `reason: r.reason` into `DeletionLogEntry.reason`, and `res.json({ success: true, logs })` returns it | `gdprService.ts:505-517`, `routes/gdpr.ts:627` |
| 6 | it is in the API contract | `originate.openapi.ts:2863`, `deletionLog: z.array(z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())).optional()` |
| 7 | only **4** non-test references to the table exist in the whole repo (2 `INSERT`, 2 `SELECT`) | `grep -rn "data_deletion_log" --include='*.ts' services packages`, minus `__tests__`; control token on the same instrument returns 0 |
| 8 | **no existing ticket covers this read** | census of **all 678** team issues, fetched paginated and matched locally: `data_deletion_log` appears in exactly one (KS-758, which names it only in its F9 prose); control term returns 0. `searchIssues` was **not** used to establish absence — it returns 12 hits for a deliberately meaningless term |

### What an `ORG_ADMIN` of tenant B therefore sees

Rows written for tenant A's subjects: the `data_type` erased, the `records_affected` count, `performed_by` (for connector erasures, `connector:<connectorId>` — a Platform-S organisation identifier), `created_at`, and `reason`. A `user_id` is present on the resolved-subject path, so tenant A's **user UUIDs** are in that payload too.

### Why it is filed now

It was found while censusing the readers of `reason` for KS-758 F9, which asks what the unresolvable connector-erasure path should record. The answer turned on this: anything written into `reason` is published on this endpoint, which is why KS-758's option (a) — the subject's `external_ref` as written — would put a Platform-S subject reference on a cross-tenant readable response. **That is evidence for KS-758's card, and the read itself is a separate defect from what KS-758 records**, so it is here rather than folded in.

### Not measured — stated plainly rather than implied

* **This is a source read.** The endpoint was **not** driven on a real Postgres while authenticated as a second tenant's `ORG_ADMIN`. Steps 1-6 are the code path; the exploit is inferred from them and has not been executed.
* **Whether a deployment actually has more than one tenant's rows in the table** is not measured here, and per-tenant database separation would change the blast radius. (The project's isolation model is per-tenant databases with RLS inert by construction — if that holds for every environment, the cross-tenant reach may be nil in practice and the defect is then the missing guard rather than a live exposure. Unverified either way by me.)
* `requireRole`**'s own semantics** — whether `ORG_ADMIN` is scoped to a tenant by the middleware before the handler runs — was not read. If it is, step 1 still permits the unfiltered query, because the handler applies no scope of its own.
* The resolved-subject path (`user_id` present) was not separately enumerated for how many such rows a real deployment holds.

### No remedy is proposed here

The shape of the fix is a design decision on a GDPR audit surface — add a tenant column and filter, scope by the caller's organisation, or restrict the route to `SYSTEM_ADMIN` — and each has a different effect on what an `ORG_ADMIN` can legitimately audit. It is ruled before it is built.

*Found 2026-10-20 by Seat G 13th while building KS-758 F9 (option (b)); develop* `3a6f1810981e3e268e77d0e4721987d186b71810`*.*

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign-cert and /:id/sign-wallet mint a derived document and record NO provenance for it, so the connector that minted it is still refused certify on its own document (the KS-1557 403, left open on the two sibling routes)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/documents/:id/sign-cert` **and** `POST /api/documents/:id/sign-wallet` **mint a derived document and record no provenance for it at all.** So a connector that mints a document through either route is still refused certify on **its own** document — the same 403 KS-1557 fixes for `/:id/version`, left open on the two sibling routes. Facts only; no fix proposed here.

## Where

`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`:

* `'/:id/sign-cert'` **at** `:2891` and `'/:id/sign-wallet'` **at** `:3159`. Both mint a new document (a fresh `external_id`, `parent_document_id` = the source) carrying `metadata.versionAction` (`'sign-cert'` / `'sign-wallet'`) and `metadata.versionedById` = `user.id` (`:3077`, `:3272`), and both set `status: 'signed'`.
* **Neither writes any** `action_provenance` **row.** Instrument: `recordOnBehalfOf|recordConnectorProvenance|recordActionProvenance` over each route body returns **0** and **0**. Control: the same matcher over the `/:id/version` body (`:2225`-`:2420`) returns **2**, so it is not silently matching nothing.
* The KS-1557 fix adds `recordConnectorProvenance(req, newExternalId, CONNECTOR_CREATE_ACTION)` to `/:id/version` **only**.

## Consequence

`callerMayCertifyDocument` (`routes/certifications.ts:119-128`) ends in `role === 'connector' && wasCreatedByConnector(document.id, userId)`, and `wasCreatedByConnector` (`services/provenance.ts:285`) needs a row with `action IN ('create','create:connector')`. A document minted by either sign route has no such row, so:

* its **minting connector** is refused certify on it, on the lineage path and the legacy path alike (403);
* `GET /api/documents/:id`'s `isCreatingConnector` read-back (`documents.ts:1138`) is false for the minter.

This is exactly Stuart's KS-1557 shape (comment `16e8498d`: a certify attached to the document's current version answers 403 and Platform S falls back to a flat anchor), reachable through these two routes instead of `/version`.

## Population, measured read-only on demo 2026-10-20

**Zero today.** Of 31 version-minted documents, **0** carry `status = 'signed'` (the discriminator — `/version` writes `'draft'`, both sign routes write `'signed'`), and **0** carry `versionAction = 'sign-wallet'`; the only `versionAction` values present are `sign-cert` and `watermark`, all 31 at `status = 'anchored'`. So the two sign routes have minted nothing on demo, and KS-1557's migration 055 therefore has nothing of this kind to backfill there. Control in the same statement: 207 documents. **kintsugi is UNMEASURED.**

## Also relevant

These two routes were the **second vector** of gate BN1's blocker on KS-1557's first backfill attempt: because they mint a child and write no row, a parent could have more children than provenance rows, and a backfill that attributed from the parent's rows credited those children to the wrong connector. The landed backfill attributes each child from its own `metadata.versionedById` instead, so it **skips** these children rather than mis-crediting them — the refusal above is preserved, not papered over.

## Not claimed

* No severity judgement beyond this ticket's priority, and **no fix design**. Whether these routes should write the row, and whether a signed document should be certifiable by its minter at all, is a product question.
* Not measured: whether Platform S uses either route. `Secuura/platform-s` is 404 to this project's PAT, so it cannot be answered from here.
* Not measured on kintsugi.

Found by Seat C 31st via gate BN1 note N5 while building KS-1557's backfill, 2026-10-20.

title: auth: a request in flight resurrects a revoked session — updateSessionActivity and rotateSessionRefreshToken write back the stale isActive:true record with a fresh 24h TTL (session.ts:270-294)
description:
## BLUF

**A revocation can be undone by any request that was already in flight.** `updateSessionActivity` (`session.ts:270-279`) and `rotateSessionRefreshToken` (`:282-294`) both do a read-modify-write: `get` the session JSON, mutate, `setex` it back. If `revokeSession` lands between the `get` and the `setex`, the **stale** `isActive:true` **record is written back with a fresh 24-hour TTL** — and the session is live again.

Worse, it becomes **unrevokable**: the revocation already removed it from `user_sessions:<id>`, so a later `revokeAllUserSessions` returns **0** and cannot find it.

Pre-existing. Filed from gate BO1's note N2 on PR #1655.

## Recommendation

Either a **revoked tombstone** that `getSession` checks, or a **conditional write** (a Lua script or a WATCH/MULTI compare-and-set) so a write cannot resurrect a record revoked since it was read. The tombstone is probably cheaper and also fixes the orphaned-from-the-set half.

## Why it matters more than a normal race

`updateSessionActivity` runs on **every authenticated request** (`middleware/authenticate.ts:160`), so the window is open continuously under load rather than at a rare moment. An attacker hammering requests on the old token widens it deliberately. It affects **every** revocation path — logout, the admin status change, user erasure, and the new password change/reset.

## The measurement (gate BO1, probe B3)

The interleave was forced deterministically:

* after the revocation (returned n=1, record inactive), the in-flight write left `getSession` returning the session **ACTIVE**;
* the session was already gone from `user_sessions:<id>`, so a second `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **0** and could not reach it.
* **Control B3c** — the same steps *without* the interleave: the session stayed revoked. So the probe measures the race, not a broken teardown.
* **Not run:** a timing measurement against real Redis. The probe drives the real `session.ts` against a fake that implements the session commands, so the *window's width* in production is unmeasured; its existence is not.

## Where

* `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:270-279` `updateSessionActivity`
* `services/auth/src/services/session.ts:282-294` `rotateSessionRefreshToken`
* called from `services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts:160`

**Board search before filing:** `updateSessionActivity` returned **0** hits; `rotateSessionRefreshToken` returned 4, none about a resurrection race (KS-756 the opaque handle, KS-1687 m365 token persistence, KS-1150 the OAuth grant, KS-329 PQC); also searched "resurrect revoked session" and "session revoked refresh token still redeems". **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated never-published token returned **0**, `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **1**.

Related KS-1407.

title: auth: the OAuth refresh_token grant never checks the ORIGIN SESSION, so a revoked session's refresh token still redeems and mints a brand-new session (oauth.ts:988-1089)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/oauth/token` **with** `grant_type=refresh_token` **never reads** `decoded.sessionId`**, so revoking a user's sessions does not reach the OAuth refresh path.** A refresh token issued before a revocation still redeems, and mints a *brand-new* session. Measured by the gate on PR #1655 (KS-1407): after `revokeAllUserSessions` (n=1, `getSession` null), the same refresh token redeemed **200**, then **200 again**, leaving the account with **2 live sessions**.

Pre-existing; **outside** that PR's diff. Filed from gate BO1's note N1.

## Recommendation

Check the origin session on this grant (or introduce a per-user credential epoch) before minting. The oracle is already in the repo: the *interactive* `POST /api/auth/refresh` does a server-side session lookup at `routes/auth.ts:688-689`, so the two refresh paths disagree about whether a session must still exist. Wednesday or Kam should rule whether the fix rides with a KS-1407 follow-up or stands alone.

## Where

`services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:988-1089` — the `grant_type=refresh_token` branch. It verifies the JWT, checks the jti denylist, pins `user.status === 'ACTIVE'` at `:1067`, and mints a new session at `:1078`. It never consults the session named by the token it is redeeming.

## The measurement (gate BO1, probe C1)

Real `session.ts`, real `refreshDenylist.ts`, real `jwt.ts`, on the ks823 scaffold:

1. created a session and minted an OAuth pair bound to public client `pub-1`;
2. ran `revokeAllUserSessions` — returned n=1, and `getSession` then returned null;
3. redeemed the same refresh token: **200**. Redeemed again: **200**. Account left with **2 live sessions**.

* **Control in the same case:** a client-mismatch redeem was refused **400**, so the harness can produce a refusal.
* **Not run:** an authorization code issued before a revocation and exchanged after it. The code grant also mints a fresh session (`:969`), so it is plausibly a smaller sibling — unmeasured, stated as such.

## Consequence

Anyone holding an OAuth grant obtained before a password change, a password reset, an admin status change or a user erasure keeps a renewable foothold. It is the direct counterexample to KS-1407's premise that no session may outlive the password that minted it.

## Scope — what this ticket is NOT

**KS-1150 R-2 already covers the rotation/denylist half of this branch** ("the refresh grant does not rotate / denylist the presented token", `:836`/`:860`) and is still OPEN — its 2026-09-14 comment records R-1 landing as `b42e260c9897` with "R-2 / R-3 stay OPEN". **This ticket is the other half: the missing ORIGIN-SESSION check.** They are overlapping-but-distinct, not duplicates — a perfectly rotating implementation would still mint a new session for an account whose sessions were all revoked, because nothing reads `decoded.sessionId`. Do not close either as a duplicate of the other.

**Board search before filing:** `revokeAllUserSessions`, `updateSessionActivity`, `rotateSessionRefreshToken`, `decoded.sessionId`, "oauth refresh token revoked session", "session revoked refresh token still redeems". Nearest neighbours KS-1150 (the rotation half, above), KS-756 (the opaque session refresh handle, a different mechanism), KS-1280 (a revoked session's Bearer forwarded by originate, a different service). **Controls both ways:** a freshly generated token that was never published returned **0** hits, and `revokeAllUserSessions` returned **1** — so the search discriminates.

Related KS-1407, KS-1150.

title: Security: POST /api/documents/:id/version has NO per-document access check on its source - any write-role caller in the tenant can derive a new version from another organisation's document (the sibling of the certify path KS-1557/#1619 closed)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/documents/:id/version` **checks a ROLE, a SCOPE and the TENANT, and nothing about the caller's relationship to the source document.** Any write-role caller in the tenant can derive a new version from **another organisation's** document, and the derived row is a real child of it. This is the sibling of the path KS-1557 / pull request #1619 closed on `POST /api/certifications/issue`: the same defect class, the same service, still open on the versioning route. Measured on a scratch stack at develop `89956fe92956`. Facts only — no fix is proposed here.

## Where

`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, the `'/:id/version'` handler:

* `:2219` — `const ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES = DOCUMENT_WRITE_ROLES;`
* `:2246` — `isAllowedByRoleOrScope(req, ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES, 'documents:write')` — role or scope only.
* `:2281` — `const source = await getDocument(id, tenantId, (req as any).db);` followed by a 404 when it does not resolve, and a `metadata.documentType` guard. **There is no owner / recipient / creating-connector test anywhere in the handler** — the check `callerMayCertifyDocument` applies on the certify path (`routes/certifications.ts:119-128`, call sites `:223` legacy and `:441` lineage) has no counterpart here.

## Measured (scratch Postgres 15 at migration 054, real `documents` + `certifications` routers, `secuura_app`, both `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false` and `=true` — identical results in both)

| cell | what was done | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| G1 | **a FOREIGN organisation's connector** calls `/version` on organisation A's document | **201.** The minted row is a real child: its `parent_document_id` resolves to A's document. |
| G1 (same cell) | **the discriminating control** — that **same caller**, on that **same document**, through `POST /api/certifications/issue` with `parentDocumentId` | **403** `FORBIDDEN` |
| G2 | an **interactive write-role USER of another organisation** calls `/version` on A's document | **201** |
| G3 | **the bound** — a caller in **another tenant** calls `/version` on A's document | **404** `NOT_FOUND "Document not found in this tenant"` |

G1's two halves are the finding in one line: **the two sibling routes disagree about the same caller on the same document.** G3 bounds it — it does not cross the tenant, because `getDocument` is tenant-scoped.

## Board search before filing (symbol and path, each with a control)

* `callerMayCertifyDocument` → **2** hits (KS-1557, KS-1679); `isAllowedByRoleOrScope` → **2** (KS-1202, KS-1433). Both controls fire, so the instrument discriminates rather than returning everything.
* `ALLOWED_VERSION_ROLES`, `/:id/version`, `documents/:id/version`, `parent_document_id` → each returns the 12-hit fuzzy cap, and **none of the hits names this defect.** The nearest four, each a different thing: **KS-1538** (the legacy certify path — fixed), **KS-1557** (the lineage certify path — this route's sibling), **KS-1508** (`versionedById` is server-set — same route, different defect), **KS-1228** (a refused request still writes an `action_provenance` row — same route, different defect).
* **0 open hits for the source-access check itself.**

## Sequencing — this matters before anyone gates this route

The KS-1557 fix (shape (a′): `/version` records the creating connector on the document it mints, under the action value `create:connector`) **must land before any source-access gate is added here.** Otherwise a gate written with the same predicate would refuse `/version` on a version-minted document for exactly the reason certify refuses it today: a `/version`-created document has no creation provenance row of its own, so `wasCreatedByConnector` is false for the connector that actually made it. Measured on demo: **31 of 31** `/version`-minted documents have no such row.

## Open question, UNMEASURABLE from this project

**Does Platform S ever version a document it did not itself originate?** It decides the client-visible risk of closing this gap — if S does, closing it turns some S calls into 403. It cannot be answered from here: `Secuura/platform-s` returns 404 to this project's PAT (which sees exactly one repository), so no search of S's code is possible from Platform K's identity. **Stated as a question, not an assumption, and not asked of anyone here.**

## Not claimed

* No severity judgement beyond the priority on this ticket, and no fix design.
* The derived row carries the **caller's own** `newContentHash`, so this is not an alteration of the source document's bytes; the source gains a child it did not consent to, and the derived row presents as part of its lineage.
* Not measured: whether any such cross-organisation version exists in live data.

Found by Seat C 31st while measuring KS-1557 (Stuart's comment `16e8498d`) at develop `89956fe92956`, 2026-10-20.

title: prism GET /api/credentials/:id returns any stored prism credential by id with no owner check (cluster-internal; not routed by the gateway)
description:
## BLUF

**prism has its own** `GET /api/credentials/:id` **that returns any stored prism credential by id, with no owner check.** It reads prism's own table (`svc_prism_credentials`), not vc-issuer's, and it is reachable only from inside the cluster: the gateway does not route `/api/credentials` to prism. KS-1116 bound vc-issuer's route of the same name; this one is untouched. Gate BH1 NOTE 6 on #1648 (census side-finding).

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`, `services/prism/src/index.ts`)

* `:690` `app.get('/api/credentials/:id', …)` → `dbGetCredential(req.params.id)` (`:231`): `SELECT * FROM svc_prism_credentials WHERE id = $1`. The handler returns the credential or 404. There is no read of `req.user`, and no owner or tenant condition.
* Siblings on the same table, not examined for this ticket: `GET /api/credentials/subject/:did` (`:707`), `POST /api/credentials/revoke` (`:814`).
* Reachability: the gateway proxies only `^/api/did` to prism (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:920`; control: the same search finds 6 vcIssuer mounts). `docker-compose.yml` has prism's host port commented out ("Was: - "6001:4001""). So a caller needs to be inside the cluster network, and must still pass prism's own bearer check on `/api`.

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 6, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `svc_prism_credentials`, `dbGetCredential`, `prism/src/index.ts:690`, `prism GET /api/credentials` → 0 each (control: a never-written token → 0; `generateAccessToken` → 2).

title: Every API key without a connector id is the same principal (connector:api-key) within its tenant, so under KS-1116 those keys read each other's presentations and credentials
description:
## BLUF

**Every API key minted without a connector id authenticates as the SAME principal within its tenant,** `connector:api-key`**. Under KS-1116's "owner = the principal that created it", those keys therefore read each other's presentations and credentials.** Cross-tenant stays separated, because a key's tenant is fixed at mint. The shape predates KS-1116; KS-1116 is what makes the principal an ownership boundary. Gate BH1 NOTE 3 on #1648.

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`)

* `services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:289`, in `generateConnectorToken` (the sk\_-key → JWT exchange the gateway performs for an `x-api-key` caller): `userId: \`connector:${meta.connectorId || 'api-key'}\`\`. A key with no connector id gets the literal fallback.
* `services/security/src/index.ts:445-448`: `tenant_id` is written on every key INSERT and is immutable per key ("a key minted for tenant A never moves to tenant B"). So the collapse is per tenant, not global.
* vc-issuer (since #1648) stamps `created_by_user_id` from `req.user.userId` and compares it on read (`services/vc-issuer/src/ownership.ts`). It has no special case for the fallback: `git grep "api-key"` over `services/vc-issuer/src` → 0 files.
* **Precedent in the codebase:** originate already refuses the fallback principal for erase-connector — `isFallbackConnectorId` (`services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:114`, used at `:146` and `:295`; KS-695, wording residue in KS-1579). There the fallback is treated as "not a distinct principal". vc-issuer treats it as one.
* Related, not this defect: KS-869 (merged) made a key's connector id persist across restarts. It does not change what a key minted WITHOUT one becomes.

## Open question

What should "the principal that created it" mean for a key with no connector id: the key itself (its key id), the fallback shared by every such key in the tenant (today), or not a principal at all (originate's erase-connector stance)?

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 3, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `connector:api-key` → KS-869, KS-1579; `generateConnectorToken` → KS-1584, KS-1409, KS-1152; none owns the shared-principal question.

title: vc-issuer: after a revoke, the credential's creator can be refused GET /api/credentials/:id on the memory fallback - revoke() stores the row with no owner entry (fails closed)
description:
## BLUF

**After** `POST /api/credentials/:id/revoke`**, the credential's own creator can be refused** `GET /api/credentials/:id` **(404) whenever vc-issuer then falls back to memory.** `revoke()` writes the row into the in-memory store with no owner entry, so the KS-1116 bound reads it as owner-less. This fails CLOSED: a foreign caller is refused too, so the cost is availability, never a leak. Gate BH1 NOTE 2 on #1648.

## What was measured (develop `c66b834ed451`, `services/vc-issuer/src/repositories/credentialRepo.ts`)

* `revoke()` (`:288`) reads the row with `getById(id)` (`:292`) — from the database when it is available — and then calls `memoryStore.set(credential.id, revokedCredential)` (`:306`). It writes **no** `memoryOwners` entry.
* `getRecordById()` takes the owner from `memoryOwners.get(id) ?? OWNERLESS` on the memory path. So for any row this process did not itself `store()` or boot-load — one created on another replica, or after this process booted — and then revoked here, the memory copy is OWNERLESS.
* `mayRead()` refuses an OWNERLESS row under the interim reading (`ownerlessRowReadable()` returns false). With the database unavailable, or the SELECT throwing, the creator gets the unknown-id 404. Gate BH1 measured exactly that: its Q1 cell, "Alice 404".
* The foreign-caller half is pinned by cell Q1 in `ks1116-presentation-and-credential-reads-bound-to-the-creator.test.ts` (test-only follow-up to #1648). The creator's 404 is deliberately NOT asserted there, so that this ticket's fix does not have to edit a cell.

## Shape of a fix (not decided)

`revoke()` carries the owner it read — `getRecordById` instead of `getById`, writing `memoryOwners` alongside `memoryStore` — and a cell pins that the creator still reads her revoked credential on the memory path.

## Provenance

Gate BH1 (Opus, tier 1) on #1648, NOTE 2, 2026-10-20; re-read at develop `c66b834ed451` by Seat C 30th. Board search first: `memoryOwners`, `revoke() puts`, `Map-miss` → 0; `credentialRepo.revoke` → KS-1352 only, which is revoked-credential verification, a different defect.

title: Five tracked files cite DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md as a repo document, including two product-code comments deferring a correctness condition to it, but the file is not in the repo
description:
## BLUF

**Five tracked files at** `develop` **cite** `DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md` **as though it were a repo document. It is not in the repo, has never been in the repo, and two of the five citations are product-code comments that defer a correctness condition to it.** The file is real, but it lives in the coordinator's own notes outside this repository, so nobody working from a clone can open the authority those comments point at.

Measured at `develop` `292fe0b1642a`:

* `git ls-tree -r --name-only` returns **4,604** entries, of which **0** match `blocker` in any case. Control on the same listing: `DEV-PROCESS` matches **1**, so the zero is a real absence and not a broken instrument.
* `git log --all --diff-filter=ADR -- '*DEPLOY-BLOCKERS*'` is empty: it was never added and never deleted.
* Not under `2_Project_Files`, not elsewhere in the project folder.

## Recommendation

Pick one of two, then make the five citations consistent with it:

1. **Add an in-repo deploy-preconditions document** that the product-code comments can cite, leaving the coordinator's file as the working copy; or
2. **Keep the authority outside the repo and change the five citations to say so** — name it as an external document rather than a path a reader will look for in the tree.

**Do not copy the coordinator's file into the repo** as-is; which of the two above applies is a maintainer call, not an agent one. Nothing is blocked today: Seat D 22nd's deploy brief named the file by its absolute path and that seat worked from it.

## Detail

### The five citations at `develop` 292fe0b1642a

| File | Line | What it defers to the missing document |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts` | 73 | *"DEPLOY-BLOCKERS step (3) asserts* `data.tenantId` *equals Platform S's key tenant"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/metering.ts` | 77 | *"That is a DEPLOY gate, not a merge gate, and it is on DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1032-unconfigured-vouch-fails-closed.test.ts` | 24 | *"deploy condition lives in DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md; it is not a condition on this code"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1041-gateway-provenance.test.ts` | 213 | *"the risk it named is real and is handled as a DEPLOY gate in DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docs/ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md` | 120 | *"DEPLOY-BLOCKERS step (3) asserts* `data.tenantId` *equals Platform S's key tenant"* |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` | 255 | *"*`DEPLOY-BLOCKERS.md` *row 7 condition … is closed"* |

### Pre-existing, not introduced by the docs refresh

At the base of PR #1625 (`4a065fb7535`) **four** of those files already carried the citation (`ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md`, both tests, `metering.ts`). PR #1625 added the fifth file (`DEV-PROCESS.md:255`). So this is a repo defect that the docs refresh widened by one, not a defect of that PR, and it is filed separately for that reason.

### Why it is worth fixing rather than tolerating

`metering.ts:73-77` is product code stating that a correctness property — the metering response's `data.tenantId` equalling Platform S's key tenant — is *not* checked at merge time because a deploy gate covers it. A reader auditing that code cannot reach the gate to confirm it says so, or that it is still current. Separately, that step-3 detector was independently measured **vacuous on kintsugi** during the 2026-10-19/20 deploy census (`DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` equals the tenant of all 14 `svc_api_keys` rows with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=false`, so the assertion passes whether the vouch works or not) — which is exactly the kind of thing an unreachable gate document lets persist.

### Board search before filing

`searchIssues` is fuzzy here and returns its 40-hit cap for every term, so absence was established with exact substring filters instead:

* `title contains "DEPLOY-BLOCKERS"` → **0** issues.
* `description contains "DEPLOY-BLOCKERS"` → **2** (KS-1594, KS-1582), both of which *cite* the file as the home of a deploy condition rather than owning this defect.
* Positive control: `description contains "admin_organisation_scopes"` → **3** issues (KS-1601, KS-1592, KS-1585), so the filter does match when there is something to match.
* Negative control: a freshly generated random token, deliberately not written into any ticket → **0** hits.

*Filed by the Platform K agent (Seat C 29th) during the KS-1668 review of PR #1625. Facts only; no code or document was changed by this ticket.*

title: m365 admin setup wizard sends a Secuura tenant id as organizationId - after KS-1673 the tenant choice is ignored
description:
**BLUF:** The admin M365 setup wizard sends a **Secuura tenant id** in the `organizationId` field — or the literal `'default'` when no tenant is selected. Since KS-1673 (merged 2026-10-20, #1633), the m365 service takes the organisation from the caller's login token and **ignores** that field. So the tenant a system admin picks in the wizard no longer decides anything: the connection, or the Teams webhook, lands in the admin's **own** organisation.

**Read statically at develop** `9207fe336797`**. Not driven.**

## What the wizard sends

| line | call | sent |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `frontend/admin/src/components/M365SetupWizard.tsx:94`, `:98` | `POST /api/m365/connections/init` | `organizationId: selectedTenantId \|\| 'default'` |
| `M365SetupWizard.tsx:171` | `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` | `organizationId: selectedTenantId \|\| 'default'` |

* `selectedTenantId` comes from `useTenantStore` (`M365SetupWizard.tsx:84`).
* The store is filled only for `super_admin` / `system_admin` / `SYSTEM_ADMIN` (`frontend/admin/src/components/Layout.tsx:107-112`, via `fetchTenants()`).
* Its values are **tenant** ids. A login token's `organizationId` is an **organisation** id. These are two different id spaces.

## What happens now (after KS-1673)

* **The field is stripped and ignored** on both calls. A system admin's new connection is owned by the admin's own organisation, whichever tenant the wizard shows as selected.
* **A token with no organisation gets 403** from both calls.
* **Tenant admins**, who previously got 400 because `'default'` failed the old UUID check, now succeed under their own organisation.
* **Rows written before KS-1673** carry a tenant id in `organization_id`. They now match no token, so they are owned by nobody. **Re-connecting is the remedy** (ruled 2026-10-20). Read-only measurement on 2026-10-19 found **0** connections and **0** Teams webhooks on kintsugi and on demo.

## Open question — not decided here

Whether a system admin may set up Microsoft 365 **on behalf of a customer organisation** is a product decision. It has gone to Kamil. Until it is ruled, the fail-closed behaviour above stands, consistent with KS-1673's no-bypass ruling. **No fix is proposed in this ticket.**

## How it was found

Gate AS1's note N1 on #1633 (KS-1673 PR A). Both frontend facts were re-read at develop by Seat R 56th before filing. Five Linear searches found no existing ticket: "M365SetupWizard", "m365 setup wizard organizationId", "wizard tenant id organizationId", "selectedTenantId m365", "m365 wizard default organization". The control search returned KS-1677. KS-1490 names the same file only because of a stale host URL.

title: m365: connections probably never persist or reload - svc_m365_connections is fail-closed RLS, read as secuura_app with no tenant GUC, and the save error is swallowed
description:
**BLUF:** m365-integration probably **never saves a Microsoft 365 connection to the database, and never reloads one**, and it does so without any visible error. Its table is under fail-closed row-level security. The service reads and writes it as a role without bypass, and never sets the tenant setting the policy checks. Every save fails and is swallowed as a single warning, and every reload returns nothing. So a connection lives only in the memory of the process that created it, and is lost on restart.

**The policy also matches on** `tenant_id`**, which for this table holds the Microsoft (Entra) directory id, not the Secuura tenant.** So even a correctly set tenant would never match a row.

Found while measuring KS-1673. **This ticket rests on reading the source plus two measured flags. Nothing was driven.** By Wednesday's ruling, nothing more was measured on any box for it.

## Facts

| fact | where |
| -- | -- |
| `svc_m365_connections` is in the consolidated tenant-policy table set | `migrations/038_rls_consolidate_policy.sql:42` |
| 038 creates `tenant_isolation`, `USING` / `WITH CHECK` on `tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true)` (fail-open when unset) | `038:84-93` |
| 039 re-declares it **fail-closed** on the 038 table set (an unset setting admits nothing) | `migrations/039_rls_fail_closed.sql:2-8` |
| **Measured on both kintsugi and demo** (flags only): RLS enabled = t, forced = t, 1 policy | read-only count pass, 2026-10-19 |
| **Measured on both boxes:** m365's database role is `secuura_app`, `rolsuper` = f, `rolbypassrls` = f | same pass |
| m365 never sets the tenant setting: **0** hits for `app.current_tenant_id`, `set_config`, `tenant_scope_bypass` or `withTenant` in `services/m365-integration/src/` | develop `390cc0a317c9` |
| `dbSaveConnection` catches every error and logs one warn (`'DB save connection failed'`) | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:189` |
| `svc_m365_connections.tenant_id` holds the **Entra directory id**, not the Secuura tenant UUID | repo `BACKLOG.md` (an existing entry), and the connection's `tenantId` field |
| `svc_m365_connections` has **0 rows** on both boxes | same pass. Consistent with "never saves", but also consistent with nobody having connected, so it **does not prove it** |

**Compare:** `svc_teams_webhooks` has row-level security **disabled**, with 0 policies (measured on both boxes). The two m365 tables are inconsistent with each other. The Teams side has the cross-organisation exposure tracked in KS-1673.

## Not measured

* Whether an INSERT as `secuura_app` with no setting is actually refused on these boxes. This is a static reading of 039's intent; the flags are measured.
* The service log's count of `'DB save connection failed'` lines. I measured nothing more on the boxes, by ruling.

## Why it matters

* **Correctness:** M365 connections cannot survive a restart.
* **Interaction with KS-1673:** the connections that matter are the in-memory ones, so binding in-memory connections to an organisation is the whole fix there. A future fix to this ticket must keep that binding when rows start reloading. The `organization_id` column is already written and read.

## Searched before filing

"svc_m365_connections RLS", "m365 loadFromDb connections reload", "svc_teams_webhooks row level security", "secuura_app m365 FORCE". The negative control `qzxwvkplmrty` returned 0. KS-1673, KS-1670, KS-693, KS-1335 and KS-934 were read; none owns this.

title: auth: no provider identity is ever stored - createUser and updateUser both drop social-id fields, so /social/link answers linked:true over nothing
description:
**BLUF:** The auth service never stores a provider identity (Google, Apple, GitHub, Microsoft personal). All three code paths that try to save one drop it silently, while the code that reads it back works. So no account can ever be found by the social account linked to it. `POST /social/link` answers `linked: true` with nothing saved, and its "already linked to another user" check can never fire. **Nothing is exposed today**, because an identity that is never stored authenticates nobody. **But the fix is security-sensitive.** The code warns that once ids persist, a risk that is latent today becomes live.

Measured by Seat R 55th at develop `4a065fb7535080190c407237f948d0af3538f2dd`. Line numbers come from a byte-identical copy of `services/auth` at `115797747cb6`. #1626 changed `routes/auth.ts` by +2/-2 at `:257` only, so they still hold.

## The three write sites, all dropped

| site | path | what happens |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `routes/auth.ts:1180` | social sign-in, **new user** | sets `newUser[`${provider}Id`] = profile.providerId` and passes it to `createUser`, whose INSERT names **no** social-id column |
| `routes/auth.ts:1249` | social sign-in, **existing account matched by email**, after the KS-795 gate | `updateUser(user.id, { [socialIdField]: providerId })`, and `updateUser` issues **no statement** for that field |
| `routes/auth.ts:1323` | `POST /social/link` (authenticated) | same `updateUser` call, then answers `{ success: true, linked: true }` |

**Why both writers drop it:**

* `updateUser`'s `fieldMap` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:801-824`) has 20 keys and **none** for a social id. A key that is not in the map is skipped, so a call carrying only a social id issues zero statements and returns the unchanged row. Control: the same read finds `walletAddress` once.
* `createUser` (`:668`): the 60 lines from its declaration mention **no** `google_id`, `apple_id`, `github_id`, `linkedin_id`, `facebook_id` or `microsoft_personal_id`.

## The columns and the reader exist

* `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:534-539` adds `google_id`, `apple_id`, `github_id` and `microsoft_personal_id`.
* `userRepo.getUserBySocialId` (`:618`) reads them through the `SECURITY DEFINER` function `auth_find_user_by_social($1, $2)`.
* It is called at `routes/auth.ts:1039` (sign-in) and `:1317` (`/social/link`). It can only ever return null for an identity this app linked.

## What follows from that

* Every social sign-in resolves its account **by email**. A provider account whose email differs from the platform account can never sign in to it, even after a "successful" link.
* `/social/link`'s conflict check at `:1318` ("This social account is already linked to another user") cannot fire. So two users can each "link" the same provider account and both get `linked: true`.
* `/social/link` also raises `verificationLevel` to `SOCIAL` at `:1327` on the strength of a link that was never stored.

## ⚠ The fix is the dangerous part, and the code says so

`routes/auth.ts:1233-1240`, verbatim in substance: the link write's danger *"is LATENT rather than current: today* `updateUser` *has no social-id fields in its fieldMap, so the write is silently dropped. The moment that persistence defect is repaired, a pre-gate link write would attach an ATTACKER's provider identity to a SUSPENDED victim's account … That is why this reordering lands BEFORE the persistence fix, not after it."*

The KS-795 F-4 comment at `:1044-1050` also notes that the email-key rules start to matter *"the day the social-id persistence defect is fixed and this lookup starts finding rows"*.

So the fix must:

* keep every link write **after** the gate;
* re-check the `:1318` conflict path, which becomes live;
* decide what happens to accounts that were "linked" while nothing persisted (there are none in the database to migrate, by construction).

It should go through a tier-1 gate.

## Priority: Medium, and why

* **Not High:** nothing exploitable is live. The defect fails closed, and normal sign-in works through the email branch.
* **Not Low:**
  * A user-facing success answer is false: `linked: true` with nothing saved.
  * A verification level is raised over it.
  * The repair re-opens the KS-795 class unless it is done deliberately.

## Where it is already written down

* The repo's `BACKLOG.md` entry: "`userRepo.updateUser` silently drops EVERY social-id write — the account-linking it performs never reaches the database". It was widened on 2026-09-05 to say that `createUser` drops it too. That entry is the source; this ticket is its Linear home, because no Linear ticket owned it.
* The code comments at `routes/auth.ts:1233-1240` and `:1298-1301`.
* **KS-1460**, the discarding-`updateUser` sweep. Gate AO1's census on #1626 noted that at `:1249` and `:1323` `updateUserOrThrow` **would not catch** this, because no write is issued at all. See KS-1460's comment `73f91c88-be30-4865-92a7-98cc7a146017`.

Searched before filing:

* Phrases: "social id link updateUser drops", "socialIdField fieldMap", "social/link linked true", "verificationLevel SOCIAL unconfirmed".
* Negative control: `qvzkxmplorft` returned 0.
* The only hits were KS-1460 (the sweep, which cannot fix this) and KS-1617 (social sign-in diagnostics).

title: renovate.json at the repo root: does Renovate for the systemTest pins conflict with the 2026-07-04 ruling "Dependabot, not Renovate" (KS-352 / KS-353)?
description:
## Found while

Aligning the docs with the rulings in the Linear tickets ([KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or)).

## What is there

`renovate.json` is tracked at the repo root. It was last changed 2026-10-07 for [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is) and [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) ("Renovate sees the k6 pin"). It extends `config:recommended`, ignores `Blockchain/Dev/**`, runs before 6am on Monday, groups the observability stack images and the k6 runtime, and patches systemTest npm updates.

## The ruling it may conflict with

[KS-352](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-352/start-secuurash-rebuild-triage-npm-audit-vulnerabilities-across) and [KS-353](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-353/start-secuurash-rebuild-clear-npm-dependency-deprecation-warnings) (2026-07-04): "Dependabot, not Renovate". The repo docs and `.github/dependabot.yml` follow that ruling; the docs do not mention Renovate at all.

## Question for Kamil

1. Is Renovate allowed for the **systemTest** pins (everything outside `Blockchain/Dev/**`), with Dependabot kept for the platform, or should `renovate.json` go?
2. Whichever you choose, the docs should say it. I will write the answer into the docs under this ticket's number and the date.

## Related

[KS-1446](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1446/renovate-cannot-bump-base-image-watchsh-excluded-bases-blockchaindev) already asks whether Renovate may bump `base-image-watch.sh` (it is under `ignorePaths`) and says it needs Kamil's agreement; the answer to question 1 decides it.

## Not in scope

No change to `renovate.json` is proposed here. The docs-only PR for [KS-1668](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1668/docs-record-kamils-linear-rulings-that-platform-k-docs-omit-or) leaves this file alone.

title: Azure: a missing secuura-app-db-password key-vault secret silently puts every runtime service on the ADMIN role, so RLS does not bind at all
description:
## BLUF

**On Azure, if the** `secuura-app-db-password` **key-vault secret is absent, every runtime service**
**connects as the ADMIN/OWNER role — and row-level security then does not bind at all.** It is a
deliberate, documented fallback so a first-time deploy works; the cost is that in that state RLS is
not the enforcement anywhere, and only each query's own bound predicates stand between a caller and
another tenant's rows.

## Recommendation

Do not remove the fallback — a first deploy needs it. Make it **loud and detectable** instead:

1. have the deploy print a clear warning when it takes the admin path, naming what is not enforced;
2. add a post-deploy check that asserts `current_user` is `secuura_app` (or that an unset tenant GUC
   sees zero rows), so "RLS is binding" is a measured deploy fact rather than an assumption;
3. decide whether a *re-run* is mandatory before an environment is considered deployed — the
   fallback's own comment says a re-run picks up `secuura_app`, but nothing enforces one.

## Detail

`deployment/azure/deploy.sh:679-702`:

```
APP_DB_PASSWORD=$(az keyvault secret show --vault-name $KEY_VAULT_NAME \
    --name secuura-app-db-password --query value -o tsv 2>/dev/null || echo "")
...
if [ -n "$APP_DB_PASSWORD" ]; then
    DATABASE_URL="postgresql://secuura_app:${APP_DB_PASSWORD}@${PGBOUNCER_HOST}:6432/secuura"
else
    # Fallback (no KV secret yet): stay on admin-DIRECT so a first-time deploy
    # still works. The gateway then provisions the role; a re-run picks up
    # secuura_app + pgbouncer.
    DATABASE_URL="$ADMIN_DATABASE_URL"
```

Note the secret read is `|| echo ""` on failure, so **a permissions problem, a missing vault or a**
**transient Azure error is indistinguishable from "not configured yet"** — all four take the admin
path silently.

`services.bicep` says the same of its own wiring: the `MIGRATION_*` vars fall back to the app URLs,
so "Stage 1 (plumbing only, not flipped) is inert — both still resolve to the admin URL"
(`:50-54`), and "Falls back to the app URLs until the Stage-2 cutover wires distinct values, so this
plumbing is inert today" (`:265-268`). Background: `RLS_ROLE_CUTOVER.md`.

**Why it matters.** Measured at develop `a0da739b6954`: `users` is FORCE RLS, its `tenant_isolation`
policy is `roles={public}` and keyed on the tenant GUC, and the owner role is
`rolsuper=t, rolbypassrls=t`. So as `secuura_app` an unset GUC sees **0 rows** and a cross-tenant row
is invisible; as the owner **every row is visible** and the policy is bypassed entirely. Compose is
`secuura_app` (`docker-compose.yml:581`), so local stacks are not affected — this is the Azure path.

## Not measured

**Which role the live demo and kintsugi boxes are actually running as.** Both were deliberately left
untouched (nothing was run against either), so whether that key-vault secret is present on them is
**unknown from here**. That is the first thing to check, and it is a read-only check.

## Relationship to KS-1054 — same symptom on the same occasion, DIFFERENT cause, and they compound

KS-1054 is *"Fresh databases are FAIL-OPEN until the second boot — 039_rls_fail_closed does not*
*apply on boot 1"*. That is the **policy DDL** not being in place. This ticket is the **connection**
**role** not being the one the policy binds for. Either alone leaves a fresh deploy unprotected by
RLS, and **fixing 039's stage ordering does not fix this one** — a service connected as the owner
bypasses even a correctly fail-closed policy. Worth settling both before any "RLS is enforcing"
claim about a new environment.

## Provenance

Found while measuring KS-1662 (a) — which is why the new suite
`ks1662-tenant-predicate-without-rls.integration.test.ts` matters more than it first appeared: it
pins the bound predicates with RLS out of the loop, i.e. exactly the state this fallback produces.
`deploy.sh` is **not** changed by that PR.

title: POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify anchors BEFORE it writes its documents row - the same orphan-anchor ordering as KS-1633, on the sibling handler (gate AI1 note N7)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify` **has the same ordering as the** `/issue` **route KS-1633 fixes: it anchors BEFORE it writes its** `documents` **row, so any failure of that write leaves an** `anchor_store` **row naming no document.** Same class, same file, different handler — and it is **not** changed by KS-1633, deliberately.

**Filed on gate AI1's note N7 (PR #1623). Read-only at develop** `a0da739b6954d42333640ea190d877f031803c7f`**. No code touched.**

## The ordering

In `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts`, the recertify handler:

| step | what |
| -- | -- |
| 1 | the anchoring POST (`const anchoringBase = …`, then `fetch(…/api/anchors…)`) — anchoring persists its `anchor_store` row **before** it answers 202 (`anchoring/src/index.ts:507` `await dbPersistAnchor(...)` precedes `:543` `res.status(202)`) |
| 2 | the production refusal: `if (anchoringStatus === 'failed' && process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production')` → 503 |
| 3 | `await saveCertification(verificationCert, tenantId, (req as any).db)` |

So the anchor row exists before the `documents` row, and a failure at step 3 leaves an orphan anchor — a row whose anchored identity another registration can later claim (the KS-1612 round-2 Major), created by a legitimate authenticated flow with no cleanup.

## Why it is not in KS-1633's PR

KS-1633's scope is `POST /api/certifications/issue`, which is what its description and its gate measured. Widening the PR to a second handler mid-gate would have changed the surface under review at the cap round. The two handlers do not share the ordering code, so the `/issue` fix does not reach this one.

## What the /issue fix looks like, for whoever picks this up

The shape ruled for `/issue` was: write the `documents` row **first** via an **event-free reservation** that shares the row SQL with `saveCertification`; make that reservation **non-deciding** (a failure is logged and the request continues, so the production 503 is never replaced by the write's own error); and on the production 503 **compensate the row away**, reporting any delete that removes no row. Three things that fix needed and this one will need too:

1. **The reservation must not decide the response.** On `/issue` an unwrapped early write turned the 503 into 400 for a NUL byte, 400 for a connector principal and 500 for a throwing save — measured.
2. **The compensating delete must carry the tenant GUC and the request's pool.** `documents` is FORCE RLS under `tenant_isolation`, whose USING clause reads the transaction-local `app.current_tenant_id`: a DELETE outside that transaction answers `DELETE 0` **and raises nothing**, so a compensation can silently remove nothing and still look like success.
3. **Only one writer may write the** `certification_events` **row**, or an accepted recertify ends with two ISSUE events instead of one.

## Rating

**Medium**, matching KS-1633's own rating for the same defect on the sibling handler, with the same caveat: nobody has shown live harm on a real box, and the orphan requires the write to fail. **A re-rate is reasonable and is not mine to do.**

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues`, archived included: `recertify anchors before it writes the documents row`, `recertify orphan anchor ordering certifications`, `POST /api/certifications/{id}/recertify` — 25 hits each. The near neighbours are **KS-1633** (the `/issue` handler — this ticket's sibling, not this handler), **KS-1384** (one anchor row per `(document_id, network)`), **KS-1650** (originate's already-anchored check) and **KS-1603** (anchoring never checks who owns `documentId`). **None covers the recertify handler's ordering.**

## Related

**KS-1633** (the `/issue` handler, at review as #1623) · **KS-1612** / **KS-1384** (what an orphan anchor allows once it exists) · **KS-1656**, **KS-1659**, **KS-1660** (the other findings from the same reading of this file).

title: anchoring readOwningDocument: a correct tenant bound resting on a false reason — `users` is NOT open for SELECT (users_auth_lookup is role-restricted, not public)
description:
## BLUF

**A correct guard resting on a false reason.** `services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:255-261`
justifies the LEFT JOIN's own `u.tenant_id = $2::uuid` bound by stating that `users` is open for
SELECT by construction. **That is not true.** The guard itself is right and should stay; only its
stated reason is wrong, and the same wrong inference is repeated in a test.

## Recommendation

Correct both comments to the measured facts below, keeping the bound. Then answer the one question
this ticket leaves open (see "Unmeasured"), because that is the only part that could be a real
defect rather than a wrong sentence.

## The two sites

1. `services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:255-261`, inside `readOwningDocument`:

   ```
   // `users` has a SECOND, permissive policy — `users_auth_lookup`, whose qual is literally
   // `true` — and Postgres ORs permissive policies together, so tenant isolation on `users` is
   // open for SELECT by construction. Measured on the repo schema. A join without its own
   // bound would read a custodian row from ANY tenant.
   ```
2. `services/anchoring/src/__tests__/ks1385-anchor-store-keeps-the-latest-events-metadata.integration.test.ts:535`
   — the same inference, in the test's own prose.

## Why it is false — measured on the repo's migrated schema (pg 15), 2026-10-19 at develop `a0da739b6954`

The claim omits the policy's `roles` column, which is what decides it:

| instrument | value |
| -- | -- |
| `users` | `relrowsecurity = t`, `relforcerowsecurity = t` |
| policy `tenant_isolation` | `cmd = ALL`, `roles = {public}`, keyed on `app.current_tenant_id` |
| policy `users_auth_lookup` | `cmd = SELECT`, qual `true`, `roles = {secuura_auth_lookup}` — a dedicated role, NOT `public` |
| `secuura_app` | `rolsuper = f`, `rolbypassrls = f` |
| as `secuura_app`, no GUC | **0 rows** in `users` |
| as `secuura_app`, GUC = tenant A | tenant B's row **0** (invisible); tenant A's row **1** |
| control | `documents`: **0** as `secuura_app`, **17** as the owner — so the instrument discriminates |

**A permissive policy restricted to a role you are not does not OR into your result.** anchoring
connects as `secuura_app` (`docker-compose.yml:1294`; Azure wires the same split — the owner
connection is `MIGRATION_*` only, `services.bicep:51-55`), so `users_auth_lookup` never applies to
it and `tenant_isolation` is live. `users_auth_lookup` is created by
`migrations/039_rls_fail_closed.sql:156-157`.

## Unmeasured, and the reason this is a ticket rather than a comment fix

**Does anything else in anchoring lean on the belief that** `users` **is open for SELECT?** Not checked.
The one site found draws a conservative conclusion, so it is safe; a site that relied on the belief
the *other* way — e.g. assuming a cross-tenant `users` read will succeed, or treating an empty
result as "no such user" rather than "not in this tenant" — would be a real defect. Worth a grep of
anchoring for `users` reads before closing.

## Method note, because the error is reusable

The false claim traces to a schema read that captured each policy's `qual` and **not** its `roles`.
Any conclusion about an RLS policy needs `cmd` **and** `roles` together:
`SELECT policyname, cmd, permissive, roles::text, qual FROM pg_policies WHERE tablename = '…'` —
then a behavioural check as the role the service actually connects as, with a control table that has
no escape policy.

## Provenance

Found while measuring KS-1662 item (a). Not edited: `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts` is another lane's
partition. The equivalent claim in originate was the inverse error — `documents.ts:1907` / `:1999`
call tenant RLS *inert* when it is the enforcement — and that is being corrected under **KS-1662**.

title: POST /api/certifications/issue asks assertNoCycle about the certification uuid, not the derived row's external_id, so the lineage-cycle arm cannot fire for the row it creates - the three documents.ts call sites pass the minted external id
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/issue` **asks the cycle walker about an identifier the row it creates never carries, so the lineage-cycle arm on that route cannot fire for the row being created.** `certifications.ts:417` passes `id` — the certification's uuid from `:363` — as the walker's `newExternalId`, while the derived document it goes on to write carries `external_id = doc-${Date.now()}-${id.slice(0, 8)}` (`:544`). The walker searches the proposed parent's ancestor chain for the first value and never for the second.

**The other three call sites do it the other way round, and they are the control.** `documents.ts:2055`, `:2788` and `:2986` each mint `const newExternalId = doc-<ms>-<8hex>` **first** and pass **that** — the value that becomes the new row's `external_id`. **One outlier in four.**

**Measured read-only at develop** `80868551e67934cb951d28eec44ce3bdf835944c`**. No code touched. Facts and a suggested shape; the owner decides.**

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a comment

The guard exists to stop a lineage loop being written and anchored — `certifications.ts:409-412` says so: *"Walk the proposed parent's ancestor chain to reject cycles BEFORE we anchor or write — the anchoring call is expensive and an invalid lineage shouldn't be visible on-chain."* On the certify route that sentence is not true of the row the request creates. Whatever a loop through a certification-derived row would cost, this call cannot refuse it.

## The mechanism, line by line

* `repositories/documentRepo.ts:891` — `assertNoCycle(newExternalId, proposedParentExternalId, tenantId, options)` delegates the whole walk to `walkAncestors` and then compares `entry.id === newExternalId` for each ancestor.
* `repositories/documentRepo.ts:744` — `walkAncestors` resolves each step with `WHERE d.external_id = ${cursor} AND d.tenant_id = ${tenantId}::uuid` (`:781-782`), following `p.external_id` through a `LEFT JOIN documents p ON p.id = d.parent_document_id`. So every `entry.id` it yields is an `external_id` (or, for a row with none, that row's pkey — `:789`).
* `routes/certifications.ts:363` — `const id = uuidv4()`. Assigned once; the only other `id =` in the file is inside a SQL string at `:347`.
* `routes/certifications.ts:417` — `await assertNoCycle(id, parentDocumentId, lifecycleTenantId, { db })`.
* `routes/certifications.ts:544` — `const derivedExternalId = \`doc-${[Date.now](<http://Date.now>)()}-${id.slice(0, 8)}\``, and `:546`builds the row with`id: derivedExternalId`, which `saveDocument`binds into`external_id\`.

A `doc-<ms>-<8hex>` string is never a uuid, so the compared value and the written value **cannot** coincide.

## The second half, and the reason this is ONE ticket and not two

Even at the three `documents.ts` sites the compared value is **freshly minted for a row that does not exist yet**, so no ancestor can equal it there either. Taken literally, `assertNoCycle`'s own comparison arm is unreachable from every route; what actually bounds a malformed chain at runtime is `walkAncestors`'s `seen` set (`:756-758`) and `MAX_LINEAGE_DEPTH`. The difference is that `documents.ts` passes the identifier that **will** be the row's `external_id`, so it is correct the moment a caller can supply or reuse one; `certifications.ts` passes an identifier that never becomes one, so it is wrong independently of that. Both readings are about the same call, so they belong on one ticket.

## What corroborates it, with the control stated

* **No route-level cell anywhere asserts the 422 fires.** Searched `services/originate/src/__tests__` for `LINEAGE_CYCLE`: **2 files**. `ks1228-a-refused-request-writes-no-provenance-row.test.ts` reaches the 422 **only by mocking** `assertNoCycle` **to throw** (`mockAssertNoCycle.mockImplementation(async () => cycle())`), which tests the handler and not the walker. `documentRepo.test.ts` exercises `walkAncestors`/`assertNoCycle` at **unit** level, where the caller can pass an id that genuinely IS in the chain — which is why the arm is provably alive there and nowhere else.
* **Control for that search:** the same grep over the same directory for `assertNoCycle` returns `documentRepo.test.ts`, so the search does find what is there.

## Rating

**Low.** Nothing is known to be exploitable: a caller cannot choose the derived row's `external_id` (the server mints it from a timestamp and the fresh certification uuid), so there is no demonstrated way to construct the loop the arm would have caught. The cost is a guard that reads as protection and is not, plus the 422 it documents being unreachable on that route. **A re-rate is reasonable and is not mine to do.**

## Suggested shapes — a choice for whoever picks it up

1. **Mint the derived external id before the walk and pass it**, as `documents.ts` already does — moves `derivedExternalId` above the `assertNoCycle` call and passes it. Smallest change, makes the four call sites consistent, and makes the arm correct in intent at all four.
2. **Decide the arm is redundant and say so** — if `walkAncestors`'s `seen` set plus the depth cap are the real protection, keep the walk for its lineage read and drop the comparison, with the comment rewritten to stop promising a refusal that cannot happen.
3. **Give the arm a route-level cell** that constructs a chain the walk must refuse, so whichever of (1) or (2) is chosen is pinned by a test rather than by a reading.

**A cell either way:** a certify whose proposed parent chain already contains the identifier the new row will carry must answer 422 `LINEAGE_CYCLE`, and the route must have no path that reaches `saveCertification` in that case.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues`, archived included: `assertNoCycle` → **2 hits**, both Done (**KS-70**, which introduced `parent_document_id` lineage and the walker, and **KS-86**, the watermark endpoint) — neither is about which identifier the walker is given. `lineage cycle detection external_id` → 25 hits, none on this call (the nearest, **KS-299**, is a verify-side walk-input gap, and **KS-280** is forward lineage). Also read **KS-1612** and **KS-1633**, which are about `anchor_store` and the certify route's write ORDER, not its cycle check.

## Related

* **KS-1557** — found while building its write side; that PR adds the parent-access predicate immediately above this call and deliberately does **not** touch it. The access check runs **before** the walk there, so a caller who may not read the parent no longer has its chain walked at all.
* **KS-1633** — the same route's anchor-before-row ordering.

title: No retention rule for never-claimed INVITED stub users — a transfer to an unknown email now creates a durable row
description:
## BLUF

Since KS-1402's invited-stub build, a custody transfer naming an email Platform K has never seen
**creates a durable** `users` **row** (`status = 'invited'`) instead of answering 404 and leaving no
trace. A stub is claimed when that person signs up. Nothing expires or reviews the ones that are
never claimed, and there is no documented retention position for them.

## Recommendation

Decide and document a retention rule for `users` rows that are `status = 'invited'` and never
claimed — a review/erase window, or an explicit "retained indefinitely" position with a reason.
This is a privacy decision, not an engineering one, so it wants an owner rather than a default.

## Detail

* **The privacy delta, stated plainly:** an email address that previously produced a 404 and
  persisted nothing is now stored. It is the only PII the row carries, and it is PII the caller
  already supplied in the request.
* The row carries: `id`, `email` (encrypted at rest, with `email_lookup_hash` as its HMAC sibling),
  `email_verified = false`, `status = 'invited'`, `tenant_id` = the caller's tenant. No password
  hash, no name, no phone (auth `repositories/userRepo.ts:753-793`, `createInvitedStub`).
* Not a new PII **class** — K already held and hashed these emails transiently to resolve them. What
  changed is persistence.
* Pre-dates KS-1402 in one respect: `certifications/issue` has minted stubs the same way since
  KS-74, so any rule should cover both paths rather than only transfer-custody.
* Adjacent, not duplicate: KS-1406 (cross-tenant guard fails open for tenantless tokens on
  `/lookup` and `/stub`); PS-1144 (invitation link carries the email in the URL).

title: Two routes answer the same cross-tenant recipient miss with different codes: RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND vs RECIPIENT_NOT_AVAILABLE
description:
## BLUF

For the identical situation — a recipient email that already belongs to a user in a **different**
tenant — `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` answers `404 RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` while
`POST /api/certifications/issue` answers `404 RECIPIENT_NOT_AVAILABLE`. Both come from auth's same
deliberate cross-tenant 404 on `/api/users/stub`.

## Recommendation

Pick one code and converge, as a contract change with Platform S in the loop — not unilaterally.
KS-1402 deliberately kept `RECIPIENT_NOT_FOUND` on transfer-custody because changing it would be a
contract change Platform S did not ask for.

## Detail

* transfer-custody: `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts`, the `mintInvitedStubHolder`
  helper's `stubRes.status === 404` arm.
* certifications/issue: `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts:287-300`.
* Both are the same upstream condition (auth `userRepo.createInvitedStub` throwing
  `EMAIL_RESERVED_ELSEWHERE`, surfaced as 404 to avoid cross-tenant existence disclosure).
* The status is the same (404) in both, so this is a code-string inconsistency, not a behavioural
  divergence. Anything branching on `error.code` across the two routes has to special-case them.
* Worth checking against PS-side handling before changing either.

title: KS-1603 residue: the interim anchor-ownership check does not apply to a tenantless caller, so absence of a tenant claim still permits a cross-tenant anchor write
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-1603 interim ownership check does not apply to a caller whose token carries no usable tenant claim: that caller can still write an anchor onto another tenant's document, exactly as on develop.** Landed in `anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:544-550` (develop `ad784e702ca205230e39d329abefa8a85fb5946c`), where a tenant claim that is absent, blank or not uuid-shaped returns `allow: true, reason: 'caller-has-no-usable-tenant'` with a warn.

**This was accepted deliberately at plan time, not missed.** Wednesday's ruling on the KS-1603 plan (2026-10-19T05:55:40Z, Recommendation item 3) reads, verbatim: *"Everything else is develop: no document anywhere (S's flat anchors, including retries) allow; own tenant allow; **no tenantId allow + warn**."* PR #1615's own predicate table states it, and the code comment at `:541-543` gives the reason. Gate AA1 raised it as note 1 and characterised it as outside those rulings; that characterisation is mistaken — the acceptance is in the ruling mail. **What is correct is that an accepted interim limitation deserves its own ticket rather than living only in a merged PR body, which is why this exists.**

## Why it was allowed, and why that reasoning has a limit

`tenantId` is genuinely optional on the token: auth signs it conditionally (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:263`). A claim that is absent or not uuid-shaped is not something a Postgres-rendered `uuid` can equal, so **comparing** it would refuse rather than compare — and KS-1603 was ruled a pure narrowing, so a new refusal there was out of scope.

The limit of that reasoning: "cannot be compared" and "should therefore be allowed" are different statements. The second is a choice, and it makes the absence of a tenant the thing that widens access.

## Scope

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/anchorOverwriteGuard.ts:535-575` — `mayWriteAnchorRows`, the `isUuidShaped(callerTenantId)` arm at `:544`.
* Reached from `index.ts:1403` (every persist, via `dbPersistAnchor`) and `index.ts:761` (the batch pre-check).
* `POST /api/anchors` and `POST /api/anchors/batch`.

## The question to settle before fixing

What should a tenantless caller get? Candidates, none chosen here: refuse (403, so absence never widens); allow only when no `documents` row holds the id at all (which keeps Platform S's flat anchors working while refusing anything that names a real document); or platform-principal-only. **The Platform S constraint is the thing to check first** — S's flat anchors must keep working, including retries, and whether S's token carries a tenant claim has not been measured here.

## Same class, different component

**KS-1406** is the same shape in the **auth** service — the cross-tenant guard on `GET /api/users/lookup` and `POST /api/users/stub` is skipped for a tenantless token (`userRepo.ts:759`). Different service, different route, same principle: the absence of a tenant should never be what widens a read or a write. Worth settling the two together so the convention is one decision.

## Two further gate AA1 notes, same two files

**1. Cell D1's leak proof is weaker than it reads.** `ks1603-the-flat-anchor-write-refuses-a-foreign-tenants-document.integration.test.ts` D1 asserts that the transaction-scoped `app.tenant_scope_bypass` does not survive the probe's transaction, by reading again on the same pool. It only catches a leak because the pool hands back the most recently released connection; it does not pin one. Harden it to pin a single backend by its pid (`pg_backend_pid()`), as gate AA1 did in its own connection-tracking cells. **Test hardening only — the product behaviour is correct and the gate's own cells pass.**

**2. The batch route probes N+1 times.** The batch pre-check reads every id once up front, and `dbPersistAnchor` then probes per item, so a 100-item batch runs up to 101 short transactions. Deliberate at the time: the pre-check buys "writes nothing on refusal", the per-item gate buys "no later caller can route around it".
