title: An ADMIN's organisation scope rows SURVIVE demotion and deletion, so the grant revives if the account is restored
description:
## BLUF

`admin_organisation_scopes` **rows are never purged when the user they grant to stops being an ADMIN, or is deleted.** The grant sits dormant and **revives silently** if the account is reactivated or re-promoted.

Raised twice and still open as a question, which is why it now has its own ticket:

* the pull request 1535 gate's **m3** (PR A);
* the pull request 1539 gate's **m2** (PR B), which measured that a user with `role='ADMIN'` and `status='deleted'` could be **granted** a scope — 200, row written.

## What IS now closed, and what is not

**Closed in PR B's delta (KS-1570):** the write side. `PUT /api/keys/admin-scopes/:userId` now requires the target to be `status = 'active'`, so a non-live user cannot be *given* a scope (404, nothing written), pinned by a cell.

**NOT closed, and deliberately out of that PR:** existing rows. Nothing removes them on demotion, on status change, or on delete. There is no cascade — `admin_organisation_scopes` has **no foreign keys** (by design: the pull request 1535 gate's m3 is why the route does write-time checks instead).

## The decision needed

1. Purge on demotion / deletion — a trigger, a cascade, or an application step on the role-change and delete paths; or
2. filter at **read** time (`getAdminOrganisationScope` joins `users` and requires live + ADMIN), which leaves the rows but makes them inert; or
3. accept it, and say so, since the account cannot authenticate while non-live.

**(2) is the cheapest fail-closed option** and needs no migration, but it adds a join to a per-decision read. Not built; this is an owner's call.

## Not measured

Whether any production or demo row is currently in this state. A census belongs with the deploy seat, not here.

Filed by Seat V 7th from the pull request 1539 gate (m2) and the 1535 gate (m3).

title: verify-file's cross-tenant registry lookup compares the sha256:-prefixed hash against platform_document_registry.content_hash with no normalisation, so it never matches a bare-hex registration (measured; facts only, no fix)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/verification/verify-file` searches `platform_document_registry` with the `sha256:`**-prefixed** hash, by exact equality and with no normalisation. The registry stores whatever the registering caller passed, verbatim. **So where registrations carry a bare hex hash, verify-file's entire cross-tenant path is unreachable** — a file certified in another tenant answers "not found" rather than being found through the registry.

**Facts only. No fix shape, no severity rating, and I have not measured which format real rows carry in any environment** — I have no box access. Filed on Wednesday's instruction, as a side reading from the KS-1119 proof.

## The two lines

* **The search**, `services/originate/src/routes/verification.ts:528-537` inside `crossTenantLookup`: when `documentId` is empty, the registry is queried as
  `SELECT * FROM platform_document_registry WHERE content_hash = $1 LIMIT 1` with `$1 = hashToVerify` — **exact equality, no** `sha256:` **handling on either side.**
* **The caller**, `:663`: `crossTenantLookup('', fileHash)`, where `fileHash` is built at `:639` as
  `` `sha256:${crypto.createHash('sha256').update(fileBuffer).digest('hex')}` `` — **always prefixed**. (`hashNorm`, the unprefixed form, is computed on the next line and is *not* what is passed.)
* **The write**, `registerInPlatformRegistry` (`:487-509`): stores `doc.contentHash` verbatim, with no normalisation either. The format in the table is therefore whatever the registering caller supplied.

Contrast: the *tenant-DB* query a few lines later (`:553-566`) is careful about exactly this — it strips the prefix into `searchHash` and matches `content_hash = $1 OR = $2 OR = $3` across all three forms. The registry query above it does not.

## The measurement

From the KS-1119 probe, on a local scratch PostgreSQL 15 with `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`, as `secuura_app` (`rolsuper=false`, `rolbypassrls=false`), 3/3 cells in each run. The **only** difference between the runs is the format stored in `platform_document_registry.content_hash`:

| registry row stored as | verify-file reached the cross-tenant path? |
| -- | -- |
| `sha256:<hex>` | **yes** — the registry hit, and the lookup continued into the tenant DB |
| bare `<hex>` | **no** — the registry search found nothing, `crossTenantLookup` returned `null` |

Control in both runs: a file with no registry row at all answers `verified:false`, so the instrument can tell a miss from a hit.

*(The prefixed run is also how \[\[KS-1119\]\]'s second instance was found — that is a different defect and lives there. This ticket is only about the format mismatch making the path unreachable.)*

## What is NOT established

* **Which format real rows carry**, on Kintsugi, on the demo VM, or anywhere else. That reading is on the deploy-time census list with KS-1119's.
* Whether `v1 /verify` is affected the same way. It is **not**, on the path I measured: when a `documentId` is supplied the registry is searched by `document_id` first, so the format never arises; and when only a hash is supplied, that hash is whatever the *caller* sent, which may or may not carry the prefix. I did not measure the hash-only-no-documentId shape.
* Whether this is intended. It may be that every registration is expected to be prefixed, in which case the bug is on the write side or nowhere.

## Related

\[\[KS-1119\]\] — the proof this fell out of · \[\[KS-584\]\] and \[\[KS-590\]\] — which registration a hash resolves to (a different question; this ticket is about whether the row is found at all) · \[\[KS-598\]\] — the registry upsert collapsing registrations per `(hash, tenant)`.

title: KS-1582 follow-up (pull request 1536 gate m-a, m-b, N1): pin the transaction-local timeout and its value, pin the ::text tenant compare, and handle a pg client error while checked out
description:
## BLUF

**The follow-up to pull request 1536 (KS-1582): two coverage Minors and one pre-existing note from its Sonnet delta gate** (verdict sha256/16 `7306c470a243195b`, GO WITH NOTE, 0 Major). The code change behaved correctly in every probe, so these are gaps in the PR's own cells. Facts only, from the gate's report. Filed on Wednesday's GO.

## m-a: nothing pins that the timeout is transaction-local, or its value

* Where: `services/referral/src/__tests__/ks1582-referrer-wallet-read-gate-cells.integration.test.ts`, cell P (its connection probe reads only the tenant GUC) and cell B1 (`expect(ms).toBeLessThan(8_000)`). Code under test: `services/referral/src/db.ts:210` (`SET LOCAL statement_timeout = ${WALLET_READ_TIMEOUT_MS}`), the constant at `:199`.
* The gate's mutants **Z1** (`SET statement_timeout = 3000` before `BEGIN`), **Z4** (`SET` without `LOCAL` inside the transaction) and **Z3** (the value 7000) all leave the PR's 20 integration cells and 3 unit cells green.
* Z1 and Z4 would leave a permanent 3 s `statement_timeout` on a pooled connection that every other referral query also uses.
* Fix asked for:
  * in P's probe, also read `current_setting('statement_timeout')` and assert `'0'` for each distinct pid (the gate's T1 does this; its control T0 shows the probe can see a leak);
  * tighten B1 to a window around the bound, for example more than 2500 ms and less than 4500 ms.

## m-b: the stated reason for `::text` (no cast error) is not pinned

* Where: `ks1582-tenant-bound-in-sql.integration.test.ts`, which exercises only the exact tenant and one other uuid tenant; code at `db.ts:212` (`tenant_id::text = $2`).
* The gate's mutant **Z7** (`tenant_id = $2::uuid`) passes every PR cell. With it, a token whose `tenantId` is not a uuid (`not-a-uuid`, an array, a number) makes generate answer **5xx** for a signed-in user, where develop answers 201. The head answers 201 for all 13 shapes the gate tried.
* Fix asked for: one cell of the gate's M2 shape (a non-uuid, an array and a number `tenantId` under the app role answer 201 with no wallet), or a non-uuid tenant added to the bypass file's RED cell.

## N1 (pre-existing, the same on develop `c855cfc2`): an unhandled `pg` client error

* When the database kills the backend mid-read (or on a failover), the checked-out `pg` client emits an `error` event that nothing listens for. vitest reports `Uncaught Exception: Connection terminated unexpectedly`, while the request itself correctly answers 500 and the next one works.
* The identical pattern exists in `queryWithTenantGuc` in `packages/shared`.
* In production an uncaught exception exits the process, per `packages/shared/src/utils/gracefulShutdown.ts`.
* Not introduced or worsened by KS-1582: a statement timeout is an ordinary query error, not a connection error.
* Fix asked for: a `client.on('error', …)` while a client is checked out, in shared code (outside KS-1582's scope).

## Notes carried, no action asked

* N2: a read slower than 3 s now fails closed (500). That is the intended trade, and the bound is a product decision.
* N3: B1 takes about 12 s on a red run and about 3 s on a green one.

title: security's own audit INSERT can never succeed on a repo-built database (previous_state/new_state undefined; encrypted details into jsonb) — POST /api/audit persists nothing, silently
description:
## BLUF

**On a database built from the repo,** `services/security`**'s own audit INSERT can never succeed, and** `dbSaveAuditLog` **swallows the error.** So `POST /api/security/audit` (`/api/audit` in the service) never persists its rows to `audit_logs`; they live only in the service's in-memory cache. **Measured** on a scratch PostgreSQL 15 built from `docker/init/*` and `run-migrations.sh`. Facts only, no fix. Found while building KS-1570 PR B, which avoids the path and does not change it.

## Two independent causes (develop `2cdf1d7a`)

1. **Columns that no schema source defines.**
   * `dbSaveAuditLog` (`services/security/src/index.ts:122-146`) inserts into `previous_state` and `new_state`.
   * Neither column exists in `docker/init/01-schema.sql:390` (`CREATE TABLE audit_logs`) or `migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:347`, and no later migration adds them (git grep: 0 hits in docker/ and migrations/).
   * Only `prisma/schema.prisma:524-525` declares them.
   * Measured error: `column "previous_state" of relation "audit_logs" does not exist`.
2. **Encrypted text into a** `jsonb` **column.**
   * `details` is written as the output of `encryptDetails` (a `v1:…` ciphertext string). The column is `jsonb` in both schema sources.
   * The service's boot widens it to TEXT (`runDbBootTasks`, the `ALTER TABLE audit_logs ALTER COLUMN details TYPE TEXT` block). That boot step runs as `secuura_app`, which by design has no DDL rights (`docker/init/01-create-app-role.sh`; KS-92's runtime-DDL class), and it logs a failure as "non-fatal".
   * So on a fresh database the column stays `jsonb`. Measured error once cause 1 is avoided: `invalid input syntax for type json`.
   * When PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset, the details are plaintext JSON and cause 2 does not apply. Cause 1 still does.

## What is not known

Whether the Kintsugi and demo databases happen to have these columns, or a widened `details` (for example from a `prisma db push`, or an earlier owner-run boot). That needs a read-only check by a deploy seat:

```sql
SELECT column_name, data_type FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_name = 'audit_logs' AND column_name IN ('details','previous_state','new_state');
```

## Why it matters

The security service's audit endpoint reports success while persisting nothing (it fails open, silently). The gateway (`api-gateway/src/middleware/audit.ts:313`) and tokenisation (`services/tokenisation/src/index.ts:198`) write `audit_logs` with their own statements and are not covered by this ticket.

## Not decided here

The fix shape. Options: add `previous_state`/`new_state` and the TEXT widening as an owned migration; or drop the two columns from the INSERT and stop the runtime DDL.

title: KS-998 item 1 gate follow-ups (#1532): the six Minors of the Opus gate, and the Info that matters
description:
## BLUF

**The Opus tier 1 gate on pull request #1532 (KS-998 item 1) returned GO WITH NOTE: 0 Major, 6 Minor, 7 Info.** This ticket carries the six Minors and the Info that matters, so they are findable after #1532 merges. Facts only, from the gate's report.

* **Report:** `0_Brain/reference/2026-10-13_gate-pr1532/verdict.md` in the Wednesday tree, sha256/16 `85bf04b8ef22923b` (recomputed by the report's own recipe, placeholder replaced: equal; a one-byte change breaks it).
* **Head it is bound to:** `3dbfdf7e36443a8665b6a106e2d8ccbb6763cd44`. Instruments: macOS, `/bin/bash` 3.2.57, node v24.7.0, npm 11.5.1.
* **None of the six hides a formatting red or lets a push pass without a check.** (1) fails closed; (2) and (3) are properties of `npm ci` that the gate now triggers automatically.

## Where each rides (Wednesday's rulings, 2026-10-13)

* **Minors 1, 2, 4, 5, 6:** the stacked **item 2** pull request (same functions), each with its cell.
* **Minor 3:** a **third pull request stacked on item 2**, so item 2 stays reviewable: the lock-source allowlist AND a scrubbed install environment, lifecycle scripts still running as ruled. A plan mail comes first.

## The six Minors

1. **The final rename races (**`check-package-format.sh`**, the** `mv` **into place).** The `[ -e node_modules ]` guard is not atomic with the `mv`; BSD `mv` onto an existing directory moves the source INSIDE it, and onto a symlink to a directory moves it into the target. `_rm_stage` can then delete a `node_modules` the gate did not make. Measured with a PATH `mv` shim: a hollow in-progress tree was deleted; a symlink arrival had our tree written into the outside target; a complete tree arrival left `node_modules/node_modules`. **Two real gate processes on one package REFUSED a correct push in 4 of 5 trials** (`mv` loses its own rename race: ENOTEMPTY). It fails closed and what can be lost is a regenerable, gitignored tree, but it falsifies "deletes only what it made". **Fix:** `rename(2)` (via `node -e 'fs.renameSync'`), which refuses a non-empty or symlink target; map that to `raced`, not `mvfail`; drop a marker file into the staged tree before the rename and require it at `$dir/node_modules/` before any move-back.
2. **The watchdog and the TERM path kill npm's pid, not its process group.** A dependency's postinstall child outlives the gate (ppid 1) on the watchdog, on SIGTERM and on SIGKILL; only a Ctrl-C to the whole group removes it. esbuild's `install.js` fallback (`downloadDirectlyFromNPM`: `https.get`, no timeout, hard-coded registry) is the process that would be orphaned against a silent registry. **Fix:** start npm in its own process group (`set -m` in bash 3.2, or `perl -e 'setpgrp; exec @ARGV'`) and signal the group: TERM, then KILL, in both the watchdog and the cleanup. Same class as KS-1331 (a different script: `run-shell-suites.sh`).
3. **The gate does not check lock sources.** A lock entry whose `resolved` points at a non-registry host is fetched, and its postinstall runs on the push (measured: 1 GET at the listener, INSTALLED, a sentinel written outside the repo; a tampered integrity was refused with EINTEGRITY). Lifecycle scripts see `NPM_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and other `*TOKEN` names from the environment, and `~/.npmrc` is in scope; `--fetch-retries=0` and `--fetch-timeout` reach lifecycle children through `npm_config_*`. This is what a manual `npm ci` does too; the difference is that it now runs automatically on push, including for a package selected by a stale base or a merge the developer did not author. **Today's four lockfiles are clean:** 411/411, 344/344, 269/269 and 217/217 entries are `registry.npmjs.org` with an integrity hash. **Ruled YES:** every non-link entry must have `resolved` starting `https://registry.npmjs.org/` and a non-empty `integrity`; every `link` must resolve inside the repo; otherwise refuse with a named reason and run nothing; AND scrub the install's environment to a minimal set (`PATH`, `HOME`, what npm needs; no `*TOKEN`, no `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`).
4. `m23b` **("no EXIT trap") is NOT equivalent, contrary to the item 1 table.** On bash 3.2 the EXIT trap is what cleans up on untrapped fatal signals other than QUIT. SIGUSR1 mid-install: head kills npm and removes the stage; with the EXIT trap removed, npm stays alive and the stage stays. Same for SIGALRM and SIGPIPE. The other four survivors (`m13a`, `m23`, `m25`, `m35`) were re-derived by the gate and are equivalent. **Fix:** one cell that sends SIGUSR1 or SIGALRM mid-install and expects no orphan and no stage.
5. **Four mutants survive that are test gaps, not equivalents.** `Q8` (the post-move `-x` → `-e`): no cell has a non-executable prettier. `Q11` (the hollow re-check dropped): a raced-in hollow tree would be reported as a *formatting failure* instead of the environment refusal, the KS-991 confusion. `Q12` (`.npmrc` not copied to the stage): no fixture has a package `.npmrc`. `Q13` (the six-digit length guard dropped): a 20-digit `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT` overflows and refuses at once with "timed out after 99999999999999999999s"; head exits 2 naming the variable. **Fix:** one cell each.
6. **SIGQUIT to the gate alone leaves npm and the stage.** It is not trapped and bash 3.2 does not run the EXIT trap for it: rc 131, the hung npm alive, one stage left (the next run sweeps the stage). **Fix:** add QUIT to the trap list.

## The Info that matters

* **Info 2 (pre-existing, KS-1483):** a branch deletion (`git push origin :todelete`) and a tag push were both REFUSED because HEAD's branch touched an uninstallable package: the hook computes the changed set from `@{upstream}..HEAD`, not from the pushed refs. The develop control refuses the same two pushes (KS-1063 NOTHING CHECKED), so it is not a regression of #1532. **KS-998 item 2 with KS-1483 fixes it** (per-ref judging; a deleted ref is skipped before anything runs).
* **Info 3:** `_rm_stage` with an EMPTY `STAGE_PREFIX` would delete a relative single-component directory under the cwd (demonstrated on the extracted function). Unreachable today: the prefix is assigned once, never empty, and `set -u` aborts if unset. **Defence in depth:** `[ -n "$STAGE_PREFIX" ]` and require an absolute `$d`.
* **Info 5:** `-x` is true for a *directory* named `.bin/prettier`, so it is INSTALLED and then reported as a formatting failure with rc 126. npm never produces this. Cheap: `[ -f ] && [ -x ]`.
* **Info 6:** an invalid `FORMAT_GATE_INSTALL_TIMEOUT` blocks every push, including pushes that touch no systemTest file (validation exits 2 before selection), and the hook's wrapper then says "fix the files named above", which is wrong for it. Loud and self-inflicted; the wrapper's wording is the defect.
* **Info 7:** esbuild's install-script network fallback, exercised under the sandbox: with `@esbuild/darwin-arm64` removed, `install.js` tries `npm install` and then a direct download. **70.4 s** with npm defaults, **0.43 s** with `npm_config_fetch_retries=0`, and that value IS inherited from the gate's `npm ci` (measured through a postinstall). Both paths verify the binary with a sha256 before use.

## NOT tested by the gate (carried as unmeasured)

Linux (GNU `mv` has the same move-into-directory behaviour, so Minor 1 is expected to apply, not measured); preflight legs 3, 4, 8 and the full A/B; a real pty Ctrl-C (emulated); a silent registry against esbuild's direct download (reasoned from the code); the `--no-update-notifier` request census (not repeated).

## Related

KS-998 (the parent, stays In Progress: item 2 and KS-1483 are unbuilt), KS-1483 (item 2 folds it in). Same class as KS-1331 (process-group signalling), in a different script. Pull request #1532, head `3dbfdf7e3644`.

title: GET /api/keys has no tenant-level mode: organisation-less keys cannot be listed, so the Admin Dashboard cannot show or revoke them
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/keys` **can list only keys that carry an organisation id. An API key minted with no organisation (a tenant-level key) is never returned by any list call**, so the Admin Dashboard cannot show it and cannot offer its revoke (the page revokes by the key id it read from the list). **This is design work, not a defect:** the exclusion is deliberate in the handler. It matters now because the unqualified mint is the only mint an unscoped `ADMIN` will be allowed after KS-1570, and because Admin Dashboard change KS-1564 therefore leaves the "no organisation" option out of its dialog.

## Recommendation

Decide whether the list gets a tenant-level mode. No action is needed on KS-1564, KS-1570 PR A or PR B for this; none of them depends on it. Facts only.

## Detail (read at develop `343a7b4e`, not run)

* `services/security/src/index.ts:1319-1322`: `organizationId` is REQUIRED on `GET /api/keys`; a missing one answers 400 `organizationId required`.
* `index.ts:1356-1358`: a key is returned only when `wantedOrg !== null && normaliseOrgId(k.organizationId) === wantedOrg`. The comment at `:1347-1353` says the null case is intended: "null must not equal the stored null of every org-less, tenant-level key". So a key stored without an organisation never equals any non-null query.
* The mint allows it: `organizationId` is optional (`index.ts:627`), and an unqualified mint is allowed under the 2026-09-03 ruling (comment at `index.ts:1169-1175`). `tenant-provisioning`'s metering key is minted this way (`meteringKey.ts:45`, no `organizationId`).
* Revoke of such a key works today when the caller has the key's id (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:208`, org-less keys stay revocable). Only the list is missing, so the id has to come from somewhere other than this endpoint.
* A list for "keys in my tenant with no organisation" would also have to keep the tenant filter of KS-742 (`index.ts:1359`) and the role check, and would be a published-spec change (`security.openapi.ts` lists `organizationId` as required).

## Not covered

No dashboard behaviour was run; no key counts were taken on any environment (no box access).

## Dedupe (2026-10-13, Seat J 6th)

`searchIssues` with comments and archived included, five terms, 266 distinct issues; positive control: the term `default-org` found KS-1564, KS-1565, KS-1578. Near hits read: KS-1574 (the list has no organisation arm for ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN: a different gap on the same handler), KS-1570, KS-1533, KS-764, KS-779. None describes a tenant-level list mode.

Related: KS-1564, KS-1570, KS-1574 (same handler).

title: KS-695 follow-up: distinguishing code for a key revoked by erasure (S's ask, KS-695 comment 7221c520)
description:
## BLUF

Platform S asked K for a distinguishing code or status for an API key that was revoked **by erasure**, so S can read that fact instead of inferring it. **This is design work, not a defect, and nothing in the merged change (pull request 1497, squash** `343a7b4e`**) depends on it.** Nobody has decided whether to build it.

## Recommendation

Decide first whether K builds it. If yes, it is a small design: see "What K does today". No action needed for the erasure itself.

## The ask, verbatim

Stuart, ticket KS-695, comment `7221c520-c6fb-4343-aedd-7bffbfdc9b75`, 2026-10-12T23:00:58Z:

> **One ask of K:** a distinguishing code or status for a key revoked *by erasure* — on the POST (for example a 401 whose `error.code` says so) or on the status GET — would let S drop the inference in (2) and read the fact directly. Until then the attempt-count rule is what S will use. Nothing here blocks part ii's gate; S's change is small and I will note on this ticket when it is on develop.

The inference in (2), same comment: *"A 401 'Invalid API key' on this route counts as 'already erased, Confirmed' only when S has already recorded at least one attempt on that organisation's erasure (the row's attempt counter is non-zero)."* S's side of this is PS-1201 (point 4) and platform-s pull request 972 (In Review at 2026-10-13T00:52Z, per the ticket).

## What K does today (read at develop `343a7b4e`, not run)

* The erasure revokes the calling key last: `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false` (`services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:440`), the same write the security service's rotate makes (`services/security/src/index.ts:186`). Nothing on the row records why the key is inactive.
* A repeat call is refused at the gateway before the originate route runs: a presented `sk_` key that fails `validateApiKey` is answered `401 {"code":"UNAUTHORIZED","message":"Invalid API key"}` (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:367-368`). That branch has no sub-code, so it cannot say why validation failed.
* The status GET (`GET /api/platform/organizations/erase-connector/:organisationGuid`, `routes/platformOrganizations.ts:152`) has a connector-role guard in originate. I did not trace the gateway mount of that path, so I do not know whether the same revoked key reaches it; if it does not, "a code on the status GET" would need a credential other than the revoked key.
* So any distinguishing code needs (a) a durable marker of the reason at the revoke, written in the erasure transaction, and (b) a gateway change, because the refusal happens at the gateway. Neither exists. A new `error.code` on that 401 is also a client-visible change to a shared door.

## Not covered

No S behaviour was read (K cannot read S's code); everything about S is Stuart's text above. No live check on any box.

## Dedupe (2026-10-13, Seat J 6th)

`searchIssues` with comments and archived included, five terms, 196 distinct issues. Positive control: the term `PlatformKErasureClient` found 4 issues (PS-1201, PS-699, PS-700, PS-701). Zero literal hits in title or description for "revoked by erasure". Near hit: PS-1201, the S-side counterpart, not a duplicate.

Related: KS-695 (the erasure), PS-1201.

title: KS-695 erase-connector round 6 gate follow-ups (pull request 1497): description wording for whitespace-only ids, an R3 cell for the second read, a stale cell title, an inaccurate header sentence, a legacy-key divergence
description:
## BLUF

Five facts from the Opus delta gate on pull request 1497 round 6 (report sha256/16 `0d886f63f692f62a`, head `c48d71638f330eb3a603a6e123471c4a1bbdf93e`) that are not defects in the merged change but are worth fixing or recording. One checklist; split an item out when someone picks it up. The code was deliberately NOT touched while the pull request was at the gate. Each item below was checked by me against the source (the lines are the ones read), except where it says it is the gate's measurement.

- [ ] **1. The published description understates the refusal (gate Minor m-1, cell V1).** `services/originate/src/originate.openapi.ts:3728` and the regenerated yaml `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml:31211` say a key "with an empty or absent id" authenticates as `connector:api-key` and is refused. The predicate is `isFallbackConnectorId(id) = id.trim() === '' || id === 'api-key'`, so a key whose stored connector id is **only whitespace** (a space, TAB, U+00A0, U+FEFF, U+3000, U+2028) is refused too: the gate measured 403 with nothing written on the real route in both tenancy modes, and 200 `completed` when both refusals were removed. Those ids are NOT the fallback principal: the gateway keeps a whitespace-only string as it is (`connectorId || 'api-key'`), so each is its own principal. Wording-only options: add "blank or whitespace only" to the description and the yaml, or narrow the predicate to `''` and the label. The pull request body was corrected; every real connector id is `platform-s:<guid>`.
- [ ] **2. Add an R3 cell beside R2 (gate N-1).** Mutant X2 (the second guard read moved to just BEFORE the blanking UPDATE, after the count) **survives the real-Postgres file** `ks695-ask3-erase-connector-fallback-principal.integration.test.ts` in both modes (gate: 8/8 green). Reason: R2 holds `LOCK TABLE documents IN ACCESS EXCLUSIVE MODE`, so the erase stalls at the count, and a read placed anywhere after the count still sees the key. X2 is killed by the three unit statement-order cells and by the gate's R3: `LOCK TABLE documents IN EXCLUSIVE MODE` lets the count run (a read takes ACCESS SHARE) and stalls the UPDATE itself; the key and root commit there; the code answers 403, X2 answers 200. This is the gate's measurement; I did not re-run X2.
- [ ] **3. A stale unit-cell title (gate N-2).** `__tests__/ks695-ask3-erase-connector-refusals.test.ts:279` says a key with a NULL id and one with an empty id "already got 403 from the ownership comparison and still does". After round 6 the 403 for those keys comes from the fallback refusal (the gate's direct resolver call gets `OrganisationErasureFallbackPrincipalError` for both); with both refusals removed the status is still 403, through the ownership mismatch. The cell pins the status, not the reason. Reword the title.
- [ ] **4. An inaccurate header sentence (gate N-4).** `services/originate/src/services/connectorOrganisationErasure.ts:220`: "a key that was deleted or rotated away". A rotation only deactivates or shortens the old key: `retirePriorStatement` in `services/security/src/index.ts` is an `UPDATE svc_api_keys SET is_active = false` (grace 0) or an `UPDATE ... SET expires_at = LEAST(...)`, and the security service source contains no `DELETE FROM svc_api_keys` (checked; the search found the two `UPDATE`s as its control). The guard reads inactive keys, so a rotated key IS seen. Only a DELETED key escapes it (the gate's cell C5: 200, 2 blanked, reachable only by a DBA delete).
- [ ] **5. A legacy key's connector id can differ between memory and the database (gate N-5; read from code only, NOT run).** The security service upserts `connector_id = COALESCE(EXCLUDED.connector_id, svc_api_keys.connector_id)` (`services/security/src/index.ts:401`, with a KS-869 comment that a pre-KS-869 row holds NULL and the next save backfills it) and validates from the in-memory key (`connectorId: apiKey.connectorId || null`, `:1299`, `:1569`); the boot load reads rows (`SELECT * FROM svc_api_keys`, `:535`). So a pre-KS-869 key that is live in memory with id X while its row holds NULL would authenticate as `connector:X`, while the erasure's guard, which reads rows, would not see it as carrying X. It closes on the next save or a reload. A census of Kintsugi's keys is the deploy seat's read-only item; nothing here was run against a box.

## Recorded in the verdict, no action asked

* **N-3.** A colliding key alone, with no document, can turn another organisation's erasure into a terminal 403 (the same availability property the first guard always had); minting a named connector id is platform- or provisioner-only since KS-1533 arm 1.
* **N-6.** The added guard read costs 4.2 to 6.5 ms with 50,000 keys in one tenant (a sequential scan, no index on `connector_id`), twice per erasure; negligible against the 25 s budget.

Related: KS-695.

title: /health/deep reports startupMigrations.applied=46 on a deploy that applied ZERO migration files — the field sums file-based DDL with in-code idempotent steps
description:
## BLUF

`/health/deep` **reported** `startupMigrations.applied=46` **on a deploy that applied ZERO migration files.** Measured on kintsugi during the round-2 deploy (2026-10-13, pin `361537eed238`), where the migration delta was independently established as **0 migration-path files** out of 123 changed files. The field aggregates two different kinds of work under one name, so the number cannot be read as "migrations applied". Facts only; no fix proposed.

## The reading, and what it decomposes into

`GET /health/deep` body, immediately after the api-gateway recreate:

```
"startupMigrations":{"ran":true,"applied":46,"failed":0,"lastRunAt":"2026-10-13T00:06:34.420Z"}
```

The same boot's own log lines, in order:

```
[startup-migrations] loaded 50 migration files from /app/migrations
[startup-migrations] File-based main DB migrations complete     {"applied":0,"failed":0}
[startup-migrations] File-based platform DB migrations complete {"applied":0,"failed":0}
[startup-migrations] Main DB migrations complete                {"applied":39,"failed":0}
[startup-migrations] Platform DB migrations complete            {"applied":7,"failed":0}
```

**0 + 0 file-based, then 39 + 7 = 46.** So the health body's `applied` is the sum of the **in-code idempotent** steps (tenant seeds, per-client tenant re-sync, vocabulary ensures), and the **file-based** `.sql` **counters — the ones that correspond to a schema change — are both zero and are not represented in the body at all.**

## Why the distinction matters

The in-code steps **write no row to the** `_secuura_migrations` **tracker**, so they leave no schema trace, while a file migration does. Independently measured on the same deploy:

| reading | before the swap | after the swap |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `_secuura_migrations` rows, `secuura` | 49 | 49 |
| `_secuura_migrations` rows, `secuura_platform` | 1 | 1 |
| tracker rows dated 2026-10-13 | — | **0** |
| `Applying` lines in the boot window | — | **0** (control: impossible word 0, 153 total lines) |

Newest tracker row is dated 2026-09-30. So nothing was applied in the file sense, while the health body says 46.

## The consequence

A deploy check that reads `startupMigrations.applied` as a migration count will report 46 applied migrations on a zero-migration deploy. The repo's own deploy discipline is to **read the schema state rather than a runner summary line**, precisely because a summary line has reported success over a stale image before; this field is the same shape of trap one layer out, in the health surface rather than the runner.

## Nearest class members — read in full before filing, neither is this

* **KS-1062** (Done, P2) — the *tenant* loop's `migrated` counter cannot report a failure. Same family (a migration counter that misreports) but a different counter and a correctness defect, not a reporting-aggregation one.
* **KS-1272** (Done, P4) — `Platform DB migrations INCOMPLETE — 1 FAILED {"applied":6,"failed":1}` on kintsugi. Shows these same counters in the log, but is about a failing DELETE, not about what `applied` aggregates.
* Also read and distinct: KS-1125, KS-1055, KS-1401, KS-1096.

*Dedupe: all **1,564** Secuura-PK issues were pulled **including archived** and matched LITERALLY (not via the fuzzy* `searchIssues`*) on* `startupMigrations`*,* `startup-migrations`*,* `health/deep`*,* `File-based`*,* `migrations complete`*,* `applied=46`*,* `idempotent`*,* `tracker row`*. Positive control* `secuura` *matched **998**; negative control* `zzQqXx-no-such-token-d19` *matched **0**, so the matcher discriminates.* `applied=46` *matched 0 existing issues.*

Found by Seat D 19th during the kintsugi round-2 deploy; filed on Wednesday's instruction (2026-10-13T00:16:31Z). Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-13_seatD-19th/stepFG/` and `/home/secuura/secuura/Dev/REVISION`.

title: Anchor a detached signature against the existing K document (sign without a new version)
description:
Raised from platform-s [PS-1070](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1070/signing-formats-a-detached-signature-is-bound-on-chain-by-content-hash) (Stuart, 2026-10-13). This is a platform-k change. Platform-s will switch to it once it ships on the paired K.

## Today

Platform-s now signs non-PDF documents **detached**: a CAdES `.p7s` is stored beside the unchanged file ([PS-1043](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1043/signing-formats-p1-detached-signing-baseline-signformatpolicy)). The content is unchanged, so S does not fork a K version for it. Instead S posts a **flat** `/api/anchors` anchor whose `DocumentId` is S's own transaction id (`ToHyphenatedGuid(tx.ChainId)`), not K's document id. That has two consequences:

* The signature sits outside K's lifecycle for the document.
* The anchored hash is the content hash, and the upload's anchor carries that hash too. **K's verify-by-hash therefore returns two unrelated anchors for one hash.**

## Ask

A way for S to record a **sign event against an existing K document without creating a new version**. Either of these would do:

* a sign/attest verb that keeps the document's version tip where it is; or
* a `sign` event on `/lifecycle-events` for that document.

It must carry:

* the content hash, which must equal the tip's;
* the signature's own hash, `metadata.signatureHash` ([KS-1454](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1454/anchor-schema-accept-and-anchor-platform-ss-signaturehash-the-plain), so the two should be sequenced together);
* the usual non-PII whitelist only. `PayloadJson` never leaves S.

**Verify** should then return one document with a signature event on it, not two anchors.

## Platform-s side, once this ships

S retires the flat path for detached signs in `CardanoAnchorService.PerVerb.cs` `case "sign"`. That change is gated on the paired K's published spec declaring the new verb or event.

title: GET /api/keys has no organisation arm: an ORG_ADMIN or ISSUER_ADMIN lists another organisation's keys in the same tenant
description:
## BLUF

`GET /api/keys` **has no organisation arm.** An `ORG_ADMIN` or `ISSUER_ADMIN` of organisation A lists organisation B's API keys when B is in the same tenant, using B's exact id. The mint and the revoke are both organisation-bounded for these roles; the list is the only one of the three routes that is not. **Measured** at develop `7c6b3d88`, details below. Facts only, no fix. Filed on Wednesday's ruling while building KS-1553 PR 1, which does **not** add the bound.

**What is exposed:** each key's **id, name, prefix, scopes and connector id**, plus `lastUsedAt`, `usageCount`, `isActive` and `createdAt`. **Not key material:** the list never returns the key or its hash.

**Not reached by Kam's ADMIN ruling.** That ruling (KS-1570) concerns the tenant-level `ADMIN` role on the mint. The roles here are `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`, which are organisation-bounded on the mint (KS-1533) and on the revoke (KS-764).

## The code

At develop `7c6b3d88`, `services/security/src/index.ts:1318-1366`:

* The handler filters `k.organizationId === organizationId`, where `organizationId` is the raw query value, and then `callerIsPlatform || k.tenantId === caller.tenantId`. That second filter is KS-742's tenant bound.
* Nothing in the handler reads `caller.organizationId` or calls `isOrgBoundedRole`.
* The mint, by contrast, calls `decideTenantAccess(user, tenantId, { targetOrganizationId })` (`index.ts:1173`). That engages the organisation arm for `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES = {ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN}` (`packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`).
* The revoke is bounded by `decideKeyRevoke` (KS-764).

## Measured

A throwaway in-process probe, using the same harness as `ks1533-key-mint-organisation-arm.test.ts` (memory-backed; the list reads only `memApiKeys`). Organisation ids contain hex letters, so the upper-case form is not identical to the original.

| caller | lists | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| platform (`super_admin`) | mints for A1 and A2 | 201, 201 |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` of A1 | A1 | 200, 1 key |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` **of A1** | **A2, exact id** | **200, 1 key (the gap)** |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` of A1 | A2, upper-case | 200, 0 keys (only because the compare is raw; see below) |
| CONTROL: `ISSUER_ADMIN` of a tenant-B org | A2 | 200, 0 keys (the tenant filter is real) |
| CONTROL: platform | A2 | 200, 1 key |

**After KS-1553 PR 1** the list normalises the query, so the upper-case form of A2 also lists A2's key. That reveals nothing the exact id does not already reveal. PR 1 pins both as cells labelled MEASURED GAP that name this ticket, so adding a bound later is a visible edit.

## Dedupe

I scanned all 1,560 issues, archived ones included, with their comments, for list / another-organisation / organisation-arm wording. The positive control (KS-1533 matching "organisation arm") fired, and a bogus-symbol control returned 0. Nothing covers the list. KS-742 bounded the list by **tenant** only.

## Not decided here

The shape of the bound: refuse, or filter as KS-742 and `GET /api/audit` do. Also how it treats the org-less bounded accounts KS-779 recorded as intentional.

title: The gateway forwards an inbound x-wallet-address to originate on POST /api/documents, and originate never reads it — dead forward (facts only)
description:
## BLUF

**The gateway hand-forwards an inbound** `x-wallet-address` **header to originate on** `POST /api/documents`**, and originate never reads it.** The forward is dead code. It carries a client-supplied value past the gateway for no consumer. Facts only, no fix. Filed on Wednesday's ruling while planning KS-1223, which leaves this code untouched.

## Facts

All at develop `7c6b3d88`:

* `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1383`: `if (req.headers['x-wallet-address']) forwardHeaders['x-wallet-address'] = req.headers['x-wallet-address'] …`, inside the hand-built forward to originate on POST /api/documents.
* Originate has **0** reads of `x-wallet-address`. Control: originate does read `x-user-id` from headers, in `metering.ts`.
* A `git grep -i x-wallet-address` over all 4,392 tracked files finds exactly two non-test files. One is this line. The other is `services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:55`, which KS-1223 changes.
* A pin test asserts today's behaviour: `services/api-gateway/src/__tests__/ks1223-wallet-forwarded-to-originate.test.ts` (:84 RED, :87 CONTROL). Removing the forward flips it.
* Separately, `ks1041-vouch-header-strip.test.ts:113` pins that the header is **not** in the gateway's edge strip.

## Not decided here

Whether to delete the forward (one line, plus the pin test flipped) or leave it.

title: POST /api/referrals/apply takes the applicant's userId from the request body, not the token — read from source, NOT exercised (facts only)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/referrals/apply` **takes the applicant's** `userId` **from the request BODY, not from the signed-in caller's token.** Read from source, **NOT exercised**. The route is authenticated, but the token's userId is never used. Facts only, no fix. Noticed while planning KS-1223 and filed on Wednesday's ruling. It is not part of the KS-1223 pull request.

## What the code does

All read at develop `7c6b3d88`:

* The body schema `applyCodeSchema` requires `userId: z.string().uuid()` and accepts an optional `walletAddress` (`services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:23-30`).
* The route passes `body.userId` and `body.walletAddress` to `referralService.applyCode` (`referrals.ts:126-137`). Nothing in the route reads `req.user`.
* The route **is** authenticated. `services/referral/src/index.ts:81` runs `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())` before `:83` mounts `/api/referrals`, and the gateway runs `authenticateToken(false)` before proxying (`api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1053-1055`).
* `applyCode` (`services/referral/src/services/referralService.ts:419`) uses the body `userId` for every identity decision:
  * the self-referral check `referralCode.ownerId === userId` (`:441`);
  * the already-referred check `dbGetReferralByReferredUser(userId)`;
  * `referredUserId` on the stored referral;
  * the signup reward, `createReward(userId, …)`, when the fraud check passes.

## What that would allow (NOT exercised)

Reading the code, a signed-in caller could:

* apply their **own** code while naming a different uuid. The self-referral check would compare the code owner with that other uuid and pass.
* create a referral, and the signup reward, for a `userId` that is not theirs.

I have **not** run this on any stack. Whether a reward is ever paid out from these rows was not traced.

## Callers

There is no product caller of `/apply` in the repo: 0 non-test hits outside the spec, the route table and the schemathesis baseline (`git grep "referrals/apply"` over all 4,392 tracked files). The route is in the published spec, so any API client can call it.

## Dedupe

The eight tickets naming `referrals/apply` (KS-1016, KS-971, KS-784, KS-565, KS-466, KS-445, KS-431, KS-430) are all schema or status-code sweeps, read in each case. None covers the body `userId`. `applyCodeSchema`, `body.userId`, `referred_user_id` and "apply on behalf" have 0 hits on the board.

title: Count the referral codes already stored with a header-supplied owner wallet (svc_referral_codes.owner_wallet_address) read-only on Kintsugi and demo — facts only, KS-1223 residue
description:
## BLUF

**Referral codes already stored with a header-supplied** `svc_referral_codes.owner_wallet_address` **keep that value after the KS-1223 fix ships. The fix changes only codes generated after it is deployed.** This ticket is **facts only, no fix**. It exists so the rows can be counted read-only on an environment before anyone decides what to do with them. **I cannot count them: I have no box access.** Filed on Wednesday's instruction while planning KS-1223 (Kam ruled option (a) on 2026-10-13: the referral service reads the wallet linked to the signed-in user and stops reading the header).

## Why every stored wallet today came from the header

All measured at develop `7c6b3d88`, by `git grep` and by reading the code:

* `POST /api/referrals/generate` sets the wallet as `req.user.walletAddress || req.headers['x-wallet-address']` (`services/referral/src/routes/referrals.ts:55`).
* No access token carries a wallet. `generateAccessToken` (`services/auth/src/services/jwt.ts:187-209`) signs userId, email, role, organizationId, verificationLevel, sessionId, tenantId, tenantSlug and scopes, and nothing else. So the first operand is always empty and the header is the only source.
* `generateCode` (`services/referral/src/services/referralService.ts:310`) is the only writer of the value. The route at `referrals.ts:63` is its only non-test caller. It stores `ownerWalletAddress: walletAddress` (`:353`) through `INSERT INTO svc_referral_codes` (`:62-65`). No `docker/init` or migration seeds that table.
* **A stored wallet is never rewritten.** The save is `ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE SET is_active = EXCLUDED.is_active, current_uses = EXCLUDED.current_uses` (`referralService.ts:64`). `owner_wallet_address` is not in that list.

So on any environment, every non-null `owner_wallet_address` was sent by the client that generated the code, unless the code was written by hand.

## Why it matters, and how much

The stored wallet is the **referrer side** of the `WALLET_COLLISION` fraud flag. That flag is an exact `===` comparison against the wallet in the `/apply` request body, and it is skipped when either side is absent (`services/referral/src/services/fraudDetection.ts:166-168`; `referralService.ts:455-456`). A header-supplied value on an old code can:

* raise the flag on an honest applicant who sends the same string, or
* hide a real collision because the stored value is not the owner's wallet.

Per J 5th's measurement, which Wednesday relayed and which I did **not** re-run, the stored wallet drives only this flag and never a payout.

## What is not known

**The count, on every environment.** It can be taken read-only with the following query. By the reasoning above, every non-null row it counts is header-set:

```sql
SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE owner_wallet_address IS NOT NULL) AS with_wallet,
       count(*) AS total
FROM svc_referral_codes;
```

`svc_referral_codes` is not under row-level security, so the app role sees every row.

## Not decided here

Whether those rows should be left alone, have their wallet cleared, or have it re-derived from the owner's linked wallet. Nobody has ruled on it. Count them first.

title: API-key revoke route writes the revoke into shared memory before its database save commits; under a REPEATABLE READ/SERIALIZABLE default a revoke behind a committing rotate fails 40001 (o1), plus o4/o2/o5 from the #1529 round-2 gate
description:
## BLUF

**The API-key revoke route writes its revoke into shared in-memory state BEFORE its database save commits** — the memory-first pattern KS-1556 removed from the rotate path. With no undo left anywhere it no longer causes the n1 regression, but it is the same shape, and the round-2 gate measured a latent failure on this route. **Facts only; no build.** Filed on Wednesday's ruling as the revoke-route ticket owed from PR #1529 (KS-1556), carrying the gate's observations **o1, o4, o2 and o5** (verdict sha256/16 `b662a71501b66490`, at head `d19b7a708e5b`).

## The shape (lines at `d19b7a708e5b`, `services/security/src/index.ts`)

* `DELETE /api/keys/:id` is at `:1374`. It builds the revoked object and saves it through `dbSaveApiKey`.
* `dbSaveApiKey` (`:409`) **first statement** is `:410` `memApiKeys.set(k.id, k);` — so memory holds the revoke **before** the upsert runs, and the upsert can then wait on a row lock (a concurrent rotate's retire holds one).
* Under KS-888 R2 a revoke whose save **fails** keeps its in-memory revoke deliberately, so the key stops working in this process. That contract is kept; the question is the ordering, not the fail-closed rule.

## o1 — MEASURED by the gate, latent: a revoke behind a committing rotate fails 40001 under REPEATABLE READ / SERIALIZABLE

* Under a REPEATABLE READ or SERIALIZABLE pool default, a revoke whose save waits behind a rotate that then COMMITs fails with **SQLSTATE 40001**, and the route answers **500 "revoke not stored"** (the KS-888 log line is at `:1421`).
* At **grace 60** the database keeps the revoked key `is_active = true` with up to 60 s left, so **other replicas honour it until expiry**; this process refuses it (KS-888 R2).
* Measured in 2/2 grace-60 rows and 4/4 grace-0 rows per run (harmless at grace 0, where the rotate already retired the key). **Head and develop identical** under RR and SER; **absent at READ COMMITTED**.
* **Latent:** nothing sets that default today — the same class as KS-1556's m2, which pinned READ COMMITTED on the rotate transaction. The revoke path has no such pin.

## o4 — the DB branch of `revokePriorConnectorKeys` is unreachable but keeps the old pattern

`revokePriorConnectorKeys` (`:231`) has a memory-first branch and a DB branch; its only caller (`:348`) runs only when `!isDbAvailable()`, so the DB branch is unreachable in production. It still holds the memory-first-then-DB pattern KS-1556 removed from the rotate path; a future caller on the DB path would bring it back. Already true on develop.

## o2 and o5 — related memory-ordering observations from the same gate (pre-existing, not findings)

* **o2:** the rotate chain's bounded wait can lose memory order only when the post-COMMIT apply is delayed, which the code cannot do on its own; when forced, the key list shows a retired key as active until a validate corrects it.
* **o5:** `loadFromDb` (clear at `:536`) can leave memory stale if its SELECT straddles a rotate's COMMIT. Validate stays right. **Not measured.**

## Not decided here

Whether the revoke should apply to memory only after its save commits (as the rotate now does), take the same per-connector chain or advisory lock, or pin READ COMMITTED like the rotate. Each changes KS-888 R2's mechanics and is the owner's call.

## Related

KS-1556 / PR #1529 (the shape this mirrors), KS-888 (R2: a failed revoke save keeps the in-memory revoke), KS-1370 (validate's stale read and usage write — a **different** defect in the same function: read in full before filing; not a duplicate), KS-1549.

title: KS-1557 read side (pull request 1531 gate observations): lookups per examined row, three mutants killed by one cell each, an undocumented pool-mode prerequisite, revoked certifications still count
description:
## BLUF

Five observations from the Opus gate on pull request 1531 (head `1ffc0d7a4ad740a91f2c04122fb55cd44477c928`, report sha256/16 `64b8bfc92d36e2b6`) that are not findings against that pull request and deserve a ticket. One checklist; split an item out when someone picks it up. Facts only, each checked by me against the source at that head unless it says otherwise.

- [ ] **1. Lookups per examined row (gate O1).** The cap bounds EXAMINED rows to 8, not lookups. An examined row can cost two logical lookups: the parent fetch (`fetchParentHash`, called at `routes/verification.ts:299` when the parent is not in the same-hash set) plus the certification lookup.
  * **Measured by the gate:** 2 lookups for v2 by `derivedDocumentId` (+8 statements); 8 parent fetches when nine claimed rows have parents outside the set (+32).
  * **By code, NOT constructed by anyone:** worst case 16 logical lookups (64 statements) when 8 same-hash rows have same-hash parents pushed out of the set by `VERIFY_ROWSET_LIMIT` (24). The v1 registry path can re-resolve one row after `crossTenantLookup` (at most 1 more).
  * The pull request body says "one lookup per examined row"; that holds for parents inside the set.
  * **Asks:** build the 16-lookup case and measure it, and decide whether the bound should be on lookups rather than rows.
- [ ] **2. Three mutants killed by ONE cell each (gate O4).** V22 (v1 cross-tenant site skips resolution), V26 (the certification fetch drops the issuer column) and G8 (cross-tenant rows not tagged `_tenantId`) are each red only in the pool-mode x-tenant cell (`MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true`) and green in single-tenant mode. A second pin each, or one cell that does not lean on its environment for that path.
- [ ] **3. Rule 2 duplicates itself (gate O3).** "The parent link is set" is also enforced by the hash check: a NULL parent fails `fetchParentHash`'s UUID test (`:259-261`). So mutant V03 (the parent-link check dropped) is killed only by the unit cell "rows that fail the cheap checks do NOT consume the lookup cap"; the integration cell "has NO parent link" passes under V03.
- [ ] **4. An undocumented prerequisite (gate O8).** The pool-mode run of `ks1557-verify-trusts-certification-evidence.integration.test.ts` needs `platform_document_registry` in the SAME database as the app's `tenants` table (apply `docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql` to the app database and point `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL` at it). With a separate platform database the registry insert fails its foreign key as a logged warning and the x-tenant cell goes red, 1 of 17. The file header does not say so; the only trace is the two env lines at `:26-27` (checked). The previous seat and the gate both lost time to it.
- [ ] **5. A revoked certification still counts (gate O9, case P05).** When the cited certification row is REVOKED, verify still presents the derived row as certified. Identical on develop and on the head; the pull request body discloses it ("revoked certifications are not examined"). Ticket KS-521 (Done) was a revoked DOCUMENT; this is a revoked CERTIFICATION row, a different artifact. **Needs a ruling on whether verify should honour certification revocation**, and then a cell. Possibly a higher priority than this ticket; it is filed here so it is not lost.

## Recorded, no ticket

* Connector principals: rule 5 (owner equals issuer) is vacuous for connectors because both are NULL, so the 32-bit suffix is the only binding left (gate P03). The pull request body names that residual and it is the write side of KS-1557 that addresses it.
* The two rewritten ks584 tests pass on develop as well, so they are regression fixtures, not pins of the new rule (gate O7); acceptable for what they are.

Related: KS-1557, ticket KS-1561, pull request 1531.

title: Count the existing non-canonical svc_api_keys.organization_id rows (every 'default-org' row included) read-only on Kintsugi and demo — facts only, no backfill
description:
## BLUF

**Rows already stored with a non-canonical** `svc_api_keys.organization_id` **keep their stored value, and a canonicalising list comparison will not find them by the canonical id.** This ticket is **facts only, no fix**: it exists so the count is taken read-only on an environment before anyone decides whether a backfill is wanted. **I cannot count them — I have no box access.** Filed on Wednesday's ruling while planning KS-1553.

## Why non-canonical rows exist

`normaliseOrgId` (`packages/shared/src/security/orgId.ts:42`) is the whole normaliser and its body is:

```ts
typeof v === 'string' && v.trim() !== '' ? v.trim().toLowerCase() : null
```

It trims, lower-cases, and treats blank as absent. It does **nothing** about braces, the no-hyphen 32-hex form, a zero-width space, or any other rendering. The mint stores whatever comes back (`services/security/src/index.ts:1242`), and the column is `TEXT`, not `UUID` — so a non-uuid string is storable and is stored verbatim.

## The measured in-repo SOURCE of such rows: the Admin Dashboard

This is the part that makes the residue more than theoretical. The Admin Dashboard hard-codes a non-uuid organisation id on **both** operations:

* `frontend/admin/src/pages/ApiKeys.tsx:92` — mints with `organizationId: 'default-org'`.
* `frontend/admin/src/services/api.ts:358-360` — lists with `organizationId || 'default-org'`, and `ApiKeys.tsx:75` passes no argument, so it always sends the literal.

**Measured** (2026-10-13, Seat V 6th, own scratch PostgreSQL 15, service as `secuura_app`, the real routes, every arm with a control):

| what | result |
| -- | -- |
| the admin's exact mint body, `organizationId: 'default-org'` | **201** |
| the stored value | `default-org`**, verbatim** |
| the admin's exact list, `?organizationId=default-org` | **200, and it returns that key** |
| CONTROL: a different org id | 0 keys, so the list really filters |
| the UPPER-CASE form of the same id | **0 keys** (the KS-1553 (a) mismatch) |
| CONTROL: a mint with no `organizationId` (the metering-key shape) | 201, stays absent |

So **every key ever created through the Admin Dashboard's API Keys page carries** `organization_id = 'default-org'`, which is not a uuid. `'default-org'` appears nowhere else in the tracked tree — it is not seeded by any migration or `docker/init` script — so it exists only where that page created it.

## What needs counting, read-only, on Kintsugi and demo

A deploy seat with box access should run, per environment, and record the numbers on this ticket:

```sql
SELECT count(*) AS total,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE organization_id IS NULL)                             AS absent,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE organization_id = 'default-org')                      AS admin_literal,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE organization_id ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$') AS canonical_uuid,
       count(*) FILTER (WHERE organization_id IS NOT NULL
                          AND organization_id <> 'default-org'
                          AND organization_id !~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$') AS other_non_canonical
FROM svc_api_keys;
```

**Pair it with a control**: the five buckets must sum to `total`, or the predicate set is wrong. If `other_non_canonical` is above zero, list the distinct values (they are organisation identifiers, not secrets) so the brace / 32-hex / zero-width question is answered with data rather than inference.

## Explicitly NOT proposed here

* **No backfill.** Rewriting stored credential metadata is not something to do on the side of a validation change, and it is approval-class.
* **No fix in KS-1553's PR.** That PR states this residue and points here.
* **No claim about any environment's numbers.** I have measured only my own scratch database.

## Related

* **KS-1564** — the Admin Dashboard's hard-coded `'default-org'`: the measured **SOURCE** of these rows. Count that ticket's page as the producer when reading the numbers below.
* **KS-1553** — the raw-vs-canonical list comparison and the non-canonical forms. This residue is its stated consequence.
* **KS-1514** — item 2 (the declared-but-unenforced `uuid` on the list query) is the other half of the same seam.
* **KS-748** (P4) — `organization_id` vs `tenant_id` *coherence*. A different gap in the same column: it is about the pair being incoherent, not about the id's text form. Read in full before filing this; not a duplicate.
* **KS-889** (P2) — the `connector_id` backfill window. A different column; it names `organization_id` only as a candidate backfill source. Read in full; not a duplicate.
* Class: **KS-1022** (the id-format contract seam).

*Dedupe: all 695 Secuura-PK issues were pulled and matched LITERALLY (not via the fuzzy* `searchIssues`*) on* `non-canonical`*,* `default-org`*,* `organization_id`*,* `organizationId`*,* `normaliseOrgId`*,* `backfill`*,* `32-hex`*,* `no-hyphen`*,* `zero-width`*, with a bogus-symbol control returning 0.* `default-org` *returned **0** existing issues. The four near-misses matching two or more terms (KS-1553, KS-1525, KS-959, KS-748, KS-889) were read before filing.*

title: QUESTION: should ks860 WALK_ROOTS and ks879 DEV_ROOT walk systemTest/ (which 499 .py files would still escape)?
description:
## BLUF

A scope question, not a defect and not a merge blocker — filed so
[KS-1347](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1347)'s third acceptance box has a home, which that
box explicitly allows ("a decision is recorded … **or a separate ticket exists for it**").
**Neither** `ks860` **nor** `ks879` **walks** `systemTest/`, so that whole tree has no loopback-bind guard
and no raw-control-byte guard, and nothing structural would have caught the KS-1347 percent-encoding
class there either. Facts and costs are measured below. **No build, and no ruling on the behaviour**
**from me** — Wednesday ruled only that this is filed separately, not what the answer is.

Same class as [KS-1141](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1141) (are `crypto-agility.guard.test.ts:44`
`SCAN_DIRS` and `ks727-errorhandler-class-guard.test.ts:150` `SCAN_ROOTS` the intended scopes?),
**different sites** — that ticket covers those two guards and not these. Read in full before filing.
It also records the precedent cost: KS-886's earlier widening of `ks879` from
`services/`+`packages/` to the whole Dev tree **cost ≈0.8 s per walk and found 0 offenders**.

## What each guard walks today (read at source, develop `5d5aea41feca`)

| guard | root | mechanism |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks860-test-listeners-bind-loopback.test.ts` | `Dev/services` + `Dev/packages` | `:98` `const WALK_ROOTS = ['services', 'packages']`, joined to `DEV_ROOT` at `:472` and `:726` |
| `packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks879-no-raw-control-bytes-repo-wide.test.ts` | all of `Blockchain/Dev` | `:98` `DEV_ROOT = findDevRoot(process.cwd())`, `:153` `sourceFiles(DEV_ROOT)` |

`systemTest/` is a **repo-root sibling of** `Blockchain/`, so it is outside both — including outside
`ks879`, whose name says "repo-wide" but whose root is `Blockchain/Dev`.

`ks879`'s filter: `SKIP_DIRS = {node_modules, dist, build, coverage, .turbo}`,
`EXTS = [.ts, .tsx, .js, .mjs, .cjs]` (`:117-118`).
`ks879` declares `WALK_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` (`:159`); `ks860` **declares no walk timeout.**

## What walking `systemTest/` would ADD (tracked files, so reproducible)

|  | today | `systemTest/` would add | change |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ks860` — test files | 552 | **+248** | +45% |
| `ks879` — `.ts/.tsx/.js/.mjs/.cjs` | 1567 | **+545** | +35% |

## What it would COST

Measured on this host by reproducing `ks879`'s own walk (same `SKIP_DIRS` and `EXTS`), twice:

```
ks879 today      (Blockchain/Dev):  1567 files walked in 50 ms / 28 ms
ks879 + systemTest             :  2112 files walked in 44 ms / 44 ms
systemTest alone               :   545 files walked in  8 ms / 13 ms
```

So the **directory walk** is not the cost — about +10 ms. The real cost is the per-file read for
control bytes, which scales with the +35%. For comparison, KS-886's widening to the Dev tree cost
≈0.8 s per walk (KS-1141).

⚠ **The cost interacts with a known fragility.** [KS-1155](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1155)
is open on exactly this: "packages/shared tree-walking guards exceed vitest's 5 s default under
fleet load". A 35% larger walk makes that worse, and `ks860` has no declared timeout at all. Any
widening should be sequenced against KS-1155 rather than before it.

## ⚠ The fact that most changes the answer

`systemTest/` **holds 499 tracked** `.py` **files, which are outside BOTH guards'** `EXTS` **entirely.**
So extending the walk root would **not** give `systemTest/` raw-control-byte coverage — it would
cover the TypeScript/JavaScript half and leave the Python half (the Schemathesis harness) exactly as
uncovered as it is now. "Walk `systemTest/` too" and "`systemTest/` is guarded" are not the same
statement, and a ruling that assumed they were would buy less than it looks.

## What a ruling should say

Following KS-1141's shape, for each of the two guards: **(a) scope INTENDED** — add one sentence to
the docblock naming the excluded trees and why, so the next reader does not re-derive this; or
**(b) widen** — the builder first measures the red set on the wider tree (KS-886's precedent: 0
offenders) and sequences it against KS-1155, then files the change. And separately: whether the
Python half needs a guard of its own, or is out of scope by design.

## Board search before filing

`searchIssues` (fuzzy, 6 per term) by symbol: `WALK_ROOTS`, `ks860`, `ks879`,
`raw control bytes systemTest`, `loopback bind guard walk root`. Nearest hits read in full:
**KS-1141** (same class, two other guards — cited above), **KS-1155** (the walk-timeout cost,
cited), KS-1140 (Done — the ks879 🔴 cell walking the tree on its own), KS-1147 (Done — a ks860
boundary case), KS-807 (the control-byte guard cannot see a raw body — a different blind spot in the
same guard family), KS-492 and KS-1042 (systemTest coverage, but security-regression scope, not
structural guards). **None names the** `systemTest/` **walk-root question for ks860 or ks879.** Filed new.

title: KS-1538 gate follow-ups (m1-m4): a pkey-addressed documentId passes the legacy-certify check but the UPDATE matches external_id only; check and UPDATE not in one transaction; stale provenance admits a former creator; ~0.55 ms timing difference
description:
**ACTION (owner: the originate build lane; P3, one checklist):** four Minor findings from the Opus gate of PR #1525 (KS-1538), none of which blocks it. Each is quoted with the gate's measurement and its fix-shape. Decide per item whether to build, accept or close. No build is started by this ticket.

## m1. A pkey-addressed `documentId` passes the new check, but the UPDATE silently does nothing

`certifications.ts` resolves the document with `getDocument` (external_id first, then the pkey UUID), but the legacy `UPDATE documents ...` matches `external_id` only. **Measured:** the owner and a SYSTEM_ADMIN get 201 with a certification saved, while the row stays `anchored` with no `certified_at`, and nothing is logged (the new catch logs only thrown errors, not a 0-row UPDATE). **Pre-existing: identical on base.** Fix-shape: resolve to the row's `external_id` from the record the check already read before the UPDATE, or log or refuse on 0 rows.

## m2. Check and UPDATE are not in one transaction

The window spans the holder lookup and the anchoring POST, whose timeout is 10 s. **Constructed:** the owner passes the check, the owner flips to B during a 1.5 s anchoring delay (SQL simulating `transfer-custody`), and the UPDATE then lands on a document B now owns, carrying A's issuer id. Not reproduced through the real transfer route. Low severity: the caller was authorised at check time.

## m3. Stale provenance admits a former creating connector

`wasCreatedByConnector` (`provenance.ts:285-296`; the same arm `GET /api/documents/:id` uses) trusts a provenance row keyed by the document's external id. **Constructed:** connector A creates document U with `onBehalfOf`, U is deleted (superuser SQL), user B re-registers U, and connector A certifies B's document: 201, row certified. Needs a deletion plus deliberate reuse of the id. It belongs to the owner rule, not to PR #1525. Owner should consider provenance rows keyed to the pkey, or deleted with the document.

## m4. A timing oracle of about 0.55 ms (measured locally, not over a network)

The refusal bodies are byte-identical, but latency is not: for a connector, not-yours 1.474 ms (p10 1.286) vs unknown 0.923 ms (p90 1.165), so the distributions separate (A/A control 0.923 vs 0.921 ms, N=200 per series, interleaved); for humans, an unknown UUID-shaped id 1.466 ms vs not-yours 0.952 ms (the pkey fallback query). `GET /api/documents/:id` has the same shape.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for "pkey UUID addressed documentId certify UPDATE external_id", "wasCreatedByConnector stale provenance former creating connector", "check and UPDATE not in one transaction certify anchoring window", "timing difference unknown not-yours refusal connector" and "legacy certify follow-ups". 315 distinct issues read. Literal matches in title or description: `wascreatedbyconnector` 0, `stale provenance` 0. The only issue matching two or more of the seven distinctive tokens was KS-1538 itself. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. Relevance-ranked: "none in the top 75 per term", not a census.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1525 (KS-1538), verdict GO WITH NOTE (sha256/16 `0273b5bb14d3f036`), findings m1 to m4; Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (20:01Z) that they are filed as one P3 follow-up. m5 (`SUPER_ADMIN` goes 201 to 403 on this path) is stated in the PR body instead.

title: Seat handover clone recipe fails its checkout: git clone --reference of the shared 2_Project_Files stops with 'unable to parse commit 54b2a5c2' (2 seats of 2); a plain clone works
description:
**ACTION (owner: the build lane / whoever maintains the seat-handover recipe):** change the working-area recipe in the seat handovers from a `--reference ... --dissociate` clone of the shared `2_Project_Files` checkout to a plain clone from GitHub, and find out why the first one fails.

## Symptom (measured, twice)

Seat J 4th (2026-10-12) and Seat J 5th (2026-10-12T18:50Z) each ran:

```
git clone --reference "<shared 2_Project_Files>" --dissociate git@github.com:Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git <dest>
```

Both stopped with `fatal: unable to parse commit 54b2a5c26d75a28b14fdce578dd5a5aadee49039` and "Clone succeeded, but checkout failed". That commit is the tip of `main` (the PR #908 merge), the branch a clone checks out by default.

Recovery that worked both times: `git checkout -B develop origin/develop`, then `git fsck --full` (rc 0, no output) and a check that every `git ls-files -z` path exists (J 5th: 4,382 files, 0 missing).

## Control

The same clone with no `--reference` and no `--dissociate` checked out clean in 35 s (rc 0, status clean, HEAD `54b2a5c2`). One run each side, so the shared object store is implicated, not proven.

## Ruled out, read-only against the shared store

* The commit reads there: `cat-file -t` says commit, `rev-list -1` returns it.
* `git commit-graph verify` there is rc 0. Its commit-graph file is dated 30 Sep 06:16, 13 days old.
* Cause: unproven.

## Also

A clone script piped through `tee` made the harness report "completed (exit code 0)" for a clone that had failed with rc 128. The script's own printed rc was the truth. Do not pipe a step whose exit code decides what happens next.

## Searched before filing

Linear `searchIssues` (titles, descriptions and comments, archived included), 3 pages of 25 per term, for "clone --reference dissociate", "unable to parse commit", "reference clone shared checkout", "seat handover clone recipe" and "54b2a5c2". 249 distinct issues read. Literal match for `dissociate`, `--reference`, `54b2a5c2`, "unable to parse commit", "clone recipe" and `alternates` in title or description: 0 hits. Control: the same query and matcher finds KS-1538 for a term it must find. The search is relevance-ranked, so this is "0 hits in the top 75 per term", not a census of the board.

Source: Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (19:01Z) that this is filed as a priority 4 Backlog ticket.

title: KS-1517 follow-up: stale-build residue from the #1515 round 2 gate (permanent targets read as stale, C2/A11 survivors, a null package.json crash, wording)
description:
**BLUF:** Residue from the #1515 (KS-1517) round 2 Opus gate, filed as one P3 checklist per Wednesday's ruling (2026-10-12 17:59Z). None of these is reachable on today's tree. Each item carries the shape the gate measured.

**Context:** Line numbers are on #1515 head `a7d0583d`, which is the closing amendment `0723117b` plus develop `425ad3e0`. Source: the round 2 verdict (Minors m1 to m7, plus one carried item). The closing amendment already fixed MJ1 (the note's crash and hang), m1's fixture (R2), m2 (the code check restored and the regex anchored), and the comments m7 named at CLAUDE.md 399-402 and 412-413 and `check.cjs` 102-103 and 325. They are not repeated here.

- [ ] **(a) m3. A declaration target that is permanently absent is reported as a stale build ("rebuild it"), and no rebuild can fix it.**
  * Where: `check.cjs:208-219` (`mapTargets` takes the FIRST matching `*` key in object order, where TypeScript takes the longest prefix), `:331` (the "package declares nothing for this subpath, so it is left to tsc" exemption), `:332-333` (any declared target that is absent goes to `staleFatal`, exit 2).
  * Shapes, all on complete builds:
    * X17: typesVersions names `dist/ghost.d.ts`, which the build never emits. tsc says TS7016; develop rc 1, head rc 2.
    * X16: a typo subpath under a catch-all `"*": ["dist/*.d.ts"]`. tsc says TS2307; develop rc 1, head rc 2 with "missing dist/thnig.d.ts". Under a catch-all key every subpath counts as declared, so the exemption at `:331` never applies.
    * X18: the reverse resolver divergence (first-match `*` against TypeScript's longest `sub/*`). Head rc 2 names the wrong file.
    * X17b: X17 with its TS7016 baselined. Develop rc 0, head rc 2, so a push develop accepts is refused.
  * Why it is unreachable today: both committed baselines hold 0 TS2307/TS7016 entries (measured 2026-10-13). The real shared package has no catch-all key. A stale-judged entry cannot be admitted, because the exit 2 runs before `--init` or `--update` writes. But `--init` can still admit a TS2307/TS7016 whose target is on disk at the time; the comment at `check.cjs:286-293` points here.
  * The gate's suggested fix: exit 2 only where a rebuild would plausibly help (the target lies under the package's outDir), or demote to a NEW error carrying a "may be stale" hint.
  * Docs: `CLAUDE.md:422-424` ("left to tsc") should add that it does not apply under a catch-all key.
- [ ] **(b) Two mutants survive the KS-1517 cells (measured on a green baseline, 29 of 29).**
  * C2, "TS2307 for any module" (drops the `@secuura` restriction at `check.cjs:295` and `:320`). Gate shape: `thirdparty/sub` mapped by typesVersions and unbuilt. Head rc 1, C2 rc 2.
  * A11, "only the first array target consulted" (`candidates(v)` at `:216`, `anyResolves` at `:308`). Gate shape: the array-divergence fixture. Head rc 1, A11 rc 2.
  * Add one cell per shape.
  * For the record, not survivors: C1, C5 and the amendment's isFile and try/catch mutants are killed. C4 is masked by the restored code check, and the code check and the regex anchor each mask the other; all three were measured by removing the masking guard too.
- [ ] **(c) m4. Stale builds that still read rc 1 "NEW" (the pre-PR misattribution).** Leg 16 still fails on each, so none is a silent pass. The gate judged this acceptable: the design names only what its resolver can name.
  * X19: a version-range key (TypeScript reads `>=4.0`; the resolver reads only `*`).
  * Y2: a main-only package whose sibling `index.d.ts` is missing.
  * Y3: a deep path with no typesVersions.
  * Y11: a directory target that is unbuilt.
  * Y5b: a re-export chain under `skipLibCheck:false`.
  * X2b: a nearer stale copy under `src/node_modules`.
  * Decide: fix one or more, or record each as a documented limit in CLAUDE.md.
- [ ] **(d) m5. Fatal-side crash on an installed** `@secuura` **package whose** `package.json` **is literally** `null`**.**
  * Where: `check.cjs:303` (`JSON.parse` in `packageJsonOf`), dereferenced through `declTargetsFor(found.pkg, sub)` at `:327`. `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null`, rc 1. Develop is also rc 1 (TS2307).
  * The note side is already covered by the amendment's try/catch (cell "MJ1 null package.json note-side"). npm would not install such a package.
  * Fix: `JSON.parse(...) || {}` at `:303`, plus a fatal-side cell.
- [ ] **(e) m6, cosmetic.**
  * One "missing declaration target" line is printed per importing site (`check.cjs:372`); real arm B prints the same target twice. Dedupe by target.
  * "tsc itself could not resolve the module" (`:370`) is printed for TS7016 too, where tsc DID resolve the `.js`. Word it per code.
- [ ] **(f) Leg 16's exit-2** `why` **text does not mention a stale build** (`scripts/preflight/test-types-ratchet.sh:65`). The checker's own stderr lines above it do. Sibling: KS-1527 item (a) pins the rc-1 wording in the same `case`, so one PR can do both.

**Dedupe (2026-10-13):** title and description searched for typecheck-tests, check.cjs, KS-1517, test-types-ratchet, stale build, permanently absent and declaration target. Hits: KS-1517, KS-1489 (Done), KS-1523, KS-1487 (Done), KS-1513, KS-1527, KS-1520 (Done), KS-1529, PS-549. None covers these items. KS-1527's leg-16 item is the rc-1 wording, not (f).

Refs KS-1517.

title: POLICY (Kam's call): role ADMIN is a KEY_ADMIN_ROLE that the KS-764 organisation arm never engages for, so a tenant ADMIN can mint a key for any organisation in its tenant
description:
## BLUF

`ADMIN` **is in** `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` **but in neither** `PLATFORM_ROLES` **nor** `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES`**, so the KS-764 organisation arm is skipped for it entirely and** `decideTenantAccess` **falls through to** `allow: 'same-tenant'`**.** After KS-1533 arm 1 closes the hole for `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`, a caller with role `ADMIN` can **still** mint a key carrying any organisation's `organizationId` inside its own tenant — the same Path 1 shape, through one role.

**This is a policy question about who may reach an irreversible cross-organisation erasure, so it is Kam's to decide, not an engineering choice inside a PR.** Wednesday put it on his board as a card (`secuura-ks1533-admin-role-unbounded-by-org-arm-1013`) and recommended leaving `ADMIN` unbounded. **Until he rules, KS-1533 arm 1 ships leaving** `ADMIN` **unbounded and says so plainly**, and the shared role set is NOT touched.

## The three sets, read at source

```
KEY_ADMIN_ROLES    services/security/src/provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49
                   SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN, ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN, ADMIN
PLATFORM_ROLES     packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59
                   SYSTEM_ADMIN, SUPER_ADMIN
ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES  packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:76
                   ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN
```

The arm is `if (organisationScope && isOrgBoundedRole(user.role))` (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:173`). `ADMIN` satisfies neither predicate, so the arm is skipped and the function returns `allow: 'same-tenant'` at `:225`.

| role | what arm 1 does for it |
| -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN`, `SUPER_ADMIN` | platform — bypass the arm by design (KS-577 depends on it) |
| `ORG_ADMIN`, `ISSUER_ADMIN` | org-bounded — **the arm applies**, which is KS-1533 arm 1 |
| `ADMIN` | **neither — the arm never engages** |

## The two readings
