**(a) By design, and this ticket closes as "documented".** `ADMIN` reads as a **tenant**-level admin, distinct from platform — KS-1283 is about "a widened `SUPER_ROLES` would admit a tenant `ADMIN` role on six routes", which treats it as a tenant role. On that reading, acting across organisations *inside its own tenant* is what a tenant admin is for, and arm 1 is complete as scoped.

**(b) A gap.** The sink is the KS-695 connector erasure, which is **irreversible** and destroys another organisation's titles, descriptions and name. KS-764's stated hazard is "an org-bounded admin in organisation A destroying organisation B's key" — if a tenant `ADMIN` may do the equivalent to B's *documents*, the boundary is only as strong as the weakest admin role.

**This ticket does not pick.** It records the question, the evidence, and what shipped in the meantime.

## If Kam rules (b)

`ADMIN` joins `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` in `packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts`. That is a **one-line change to a shared set that also governs the revoke route**, so it is not a local edit: it would change `DELETE /api/security/keys/:id` for every `ADMIN` caller too, and it needs its own gate and its own caller-population check (the same `caller has no organisation` 403 that KS-1533 arm 1 accepts for org-bounded roles would then apply to `ADMIN` as well). It should not be folded into KS-1533.

## Where it is pinned meanwhile

KS-1533 arm 1 carries a **documenting cell** that asserts today's behaviour — a tenant `ADMIN` minting for another organisation in its tenant succeeds — labelled as undecided policy rather than as a guarantee, so that whichever way Kam rules, the change is visible as a deliberate edit to a cell rather than a silent flip.

## Dedupe

Literal, case-insensitive over title and description, archived included: `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` **1** (KS-779 — the CALLER-side population of org-bounded accounts with no organisation claim, which is KS-1533 arm 1's accepted 403 price, not this question), `isOrgBoundedRole` **0**, `tenant ADMIN` 4 and `ADMIN role` 6 (the KS-1283 / KS-1506 / KS-486 family — a widened `SUPER_ROLES`, error-handler and review tickets, none of them this question). KS-764 (Done) created the arm and deliberately scoped it to the revoke route.

*Corrected after filing: the first version of this paragraph said* `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` *0. The scan returned KS-779. The conclusion is unchanged — no ticket asks whether* `ADMIN` *should be org-bounded — but the figure was wrong and a wrong dedupe count is worth correcting rather than leaving.*

Raised by Seat V 5th while building KS-1533 arm 1, 2026-10-12. Found by reading the role sets before writing the fix, not by a test.

---

## ADDENDUM — it is TWO roles, not one, and the verdicts are MEASURED by running the predicates

I ran the real `isPlatformRole`, `isOrgBoundedRole` and `decideTenantAccess` over the whole role vocabulary rather than reading the sets. Caller is `{role, tenantId:'t1', organizationId:'oA'}`, target is the same tenant and a DIFFERENT organisation `oB` — i.e. exactly the KS-1533 Path 1 shape:

| role (as the JWT carries it) | isPlatformRole | isOrgBoundedRole | verdict naming ANOTHER org in the same tenant |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `SYSTEM_ADMIN` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `SUPER_ADMIN` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `super_admin` | true | false | ALLOW `platform-admin` — by design |
| `platform_admin` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `PLATFORM_ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `ADMIN` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `admin` | **false** | **false** | **ALLOW** `same-tenant` **— UNBOUNDED** |
| `ORG_ADMIN` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `ISSUER_ADMIN` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `issuer_admin` | false | true | DENY `cross-organisation` — arm 1 working |
| `connector` | false | false | ALLOW `same-tenant` — correct: `decideMint` pins a provisioner to its own tenant on its own branch |

Both predicates upper-case the claim (`keyRevokePolicy.ts:84` and `:123`), so casing is NOT the issue — the role simply is not in either set.

### `platform_admin` is the more interesting half

`platform_admin` is treated as a **super-role by the gateway** in at least six places, while the key policy does not treat it as platform at all:

```
services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:65      SUPER_ROLES          includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515     SUPER_ADMIN_ROLES    includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts:577        PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES includes platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1094,1227                       include platform_admin
services/api-gateway/src/routes/audit-export.ts:105 adminRoles           includes platform_admin
packages/shared/src/security/keyRevokePolicy.ts:59  PLATFORM_ROLES       does NOT
services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:193               PLATFORM_ADMIN_ROLES does NOT (it has `admin` instead)
```

So a `platform_admin` is "platform" to the gateway and an ordinary tenant user to the key policy. For arm 1 that means **unbounded**; more generally it is a role-vocabulary split across seven divergent lists, which is its own problem and not this ticket's to fix.

### What this changes for Kam's decision

The card is about who may reach an irreversible cross-organisation erasure. The answer is not "ADMIN" but "`ADMIN` **and** `platform_admin`**, in either casing**". If Kam rules them bounded, the edit is to `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` (or to `PLATFORM_ROLES`, for `platform_admin`) — still a shared set that governs the revoke route too, so still not a local change and still its own gate.

KS-1533 arm 1's documenting cell therefore pins **both** roles' current behaviour, labelled as undecided policy.

*Added by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12, after running the predicates while building KS-1533 arm 1.*

---

## ⚠ CORRECTION — `platform_admin` is NOT unbounded at the mint. It cannot mint at all. Only `ADMIN` is the open question.

**The addendum above is wrong about** `platform_admin`**, and the retitle that named it was wrong.** Measured on the running security service over real HTTP while writing KS-1533 PR A's cells, and confirmed by running the function:

```
role              decideMint (runs FIRST, as route middleware)
ADMIN / admin     ALLOW via admin   -> reaches decideTenantAccess -> unbounded   (the claim HOLDS)
platform_admin    DENY 403 "API key management requires an admin role"          (the claim was WRONG)
PLATFORM_ADMIN    DENY 403 — same
ISSUER_ADMIN      ALLOW via admin   -> the organisation arm applies
super_admin       ALLOW via admin   -> platform, bypasses by design
```

**What I got wrong, precisely.** I ran `decideTenantAccess` on its own and concluded `platform_admin` falls through to `allow: 'same-tenant'`. That is true *of that function*. But the mint route runs `requireKeyAdminOrProvisioner` → `decideMint` **first**, and `PLATFORM_ADMIN` is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES` (`provisioningPolicy.ts:43-49`), so the request is refused 403 before `decideTenantAccess` is ever called. **Order is invisible to a function call** — the exact point KS-742's route-contract test makes in its header, and that I copied into KS-1533's. The real-HTTP cell is what caught it: I had written it to assert `platform_admin` mints (201), and it read 403 on the unfixed service.

**So, for Kam's decision:** the question is `ADMIN` **only**. `ADMIN` is in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`, passes `decideMint`, reaches `decideTenantAccess`, and — being in neither `PLATFORM_ROLES` nor `ORG_BOUNDED_ROLES` — keeps cross-organisation mint inside its tenant. That half stands and is unchanged.

**What still stands about** `platform_admin`**:** the role-vocabulary split (KS-1536) is real — the gateway treats it as a super-role in six places. But its consequence *at the mint* is the opposite of what I wrote: a gateway super-role is **over**-restricted here (cannot mint keys), not under-restricted. That is an availability quirk, not a security hole, and it belongs on KS-1536, not on Kam's policy card.

The title is reverted to name `ADMIN` alone. KS-1533 PR A pins both facts in cells: `ADMIN` as UNDECIDED POLICY (201 today), `platform_admin` as MEASURED (403, refused by `decideMint`).

*Corrected by Seat V 5th, 2026-10-12. The third time this session I have had to correct a claim of mine in place; this one was on Kam's board, so it matters more than the dedupe counts did.*

title: KS-1232 gate follow-ups: share the allow-list predicate between the info reader and the create path (or pin drift), and decide whether arrays of non-strings are refused by both
description:
## BLUF

The Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1517 (ticket KS-1232) returned **GO**: 0 Major, 3 Minor notes (verdict sha256/16 `622027fcfb23dab5`). Two of them need a decision or a change and are the checklist below; Minor 3 is already ticketed (KS-1532 for the thrown settings read; the MCP relay wording is recorded on KS-1232).

## Recommendation

Do (a) first, since it removes a class; (b) is a contract question for Wednesday or Kam, to be answered for both read routes together.

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a) Stop duplicating the predicate, or pin drift (the gate's Minor 1).** The info reader's guard (`services/api-gateway/src/services/health.ts:77`) is character-identical to the create path's (`routes/verification.ts:1307`): `raw !== undefined && raw !== null && !Array.isArray(raw)`, with the same 403 text. It is **duplicated, not shared**. Drift today is guarded only by the 12-shape AGREEMENT cell in `ks1232-info-reader-refuses-a-non-array-allow-list.test.ts`; the gate's own 30-shape run (`NaN`, `Infinity`, `-0`, array subclasses, a Proxy, an object with a `length`, `new String('')`, `Object.create(Array.prototype)`) found **0 disagreements**. Options: one helper imported by both routes (this edits the create path's allow-list guard, a security surface, so it needs its own gate), or a source-level cell asserting the two guards are the same executable code (a source-text check passes when the guard is commented out, so compare the code, not the text).
- [ ] **(b) Decide whether an array of non-strings is refused, by both read routes together (the gate's Minor 2; a contract question).** Neither route checks array ELEMENTS. The info reader echoes `[1,2]`, `[null]` and `[['a']]` raw (same as before this PR), and the create path accepts the same shape at its guard; reasoned from its code (`allowedTypes.includes(requestedType)`), not run, a non-empty array of non-strings then refuses every create with the "not permitted to register document type" text rather than the list text, so the two routes would answer differently for the same stored value. KS-1230 is where element types are validated on the **write** path; this item is whether the two **reads** should also refuse such an array, and with what text. Out of the ticket's "non-array" wording, so it was not changed in KS-1232.

## Detail

* **Source:** the PR #1517 gate verdict, Minors 1 and 2. The two reasoned claims in (b) are mine and are marked as such.
* **Related:** KS-1232 (the change), KS-1230 (the write-side validation), KS-1204 (the create path's refusal), KS-1532 (the thrown read), KS-1531 (the undocumented route).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `array of non-strings` 0, `element types` 0, `shared predicate` 0, `share the predicate` 0, `non-string` 21 (scanned by title; none is about the allow-list's elements), `KS-1230` 4 (KS-1262, KS-1233, KS-1232, KS-1231; KS-1230 itself read). The same instrument returned KS-1232 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: mcp-server POST /generate-package: a falsy allowedDocumentTypes ("", 0, false) reaches the package generator as [] (all types permitted) with status 200
description:
## BLUF

**The MCP server's** `POST /generate-package` **turns a falsy** `allowedDocumentTypes` **(**`""`**,** `0` **or** `false`**) into** `[]` **before it reaches the package generator, and answers 200.** `[]` is documented as "all types permitted", so a caller who sent a value that is not a list gets back a package that says the connector is unrestricted. This is the second of the two sites that shape `allowedDocumentTypes` found while working KS-1232; it was split out of KS-1232 on Wednesday's ruling because it is a different service, a different surface (a request-body value, not the gateway's answer) and a separate test pass.

## Recommendation

A decision first, then a small build. Decide what the endpoint should do with a present, non-array `allowedDocumentTypes`: refuse (a 400, since the value is the caller's) or pass it on as unusable. The gateway's own answer for the same stored value is a 403 refusal (KS-1232), so the two should not disagree about what a non-list means. Test first against the existing pin, which the change flips.

## Detail

* **Where:** `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:258`, `allowedDocumentTypes: allowedDocumentTypes || [],`, in the handler for `POST /generate-package` (line 222), which reads `allowedDocumentTypes` from the request body (line 226) and requires `apiKey` (400 without it).
* **Reachable through the gateway:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1266` mounts `POST /api/mcp/generate-package` and forwards it to `${MCP_SERVER_URL}/generate-package` (line 1270); KS-1214 records the same.
* **What** `[]` **means:** `MCP Deployment/troubleshooting.md:123`, "An empty `allowedDocumentTypes` list means all types are permitted."
* **Pinned today, as a characterisation (PR #1120):** `services/mcp-server/src/__tests__/ks1232-generate-package-doctypes-default.test.ts`, the cell `RED KS-1232: allowedDocumentTypes "", 0 and false each reach the package generator as [] with status 200`, with a control that a list passes through unchanged. The fix flips that cell.
* **Consequence, reasoned and NOT measured:** the generated package carries the unrestricted-looking list into the agent's configuration. The gateway still enforces the real allow-list on create, so this is misinformation to the agent, not a widening; I did not run a generated package against a gateway.
* **Related:** KS-1232 (the gateway's info reader, the same value), KS-1214 (the same server's `/hash` exposure; it records the `/api/mcp/generate-package` proxy).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `generate-package` 4 (KS-1214, KS-713, KS-104, KS-95; KS-1214 read, the other three are Done and unrelated), `http-server.ts:258` 1 and `allowedDocumentTypes || []` 1 (both KS-1232), `package generator` 0, `generatePackage` 0. The same instrument returned KS-1232 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: platform_document_registry.tenant_id has three declarations that disagree (init schema UUID, gateway CREATE TEXT, main-DB copy TEXT): decide the canonical one (UNDECIDED)
description:
## BLUF

**Nobody has decided what type** `platform_document_registry.tenant_id` **is. There are three declarations of it, and they disagree:** the platform database's init schema says `UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`; the gateway's in-code CREATE for the platform database says `TEXT`; and the MAIN database's copy of the table (created by `CORE_MIGRATIONS`) is also `TEXT`. **This is UNDECIDED.** It is the item left over when KS-1272 was closed: that ticket's defect (the de-dup `DELETE` failing `22P02` on a uuid column on every boot) is fixed by making the statement type-agnostic, and its Recommendation also asked to "decide which declaration is canonical". Nothing is broken today because both spellings now work.

## Recommendation

A decision, not a build. Pick the canonical type for the platform database's table (the init schema's `UUID` with a foreign key is the stricter reading), then decide separately whether the gateway's in-code CREATE should be aligned to it, and whether the main database should hold this table at all or hold it with the same type. Unassigned: a decision-shaped item for Wednesday or Kam.

## Detail

* **Facts at develop** `551dc9808aee` (source lines, not compiled):
  * `docker/init-platform/01-platform-schema.sql:209-213`: `tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id)`, plus `idx_doc_registry_unique` on `(content_hash, tenant_id)` at line 225.
  * `services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`, platform list, lines 1123-1138: `tenant_id TEXT`, then the de-dup `DELETE` at 1135-1137 using `a.tenant_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM b.tenant_id` (the KS-1272 fix, PR #1104), then `uq_pdr_hash_tenant`.
  * Same file, `CORE_MIGRATIONS` (the MAIN database), lines 473-501: `tenant_id TEXT`, de-dup with `COALESCE(a.tenant_id, '') = COALESCE(b.tenant_id, '')`. That form is correct on a TEXT column and would raise `22P02` on a uuid one.
* **Why the declarations coexist:** the init script runs first on a fresh platform database, so the gateway's `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op wherever that script ran. KS-1272 measured the Kintsugi platform database on 2026-09-19 (read-only): `tenant_id` is `uuid`, 0 rows, `uq_pdr_hash_tenant` present.
* **Consequence, reasoned and NOT measured:** a platform database built from the gateway's CREATE alone would be `TEXT` and carry no foreign key to `tenants`, while one built from the init script is `UUID` with the key; a non-UUID tenant id would then be accepted by one and refused by the other. No run was made to confirm it.
* **Related:** KS-1272 (the defect, Done), KS-598 (the registry upsert that keys on `(content_hash, tenant_id)`; the type of `tenant_id` is part of what that ticket's re-keying would have to settle).
* **Dedupe before filing:** literal, case-insensitive matches over title and description, archived included: `canonical declaration` 0; `platform_document_registry` 10 hits, of which KS-1272 and KS-598 were read; KS-590 and KS-33 are unrelated. The same instrument returned KS-1272 for its own title phrase, so it can see ticket text.

title: Decide production VC verification: no DID resolver is wired anywhere, so with NODE_ENV=production /credentials/verify refuses every Ed25519 credential
description:
**BLUF: with** `NODE_ENV=production`**,** `POST /api/credentials/verify` **answers** `verified: false` **for EVERY Ed25519 credential, including a genuine unrevoked one, because nothing in the tree supplies the verifier a** `didResolver`**. The refusal is deliberate in code; a working production verify has never been built. DECISION NEEDED: is production VC verification intentionally off until go-live (then say so, and pin it with a test), or is wiring the resolver work to schedule? The same wiring would close KS-1383.**

## Measured (2026-10-12, develop `c63cec1f6070`)

In-process, on the real `POST /api/credentials/verify` handler and the real shared verifier, with `NODE_ENV` set per call (the verifier reads it at call time). **Not** a booted production app.

| case | `NODE_ENV=development` | `NODE_ENV=production` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| genuine, never revoked | `verified: true` | `verified: false`, `No DID resolver configured; cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production` |
| revoked, as issued | `false`, `Credential has been revoked` | `false`, the same resolver error plus `Credential has been revoked` |
| revoked, id never issued | `false`, `no issuer record` | `false`, the resolver error plus `no issuer record` |
| revoked, another LIVE credential's id | `true` (KS-1383) | `false`, the resolver error only |
| same, with a tampered `credentialSubject` | `true` (KS-1383) | `false`, the resolver error only |

So in production there is no bypass, and also no credential that verifies. Rows: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-4th/evidence/probe.env.txt`.

## From the code (read)

* `packages/shared/src/vc/verifier.ts:409-411`: `// In production, this MUST fail. In dev, allow pass-through.` then `if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') errors.push('No DID resolver configured; cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production')`. In the file since its first commit, `e50dbde98` (2026-02-18).
* `verifier.ts:67` declares `didResolver` in the config; `:385` and `:447` use it. A search of the non-test, non-doc tree finds **no caller that supplies one**: `services/vc-issuer/src/routes/credentials.ts:339-346` passes the revocation resolvers only.
* No test names the production message, and I found no document saying production verification is deliberately off.

## What I can and cannot establish

* **Can:** the refusal is by design (the guard and its comment), and a working production verify path does not exist.
* **Cannot:** whether leaving it unbuilt is an accepted decision for the current phase. That is the decision this ticket asks for.

## NOT measured

A booted production app (vc-issuer will not boot without `DATABASE_URL` and `PRISM_AGENT_URL`); any deployed production environment; the demo VM; `POST /api/presentations/verify` in production mode (it calls the same shared verifier, per the code, but I did not run it); behaviour with a resolver wired.

## Priority, and why P3

It fails closed, so nothing unsafe is accepted; there is no production environment today (Platform K has no public domain yet); and its fix is the same wiring as KS-1383, which is High. It becomes a go-live blocker for any use of the VC verify routes.

## Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included, titles, descriptions and comments, literal)

`No DID resolver configured`: 2 (KS-1375 description, as an aside "pre-existing, read, not driven"; KS-1383 only through my own comment of 2026-10-12). `verifier.ts:410`, `cannot verify Ed25519 proof in production`, `PRISM_AGENT_URL`: 1 each, all KS-1383 via that same comment. `production verif`: 2, both closed review tickets. Positive control `statusListResolver`: 4. Negative control: 0. **No open ticket tracks this as a question.** Related, not duplicates: KS-1383 (the id/proof binding), KS-1375, KS-625 (`/presentations/verify` never checks the holder signature: the opposite failure, a claim of validity with no check).

title: Timestamping: the opentimestamps and blockchain types still report verified true, and /verify accepts a forged proof with no stored row (KS-753 gate m2)
description:
**ACTION (owner: the timestamping build lane, with a policy decision first):** decide what an `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` timestamp may claim when nothing external ever checked it, then make creation and `/api/timestamps/verify` agree with that decision, the way KS-753 and KS-1404 did for `rfc3161`. Options to rule between: (a) report `verified: false` on creation and on verify for these two types until a real attestation check exists; (b) require a stored row and honour its `verified` column on verify (KS-1404's shape for rfc3161); (c) stop advertising the types in `supportedTypes` (`index.ts:185`) until they are real. Tests first, with a planted-red mutation per branch.

**Symptom (gate evidence P7, P8).**

* **P7:** creating an `opentimestamps` or `blockchain` timestamp answers `verified: true` and persists `verified = true`. Both types are placeholders by design (the proof is generated locally, `generateMockOpenTimestampsProof` / blockchain at `index.ts:689` and `:705`).
* **P8:** a **forged** `opentimestamps` JSON proof (the right hash plus one attestation) with **no stored row** returns `verified: true` from `/verify` (`index.ts:616-621`; the `blockchain` case at `:625` is the same shape: hash match plus `chain` and `slot` fields). Nothing checks an attestation against anything.
* KS-1404 closed this same forgery path for `rfc3161` only.

**Why P2.** This is "a mock timestamp reported as verified" by KS-753's own wording, on an evidentiary path (Tier 1). It is **not a regression** from PR #1502 and did not block it; the PR declared these types out of scope.

**Data, handled separately.** Rows of these types already stored as `verified = true` are a data question. A backfill is approval-class (Kam), and the count must come first, read-only per environment, classified by the proof's SHAPE rather than the `(mock)` name (the name missed 1 of 5 mocks in the gate's test). Wednesday is handing the count SQL to the deploy seat.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1502 (KS-753), verdict sha256/16 `5e1fcf87edc4e8a4`, finding m2. Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (12:20Z) that this is filed as P2. PR #1502 head `5daf8830dc46`; line numbers below are at that head.

title: Timestamping: a TSA reply flagged mock must force eidasQualified false, so requireEidas refuses it (KS-753 gate m1)
description:
**ACTION (owner: the timestamping build lane):** in `services/timestamping/src/index.ts`, `createTimestamp` (line 469 at the PR #1502 head), derive `eidasQualified` from the mock flag as well as the token, so a mock reply can never count as qualified:

```ts
eidasQualified = tsaResult.token && tsaResult.mock !== true ? tsaResult.eidasQualified === true : false;
```

Add the cell first and watch it fail: a stubbed TSA reply `{ token, mock: true, eidasQualified: true }` must answer `eidasQualified: false`, and with `requireEidas: true` it must answer **503**. Today it answers 201.

**Symptom (gate evidence P2).** With that input the route answers `201`, `verified: false`, `eidasQualified: true`; with `requireEidas: true` it answers **201 rather than 503**. The mock flag now decides `verified` (the line after, `if (tsaResult.mock === true || !tsaResult.token) verified = false;`) but not `eidasQualified`, so a mock reply could still pass the `requireEidas` gate. The PR's own "flag decides" cell uses exactly this input and asserts only `verified`.

**Not reachable today.** The real fallback hard-codes `eidasQualified: false` (`tsa/qualified-tsa.ts:333`), so the combination cannot occur until the TSA module changes or a second mock source appears. This is defence in depth, one line plus one cell.

Source: the Opus QA gate of PR #1502 (KS-753), verdict sha256/16 `5e1fcf87edc4e8a4`, finding m1. Wednesday ruled on 2026-10-12 (12:20Z) that this is filed as P3. PR #1502 head `5daf8830dc46`; line numbers below are at that head.

title: GET /api/security/keys: the declared 200 body is {keys:[...]} but the handler answers {success,data}; organizationId's uuid format is declared and not enforced (KS-747 residuals)
description:
Filed by Seat V 4th on Wednesday's ruling (L11, 2026-10-12): the two residual findings on `GET /api/security/keys` that KS-747 did NOT cover, as ONE ticket, so KS-747 can close as "declare the parameter".

KS-747's fix (#1318, squash `f28cd1fbc7a5`) declared `organizationId` as a required uuid query parameter. It is on develop, deployed, and confirmed on the SERVED spec of Kintsugi (bytes equal to the yaml at the deployed commit; the parameter reads required, in query, format uuid). These two things remain:

## 1. The declared 200 body is `{keys: [...]}`; the handler answers `{success, data: [...]}`

Read at the deployed commit `65d7722f83a6`: `services/security/src/security.openapi.ts` registers `ApiKeyListResponse = z.object({ keys: z.array(ApiKeySchema) })` for the 200, and `services/security/src/index.ts` `app.get('/api/keys', ...)` ends `res.json({ success: true, data: keys })`. So the two cannot both be right. Peter measured the consequence on all four KS-1353 sweeps (slot 3, head `d9ce1403d`, seed 1353): `response_schema_conformance` **31 of 31** own-test 200s fail with `"keys" is a required property`, and one more inside a stateful chain, 32 calls in all (KS-747, comment of 2026-09-28T12:31Z). KS-908's merge note also records the `keys`-vs-`data` naming as pre-existing drift.

Decision needed: which side is the contract. The house envelope elsewhere is `{success, data}`, which argues for changing the DECLARED schema to match the handler, not the handler (consumers already read `data`). Not decided here.

## 2. `organizationId` is declared `format: uuid`, and nothing enforces it

The handler checks only `if (!organizationId)`; a value that is not a uuid is accepted and simply matches nothing. Peter's sweeps record **5** `negative_data_rejection` failures on this operation, and KS-747's own merge note flagged it as "U-1" (declaration and enforcement are separate) and left it unfiled. Decision needed: enforce the format (400 on a non-uuid) or stop declaring it.

This is one instance of the class **KS-1022** (the id-format contract seam).

## Not established by me

I did not observe either finding LIVE: the one authed GET I was cleared to make was refused 403, because the only QA credential (role OWNER) is not in `KEY_ADMIN_ROLES`. Both are read from source at the deployed commit and from Peter's sweep data.

Related: KS-747, KS-908, KS-1022, KS-1361 (Done; the sweeps' baseline), KS-1015.

title: KS-811 gate findings (#1491): the 403-code scan reads comments, and the global CSRF middleware answers unpublished CSRF_* 403s on the same path
description:
Filed by Seat V 4th as the single P3 follow-up required by Wednesday's head-bound GO on PR #1491 (KS-811 second ask), 2026-10-12T09:55:43Z. Gate verdict `2026-10-12_gate-pr1491/verdict.md`, sha256/16 `2331702dc31cc79e`. 0 Major.

The merged work is sound and stays merged: one new test file, no product file touched, and the gate derived the emitted 403 set (`FORBIDDEN` plus the four enforcement codes) and the published set independently and they matched the author's. This ticket carries the two residuals the gate named.

## Finding 1 (Minor) — the scan reads comments, so commented-out code can red or green a cell

The derivation in `ks811-post-documents-403-code-set-agrees.test.ts` scans source text without
stripping comments. Consequences the gate demonstrated:

* a commented-out `403` on the route turns three cells red, so a purely documentary edit breaks the suite;
* nearby unrelated code can be misattributed to the handler under test.

Closing step: strip comments before deriving the set (or parse rather than text-scan), then re-run the
gate's mutation set to confirm the three cells no longer answer to a comment.

## Finding 2 (Note) — the asserted set holds at handler level only

The global CSRF middleware answers unpublished `CSRF_*` 403s on this path for cookie-only requests.
So "the 403 code set of `POST /api/documents`" is true of the handler, not of the front door: a
cookie-only caller can receive a 403 whose code is not in either set the test compares.

Closing step: decide whether the published set should include the `CSRF_*` codes reachable on this
path, or whether the test's scope sentence should say handler-level explicitly. Either is acceptable;
leaving both unstated is not.

## Known blind spots — already stated in the test file header, recorded here so they are not re-found

Three of the gate's eleven mutations stayed green: the helper, the variable and the `Object.assign`
form. The file header names them. They are not regressions and are not in scope for this ticket

title: Wallet login: a suspended account stored under a mixed-case address can be evaded by logging in with the lower-case form (needs a case-insensitive lookup, a migration)
description:
## BLUF

Residual declared on #1476 (KS-806) and confirmed by its Opus delta gate (round 3), filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. A wallet account whose `wallet_address` was stored before #1476 in a NON-canonical casing and has since been SUSPENDED refuses its own casing (401), but the same wallet logging in with the lower-case form gets a NEW ACTIVE account (200). Suspension can be evaded through the double-account path.

## Recommendation

A separate PR with a migration: replace `auth_find_user_by_wallet` (migration 039, exact equality) with a case-insensitive lookup (or add a functional index on `lower(wallet_address)` and look up on the lower-cased argument), and canonicalise the stored column for existing rows in the same migration. Then the lookup in `routes/wallet.ts` needs no presented-casing-first loop. Until then #1476's raw-casing-first lookup keeps a legacy row reachable by its own casing, which is the part it can fix without a migration.

## Detail

* **Why it exists:** CIP-8 verification compares the claimed and signed address case-insensitively (`utils/cip8.ts`), so one wallet can present several casings, but `auth_find_user_by_wallet` is `WHERE wallet_address = p_wallet_address` (exact). #1476 stores new rows in the canonical lower-case form and looks up the presented casing first, then the canonical form; a legacy row in a casing the wallet does not present is not found by any lookup there.
* **Effect (gate probe D5 and the residual cell):** legacy row `L` (mixed case, SUSPENDED). Login with the mixed-case form: 401 (the suspension holds). Login with the lower-case form: no row found, a new row `N` is created, ACTIVE, 200.
* **Related, declared in #1476:** `/link` stores the raw casing (`routes/wallet.ts`), so one wallet can also become two accounts there; `/status/:walletAddress` is not canonicalised. The same migration fixes the lookup side of both; the write side of `/link` should canonicalise.
* **Not caused by #1476:** before it, every casing was a separate account anyway; #1476 closes the double account for rows it creates and leaves this one for legacy rows.

Provenance: Opus delta gate on #1476 round 3, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476-r3/verdict.md`; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1486 (concurrent first logins), KS-1460.

title: A real-Postgres twin of the KS-1267 transfer-custody cells: the mocked flip ignores its arguments and cannot commit or roll back (PR 1486 gate note)
description:
## BLUF

A real-Postgres twin of the two KS-1267 cells in `ks1228-a-refused-request-writes-no-provenance-row.test.ts` (`/transfer-custody`: the owner flip throws, and the custody INSERT returns no row). Found by the Sonnet-tier gate on PR #1486; left out of that PR because a change to the gated head voids the GO. Not a regression.

## Recommendation

One small tier-2, test-only PR using the faithful local Postgres recipe (`5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md`) and the existing KS-1263 route-level harness, which already drives the real `/transfer-custody` route over a real database (the KS-1310 describe there seeds a document, an owner and a holder and installs a trigger as a fault vehicle). Assert on real rows: after a flip that fails there is no `action_provenance` row for the document, no `custody_events` row and the owner is unchanged; after a flip that succeeds there is one provenance row, one custody row and the owner is the NEW holder.

## Detail

The unit cells use a mocked transaction client whose `$executeRaw` **ignores its arguments** and has **no commit or rollback model**. The gate found two mutants of `routes/documents.ts` that therefore stay GREEN (31/31):

1. **Recording after the flip but before the COMMIT** (inside the transaction): a failed commit would leave a provenance row for a transfer that did not happen, and nothing can see it.
2. **The flip writing the WRONG owner** (its `SET` pointed at `fromHolderId`): the mock never looks at the value.

A twin against a real database closes both, because it reads the rows back. Also: the title of cell 3, "the custody INSERT returns no row: 500, no row, and the owner is never flipped", over-states what it asserts. The mock cannot show the owner, so the cell asserts only the WRITE ORDER (the flip statement is never issued). The PR body and squash body say so; the title is left as merged.

Refs KS-1267, KS-1263, KS-1310.

title: api-gateway: every per-IP limiter keys on the last X-Forwarded-For hop (trust proxy 1), so a caller that reaches the gateway without nginx rotates that hop and gets a fresh bucket each request
description:
## BLUF

`index.ts:108` sets `app.set('trust proxy', 1)`, so every IP-keyed control in the gateway (the global limiter at 300 per minute, the verification limiter, the login limiters, the brute-force guard) keys on the **last** `X-Forwarded-For` hop. The Opus gate on PR #1483 (KS-1479) **reproduced against the gateway directly** that rotating that last hop gets a fresh bucket each time, identically on base and on #1483, so the per-IP bound is only as strong as who can set the last hop. Pre-existing, not caused by KS-1479. **Whether it is reachable in practice depends on whether anything reaches the gateway without nginx appending the hop; that part is unmeasured.**

## What the repo's own configs say (READ, not measured)

* `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx.conf:133`, `nginx-production.conf:296` and `nginx-demo.conf:334` all set `proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for`, which **appends** nginx's `$remote_addr` to whatever the client sent. Through that nginx, the last hop is the address nginx saw (and on demo, `nginx-demo.conf:100-107` resolves it from `X-Forwarded-For` only for trusted source addresses with `real_ip_recursive on`). A client behind it can prepend hops but cannot choose the last one.
* The gate's reproduction sent the header **straight to the gateway**, with no nginx in front. So the exposure is any path that reaches the gateway without that nginx: a published gateway port, another container on the compose network (the comment at `nginx-demo.conf:89` already names this for nginx's own rate limit), or an ingress that passes the header through.
* The related finding on how the IP is derived at all is **KS-618** (archived, Backlog, P2): on demo every IP-keyed control saw the Docker bridge address because two proxy hops met `trust proxy 1`; its recommended fix (an explicit trusted-subnet list rather than a hop count) is also the fix shape here. Its nginx realip half appears to be in `nginx-demo.conf` now; whether it is deployed on demo and Kintsugi is not known to me.

## Recommendation

1. **Measure first, read-only, after the Kintsugi window:** through the real public front door, send several `GET /api/credentials/abc` (answered 401 by the gateway's own gate, after the global limiter) with different client-supplied `X-Forwarded-For` first hops and read the `RateLimit-Remaining` header each time. If it keeps decrementing across them they share one bucket (the edge fixes the hop); if it resets, the hop is client-controlled at the real ingress. This needs no credential and writes nothing but limiter counters. Also check the compose files and VM firewalls for any published gateway port.
2. **If any path reaches the gateway without nginx:** replace the hop count with an explicit trusted-proxy list (KS-618's recommendation), so `X-Forwarded-For` is honoured only from the nginx peer.
3. Add a cell that sends a forged last hop to the real app with `trust proxy` configured as intended. Priority P2 as Wednesday ruled; it may drop to P3 if step 1 shows the edge appends the hop.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1483, 2026-10-12, note N3 and its XFF probe (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1483/verdict.md`, `evidence/`): "the key is the last hop; rotating the last hop bypasses the limit, as on develop; rotating the first hop with the last fixed does not". Edge configuration was not checked by the gate.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `X-Forwarded-For`, `trust proxy`, `last hop`, `XFF`, `x-real-ip`, `set_real_ip_from`, `spoof`: nearest is KS-618 (above); nothing covers a client-chosen last hop.

Related: KS-618, KS-1479, KS-946, KS-1469.

title: Wallet login: two simultaneous first logins for one address issue a token for an id that is not in the database (4 of 5 rounds)
description:
## BLUF

Pre-existing on develop, found by the Opus gate on #1476 (KS-806) and filed at the priority Wednesday asked for. Two concurrent FIRST wallet logins for the same address both succeed with 200, only one row is created, and in 4 of 5 measured rounds one of the two responses carries an access token for a user id that does **not exist** in `users`. `userRepo.createUser` returns the object it was given, not the row `ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE` actually stored, and `getOrCreateWalletUser` trusts it.

## Recommendation

Make the wallet create path read back the stored row (or `RETURNING` it) and use THAT id, or fail and retry the lookup when the returned row's `wallet_address` does not match. Add a concurrency cell against a real Postgres (Seat J's native recipe). This is the same "fabricated object, not in the table" class KS-806 names; #1476 removes the collision between different wallets but not this race between two requests of the same wallet.

## Detail

* **Measured** (gate probe P4, real Postgres 15 built from the repo's init SQL + 49 migrations, app role `secuura_app` under RLS, the real route, real `/register`, real `userRepo`, real 039 lookup): 5 rounds of `Promise.all([login(A), login(A)])` for a fresh address A. Every round: both statuses 200, exactly 1 row. `idsInDb` per round: `[true,true]` (same id) once, then `[false,true]`, `[true,false]`, `[true,false]`, ... so in 4 of 5 rounds one returned id is not in the table. The token for that id then works until something looks the user up.
* **Where:** `services/auth/src/routes/wallet.ts` `getOrCreateWalletUser` (lookup, then `userRepo.createUser(user)` with a fresh `uuidv4()`), and `userRepo.createUser`'s upsert on `email_lookup_hash` returning its input.
* **Not caused by #1476:** the same shape exists on develop; with the old 8-character email the collision made it worse (every second wallet), with the new email it only happens for a true double submit of one address.
* Evidence: `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/logs/probe_head.out` (line 4) and `gateprobe1476.test.ts` (cell P4).

Provenance: Opus QA gate on #1476, verdict `/Volumes/DevMASTER/WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1476/verdict.md` (sha256/16 `b4615b4a35be26fb`), Minor-4; filed by Seat V 3rd on Wednesday's instruction. Related: KS-806, KS-1460 (`updateUser` callers that discard the result), KS-1052.

title: pre-push gate: pushing a branch that is not checked out skips the preflight, because the hook diffs HEAD and not the pushed commits
description:
**BLUF.** `.githooks/pre-push` decides whether to run the preflight from `HEAD` (`git diff --name-only "@{upstream}" HEAD` at `:80`, `"$_b" HEAD` at `:184`), and the preflight then tests the working tree. The refs git hands the hook on stdin are read only for the force-push check (`:48-69`). So `git push origin some-other-branch`, with a clean `HEAD` on another branch, skips the preflight for a `Blockchain/Dev` change in the branch actually pushed. The push lands with no `[pre-push]` output. Pre-existing; identical in the tip's hook, `302d8d081` and the KS-884 fix. Found by the KS-884 ref matrix (scenario S15).

**Recommendation.** Make the hook judge what is pushed, not what is checked out. Read the stdin lines (`<local ref> <local sha> <remote ref> <remote sha>`) and:

1. Compute the changed set per pushed ref from `<local sha>` against its base, not from `HEAD`.
2. Because the preflight tests the working tree (HEAD), also FAIL CLOSED: when a pushed `<local sha>` is not `HEAD` and it changes `Blockchain/Dev`, refuse with a clear message ("check out what you push, or push with the bypass deliberately"), rather than run the wrong tree. Running the preflight in a temporary worktree of the pushed sha is the heavier alternative.
3. Handle the shapes the stdin loop already skips: branch deletes (`<local sha>` all zeros), brand-new remote branches, tags (`refs/tags/...`), and multi-ref pushes (`--all`, several refspecs).
   Add a test cell per shape (red against today's hook for the unchecked-out branch). Not built here; this is the larger of the two KS-884 follow-ups because it changes what the hook refuses.

**Detail.**

* Measured 2026-10-12 by Seat F 17th. Scenario S15: `b-other` carries a `Blockchain/Dev` change, `HEAD` is back on a clean branch at `origin/develop`, then `git push origin b-other` to a local bare remote. Result SKIP for the tip's hook, `302d8d081`'s hook and the KS-884 fix; the saved push output is only git's two `To ...` / `* [new branch]` lines, so nothing tells the pusher the gate did not run.
* Why it is more than a corner case: `git push origin <name>` from a different checkout is an ordinary shape (a seat pushes a sibling branch, or a script pushes a ref), and the result reads like a green push.
* Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatF-17th/ks884_ref_matrix.sh` (S15) and `ks884_matrix_full_OLD.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_CURRENT_302d8d0.txt`, `ks884_matrix_full_FIXED.txt`.
* Related: KS-884 (PR #1474). Not caused or changed by it.

title: api-gateway: dot-segment and extra-segment spellings (/abc/., /./abc, /abc/%2e ...) are forwarded verbatim without the spec method and auth gate; whether any reaches an upstream handler is unmeasured
description:
## BLUF

A request whose path differs from a spec path by a **dot segment or a percent-encoded dot/space/slash segment** is not matched by the gateway's spec method and auth gate, so the gate has no opinion and the request is **forwarded to the upstream verbatim**. The Opus gate on PR #1472 (KS-1469) measured this on base and on the merged tree; **I reproduced it independently on the merged develop tip** `d38302a9a27e` (the real app over real HTTP, a recording stub for every upstream, `NODE_ENV=test`). Unchanged by KS-1469.

| unauthenticated `GET` | gateway | upstream saw |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/api/credentials/abc` (canonical) | **401** | nothing |
| `/api/credentials/abc/` (KS-1469 fixed this one) | **401** | nothing |
| `/api/credentials/abc/.` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/.` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/./` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/./` |
| `/api/credentials/./abc` | **200** | `/api/credentials/./abc` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/..` | **200** | `/api/credentials/abc/..` |
| `/api/credentials/abc/%2e`, `/%20`, `/%2F` | **200** | the same raw path |
| `/api/./credentials/abc`, `/api/zzz-not-in-spec/.` (controls) | **404** | nothing |

**What this does and does not show.** It shows the gateway's gate is skipped and the raw path is forwarded (the stub answers 200). It does **not** show an exposure: whether a real upstream router (Express in vc-issuer, originate, ...) ever routes `/abc/.` or `/./abc` to a handler is **not measured**. By reading, Express does not collapse dot segments, so most of these should 404 at the upstream; the per-route `authenticateToken` and the upstream's own auth are the layers behind the gate. So this is a skipped defence-in-depth layer with an unmeasured tail, not a demonstrated bypass.

## Recommendation

Two steps, the first before the second:

1. **Measure** (read-only, in process): for each service router behind a `bearerAuth` spec op, send these spellings to the real router and record whether any reaches the handler. If none does, close this as defence-in-depth.
2. **If any does, or to close the class:** do not widen the spec regexes. Add a front-door normaliser in the family of KS-858's `normaliseRepeatedSlashes` that answers `400` (or rewrites) any path containing a dot segment, raw or percent-encoded, so the gate and the router can never see different paths. Tests first, a cell per spelling above, the canonical and the not-in-spec controls kept. Priority P3.

## Detail

* Source: the Opus gate on PR #1472, "Not changed, and not checked" (`WEDNESDAY/0_Brain/reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1472/verdict.md`; rows 12 to 22 of `evidence/probe_head.out`), plus my independent run above.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `dot-segment`, `dot segment`, `normaliseRepeatedSlashes`, `path spelling`, `%2e`: nearest are KS-858 (the repeated-slash class, fixed) and KS-983 (no systemTest suite drives a path-spelling variant), neither covers dot segments.

Related: KS-1469, KS-1461, KS-858, KS-983.

title: updateDocument atomicity follow-ups: two blob writers still decide from a prior read, plus a type guard and test nits (KS-1124 gate)
description:
## BLUF

PR #1471 (KS-1124 option A) made every blob write that goes through `updateDocument` atomic. Its Opus gate (GO WITH NOTE, head `4a822bd8c244`, no Major) and Wednesday's GO list what it does not cover. Filed as ONE ticket so none is rediscovered. **None is a regression and none blocks #1471.**

## Recommendation

Fix the first two together in one tier-1 PR (they are the same defect class #1471 closed, in the two places it did not reach), test first with a forced interleaving on a real Postgres as K1-K10 do (recipe: `5_Project_History/2026-10-12_seatJ-2nd/RECIPE-faithful-local-postgres.md`). Take the guard and the nits with it or as a small tier-2 PR after.

## Detail

1. `anchorStateSync.ts:178-212`**,** `markDocumentAnchorFailed` decides from a read taken before the `UPDATE`: the `confirmed` guard (`:180`) and the `txHash` / `blockHeight` / `network` / `anchoredAt` carry (`:190-196`). A confirm write landing between the read and the write can be downgraded to `anchor_failed` with its `txHash` erased. Same family as KS-1004. (Line numbers at the PR head.)
2. `routes/certifications.ts:563` replaces `certification_metadata` wholesale, outside `updateDocument`. It drops `threadToken` from the authoritative blob, and the KS-550 heal then copies that loss into `metadata`.
3. **Hardening,** `documentRepo.ts:632/640/661/669`**.** The replace branch has no `jsonb_typeof(supplied) = 'object'` guard. A future `blockchain: null` would store `[{…}, null]` (`'{}'::jsonb || 'null'::jsonb` gives `[{}, null]`), where the old code stored `null`. No current caller can reach it (`verification.ts:393` guards `!healed`).
4. **Test nits in** `ks1124-blockchain-blob-writes-are-atomic.integration.test.ts`**.** (a) K9 (`:218-224`) seeds `anchored`, which `mapDbStatus` round-trips, so it cannot detect a status write-back; seeding `deleted` or `certified` would pin the "status not supplied keeps the stored status" semantics (only K1 reds on that mutant today). (b) `waiting()` (`:93`) counts lock waits cluster-wide, with no `datname` or `pid` filter; on a shared server a parallel job could satisfy it and make a forced interleaving vacuous. (c) `documentRepo.ts:697-702`: the returned record carries `threadToken` and the status from the first read; presentation only.
5. **Pre-existing, outside KS-1124's scope, and the largest.** Every `updateDocument` rewrites `certification_metadata` to `{ signatures, blockchain }`, which erases `issuerName`, `certificationId` and `certifiedAt` written by `certifications.ts:563` and the admin backfill. `signatures` and `data` also remain read-then-write: a concurrent sign and anchor write can drop a signature. Consider splitting this into its own ticket when it is picked up.
6. **Left in place on purpose:** the pollers' `carriedForward` (`anchorStateSync.ts:111-113`) is now redundant with the SQL carry; it was kept to keep #1471 off `anchorStateSync`. It can go with item 1.

Refs KS-1124, KS-1074, KS-1004, KS-550.

title: No gate executes the DB-backed integration suites: the default test run ignores them and CI is retired
description:

title: The developer portal page documents POST /api/verification/verify-batch, which no service and no spec implements (CSRF carries exclusions for it)
description:
## BLUF

`services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html:294` lists `POST /api/verification/verify-batch` ("Verify mul\[tiple documents\]") as a public endpoint. **Nothing serves it.** The OpenAPI spec (310 paths) declares `verify` and `verify-file` for the unversioned and v2 families but no `verify-batch`; no router in `services/originate` or any other service registers `/verify-batch` under verification (the only `verify-batch` code is the separate MCP server's own root-level `/verify-batch` in `services/mcp-server`). So a developer who follows the portal gets a 404, and `csrf.ts` carries CSRF exclusions for `/api/verification/verify-batch` and `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` that cover a route nothing implements.

## Recommendation

Owner decision, then one of: (a) implement the route and add it to the spec, so the page and the exclusions are true; (b) remove the row from the portal, and drop both CSRF entries in the same change (a dead exclusion is a latent hole: a future route at that name would be silently CSRF-exempt). Priority Low. Until then the two CSRF entries are PINNED by cells (KS-1469) so they cannot vanish or change unnoticed; that pin is deliberately not a statement that the route exists.

## Detail

* Found while resolving the m1 note from the Opus gate on PR #1466 (the `/api/v2/verification/verify-batch` exclusion was pinned by no cell). Evidence, from a repo-wide search at develop `b4a245fba1ca`: spec path scan (310 paths, none `verify-batch`); `git grep` for verify-batch in non-test code finds only the portal row, the two `csrf.ts` entries, and the MCP server; a control with the same grep shape finds the real `/verify` and `/verify-file` routes.
* Other rows on that page were NOT checked against the code.
* **Searched first** (Linear, includeArchived, literal title and description): `developer-portal`, `developer portal`, `verify-batch`: no ticket about this page's rows.

Related: KS-1469, KS-1461, KS-1165.

title: api-gateway: an untyped create never meets the catalogue's DOCUMENT rules (enforcement.ts:101), plus two KS-1203 follow-ups (PR #1465 gate notes)
description:
## BLUF

Three notes from the Opus QA gate on PR #1465 (KS-1203 option A, merged as `a2f575a642638d64493997d0f68747a1d1f03dc6`), left out of that PR on purpose because a change to the gated head would have voided the GO. **Note 1 matters most:** an untyped `POST /api/documents` never meets the type catalogue's `DOCUMENT` rules, so the type's own requirements are skipped for exactly the body KS-1203 is about. It is pre-existing and outside the ruled scope. The gate graded it Minor; I filed it at Medium because it is an authorization-shaped gap.

## Recommendation

One small tier-1 PR, test first:

1. **Resolve an untyped body to the default type in** `enforceDocumentTypeRules`**, not just in the connector allow-list.** `services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts:101` still resolves a body with no type to `''`, so the function returns `docType: {}` and enforces nothing. The catalogue's `DOCUMENT` entry (seeded at `routes/admin.ts:316-336`, described as "the default when a creation request names no documentType") is never applied to an untyped create: `isActive`, `creatorVerificationLevel`, `requireMFA`, `metadataSchema` and `requiresApproval` are all skipped. Use the shared `DEFAULT_DOCUMENT_TYPE` there. **Measure first** (read-only): what the stored `DOCUMENT` entry requires on each environment, because enforcing it on untyped creates can newly refuse callers who rely on the gap, the same lockout risk KS-1190 names.
2. **Behavioural cells for the two sites that are only source-pinned.** `originate/src/routes/documents.ts:584` and the gateway workflow gate (`enforcement.ts:264`) are covered only by a regex over the source text; the gate's three mutations turned only that cell red. Add a cell asserting that originate stores `DOCUMENT` for each of the eight untyped shapes. Note that after item 1 the workflow-gate site becomes reachable for an untyped body, and can finally be tested behaviourally.
3. **Tell operators about the new 403.** `MCP Deployment/troubleshooting.md:119-123` does not say that an untyped create from a restricted connector is checked as `DOCUMENT`. A connector operator who hits the new 403 has no hint.

## Detail

* **Source:** Opus gate on PR #1465, verdict `GO WITH NOTE`, no Major. Verdict file sha256/16 `8d8a2c2d745d81c5` (Wednesday's `reference/2026-10-12_gate-pr1465/verdict.md`).
* **What PR #1465 did and did not claim:** it made the allow-list apply to the resolved default type. It did not claim the catalogue rules apply, and its comment "the check and the stored type cannot drift apart again" is true for the allow-list only.
* **Related:** KS-1203 (the parent; stays In Progress until deployed), KS-1190 (a different gap in the same enforcement code: an unknown required level fails open).

title: packages/shared: one test imports services/demo-service and needs cors, so the suite cannot pass on a member-only install
description:
**BLUF:** one test file in `packages/shared` needs another workspace member's dependency, so the package's suite cannot pass on an install that provides only `packages/shared`'s own closure. It passes on a full `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`, where `cors` is hoisted from `services/*`.

**Measured** (2026-10-12, Seat F 17th; clean-room copy of develop `a31b77577` with no `node_modules`; node v24.7.0):

* `npm ci` run inside `packages/shared` is an implicit-workspace install from the root lock (npm's prefix there is `Blockchain/Dev`). A stock one has no vitest at all, so to see this I made vitest resolvable in that install (a variant lock carrying the KS-1317 vitest declaration). Then `npm test`: `Test Files  1 failed | 48 passed (49)`, `Tests  945 passed | 4 skipped (949)`.
* The one failing file is `src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts`: `Error: Cannot find package 'cors' imported from .../services/demo-service/src/app.ts` (`app.ts:14`), thrown from the file's `KS-832 ACCEPTANCE BAR` suite, whose 4 tests are then skipped.
* Control, same develop on a full `npm ci` at `Blockchain/Dev`: `node_modules/cors` present, `Test Files 48 passed (48)`, `Tests 945 passed (945)`, `tsc --noEmit -p packages/shared` rc 0. In the member-only install `node_modules/cors` is absent.
* `cors` is declared by 21 of the `services/*/package.json` files (`demo-service` among them) and not by `packages/shared`, so nothing in `packages/shared/package.json` tells a reader the suite depends on it.

**Why it matters:** the dependency is invisible and works only through hoisting, so the failure appears only when someone runs the package's tests without the full install. It is lower urgency than it looks: since the KS-1317 guard, a member-only `npm test` stops early with a message naming the full install, so this is reached only when someone supplies vitest another way.

**Suggested shapes (not prescribed):**

* Move the test to where its dependency is declared (`services/demo-service`), or to a root-level guard suite that is only run after a full install.
* Do not declare `cors` in `packages/shared`: the 25 service Dockerfiles (of the 29 that reference `packages/shared`; the other four are frontends) copy `/shared` (with its `node_modules`) from the `shared-builder` stage into the runtime image, so any new dependency there ships in every image. That is the cost that made the Spark's vitest declaration for KS-1317 the wrong shape.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/__tests__/ks781-p3-3-body-parser-order.test.ts` (the boot of the demo-service app, around line 5601), `Blockchain/Dev/services/demo-service/src/app.ts` line 14.

Found while raising KS-1317. Filed unassigned in Backlog on Wednesday's instruction, 2026-10-12.

title: Renovate cannot bump base-image-watch.sh EXCLUDED_BASES — Blockchain/Dev/** is in ignorePaths (split from KS-1367; needs Kamil's agreement)
description:
## BLUF

Split from [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not) at Peter's request (2026-10-07). [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not)'s branch (`feature/ks-1445-…`, shared with [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is)) makes Renovate see `systemTest/performance/config/observability.yml` `k6Image`. The remaining part needs a change to the repo's `ignorePaths`, which sits in Kamil's work-stream E ([KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490/review-e-deployment-containers-and-cicd-supply-chain)). **This ticket waits on Kamil's agreement.** He has not commented on [KS-1367](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1367/renovates-k6-rule-sees-only-the-dockerfile-from-not), so there is nothing of his to quote yet.

## Re-verified from source (2026-10-07, worktree at `origin/develop` 652cf5f6e)

* `renovate.json:4` has `"ignorePaths": ["Blockchain/Dev/**"]`. Renovate skips every manager, including a `customManagers` regex, under that path.
* `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` `EXCLUDED_BASES` names `grafana/k6:2.3.0` and every `observability/docker-compose.yml` image tag.
* Two tests fail when that list disagrees with the files Renovate does bump:
  * `systemTest/performance/tests/unit/config/k6ImagePinParity.test.ts` (k6)
  * `observability/test/compose-image-pins.test.mjs` (observability, added in [KS-1445](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1445/pin-systemtest-k6-to-the-latest-release-or-later-the-macs-native-k6-is))
* So a Renovate PR is red until a person edits the list by hand. That is safe, because nothing slips through, but it is noise.
* Renovate app: `gh pr list --state all --author app/renovate` returns no PR ever. That is consistent with the app not being installed. The installation itself could not be read with the available token.

## Options for Kamil

1. Narrow `ignorePaths` so `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/base-image-watch.sh` is visible, and add a regex `customManagers` entry for its quoted `"image:tag"` lines, grouped with `k6 runtime` and `observability stack images`.
2. Leave it as a hand edit. The red parity tests are the prompt, and that is documented in `systemTest/performance/docs/quick-start.md`.

## Done when

- [ ] Kamil has chosen 1 or 2. Quote his reply verbatim here.
- [ ] If 1: the config passes `renovate-config-validator --strict`, and a dry run shows one grouped update covering all three k6 sites.

title: start-secuura.sh --rebuild leaves ~30 untagged images per slot per rebuild (and interrupted rebuilds pin them)
description:
Raised from platform-s ([PS-1012](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox>)) rather than fixed from there, because `Start_Up/start-secuura.sh` is platform-k's.

## What happens

`docker compose` names each built image `<compose project>-<service>`: `platform-k-*` for slot 1, `secuura_slot2-*` for slot 2, and so on. `start-secuura.sh --rebuild` builds every service again (the serial per-service `docker compose build` from [KS-345](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-345/start-secuurash-rebuild-hangs-on-the-full-33-service-compose-bake)). Each rebuild moves those tags to new images, and the previous image of each service is left untagged as `<none>`. That's about 30 images per slot per rebuild, some of them 0.6–2.2 GB. Nothing in the script prunes images or the build cache. A grep of `start-secuura.sh` for `prune`, `rmi` and `image rm` finds nothing.

**The worse case is an interrupted rebuild.** On 2026-10-02 the Pro had 29 `<none>` images, every one held by a container in K slot 1's project (`platform-k`) that was `Created` **but never started**: `secuura-auth`, `secuura-api-gateway`, `secuura-originate` and others. Docker won't prune an image a container uses, so those stayed until someone removed them by hand (Stuart did).

## Measured (MacBook Pro, Docker Desktop, 2026-10-07)

* `docker system df`: images 20.7 GB, of which 1.76 GB is reclaimable. The **build cache is 39.6 GB, of which 22.65 GB is reclaimable**, mostly entries last used in the previous two days by slot rebuilds.

## Suggested fix (for Kamil's judgement)

The platform-s side is doing this in [PS-1012](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1012/dep-ssd-local-systemtest-make-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox) / [Secuura/platform-s#909](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1012-stack-slots-safe-across-two-dropbox-synced-machines-994c737d0439):

* **Label every build with its owner:** for compose, a `labels:` entry under each service's `build:` such as `com.secuura.slot-image=<project>-<service>`, or one label per project.
* **Before rebuilding,** run `docker image prune -f --filter label=…` scoped to this compose project. Without `-a`, this removes only dangling, unused images from earlier builds of this slot. It never touches another slot, platform-s, a tagged image, or an image a container still uses.
* **After an interrupted rebuild,** remove that slot's `Created`-but-never-started containers, so they stop pinning old images.
* **Don't prune the build cache automatically.** It's shared by every slot on both platforms, so pruning it makes everyone's next build cold. Documenting a manual `docker builder prune --filter until=168h -f` is enough.

title: Akto full scan reports three LOW HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES results (wallet-status ×2, GET /api/settings/notifications) that no ticket or allowlist covers — classify them: by-design or a finding
description:
## BLUF

The one `test:security` run on 2026-10-07 reported three **LOW** results from `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES` on two public routes. No ticket covers them and no allowlist mechanism can express them. They are probably expected for public routes that ignore request headers, but that is **not established**, and today they fail the Full OWASP workflow on their own because the gate fails on any severity, LOW included.

## Measured (slot 1, Mac, Akto 2.37.1, 2026-10-07, run `security`, full OWASP summary `6ac60a95a141e9203079d8bf`, 50,450 result docs)

| Result |  |
| -- | -- |
| Template | `HEADER_ALL_KEYS_INVALID_VALUES`, category INPUT, severity LOW, CWE-20, nature INTRUSIVE |
| Docs for the template | 350; **90 executed** (a captured exchange); **3 flagged** (raw `vulnerable: true`); 347 not |
| Flagged 1 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/dt-seed-7` |
| Flagged 2 | `GET /api/auth/wallet/status/STRING` (the `{walletAddress}` placeholder) |
| Flagged 3 | `GET /api/settings/notifications` |

**What the template does** (read from the library file): it selects a 2xx, non-error response, replaces **every request header value** with invalid values, and flags the result when an attempt still returns 2xx with a body more than 90% identical to the original and the same schema.

**What the data shows.** Each flagged result has 4 attempts. Attempts 0–2 returned **400** (102-character body, 0% match). **Attempt 3 returned 200** (50 characters for wallet-status, 83 for settings/notifications) with a **100% match** — that attempt is what tripped the template. The altered request carried 3 headers for wallet-status (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`, `authorization`) and 2 for settings/notifications (`host`, `x-akto-ignore`). Which values attempt 3 used was **not examined**.

## Why this needs a ticket

* The two routes are already known to be public: `wallet/status` is public by necessity and cannot be allowlisted ([KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous); Kamil, PR #802, quoted in `endpointFalsePositives.ts`: "the registry has no representation for a parameterised route"), and `GET /api/settings/notifications` keeps optional auth by ruling ([KS-719](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-719/security-put-apiprivacysettings-and-apisettingsnotifications-accept), quoted in the same file from `routes/admin.ts`: "The GET above keeps optional auth so anonymous readers still get the documented defaults").
* No existing allowlist mechanism fits. `KNOWN_FALSE_POSITIVE_ENDPOINT_TESTS` admits two ruled kinds with compile-time bounds (`public-by-design` only for `REMOVE_TOKENS`; `similarity-undiscriminating` only for three templates — Kamil's [KS-708](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-708/security-akto-add-user-id-bola-high-on-get-apiplatformaudit-log) bound), and a LOW from an INPUT template is neither. The wallet-status URL also carries a path parameter the registry cannot express.
* The gate (`assertNoVulnerabilities`) fails on any severity. So even after [KS-1009](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1009/security-get-apiauthwalletstatus-returns-userid-role-to-any-anonymous)'s HIGH is fixed, any of these LOWs that recurs will keep the Full OWASP workflow red.

## Not established

* **Whether it is a real input-validation gap (CWE-20) or expected** for routes that never read the headers being altered. For `settings/notifications` the altered headers do not include `authorization`, so "it ignores a bad token" does not explain it.
* **Why it was not reported before.** The 2026-10-05 full runs on slots 2 and 4 listed only the nginx LOW ([KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)). This stack's collection also carried authenticated samples for these URLs (a `feed-har` added them, 343 → 349 endpoints). Not shown to be the cause.
* Related, not claimed: [KS-1207](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1207/security-an-unknown-sk-key-on-an-optional-auth-mount-skips-the) (In Progress, Kamil) covers an unknown key on an optional-auth mount skipping the Bearer check.

## Proposed next steps (smallest first)

1. Re-run **only** this template on those three URLs with a targeted Akto `CUSTOM` run (`apiInfoKeyList`; the technique used for [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low)) and read attempt 3's actual request: which headers, which values.
2. Classify each: by design, or a finding. Kamil's call for the platform side.
3. If by design: accept it by a **narrow** rule with the ruling quoted verbatim (the [KS-1421](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1421/akto-security-tier-fails-every-run-on-the-accepted-server-nginx-low) pattern), and a control showing another endpoint or template still fails. Extending the allowlist's compile-time bound needs Kamil's ruling first. If a finding: a platform ticket for Kamil.

## Done means

1. Each of the three results has a recorded classification, with the attempt-3 evidence.
2. If by design: the Full OWASP workflow no longer fails on them, a control still fails, and Console = Akto = HTML agree on the known-FP and vulnerable counts.
3. If a finding: it is ticketed for the owner and the test keeps failing honestly.

Found while verifying [KS-1440](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1440/akto-image-23610-2371-release-v2371-2026-10-06-both-local-tags) (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1411](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1440-akto-23610-2371-with-the-ks-1416-ks-1421-and-ks-724-fixes-it-5f3e7f62426b), merged; history entry PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1412](https://linear.app/secuura/review/docs-project-history-for-the-2026-10-07-akto-2371-batch-one-pr-merged-06305b942330)). Nothing was changed for this finding.

title: Connector keys are minted `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke`, but neither scope is enforced anywhere — anchor reads are scope-ungated and revoke has no scope check
description:
## Summary

`register-connector` mints Platform S connector keys with nine scopes, including `anchors:read` and `documents:revoke`. Neither scope is checked anywhere in the request path. So a connector key's anchor reads are not scope-gated at all: a key minted WITHOUT `anchors:read` would still read anchors. And `documents:revoke` has no effect: the revoke route checks ownership only. That breaks the deny-by-default rule ([KS-539](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-539/k-define-governing-rules-for-document-operations-by-agents) R2: scopes are the authority) for these two scopes. This is a code read; nothing has been probed live yet.

+++ Evidence (read at source, `develop` `f556373b9`, 2026-10-06)

**Minted:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:485-489` (`S_CONNECTOR_SCOPES`) includes both `'documents:revoke'` (:486) and `'anchors:read'` (:487). Vocabulary: `packages/shared/src/security/scopes.ts:42` and `:76`.

`anchors:read` **— enforced nowhere:**

* `api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` gates only the two anchor WRITES: `POST /api/anchors` and `POST /api/anchors/batch` carry `attachScopes, requireScope('anchors:write')` (:852-863).
* The catch-all `router.use('/api/anchors', authenticateToken(true), proxy('anchoring', …))` (:865-868) has no `requireScope`, so every anchor read reaches anchoring with authentication only.
* A search of `services/*/src` and `packages/shared/src` (tests excluded) finds `anchors:read` only in the minting list and the vocabulary — no check in anchoring either.

`documents:revoke` **— enforced nowhere:**

* The other document verbs check their scope through `isAllowedByRoleOrScope(...)`: create and version `documents:write` (`documents.ts:372`, `:1983`), transfer `documents:transfer-custody` (`:1599`), share `documents:share` (`:2172`).
* The revoke route (`documents.ts:2344` onward) has no scope check. It gates on `document.owner?.id !== user.id` → 403. A connector principal is never the owner, so connectors cannot revoke at all. Your own [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) finding, 2026-08-26, verbatim: *"A connector principal cannot revoke at all"*.

### Not verified

* No live probe yet with a connector key minted without `anchors:read`. Whether anchoring further limits reads per tenant was not checked.
* Severity therefore not asserted beyond "the scope is not checked".

### Related, deliberately not duplicated

* Whether connectors should be able to revoke at all is the open question you put to Stuart on [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) (2026-08-26, Kam's ruling "ask Stuart to reconcile [PS-616](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-616/s-shipped-ps-569-ahead-of-ks-566-so-lifecycle-event-and-flat-anchor) first"). This ticket does not reopen that. It only records that the minted scope is dead either way: if the answer is "no", stop minting it; if "yes", the route needs the scope check plus an owner-gate change.
* Duplicate check, Platform K + Platform S, 2026-10-06: no ticket names either scope's enforcement. [KS-71](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-71/q6-scope-aware-rbac-in-originate-sk-connector-role-can-post) (Done) built scope-aware RBAC for create. [KS-858](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-858/security-class-a-scope-gate-mounted-as-an-exact-route-above-a-catch) (Deployed) is a different class: scope-gate bypass by path spelling.

### Suggested direction (your call)

1. Gate anchor reads with `requireScope('anchors:read')` for key callers (as `/api/documents` does with `documents:read`), or stop minting the scope.
2. Resolve `documents:revoke` per the [KS-566](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-566/ks-539-g-1-split-alignment-add-onbehalfof-to-revoke-drop-it-from) answer.

title: systemTest: pin originate's unhandledRejection posture (split from KS-572) — waits on KS-1427's ruling
description:
## Summary

Split from [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) on 2026-10-06. [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) pins what [KS-546](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-546/unhandledrejection-posture-api-gateway-survives-logalert-everything) actually shipped:

* `UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive` on the api-gateway only, in compose and bicep;
* the real [KS-529](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-529/gateway-intermittent-502-bad-gateway-to-healthy-upstreams-under-sweep) guard, no longer a copy;
* the live malformed-body run with `RestartCount` unchanged;
* the gateway's boot line `unhandledRejection mode: survive`.

What [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture) **can't** pin yet is originate. `services/originate/src/index.ts:72-77` registers its own listener that logs and doesn't exit, so originate survives rejections, yet the gateway comment cites it as fail-fast. [KS-1427](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1427/unhandledrejection-posture-as-shipped-differs-from-ks-546s) asks Kamil which is intended.

## Waiting on

[KS-1427](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1427/unhandledrejection-posture-as-shipped-differs-from-ks-546s) (Kamil, Backlog): survive or fail-fast for originate, and whether `setupGracefulShutdown` gets callers.

## Test (once ruled)

* **If survive:** assert originate declares it in config (`UNHANDLED_REJECTION_MODE=survive`). Extend [KS-572](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-572/systemtest-schemathesis-pin-the-ks-546-unhandledrejection-posture)'s "no other service declares survive" config assertion to an explicit allow-list of gateway + originate.
* **If fail-fast:** a live leg triggers an unhandled rejection in originate (only if a black-box trigger exists; otherwise a container-level check of the boot-logged mode) and asserts the process exits and restarts with the trace logged.
* **If** `setupGracefulShutdown` **gets callers:** sample one non-gateway service's boot log for `unhandledRejection mode: exit`.
* Red against the current shape, green after. Appears on all three surfaces (console, Schemathesis results, HTML report).
