It also has no net underneath: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/` holds 12 shell suites and **none tests this gate's parser** — the sole reference, `preflight_deps.test.sh:291`, stubs the gate to `exit 0` to test the runner's wiring. So the embedded self-test is the entire test estate for that file.

### The fix, measured

Either of these matches the finder and is refused by the parser, and both produce `could not read 1 of 67 pinned reference(s)`, exit 2:

```
uses: actions/cache@5555555555555555555555555555555555555555 with:
uses: actions/cache@5555555555555555555555555555555555555555f
```

A one-line swap. Flagged to Kamil on PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2); the change itself is correct and was approved rather than held for this.

### A related, smaller one in the same file

`:87` computes the self-test's conflicting-SHA count across **all** rows, while the production check at `:152` excludes `(none)` rows. The fixture has one unlabelled SHA appearing once, so the two agree — **by coincidence, not construction**. The self-test is not validating the expression the gate actually runs.

### A third filter for the sweep

The two filters above catch values and disjunctions. This instance suggests a third:

3. **Fixtures whose input never reaches the code path the test names.** Where a test drives a two-stage pipeline (finder → parser, producer → consumer, guard → handler), check that the fixture actually clears stage one. A fixture rejected at stage one exercises stage one's rejection, not the interaction the test is named for — and reads green forever.

*Note: this is a fourth instance, so the title's "3 instances: auth x2, originate x1" is now understated. Left as-is deliberately — it is your ticket and your framing; retitle if you want it to track.*

*Provenance: read and executed at* `dbe7ba6b3` *(PR* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2) *head), 2026-09-09. Finder/parser divergence, both red-proofs and the completeness guard's behaviour all measured by running the script, not inferred. Review:* [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#921](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-778-the-pin-label-gate-could-not-see-two-legal-shapes-and-its-guard-0ba71ba302a2)

title: Eight containers ran images their own tag no longer pointed at — "the stack is up" says nothing about what it is running
description:
## BLUF

**Eight containers in a stack everyone called "up" were running images that were not the image their own tag pointed at.** `docker compose up -d` moved them onto their current `:latest` — an image dated as far back as **2026-07-19** — which means they had been running something older still.

**The finding is not the drift. It is that "the stack is up" carried no information about what the stack was RUNNING.** That is the same hole KS-1011 records from the other side: the stack marker built to answer *"what is this stack running?"* reads `unknown` for branch, commit, owner and started_at. Between them there was no way to tell, and nobody could have noticed.

## Recommendation

Make "up" mean something checkable. Either close KS-1011's marker so the stack states its own provenance, or add a preflight/boot check that compares each running container's image id against the id its tag currently resolves to, and says so loudly when they differ. Cheap, and it converts an invisible condition into a printed line.

Not built in this session — filed while the evidence existed.

## Detail — measured 2026-09-08 during the s153 rebuild-and-delta

Container image ids recorded **before** the swap and **after**, on develop `5ffaaf396`:

| container | tag | was (image id) | now (image id) | now built |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura-admin-frontend` | `2_project_files-admin-frontend` | `1ccb569c333c` | `ae9dc7c99b50` | 2026-09-05 |
| `secuura-issuer-frontend` | `2_project_files-issuer-frontend` | `acaf87948f1a` | `5f5ab1858e02` | 2026-08-12 |
| `secuura-nginx-gateway` | `2_project_files-nginx-gateway` | `1a88d7c62acf` | `da61354d1455` | 2026-09-02 |
| `secuura-pgbouncer` | `2_project_files-pgbouncer` | `fb7bc96531ca` | `fff0c069d941` | 2026-07-29 |
| `secuura-status-frontend` | `2_project_files-status-frontend` | `30912434c7ee` | `cabba2bce603` | 2026-09-02 |
| `secuura-tokenomics-website` | `2_project_files-tokenomics-website` | `25a649012e13` | `8b2bc0c41da4` | 2026-07-29 |
| `secuura-verifier-frontend` | `2_project_files-verifier-frontend` | `3e771b8687a1` | `167864b4b09c` | 2026-08-06 |
| `secuura-website-frontend` | `2_project_files-website-frontend` | `a8f694884e17` | `3245fa82b505` | 2026-07-19 |

These eight rebuilt **byte-identical** (fully cached, so the tag never moved and the image kept its old creation date). The container still changed image — which is what establishes that it had not been on the tag's image to begin with.

For contrast, in the same swap **22** containers moved onto images genuinely built that day, and **3** did not move at all (`postgres`, `redis`, `stack-marker` — image-only services that are never built). 30 + 3 = 33.

## ⚠ The evidence was perishable and is now mostly gone

Re-checked immediately after recording: **7 of the 8 prior images are no longer resolvable on this host** — only `secuura-pgbouncer`'s (`fb7bc96531ca`, 2026-07-29) survives. The ids above are the durable record; the images behind them are not.

Control for that claim: `docker inspect` **by full id** resolves correctly for a currently-running image, so the failures are genuine absences and not a broken lookup.

## What is NOT established

* **How long** each container had been drifted. The prior images' creation dates were not captured before they were pruned, so the age of the drift is unknown and is not claimed.
* **Why** they drifted — whether from a partial `up`, an interrupted rebuild, or a `restart: unless-stopped` recovery that reattached an older image. Not investigated.
* Whether the demo VM has the same condition. **Not measured** — nothing on the demo was touched this session.

## Related

KS-1011 (the stack marker reads `unknown` for everything it exists to report) — the same gap seen from the other side.

title: The `require-pr-gates` ruleset survived the Actions retirement: 7 required checks that can never report, 0 required approvals, and ALWAYS bypass for admins
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **and** `main` **carry an ACTIVE ruleset that enforces nothing for an admin and is unsatisfiable for everyone else.** It requires seven status-check contexts whose workflows no longer exist, requires **zero** approving reviews, and grants `ALWAYS` bypass to org and repo admins.

The retirement of Actions is well tracked ([KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify), [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql)). **What is not tracked is the ruleset left pointing at it.** A branch that looks protected in the settings UI, and in the API reports `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` on a PR with no reviews and no checks, is worse than one that is plainly unprotected — the reassurance is the problem.

Found while reviewing [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), after asking the ordinary question "could this merge without an approval?". It can.

## What the ruleset actually says

`require-pr-gates` — `target: BRANCH`, `enforcement: ACTIVE`, conditions `refs/heads/develop` + `refs/heads/main`.

| rule | setting |
| -- | -- |
| `PULL_REQUEST` | required |
| — `requiredApprovingReviewCount` | **0** |
| — `requireCodeOwnerReview` | false |
| — `requireLastPushApproval` | false |
| — `requiredReviewThreadResolution` | false |
| — `dismissStaleReviewsOnPush` | false |
| `REQUIRED_STATUS_CHECKS` | 7 contexts (below) |
| — `strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy` | false |
| `DELETION` / `NON_FAST_FORWARD` | both on — these two DO work |

Required contexts: `Code Security Gates` · `Standalone locks pass clean-room npm ci` · `build / Build + push platform images (fresh)` · `Schemathesis suite` · `Playwright suite` · `Performance suite (k6 smoke)` · `Akto suite (PR)`.

Bypass actors, **both** `bypassMode: ALWAYS`: organization admins, and repository role `5` (admin).

## The three problems, separately

**1 — Seven required checks that can never report.** Every recent workflow run is `startup_failure` at **0s** (`gh run list`). The workflows producing these contexts were retired. So for a contributor without admin the ruleset is not strict, it is **unsatisfiable** — nothing they push can ever go green, and the failure reads as "waiting for a check" rather than "this check no longer exists".

**2 — Zero required approvals.** A PR is required; an approval is not. On `main` as well as `develop`, which is the part I would not have guessed. `main` is meant to be the releasable branch (CLAUDE.md → Branching Model), and it currently asks for no human sign-off at all.

**3 —** `ALWAYS` **bypass for admins hides both.** Anyone who could notice problems 1 and 2 is exactly the population the ruleset never applies to. GitHub computes `mergeStateStatus` for the viewer, so an admin sees `CLEAN` and no warning of any kind.

## The demonstration

[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), read 2026-09-08:

```
mergeable:         MERGEABLE
mergeStateStatus:  CLEAN
reviewDecision:    null      (no reviews of ANY kind ever submitted)
statusCheckRollup: 0 checks
```

Mergeable right now, by any admin, with no approval and no green check — and nothing on the PR page says so. That PR happens to be under active review, so no harm is in flight; it is the state that is the finding, not the PR.

## Reproduce

```
gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner:"Secuura", name:"Distributed_Secuura") {
  rulesets(first:5){ nodes{ name target enforcement
    conditions{ refName{ include exclude } }
    bypassActors(first:20){ nodes{ bypassMode organizationAdmin repositoryRoleDatabaseId } }
    rules(first:30){ nodes{ type parameters{ __typename
      ... on PullRequestParameters { requiredApprovingReviewCount requireCodeOwnerReview requireLastPushApproval requiredReviewThreadResolution dismissStaleReviewsOnPush }
      ... on RequiredStatusChecksParameters { strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy requiredStatusChecks{ context } } } } } } } }'
```

Note the REST endpoints (`/branches/develop/protection`, `/rulesets`) answer **403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro"** on this private repo, which is why this is easy to miss — the obvious check reports nothing rather than reporting the truth. GraphQL answers fine.

## Suggested shape — not a decree, and deliberately not one change

These are three decisions, not one, and they belong to different owners:

1. **Drop the seven dead contexts** from the ruleset, or repoint them at whatever replaced Actions. Leaving a required check that cannot report is the worst of the three states. *(Cheap; no policy decision.)*
2. **Decide the approval count deliberately**, for `main` and `develop` separately. If 0 is intended on a 4-seat team, say so in CONTRIBUTING and this ticket closes on that; if it is a leftover, 1 on `develop` and 1 on `main` is the obvious floor.
3. **Reconsider** `ALWAYS` **bypass.** `pull_request` mode instead of `ALWAYS` keeps admins able to unblock an emergency while still surfacing the state to them.

**(1) is worth doing regardless of how (2) and (3) land.**

## Relationship to what is already tracked

* [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) (Todo, High, Peter) — *"require all systemTest PR suites + pre-merge to block merges on failure (branch protection + sign-off)"*. Points **forward** to the gate we want. This ticket is the **residue behind us**: the ruleset that already exists and no longer means anything. They should probably be sequenced — clean this up, then build [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) on the cleared ground.
* [KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify) — CONTRIBUTING justifies the hook's `--no-verify` bypass with *"CI is the hard gate"*. This is the same sentence, one layer down: the ruleset also asserts a gate that is not there.
* [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql) — the Actions retirement itself and its orphaned guards. Cause; this is effect.

## Not claimed

I have not checked whether any merge to `develop` or `main` has actually gone in unreviewed — only that nothing prevents it. Nor have I touched the ruleset; changing it needs org-admin rights and is a decision, not a fix.

*Raised by Peter's session, 2026-09-08, from the #805 review. Read via GraphQL against the live repo, not from documentation.*

title: e2e: "CIP-30 API availability check" calls a route that does not exist, and its assertion passes on the 404
description:
## BLUF

`tests/e2e/.../happy-path-wallet.spec.ts:255` **calls a route that does not exist — and its assertion**
**is written so that the 404 PASSES.** The test is named *"CIP-30 API availability check"* and asserts
only `expect(response.status()).toBeLessThan(500)`, with a comment saying *"may return 404 if not*
*implemented"*. **404 < 500.** It has never been able to fail for the thing it names.

**This is not one line.** The same shape runs through the recruitment e2e suite: **13**
`toBeLessThan(500)` **assertions and 33** `if (response.ok())` **guards across 62 tests in 5 files.** An
`if (response.ok())` wrapper means that when the endpoint is absent, **zero assertions execute and the**
**test passes.**

Surfaced by @PeterObeden's `wallet/status` question on PR #802 (see KS-1009). It is a
**check-that-cannot-fail**, which is this board's most-repeated family.

## Measured

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| service-side references to `/api/wallet/status` | **0** — the route does not exist |
| service-side references to `/api/wallet/supported` | **0** — nor does this one |
| **CONTROL —** `/api/auth/wallet/challenge`**, used correctly in the same file** | **6** |

The control is what makes the zeros mean something: the same search over the same tree finds the route
that does exist, so the zeros are real absences rather than a search that cannot match.

**And the correct path is already known inside the same directory.** `fixtures/recruitment-data.ts:291`
defines:

```
walletStatus: (address: string) => `/api/auth/wallet/status/${address}`
```

The test does not use it. So this is a mistake, not a deliberate second route.

### The family, per file

| file | `toBeLessThan(500)` | `if (response.ok())` | tests |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `admin-config.admin.spec.ts` | 4 | 11 | 21 |
| `alternative-paths.spec.ts` | 4 | 7 | 16 |
| `happy-path-nft.spec.ts` | 1 | 13 | 6 |
| `happy-path-wallet.spec.ts` | 3 | 2 | 11 |
| `happy-path-web.spec.ts` | 1 | 0 | 8 |

Not every one of these is wrong — `< 500` is a legitimate assertion for *"this must not 5xx"*, and
`if (ok())` is legitimate where the test genuinely is conditional. **What is not legitimate is a test**
**whose NAME claims to check availability and whose assertion passes when the thing is absent.** The
count is the search space, not the defect count.

## ⚠ OPEN QUESTION — do not change any route until this is answered

**It is not established what these tests were meant to cover.** Two readings, and they lead opposite
ways:

1. **The path is a typo** — the intended route is `/api/auth/wallet/status/:address`, the fixture proves
   the author knew it, and the fix is to use the fixture and assert a real outcome.
2. **The route was planned and never built** — `/api/wallet/status` and `/api/wallet/supported` were
   meant to be a `wallet-connector` service surface, and these are placeholders deliberately written to
   tolerate absence.

Reading 2 is not far-fetched: the test's own comment says *"Test that wallet connector service is*
*running"*, and `wallet-connector` is a real service in this repo.

**Changing the route under reading 2 would silently delete the record that something was never built.**
So: establish the intent first, then fix. Do not repoint the URL as a tidy-up.

## Suggested shape once intent is known

* If typo: use `fixtures/recruitment-data.ts`'s `walletStatus()` and assert the actual contract
  (`exists` true/false), not a status band.
* If unbuilt: mark the tests `test.fixme()` with the ticket reference, so the gap is visible rather
  than green.
* Either way, **a test whose name asserts availability must fail when the thing is unavailable.**

*Filed by s152 from PR #802's open question, on Wednesday's instruction. Measured on* `origin/develop`
*merged into the KS-732 worktree. Nothing changed.*

title: The OAuth token endpoint is outside the credential-stuffing rate-limit zone — /api/oauth/ is not keyed in $secuura_auth_limit_key
description:
## BLUF

`/api/oauth/` **sits OUTSIDE the credential-stuffing rate-limit zone that** `/api/auth/` **sits inside.** The OAuth token endpoint — the one that exchanges codes and redeems refresh tokens — gets only the aggregate `/api/` ceiling, not the 5 r/s + burst 10 bound the config itself calls *"the credential-stuffing bound"*.

**True whether or not** [KS-823](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-823) **is fixed**, which is why this is its own ticket rather than a sub-item of it: KS-823 is about the refresh grant's missing client authentication; this is about the rate-limit zone configuration. Different logical path, per Kam's one-ticket-per-path rule.

## Measured

`Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf`, read at the demo VM's SHA `400517aaf`:

```nginx
map $request_uri $secuura_auth_limit_key {
    "~^/api/auth/"     $secuura_limit_key;
    "~^/api/v1/auth/"  $secuura_limit_key;
}
limit_req_zone $secuura_auth_limit_key zone=secuura_auth:10m rate=5r/s;
```

The map keys **two** prefixes. `/api/oauth/` is neither. The file's own comment describes the zone as *"auth at 5 r/s + burst 10 is the credential-stuffing bound"* — so the intent of the zone is explicit, and the token endpoint is outside it.

**The endpoint is reachable:** `nginx-demo.conf` `location /api/` → the gateway; `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:317` `router.use('/api/oauth', proxy('auth', …))` with no `authenticateToken` and no scope gate (deliberately — the section header reads *"AUTH / USER / SESSION (no gateway auth — handled by auth service)"*).

**Control that the map's silence is real and not a grep artefact:** the same map DOES key `/api/auth/` and `/api/v1/auth/`, and neighbouring gateway mounts in `proxy.ts` ARE guarded (`/api/webhooks` carries `authenticateToken(true), attachScopes, requireScope('webhooks:manage')`). So both instruments can produce a positive, and the negative on `/api/oauth/` means something.

**No request was made against the demo, valid or invalid.** This is a read of code and configuration only.

## Why it matters

`POST /api/oauth/token` accepts credential-bearing material — an authorization code, a refresh token, and for confidential apps a client secret. It is a guessing surface of the same class as `/api/auth/login`, and it is the one the zone was written to bound. Anything that brute-forces or sprays against it meets only the aggregate `/api/` ceiling shared with every other API path, rather than the per-key 5 r/s bound.

## Not claimed

* **No exploitability measurement.** Whether the aggregate `/api/` ceiling is in practice tight enough has NOT been measured, and doing so needs a probe that has not been authorised.
* **No claim about the local or production configs.** `nginx-demo.conf` was read; `nginx.conf` and `nginx-production.conf` were not, and they may differ. Whoever picks this up should check all three before changing one.

## Fix shape

Add `"~^/api/oauth/" $secuura_limit_key;` to the map, or widen the existing keys — then confirm the other two nginx configs and decide whether the same gap exists there. A rate-limit change wants its own verification that legitimate token exchange is not throttled.

Discovered 2026-09-08 during KS-1001's disposition pass over the P2 In Review queue, while reading KS-823's reachability.

title: 95 archived tickets sit in NON-TERMINAL states — measure whether a cascade put them there
description:
## BLUF

**97 archived tickets on the KS+PS boards are in non-terminal states.** Two were archived today (mine, restored the same session). **The other 95 predate this session and nobody has established how they got there.**

```
Backlog     83
Todo         6
In Progress  4
In Review    3
Blocked      1
```

**This is a hypothesis with evidence, NOT an asserted cause.** [KS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-995) established that `issueArchive` cascades onto sub-issues — including non-terminal ones — and that the parent-side check reads clean afterwards. **That mechanism would produce exactly this population, silently.** It may also be that some were archived deliberately.

## The measurement that would settle it

For each of the 95: **is its parent archived, and does the parent's** `archivedAt` **match the child's to the millisecond?**

That is the same discriminator that disproved a wrong third-party attribution during today's pass, applied backwards:

* **match → decisive for cascade.** One batch, one cause.
* **mismatch → closes nothing.** It was archived separately, which is consistent with a deliberate act.

One-directional, and that limit should be carried into whatever the measurement concludes — a mismatch is not evidence of intent.

## 🔴 Do NOT unarchive anything on the strength of this ticket

**83 tickets reappearing in Backlog changes what the team sees.** A restoration is as much a board change as an archive, and it is Kam's call on a measurement — not a tidy-up. **Measure first, report, then ask.**

## Items

- [ ] **1. Run the parent/timestamp measurement** across all 95 and report the split.
- [ ] **2. For any confirmed cascade victim, establish whether the work is still live** — an In Progress ticket archived by accident is different from a Backlog item nobody was going to do.
- [ ] **3. Only then** put a restoration proposal to Kam, with counts by state.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

Every count taken with a default query has been wrong on this board today — *twice*. `Tested Not Deployed` read 24 when it was 29, and a Duplicate census read 4 when it was 5 because the query capped at 250. **If 95 live-state tickets are invisible, every "what is open" number anyone has quoted is short by some part of 95.**

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, alongside KS-995.

title: Archiving a ticket silently archives its sub-issues, including NON-TERMINAL ones — and the parent-side check cannot detect it
description:
## BLUF

`issueArchive` **cascades to sub-issues.** Archiving 23 terminal tickets on 2026-09-08 also archived **KS-918 (Backlog)** and **KS-920 (In Progress)** — children of **KS-490**. Neither was in any target list. **In Progress is live work.**

**And the obvious verification cannot catch it:** once archived, the parent's `children` connection returns **nothing**. Asking the parent what it took with it reads clean.

Both were restored the same session. This ticket is about the mechanism, which is still live.

## Measured

```
child -> parent    KS-918.parent = KS-490      ✅ reveals the link
                   KS-920.parent = KS-490      ✅
parent -> children KS-490.children = 0         ❌ shows NOTHING
```

**The timestamps are what identified it as a cascade rather than a concurrent actor:**

```
KS-490  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-921  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-918  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
KS-920  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
```

Identical to the millisecond = one batch = one cause. **My own first diagnosis blamed a concurrent actor and was wrong; the timestamp disproved it.**

**Full accounting for the pass:** 33 intended + 2 collateral = 35 archived, measured 35. Only KS-490 had children, so the blast radius was bounded at exactly two.

## Why it went unnoticed until arithmetic caught it

The only reason anyone knows is the **census delta: −25 against an expected −23**. That is the shape most easily rationalised as a stale count. Every other signal looked clean:

* the archive calls all returned `success: true` — and they had, for the 23 asked;
* the parent-side `children` query returned **0**;
* no error, no warning, nothing in any response mentioning the children.

## The rule this produces

**Before archiving, query** `child → parent` **for the target's children and record the count. After, take a full paged census.**

```
expected delta = |targets| + |children found|
```

**If the delta is not exactly that, stop.** Asking the parent side for `children` is *the check that cannot fail* here — it reads zero both when there are none and when they have just been archived.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Make the children pre-check part of any archive procedure**, with the delta equation above as its pass condition.
- [ ] **2. Decide whether a cascade onto a NON-TERMINAL child should be refused outright.** Kam's standing ruling is that non-terminal work stays visible on the board; a cascade violates that silently.
- [ ] **3. Measure the historical population — see the sibling ticket** on the 95 pre-existing archived non-terminal tickets. This mechanism would produce exactly that.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the archive pass that hit it.

title: A deploy that rsyncs the OpenAPI spec and does not restart api-gateway ships a silently stale published contract — rsync breaks the bind mount by inode
description:
## BLUF

**The demo redeploy runbook can ship a stale published API contract with every check passing.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` is a **file-level** bind mount into `api-gateway` (`docker-compose.yml:542`, `:ro`). `rsync` **writes a temp file and renames it, so the updated file gets a NEW INODE** — and a Docker file bind mount resolves to the inode at container-create time. The container goes on serving the **old** file indefinitely.

It is not stale cache. The container is looking at a **different file on the same path**.

## Measured during the 2026-09-08 deploy (632f16dfe → 400517aaf)

After the rsync, before any restart:

|  | md5 | bytes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| host `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `7e43a8d89afb…` | 1332983 (new) |
| inside `api-gateway` `/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `c014b2fce71c…` | 1329831 (**old**, dated Sep 7 03:45) |
| served `GET /api/docs/openapi.yaml` | — | 1329831 = the container's copy |

After `docker compose restart api-gateway`: container md5 `7e43a8d89afb…`, identical to the host; served bytes 1332983; the new text `BOUND TO THE` went **0 → 1** and `DIFFERS FROM the ACTING` **0 → 2**, with `organizationUuid` **1 → 2** as a control and an impossible string at 0.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure mode is exactly KS-978's**, which this same deploy shipped the fix for: *the published contract says something the route does not do*. KS-978 was a wrong sentence in the source. This is the **delivery mechanism** producing the same outcome from a correct source — and it is quieter, because every signal an operator would check looks right:

* `rsync` exits 0 and reports the file transferred ✅
* the file on the VM disk **is** correct ✅
* rebuilding the image does nothing (the spec is mounted, not baked) — so "I rebuilt it" feels like the fix and is not ✅
* the container is healthy, the endpoint returns 200 ✅

Nothing surfaces the divergence except comparing the md5 **inside** the container against the host.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Add the gateway restart to the runbook as a required step**, not an optional one — `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` §Redeploy runbook. Wording should carry the mechanism (inode), because "restart to pick up the spec" reads as cargo-cult and gets dropped.
- [ ] **2. Correct the existing guidance.** The current understanding recorded in project notes is "a rebuild does not publish it, a restart does" — true but incomplete, and it does not say the container will serve the old file *forever* until something re-resolves the mount.
- [ ] **3. Add a post-deploy assertion** that fails loudly: compare `md5sum` of the host spec against `docker exec api-gateway md5sum` of the mounted path, and refuse to call a deploy complete when they differ. This is the check that would have caught it with no human judgement involved.
- [ ] **4. Audit for other file-level bind mounts with the same exposure** — `nginx-demo.conf` is the known sibling. Directory mounts are not affected; only single-file mounts are.

## Not a live defect right now

The 2026-09-08 deploy restarted `api-gateway` and the served spec is verified correct. This ticket is about the **next** deploy, by whoever does not know.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the deploy itself.

title: The published admin credential survives in USER_TESTING docs while nothing on the demo seeds it any more — and the switch that would restore seeding now suspends that account
description:
## BLUF

`USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md` advertises `admin@secuura.com` **/** `admin123` at **:68** and **:177**. KS-964/KS-966 retired that published fallback in the seeder, and separately the demo's seeder does not run at all. So the doc is a published credential for an account nobody can currently prove is loginable — and the obvious remedy (turn seeding back on) **suspends** the account unless a second variable is set in the same change.

Two items, one code path (the seed-credential surface). Filed together per the aggregate rule.

## What was measured, 2026-09-08 (s149)

**On the demo VM's** `auth` **container, read-only, authorised narrowly by Wednesday (set/unset only, value never read):**

* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` = **UNSET**
* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` = **PRESENT-EMPTY**
* `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED` = **UNSET**
* Instrument validated first: `NODE_ENV`, `DATABASE_URL`, `REDIS_URL`, `JWT_PUBLIC_KEY` all read **SET** (4 of 4 boot-critical controls), a nonsense variable read UNSET, and `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` reading PRESENT-EMPTY proves the probe separates present-empty from absent.
* ⚠ **Round 1 of this read was discarded, not reported.** Its positive control was `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD`, which also read UNSET — but that variable has a *published fallback* (`seedPw(var,'demo123')`), so its absence is invisible and it cannot prove the probe can see a present value. The control was mine and it was wrong.

**Direct evidence from the running system** (`auth` container log, started 2026-09-07T05:46:39Z, 7676 lines readable):

* `"Demo user seeding skipped — set ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true to enable"` — **present ×1**
* `"Demo user seeding skipped in non-dev env"` — **0**
* `"Demo user seeding enabled in non-dev environment"` — **0**
* Controls: 3762 unrelated startup matches (log is greppable), an impossible string returns 0.

**So** `seedDemoUsersInner` **returns at its FIRST gate on the demo and never reaches any account row.** The gate block is byte-identical between `632f16dfe` (deployed) and `400517aaf` (trunk) — sha256 `e77a5c30…` both sides, with a control block that DOES differ across the same range, so the comparison can see a change.

## Items

- [ ] **1. The doc advertises a credential the platform no longer seeds.** `USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md:68` and `:177` publish `admin@secuura.com` / `admin123`. Decide and apply: correct the doc, or restore the account deliberately. **Whether that login works on the demo today is NOT established** — the row may persist from an earlier seeding era with its old hash. Answering it needs a DB read that was outside this seat's authorisation.
- [ ] **2. Turning seeding back on now suspends the platform admin.** The moment anyone sets `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` on the demo to restore seeding, `requiredSeedPw('ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD')` returns null (`userRepo.ts:1039,1075`), and the null branch writes `status='suspended'` plus an unusable hash — **actively suspending a pre-existing row, not merely skipping it**. `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` must be set in the *same* change. This is a trap for whoever next tries to re-seed, and nothing warns them at the point of the switch.
- [ ] **3. Consider making the trap loud rather than documented** — the seeder could refuse to start (or log at `error`) when `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` is combined with a `requiredSeedPw` account whose variable is unset, instead of silently suspending it.

## Why this is filed and not fixed

Wednesday's ANSWER, 2026-09-08: *"Do not edit USER_TESTING/CREDENTIALS-AND-PORTALS.md yet… the fix depends on which way Q1 goes. File it as a ticket now so it cannot be lost."* Setting a credential on a running system is Kam's signature class and collides with his own `rotate-properly` ruling on the admin credential (2026-09-07).

**Q1 came back in a way that DE-ESCALATES the deploy:** the `632f16dfe..400517aaf` deploy does **not** suspend `admin@secuura.com`, because the seeder never runs. Item 2 is the residual risk that outlives the deploy.

## Not blocking the deploy

The 19-commit deploy is unaffected by this ticket. Recorded here so the finding cannot be lost when the deploy card closes.

title: Eight dashboards show a slot picker that filters nothing — latent today, wrong the day /metrics lands
description:
## What

All 12 dashboards under `observability/grafana/dashboards/` carry a `slot` template variable, so every one presents a slot picker. Only **four** actually use `$slot` in a query.

Measured 2026-09-07 by counting panel targets containing `$slot`:

| Dashboard | Panels filtering by slot |
| -- | -- |
| `k6_engineering` | 32 |
| `k6_executive` | 12 |
| `test_quality_trends` | 8 |
| `platform_engineering` | 4 |
| `platform_auth` | **0** |
| `platform_cardano` | **0** |
| `platform_document_lifecycle` | **0** |
| `platform_queue` | **0** |
| `platform_slo` | **0** |
| `platform_traffic_services` | **0** |
| `security_posture` | **0** |
| `test_openapi_coverage` | **0** |

On those eight, moving the picker changes nothing.

## Why it is not urgent, and why it is not nothing

It is **not currently misleading**, because those eight query application `/metrics` endpoints that no service implements ([KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never)) — the panels are empty whatever the picker says. Nothing wrong is being displayed.

It becomes wrong the moment [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) lands. Those panels will then merge all four slots into one number, with a picker sitting above them implying they are scoped. That is precisely the defect [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) existed to remove — a plausible-looking dashboard that quietly answers about the wrong system — reintroduced through the panels nobody had to touch.

## Evidence that the other four are correct

Same sweep, evaluating every slot-aware panel for `slot1` vs `slot2` against live Prometheus during a four-slot run: **56 slot-aware panels, zero returned identical data**. Where the filter exists it discriminates properly. This ticket is only about the panels where it is absent.

## Scope

Add the `slot` filter to those panels' PromQL when their metrics start existing, or drop the picker from dashboards that will never be slot-scoped. Do it **with** [KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never), since the correct filter cannot be written or tested against metrics that do not yet exist.

A validator check in the shape of `observability/scripts/checks/container-join-slot.mjs` — fail the build when a dashboard declares a `slot` variable that no panel consumes — would stop it recurring, and would have caught this.

## Depends on

[KS-984](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-984/no-service-exposes-metrics-the-secuura-services-scrape-job-has-never) (no service exposes `/metrics`).

Found while verifying [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) on a live four-slot stack.

title: No service exposes /metrics — the secuura-services scrape job has never collected a single series on any slot
description:
## What

`observability/prometheus/prometheus.yml` defines a `secuura-services` scrape job over seven service targets. Every one of them is **down with HTTP 404**, and has been since the job was written — the endpoints do not exist.

Measured 2026-09-07 on a freshly rebuilt four-slot stack:

* `secuura-services` targets: **7 down, 404 Not Found** (every other job is `up`, except `kafka`, which is phase2-only and correct).
* `prom-client` is a dependency of **no** service.
* No `/metrics` route is registered anywhere under `services/*/src`, using `/health` as a positive control.

## Why it matters

This is not an observability-stack defect — the stack is healthy and correctly configured. It is that the thing it is pointed at does not exist. The consequence is that **every application-level panel across eight dashboards renders empty**:

`platform_auth`, `platform_cardano`, `platform_document_lifecycle`, `platform_queue`, `platform_slo`, `platform_traffic_services`, `security_posture`, `test_openapi_coverage`.

So the platform currently has **no application telemetry at all** — no request rates, error rates, latency, queue depth or SLO burn from the services themselves. What Grafana does show comes from cAdvisor, the DB/Redis/nginx exporters, and the test harnesses pushing their own results.

## Not to be confused with

[KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) corrected this job's **target ports** (they were 3000-3006 against services that listen on the 4000-range and 8080) and added `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/prometheus_targets.test.sh` to stop them drifting again. That work made the job name the right addresses. It did not, and could not, make the endpoints exist.

## Scope

Instrumenting the services. Roughly: add `prom-client` to the service template, register a `/metrics` route alongside the existing `/health`, and export the handful of series the existing dashboards already query.

## Blocks

* Per-slot application metrics. The scrape job uses static container names, so only slot 1 is discovered. Making slots 2-4 discoverable needs either a Docker socket mounted into Prometheus (root-equivalent) or a generated targets file plus a per-slot `docker network connect` — not worth its cost while the job collects nothing on any slot. Revisit **after** this, not before.
* The slot picker on those eight dashboards, which currently filters nothing because their panels have no slot-aware data to filter.

Found while verifying [KS-971](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-971/k6-performance-harness-slot-isolation-a-slot-1-memory-verdict-can-be) on a live four-slot stack.

title: Neither credential guard can see a value in a .env.example — one scans the wrong roots and extensions, the other excludes the file and self-tests the exclusion
description:
**Two credential guards run on every push and NEITHER could see the one that mattered.** KS-966 F1 was a live exposure — `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` shipped a value for `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:381` plus `services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html:382` both instruct `cp .env.example .env`, so the documented setup path seeded the platform SYSTEM_ADMIN **ACTIVE and loginable** on a credential published in this repository. It sat there through a full round-1 gate.

**This is the guards' blind AXIS, not a bug in either implementation, and it was not introduced by #888.** Both behave exactly as written. That is the problem.

### Measured, from the scripts themselves

**1.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh:28-32` — cannot reach the file on two independent axes:

```
grep -rEn --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.js' \
     --exclude-dir=__tests__ --exclude-dir=tests --exclude-dir=scripts \
     ... services/ packages/
```

* **Extension:** `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` only. A `.env.example` is not scannable by construction.
* **Root:** `services/` and `packages/` only. `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` is above both.

Either one alone is sufficient to miss it. Widening one and not the other changes nothing.

**2.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/no-tracked-credentials.sh:37-38` — excludes it *deliberately*:

```
EXCLUDE_RE='\.(example|sample|template)$'
```

with the comment at `:34-36` explaining that 25 `.env.example` files are tracked on purpose and are the documented way to describe required config. **And its own self-test at** `:51-53` **asserts the exclusion holds**, naming `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` as a probe that MUST be excluded:

```
for probe in "Blockchain/Dev/.env.example" "svc/config.example"; do
  echo "$probe" | grep -Eq "$EXCLUDE_RE" || { echo "SELF-TEST FAIL: did not exclude $probe"; ok=1; }
done
```

So the guard is not merely blind here — **it is tested to be blind here.** Any fix has to change that self-test too, consciously, or it will be reverted by the next person who reads it as a regression.

### Why the exclusion is right and still leaves a hole

The exclusion exists for a good reason: an example file must be allowed to *name* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, or it cannot document the variable at all. **The distinction the guards do not draw is between naming a key and assigning it a value.** `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=` is documentation. `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=<something>` is a credential. A file-level exclusion cannot tell those apart; a line-level rule can.

### Shape when picked up

A check over tracked `*.env.example` files that fails on **a non-empty assignment to a credential-shaped key**, rather than on the file's existence. Keys named, not pattern-guessed — the pattern-guessing is what produces the false positives the current exclusion was written to avoid.

### Interim cover — real but partial, and it must not be mistaken for this ticket being done

#888 round 2 adds a cell (`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`, the `KS-966 F1` block) that walks the tree for `*.env.example` and fails on a non-empty `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` / `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. It is red-proved (restoring a value gives 2 red of 23 executing).

**It covers two key names in one service's test suite.** It is not a push-time gate, it does not run when only non-auth code changes, and it says nothing about any other credential-shaped key. The gap this ticket names is the guards' coverage axis, and that is still open.

title: 104 flat spec files in Blockchain/Dev/tests are in no runner's path — quarantine and find out, do not delete
description:
**BLUF** — `Blockchain/Dev/tests/` holds **104 flat** `*.spec.ts` **files that appear to be in no test runner's path.** They are not a credential problem; they are a dead-code problem, and they were separated out of the KS-964 credential rotation for that reason.

## The measurement

The three playwright configs are `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/playwright.config.ts`, `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/playwright.config.ts` and `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts`. Each sets `testDir: './tests'` **relative to its own directory** — so the paths they cover are `tests/e2e/tests` and `tests/e2e-v2/tests`, not the flat `Blockchain/Dev/tests/` root.

```
flat Blockchain/Dev/tests/*.spec.ts tracked : 104
under tests/e2e/                            :  48
```

No workflow or script references the flat directory. **Control:** the same search finds `tests/e2e` referenced in **5** files, so the grep can find a referenced path — the zero is a real absence, not a broken search.

The names read like ad-hoc debugging left in place: `admin-sidebar-collapse-final.spec.ts`, `admin-sidebar-collapse-fresh.spec.ts`, `admin-sidebar-simple-check.spec.ts`, `debug-system-health.spec.ts`, `admin-verify-no-mock-data.spec.ts`.

## ⚠ The limit of this evidence, stated

**I checked configs and greps. An ad-hoc** `npx playwright test <file>` **by a person would not show up in either.** So this is "nothing in the repo runs them", not "nobody runs them".

**Therefore: do NOT delete.** Quarantine (rename or move), leave it a sprint, and see who shouts. That is the standing never-delete rule and it is the right instrument for exactly this uncertainty.

## Why it was separated from the credential work

43 of these files contain the retired admin password. Rewriting a credential in a spec nothing runs is work with **no security return** — and worse, it would make the rotation look larger and riskier than it is. The credential in a dead file stops mattering the moment the credential stops working, which KS-964 item 1 achieves.

## The question to answer

1. Is anything running these — a person, a habit, a README?
2. If not: quarantine, then remove after a quiet period.
3. If some are live, they move under a config's `testDir` where the runner can see them, and they get the env-var treatment from KS-964.

**Measured 2026-09-07 during the KS-964 rotation measurement.**

title: Two schema sources disagree on whether users.email is unique — a statement valid against one is 42P10 against the other, so a suite can be green on a shape that never runs
description:
**BLUF** — the `users` table has **two schema sources that disagree about whether** `email` **is unique**, and a statement that is valid against one is a hard error against the other. This is not a row-level inconsistency; it is a **test environment diverging from the deployed environment on a constraint**, which means a suite can be green on a shape that never runs anywhere.

## ⛔ DO NOT RECONCILE THESE TWO FILES YET

**Nobody has established which source is authoritative.** Aligning either to the other closes the question by erasing the evidence that it was open — and whichever way it is aligned, the loser's behaviour silently becomes "the contract". Establish authority first, then change one file, deliberately, with the reasoning written down.

## The two sources

| file | declaration |
| -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/init/01-schema.sql:21` | `email TEXT NOT NULL` — **no unique index** |
| `Blockchain/Dev/migrations/001_initial-schema.sql:20` | `email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL` |

**The first is deliberate and is documented in place.** Its own comment reads: *"email is AES-GCM ciphertext … Lookups go via the deterministic email_lookup_hash … because non-deterministic encryption can't enforce uniqueness."* A unique index on a randomly-IV'd ciphertext cannot block duplicates, so uniqueness was moved to `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq`. `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` already reflects this — `createUser` conflicts on `email_lookup_hash` and says why.

**So the divergence is probably a migration that was never updated when the encryption landed** — but that is a hypothesis, and this ticket exists so it is checked rather than assumed.

## The evidence, measured

Against the running stack (built from `docker/init/01-schema.sql`), in **rolled-back** transactions:

```
INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (email) DO UPDATE ...
  -> ERROR: there is no unique or exclusion constraint matching
            the ON CONFLICT specification            (42P10)

INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE ...
  -> INSERT 0 1
```

Index census on the live table: `users_pkey (id)`, `users_email_lookup_hash_uniq (email_lookup_hash) WHERE NOT NULL`, and six social-id uniques. **No index on** `email`**.**

## Why this is a class hazard, not one row

**KS-949 F1 is the instance.** The api-gateway startup seed used `ON CONFLICT (email)`. The round-1 QA gate reported *"fresh DB → INSERT 0 12"* — a true measurement, taken against a database built from `migrations/001`. On every environment we actually deploy, the same statement raised 42P10 and the twelve-row seed silently failed on **every** boot, caught and logged at debug level as "skipped".

**A green test against the wrong schema source is indistinguishable from a green test.** That is the hazard: not that one seed was broken, but that the instrument could not tell.

## What "establishing authority" looks like

1. Which source builds which environment today — compose/init vs the migration runner — measured, not assumed.
2. Whether any deployed database was built from `migrations/001` and therefore **does** have the unique index (if so, the same statement behaves differently per environment, which is worse than either alone).
3. Whether `migrations/001` is still executed anywhere, or is now only a historical artefact that tests happen to build from.
4. Only then: change one file, and add a check that the two cannot drift again.

## Scope

**Not** KS-949's (that fixed the instance and is deliberately silent on which source is right). **Not** KS-957's (that is a claims path — artefacts asserting things their suites cannot check; this is a schema-authority question). Filed separately per the aggregation rule: one ticket per logical path.

**Measured 2026-09-07 during KS-949 round 2.**

---

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION INHERITED BY WHOEVER SETTLES AUTHORITY

**If an environment is built from** `migrations/001`**, does auth's** `seedDemoUsers` **run before document seeding?**

This is a live consequence of the divergence, not a hypothetical, and it is recorded here because it has no other home.

**Why it only exists on one side.** `migrations/001:107` and `deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql:105` declare `documents.owner_user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id)`. `docker/init/01-schema.sql:127` — the deployed source — declares `owner_user_id UUID` with **no** foreign key (verified on the live table via `pg_constraint`; control: that file declares no user foreign keys at all).

**So on a migrations-built database the twelve seeded user rows must exist BEFORE any document referencing them is inserted, and on the deployed schema the question cannot arise.** Same tree, same code, two different ordering requirements.

**Why it is now load-bearing.** KS-949 removes the api-gateway startup migration's user INSERT (ratified 2026-09-07: it has never once succeeded — 42P10 on every boot — and auth's `seedDemoUsers` already creates all twelve rows with identical tenancy, encrypted, with `email_lookup_hash` set). After that change, **auth is the only creator of those rows.** On the deployed schema that is safe. On a migrations-built schema it depends on an ordering nobody has measured.

**What would settle it:** whether any environment is built from `migrations/001` today, and if so, the actual boot order of auth's seeder against whatever inserts documents.

**Deliberately NOT settled here**, and not guessed at. Which source a given environment used is exactly the authority question this ticket exists to answer, and answering the ordering first would be assuming it.

**Raised 2026-09-07 during KS-949 round 2.**

title: KS-597 fallback: resolve the issuer org from the authenticated caller org context — BLOCKED, organization_members has 0 rows
description:
**BLUF — this cannot be built today, and the blocker is data, not design.** The KS-597 ask has two resolution paths for the issuing organisation. The first (resolve from a caller-supplied `organizationUuid`) is implemented and shipping. **This ticket is the second one — *"else from the authenticated caller's org context"* — and it resolves through a table that has no rows.**

Wednesday ruled 2026-09-07 that it must **not** be written as unexercisable code: *"a fallback that resolves through a table with no rows cannot be exercised, and code that cannot be exercised is a check that cannot fail wearing a feature's clothes. Worse than absent: the next reader sees a fallback in the source and believes the case is handled."*

## 🔴 THE BLOCKER, measured

Local stack, one query, with the control in the same statement:

```
documents rows                                      59
documents.issuer_organization_id populated           0
organizations rows            (CONTROL)              6     <- the query CAN see rows
organization_members rows                            0
```

`organization_members` **is empty.** KS-597's own 2026-09-02 comment measured the same zero on the larger tree (`organizations` 151, `organization_members` 0, `documents` 95,127).

**The control is what makes the zero mean something:** `organizations` returning 6 proves the query is not simply blind. Without that line, `organization_members = 0` is indistinguishable from a query that cannot see anything — and this schema is under **forced RLS** (`relrowsecurity` and `relforcerowsecurity` both true on `organizations` and `documents`), where a role without the `app.current_tenant_id` GUC set reads zero rows from a fully populated table.

## What would unblock it

Membership rows. Specifically, a path that writes `organization_members` at or before registration — org creation, invite acceptance, or a backfill from an existing signal. **Until at least one exists, any fallback written here is untestable by construction: every test would assert the null branch, and the non-null branch would never execute in any environment.**

## What NOT to do

* Do not write the fallback and mark it "covered" — see the ruling above.
* Do not reach for `documents.tenant_id` as a proxy. A tenant is not an organisation; the schema keeps both deliberately, and collapsing them would put wrong attribution in a column whose whole purpose is attribution.

## Scope note

The forward half — resolving a caller-supplied `organizationUuid` onto `documents.issuer_organization_id`, tenant-scoped, folding to NULL when unknown — is **done** and is not blocked by this. The 95k-row backfill is a separate round on Kam's `afterfix` ruling.

**Measured 2026-09-07 on the local stack; the larger-tree figures are from KS-597's own 2026-09-02 comment.**

title: KS-930 residue: a whole app tree copied into a stage that names no JS runtime is still exempt — and the gate's fix-shape for it cannot be written without denying the repo's own idiom
description:
**BLUF** — #876 round 2 closed 7 of the 8 shapes in the tier-1 gate's attack table. **Row 1d stays open**: `FROM scratch` + `COPY --from=builder /app /app` is still `A_EXEMPT` at rc 0. The gate's fix-shape for it was **built and then withdrawn**, because measurement says it cannot be expressed without denying every class file in the repo. This ticket carries the residue and the evidence, so the decision is made on numbers rather than re-derived from scratch.

**Measured, all three guards, one row driver parked outside the scanned tree (self-tested to produce three distinct arms):**

| row | base `306d0db92` | round 1 `8d3e5208a` | round 2 |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1a alpine + `apk add nodejs` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1c busybox + copied node binary + `/app` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| **1d scratch +** `COPY --from=builder /app /app` | denied | **EXEMPT** | **EXEMPT — open** |
| 1e `ENV RUNTIME_PKG=nodejs` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1g line-continuation `apk add nodejs` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1h alpine + copied node binary + `/app` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1i nginx + copied node binary + `/app` | denied | **EXEMPT** | denied (nodeish) |
| 1b / 1f (controls) | denied | denied | denied |

**Why the gate's second fix-shape was withdrawn.** It reads: *"an allow-listed base should not be exempt when the stage copies a whole directory from another stage."* Two implementations were written and both were reverted:

1. **Structural** (source path is a top-level directory, fewer than two segments below root). With it in place the guard suite went **41 passed / 12 failed**, and the reds included *"F-6 inv: nginx is still EXEMPT — the case the exemption exists for"* and *"nginx behind a REGISTRY prefix is EXEMPT — not a false block"*. Cause, measured: **every** `nonjs_case` fixture — and every real class file — contains `COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared`, a one-segment source.
2. **WORKDIR-aware** (source equals the source stage's working directory). Measured across the repo: `shared-builder` is declared `WORKDIR /shared` followed by `npm ci` in every Dockerfile that has it. So `/shared` **is** that stage's workdir and does hold a node tree — this rule matches it too.

`COPY --from=shared-builder /shared /shared` is not incidental: it is the line that makes a file a class file at all (46+ occurrences). A rule that denies it denies the entire class. The only escapes are (a) exempting `/shared` **by name** — a new allow-list, i.e. the deny-list-wearing-a-comment shape this whole round removed — or (b) accepting that the arm can essentially never grant an exemption in this repo, which removes the arm. **Both are decisions, not cleanups, which is why this is a ticket and not a commit.**

**What bounds the residue.** Every variant of row 1d that names something able to RUN the copied tree is now denied — measured: a copied `node` binary, `CMD ["node", …]`, `ENTRYPOINT ["/app/node"]`, `bun`, `deno`. What remains cannot execute what it copied, so it cannot produce the #851 crash-on-start that this guard exists for.

**The hole that is genuinely left:** an image that reaches a runtime through a file the guard cannot read — `CMD ["/app/start.sh"]` where `start.sh` runs node. No text signal in the Dockerfile names the runtime. That is not fixable by any parser of Dockerfiles alone.

**Also latent, not live:** the repo currently contains **no** `COPY --from=X /app /app` (census of every `COPY --from=` at head: `/app/dist`, `/app/node_modules`, `/shared`, and single sub-paths), and all 25 class files write node_modules in their final stage, so **none reaches the exemption arm at all** (verified with `SHARED_RELINK_VERBOSE=1` — every file reports `reinstall` or `copy-node_modules`).

**Pinned, not silent:** `check_shared_relink.test.sh` carries a cell named *"R2 row 1d: KNOWN OPEN …"* asserting the current exempt behaviour, so the day it changes something fails and a human reads why.

**Source:** #876 tier-1 verdict 2026-09-06T22:04:18Z, finding 1. **Discovered/measured:** 2026-09-07, session 144, during #876 round 2.

title: KS-858 residue: the repeated-slash collapse does not complete for the /api/billing mount — leading // still 404s where /api/governance does not
description:
**BLUF** — the KS-858 edge normalisation closes the repeated-slash class on 66 of the 67 declared gateway mount classes. `/api/billing` with a **leading** `//` still 404s. **Nothing got worse** — base 404 → head 404 — but this is the class fix not being uniform, on a ticket whose whole point is the class.

**Measured by the #884 tier-1 gate, deterministic 5/5 and again on a controlled repeat:**

```
HEAD  /api/billing/SAME     -> 401 "No token provided"   (reaches the billing upstream)
HEAD  /api/billing//SAME    -> 401 "No token provided"   (interior // fixed)
HEAD  //api/billing/SAME    -> 404 "Route POST /api/billing/SAME not found"
HEAD  //api/billing//SAME   -> 404
BASE  //api/billing/SAME    -> 404 "Route POST //api/billing/SAME not found"
```

The 404 body carries the **canonical** path, which proves `req.path` was canonicalised before the 404 handler ran — the request simply never produced billing's 401.

**Positive control that this is not the general case:** `//api/governance/zzqa` returns the upstream's own `401 No token provided`, identical to its canonical spelling. So leading-`//` does reach proxy mounts in general.

**Mechanism NOT determined.** The gate's candidate, explicitly unverified: billing is the mount whose `pathRewrite` is `{'^/api': ''}` while its neighbours self-map (`{'^/api/governance': '/api/governance'}`), so the rewrite anchor and the deliberately-untouched `req.originalUrl` may interact. **Reproduce before fixing** — and reproduce it against the round-2 head, not round 1, since round 2 changed how the target is split.

**Where:** `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` (billing mount + its pathRewrite); `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/middleware/normalisePath.ts`.
**Source:** #884 tier-1 verdict 2026-09-06T21:50:32Z, finding F-QA-3 (severity Minor). **Discovered:** 2026-09-07, session 144.

title: The default-password CI gate catches one shape and calls it clean — 16 published passwords are exempt by design, and 4 of 5 canaries walk past it
description:
## The finding

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh` is a **live CI gate** (`pr-security-gates.yml:63`, `security-scan.yml:422`). It is far blinder than its name suggests, and the documented exemption is the *small* half.

## The exemption (known, by design)

Line 34 is `| grep -v 'seedPw(' \`. With **only that line deleted** (sha-asserted both ways and restored), the lint exits 1 with **16 flagged lines — sixteen other seeded accounts' published default passwords**, invisible to it by design.

## The blind spots (not by design)

Five canaries planted through the real script:

| plant | result |
| -- | -- |
| `services/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | **SEEN** — positive control, the instrument is live |
| `services/`, `.ts`, not ending `123` | MISSED — any other password shape |
| `frontend/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `services/` and `packages/` are scanned |
| `services/`, `.sql`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `.ts/.tsx/.js`; **the seed SQL that** `fixtures.ts` **cites as source-of-truth is invisible** |
| `scripts/` subdir, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — `--exclude-dir=scripts,tests,__tests__` |

So the gate catches exactly one shape — a `*123` literal, in a `.ts/.tsx/.js` file, under `services/` or `packages/`, not in an excluded directory, and not behind `seedPw(`.

## Why this is worth its own ticket

A guard with a documented exemption is a guard with a hole of a **known** size — and the hole never appears in the guard's own green result. This one passes today, passed before [KS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-949), and would have passed with the real-person account and its published password still in place. It is a live gate that gives false assurance in CI.

- [ ] Widen the file-type and directory scope, or state the scope in the gate's own output so a green result says what it actually covered
- [ ] Decide whether the `seedPw(` exemption should survive at all now that one account (the platform admin) is held to a stricter rule than the lint enforces
- [ ] A password shape that is not `*123`

## Provenance

The exemption and the `docker-compose.yml:755` default were disclosed by the filer while doing KS-949 and **confirmed at source** by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #885 (2026-09-06T21:29:45Z); the 16-line count and the five canaries are the gate's measurement, not the filer's.

*Filed by s143 (seat A), 2026-09-07.*

title: A backtick in a shell-suite case name executes as a command and rewrote package.json mid-run — every cell still PASSED; 9 suites share the pattern
description:
## A backtick in a shell-suite case name is COMMAND SUBSTITUTION — it runs, and the pass/fail column says nothing

Found by walking into it on KS-945. **Nine tracked shell suites share the vulnerable call-site**
**pattern.** No suite carries a live instance right now, so this is a latent hazard, not an outage.

### What happened

Case names are passed as the first argument to a helper (`expect "name" <exit> '<body>' …`), so the
name sits in a **double-quoted shell word at the call site**. Seven KS-945 case names were written
with markdown-style backticks for readability:

```
expect "KS-945: `npm add` is an install" 1 '…'
expect "KS-945: `npm init <package-spec>` installs, unlike `npm init -y`" 1 '…'
```

The shell ran them. During a suite run this executed `npm add`, `npm it`, `pnpm add`, `yarn` and
`npm init` **for real, in the working tree**:

* `npm init` rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package.json` — 14 insertions, 4 deletions, including rewriting
  the unicode escapes in two long `// overrides` comments and changing the `repository.url`.
* The package managers rewrote `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` — 12 insertions, 31 deletions.

Both were restored from `HEAD` and verified byte-identical, `git status` clean on both paths. Nothing
was committed and nothing left the machine.

### Why it belongs to the KS-926 family

**It was invisible in the pass/fail column. Every affected cell still PASSED.** The suite reported
`50 passed, 0 failed` while rewriting two tracked files underneath itself.

It surfaced only because a *red-proof* run — a deliberate tamper, run for an unrelated reason —
printed package-manager output **inside its FAIL lines**:

```
FAIL: KS-945: bare yarn install v1.22.22
FAIL: KS-945: [ERR_PNPM_MISSING_PACKAGE_NAME] `pnpm add` requires the package name is an install
FAIL: KS-945:  installs, unlike Wrote to …/Blockchain/Dev/package.json:
```

A green run could not show it, because the substitution output was swallowed into a name that was
never printed on success. **The tamper is what made it visible** — which is the family's own thesis.

### Scope, with a control

* **0 of 14** tracked `*.test.sh` currently contain an unescaped backtick in a case name. **That zero**
  **discriminates:** the same query run against a deliberately bad file detects it (verified in the
  same batch), so it is a real zero and not a query that cannot match.
* **9 of 14** use the `expect()` helper and therefore share the call-site shape:
  `run_in_slot`, `slot_target`, `stop_secuura`, `stack_guard`, `check_shared_relink`,
  `check_container_isolation`, `preflight_deps`, `stack_env`, `check_script_portability`.

### Fix shape

`check_shared_relink.test.sh` now carries a per-suite check that refuses an unescaped backtick in any
case name (added in KS-945, red-proofed **without executing the tamper** — the check is a grep, so it
was run against a bad name directly). **That guard should move up into**
`run-shell-suites.sh` **so it covers all fourteen**, rather than being re-implemented per suite — which
is itself the KS-926 mechanism-1 shape: a check that exists in one place and is absent everywhere else.

Worth considering alongside: have the helper reject a name containing a backtick outright, so the
failure is a clear message rather than a silent execution.

### Provenance

* the executed commands and the two rewritten files | observed in a red-proof run of
  `check_shared_relink.test.sh`; `git diff --stat` on both paths before restore; restore verified with
  `git diff --quiet HEAD` | measured 2026-09-07
* 0 of 14 and 9 of 14, with the known-bad control | `git ls-files '*.test.sh'` piped through the same
  query, plus a purpose-built bad file that the query detects | measured 2026-09-07

title: Launcher suite: four side-effect and guarded-surface gaps from the KS-911/912 gate (incl. a SILENT destructive path on settings.local.json)
description:
Four pre-existing launcher findings from the KS-911/KS-912 by-hash gate (`PASS WITH FINDINGS`, 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z). **None was introduced by KS-911/912** — the tester says so explicitly — and none blocked the relaunch. Grouped as one path: the suite's no-damage claim and its side-effect surface.

`L`-numbers are against the shipped launcher `sha256 932a2cc3aebe6cf838bf885ac92eec08e259f0572c0e08910088ac58e269f55c`.

- [ ] **F-2 (MINOR) — the guard fails OPEN for a live seat when suite eviction composes with the documented** `SECUURA_SEAT_SCAN=0` **escape hatch.** Measured with one live fixture seat throughout:

  ```
  boot, scan OFF, BEFORE the suite : count=1, says pull: NO
  run the suite                    : seat still ALIVE, entry EVICTED from the registry
  boot, scan OFF, AFTER the suite  : count=0, says pull: YES
  ```

  Needs both halves, so it is narrow — but the escape hatch exists for the day the scan over-matches, which is also a day someone may run the suite. **Fix:** back up and restore the real `SEAT_FILE` the way the suite already backs up the preflight log, or route every registry case through `LAUNCH_TMPDIR` so the suite never writes the real registry.
- [ ] **F-3 (MINOR) — the "must not damage the live project" claim guards 1 of the 2 repos the launcher writes.** The launcher writes `user.name`/`user.email` to `${PROJECT_DIR%/*}/Extranet` at `L202-208` (KS-148) exactly as it does to `2_Project_Files`, but only `2_Project_Files/.git/config` is hashed before and after. Evidence: with the sandbox Extranet's email set to `kamil.kreiser@datasec.com.au`, **one** suite execution rewrote it to `kamil.kreiser@secuura.ai` — md5 `61238ef0` -> `8a2f8bda`, **cells that noticed: 0**. The write is intended and idempotent in steady state, so this is a guarded-surface gap rather than a launcher defect — but it is the one place workspace hard rule #5 (never mix GitHub accounts) is enforced, so it belongs inside the assertion. **Fix:** hash the Extranet config alongside `REPO_CFG`, skipping cleanly when the clone is absent.
- [ ] **F-4 (MINOR) —** `.claude/settings.local.json` **is rewritten on every launcher run (8 per suite execution) and guarded by no cell, and its failure mode is silent destruction.** A hand-formatted one-line file was reformatted by a single dry run (md5 `01ab75cd` -> `561024c9`); unrelated keys survive. But the embedded python at `L221-242` does `except Exception: data = {}` — so an **unparseable** file is silently discarded. Measured: a file containing `not json at all` came back as a fresh two-key JSON document, prior content gone, **nothing on stdout or stderr**. Pre-existing, but it sits inside the suite's own no-damage claim and it is a silent destructive path.
- [ ] **F-5 (POLISH) — the fix quotes its own detector.** The KS-911 F1 comment at `L246-247` reproduces the removed sentinel verbatim, so `grep -rl 'do not edit the sentinels'` still lists `Launch_Claude.command` itself. Any future check written as "is the sentinel gone?" reads non-zero forever. **Fix:** describe the removed wording instead of reproducing it.

**Not a finding, recorded so the next person to touch the trap sees it:** the suite's EXIT trap kills its fixtures with job control live, so bash prints `Terminated: 15` to stderr *after* the totals. Cosmetic, predates this change, same family as the operator-pane noise F-2 of KS-911 removed.

⚠️ **Do not fix while two seats are live** — the launcher is live on disk under a by-hash gate. `.pre-` restore copies exist for both files.

Source: `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura SEAT B KS-911 + KS-912 (launcher, by hash)` 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z, forwarded whole and read here. F-1 and the registry's `exec` premise are filed separately — different mechanism. Follows [[KS-911]] / [[KS-912]].

title: Launcher: the assembled boot prompt is asserted by no cell — KS-907's fix can vanish at 18/0, and the seat sentence misled a live seat tonight
description:
**Nothing asserts what the boot prompt actually SAYS.** The launcher computes `$GIT_SYNC_STEP`, the suite reads it from a standalone marker, and the prompt the session actually receives is checked by no cell. Two consumers have now been proven wrong through that gap in one night.

## Item 1 — `$GIT_SYNC_STEP` never reaches an assertion (QA FINDING 1, MAJOR)

The `DRY_RUN` markers at `L659` print the variable **directly**. The boot prompt consumes it **separately** at `L483`. Two independent consumers of one variable; the suite reads only the first.

QA evidence — a one-line tamper (`887c3c23`) replacing `${GIT_SYNC_STEP}` at `L483` with literal text, marker untouched:

```
suite result:  18 passed, 0 FAILED   — every cell green
boot prompt:   199 lines -> 191 lines, "pull latest on the current branch" GONE
```

Proven with an instrumented pair (shipped + tampered, each printing `$INITIAL_PROMPT` under dry-run): shipped YES, tampered NO.

**Impact:** a future edit near `L483` — a 200-line block that is edited often — silently reverts KS-907 while the guard stays 18/0. KS-907 exists because a second seat's boot fast-forwarded a live branch under the first seat, before that session had read the brief telling it it was a second seat.

## Item 2 — the seat sentence reads as an assignment, and it misled a live seat tonight

Seat A was told by its boot prompt that its working copy was `worktrees/seat-b` — **this seat's worktree.** Seat A measured the pane mapping, disbelieved the launcher, and proceeded correctly as seat A; nothing was written into the wrong tree. A seat that trusted the line would have written into another live session's worktree.

Seat A's measurement, verbatim:

> pane %130 -> pane_pid 1790 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain" (no -B) = SEAT A = me
> pane %129 -> pane_pid 89454 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain-B" = SEAT B = s140e,
>             live since 22:24:23, PID 89456, working in worktrees/seat-b

**⚠️ The mechanism is NOT what it was handed to me as, and the correction changes the fix.** It was relayed as "the seat registry decides which worktree a pane is told to use, and no cell asserts the assignment is right." Measured here: **there is no assignment mechanism at all, and the registry has nothing to do with it.**

```
L344-346:  SEAT_WORKTREES="$(ls -1 "$PROJECT_DIR/worktrees" | sed 's|^|worktrees/|' ...)"
L363:      Sync YOUR OWN working copy instead${SEAT_WORKTREES:+ (this project has: ${SEAT_WORKTREES})},
```

`SEAT_WORKTREES` is a plain directory listing, **byte-identical for every pane**. `grep -c SEAT_WORKTREES` = 3, all three above. The sentence states a true fact — but its subject is *"YOUR OWN working copy"*, so a one-entry list reads as an assignment. With exactly one worktree present, that misreading is at its maximum.

The launcher says so itself at `L261`: *"The cockpit passes NOTHING that distinguishes the seats — both panes invoke a byte-identical command line."*

So this is a **wording defect plus a missing capability**, not a wrong computed value — nothing computed the wrong seat. The existing mitigation is the very next clause (*"if you have not been told which one is yours, ask before writing anywhere"*), and it worked: this seat asked, seat A measured.

**Fix shape (two options, the first is trivially safe):**

1. Reword so the list cannot read as ownership — e.g. *"this project contains the following worktrees: …; if you have not been told which is yours, ask."*
2. Actually derive the pane's seat. The cockpit label **is** reachable — it is in the parent shell's command line, which is how both seats identified themselves tonight (`ps -o command` on the launcher's own parent shows `[cockpit] Secuura/Blockchain-B exited`). That is a feature, not a guard, and it should not be attempted while two seats are live.

## Item 3 — the premise the whole registry rests on is asserted by no cell (QA NOT-TESTED 2)

The QA agent rated this **above FINDING 1**. The launcher registers `$$` and its `lstart` believing `exec` **replaces** the process, keeping pid and start time. The dry run `exit 0`s instead of exec'ing, so the entry it writes is stale the instant it is written. `exec claude … "$INITIAL_PROMPT"` (`L663`) is the only line below the dry-run exit and **is exercised by nothing** — not the suite, not the QA pass.

If that line were ever changed to anything that forks (a wrapper, `claude &`, `bash -c`), every registry entry would be invalid on arrival, the guard would silently stop working, and all 18 cells would stay green.

## Why these are one ticket

All three are the same mechanism: **a value the launcher computes correctly, consumed somewhere no cell looks.** Items 1 and 2 are literally the same variable's journey into `$INITIAL_PROMPT`; item 3 is the assumption that the prompt is ever `exec`'d at all. One fix — emit the assembled prompt behind a `DRY_RUN_INITIAL_PROMPT` marker and assert its **text** — makes all three assertable.

## Regression tests

Two cells against the assembled prompt, not the marker: empty registry -> prompt contains PULLTEXT; one live seat -> contains ROTEXT and **not** PULLTEXT. Red-proof by deleting the `L483` interpolation and requiring exactly those cells to fail. Item 2 adds a third: the prompt's named-worktree text against the pane's own cockpit label.

⚠️ **Do not fix the launcher while two seats are live.** It is live on disk under a by-hash gate; a relaunch is gated. `.pre-` restore copies exist for both files.

Sources: QA verdict `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura SEAT B KS-911 + KS-912 (launcher, by hash)` 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z, read whole; item 2 from Wednesday's addendum quoting seat A, with the mechanism re-measured in this seat and corrected. Follows [[KS-911]] / [[KS-912]].

title: Launcher boot step tells every agent session to POST /api/seen as EXTRANET_ME=kam, which clears Kam's own unread flags — and the extranet is input-only
description:
## What is wrong

`Launch_Claude.command:522` (boot step 7) instructs every session:

> "…GET the summary for this operator (EXTRANET_ME), and fold my open tasks + replies-to-me + new documents into the confirmation below; **mark seen afterwards**."

which routes to the `extranet` skill's step 3:

> `POST $EXTRANET_URL/api/seen {"person":"$EXTRANET_ME"}` so "new" resets next session.

And in this project's `4_Credentials/.env`:

```
EXTRANET_ME=kam
```

So the "operator" an agent marks caught-up as **is Kam himself**. An agent that follows the boot step clears **Kam's** unread flags on his own portal — the tasks, replies and documents he has not yet read. The next time he opens the extranet, the things an agent read on his behalf are no longer marked new to him.

It is the human's signal, and an automated session destroys it as a side effect of booting.

## Why it is a defect and not a preference

Two independent reasons, either of which is sufficient:

1. `EXTRANET_ME` **is doing two jobs.** It identifies *whose* summary to fetch — correct, an agent working for Kam should see Kam's queue — and it also identifies *who has now seen it* — wrong, because the agent saw it and Kam did not. One variable, two meanings, and the second one is only ever wrong when an agent uses it.
2. **The extranet is input-only for agents** (standing rule for this project). `POST /api/seen` is a write. The boot step asks for a write the operating rules forbid, so the instruction cannot be followed as stated regardless of who `EXTRANET_ME` names.

## Reproduced

Not by running it — running it *is* the defect, and it is not reversible from the API. Established from the artefacts instead:

* `4_Credentials/.env:4` → `EXTRANET_ME=kam` (agent key on line 3 not reproduced here)
* `Launch_Claude.command:522` → the "mark seen afterwards" instruction
