* `Notes (MASTER)/skills/Current/extranet.md:27` → the `POST /api/seen {"person":"$EXTRANET_ME"}` step
* `…/extranet.md:111` → `POST /api/seen | {person}` in the endpoint table

The three artefacts compose into the behaviour without needing to execute it. **This session declined the step and said so rather than skipping it silently** — that is the current mitigation, and it relies on every future session making the same judgement, which is not a control.

## Fix shape

Any of these closes it; the first is the smallest:

1. **Drop "mark seen afterwards" from the launcher's step 7** and the corresponding step from the skill, for agent sessions. The summary is read-only; nothing needs the flag reset, and "new since last session" is more useful to an agent unreset anyway.
2. **Separate the two meanings** — `EXTRANET_ME` for whose queue to read, a distinct `EXTRANET_SEEN_AS` for whose flags to clear, unset by default so the write never happens unless someone deliberately sets it.
3. **Make** `/api/seen` **refuse an agent key** for a person other than the key's own identity, server-side, so no launcher wording can cause it. This one belongs to the extranet app rather than the launcher.

## Scope

The launcher is a per-project copy of a master template, so fixing this copy does not fix the others — the same boot step exists in every project's launcher, and any project whose `EXTRANET_ME` names a human has the same defect. Whoever picks this up should decide at the template level, not here.

Filed at Wednesday's direction (2026-09-06) after this session declined the boot step. Not applied mid-queue: the launcher is not this seat's to edit.

title: Demo platform-admin account has mfa_enabled = false — deliberate demo posture, or a gap that outlived KS-737?
description:
## The demo platform-admin account has MFA disabled — decision needed, not a fix

**Measured, not inferred.** Found while running the KS-913 pre-check on the demo box (read-only).

| property | value |
| -- | -- |
| id | `a0000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000060` |
| role | `system_admin` |
| status | `active`, `email_verified = true` |
| `mfa_enabled` | `false` |
| credential | `$argon2…`, unique among the 30 users |
| last login | **2026-07-14 10:36:41Z — the account is genuinely used** |

This is the demo environment's real platform-admin account, reachable at the public demo URL.

### Why this is a question and not a defect report

[KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) — *platform-admin login skips MFA entirely when* `mfaCode` *is omitted* — is **archived**. I have **not** established whether this row is the same case, a deliberate demo posture (an admin nobody wants to carry a TOTP device for on a throwaway environment), or a gap that outlived its ticket. Establishing that would mean testing an authentication path against a real person's account, which I am not doing to close an observation.

**So this ticket carries the measurement only.** No fix is proposed and nothing changes until it is ruled on.

### The decision

Is MFA-off on the demo `system_admin` intended? If **yes**, close this and the row is documented for the next reviewer who trips over it. If **no**, it becomes a remediation ticket and should say whether it is demo-only or reaches the same code path as KS-737.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the KS-913 pre-check.* `needs-decision`*.*

title: vite is a production dependency of services/auth — esbuild and fsevents ship into the runtime image, imported by nothing
description:
## `vite` sits in auth's production `dependencies`, dragging esbuild and fsevents into the runtime image

Found by the #849 (KS-490) tier-2 gate as F-2, and measured before filing.

### The measurement

| Reading | Value |
| -- | -- |
| `services/auth/package.json` → `dependencies.vite` | `7.3.6` |
| `services/auth/package.json` → `devDependencies.vite` | **absent** |
| runtime sources under `services/auth/src` importing `vite` (excluding `__tests__`) | **0** |
| CONTROL: runtime sources importing `express` | **15** |

The control is what makes the zero mean something — the same grep shape finds 15 files for a package auth genuinely uses at runtime, so 0 for `vite` is a real absence and not a grep that cannot match.

### Why it matters

Because `vite` is a production dependency it survives `npm prune --omit=dev` and `npm ci --omit=dev`, and it pulls `esbuild 0.28.1` and `fsevents 2.3.3` with it. Both carry install scripts, which is why auth's production set shows three `hasInstallScript` entries where the estate has only one package that actually requires compilation.

**This is not a security finding on its own** — the runtime `npm ci --ignore-scripts` means none of those install scripts ever runs, and that is why #849 passed. It is image weight and attack surface: a build toolchain shipped into a running container that no runtime code imports.

### The fix

Move `vite` to `devDependencies` in `services/auth/package.json`, regenerate the lock, and re-measure the runtime `node_modules` file count (the tester counted **5,591 files** in auth's runtime tree). Expect esbuild, rollup and fsevents to leave with it.

**Verify before assuming:** confirm nothing in auth's build path (not just `src/`) needs `vite` at runtime — a config file or a script entry could. The import walk above covers `src/` only.

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from #849's gate findings.*

title: A clean stack has no supported way to obtain its first privileged account
description:
## The gap

On a freshly built stack there is no supported path to a first privileged account:

* `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` is now default-deny (B-3 hardening) and needs **both** `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` and `ENABLE_DEMO_SEED=true`.
* Registration cannot mint a privileged role — KS-82 deliberately refuses a client-supplied role.

Both of those are **correct** and neither is questioned here. The gap is that nothing owns the bootstrap step, because historically the seed accounts were simply always present, so no one had to.

## Status of the original claim — corrected

An earlier KS-487 comment (2026-09-01 11:36Z) asserted a hard **deadlock**: that a clean stack could never call `seed-demo-users` at all. **That was retracted 21 minutes later by its own author** (11:57Z) — `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:47` fires `userRepo.seedDemoUsers()`, so there is no deadlock. This ticket carries the *remaining* gap only: not "impossible", but "undocumented and unowned".

## What would close it

One of: a documented first-run procedure naming the two env vars and their intended lifetime; or a one-shot bootstrap command that creates a single named admin without the demo-persona list; or an explicit decision that operators set the env vars, written where an operator will find it (`DEV-PROCESS.md` or the deployment runbook).

## Provenance

Recorded on [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487) as prose (2026-09-01, with its correction) rather than a ticket, because the Linear workspace was at its free issue cap. The cap was lifted 2026-09-06, so it is filed now. **This is the finding whose existence-only-in-prose was the reason the table was built.**

*Filed by s140 (seat A), 2026-09-06, from the KS-487 stream-B table.*

title: Audit the eleven cwd- and script-relative repo-root derivations under scripts/ and systemTest/ — one family, several blind in different ways
description: ## BLUF**The** `$(cd ../.. && pwd)` **/** `$(dirname "$0")/../..` **family appears eleven times across** `scripts/` **and** `systemTest/`**, in at least three variants with different failure modes.** KS-859 fixed one of them (`no-tracked-credentials.sh`); the rest are unaudited.## ScopeEnumerate every repo-root derivation under `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/` and `systemTest/`, classify each as script-relative, cwd-relative, or git-derived, and record for each whether it is:- **layout-dependent** (breaks where the repo root is not two levels up — the KS-859 defect), and/or- **cwd-dependent** (breaks when invoked from elsewhere — worse), and/or- **env-dependent** (breaks under an inherited git environment).Known starting points, measured at `34347a8fa`: `action-pins-labelled.sh:46` and `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh:57` are cwd-relative. `run-shell-suites.sh:45` **is NOT blind** — its KS-731 zero-suites guard fails loudly, and is the model for what a safe one looks like.## Why one ticket rather than elevenThis is a survey, not a defect: the deliverable is the classification plus a ticket per genuinely-blind site. Filing eleven speculative tickets before measuring would be the aggregation shape Kam withdrew.## Fix shapeThe audit first. Then, per blind site, the KS-859 idiom — ask git from a self-derived directory with the environment scrubbed — and a shared helper if the count justifies one.Charter named by the #858 gate as its round-2 work. Parent: KS-859, merged at `34347a8fafb5feca69d59dcee12b8aca9ce4a69d`.

title: no-tracked-credentials.sh cites two scripts as "structurally immune" exemplars — both use a WORSE cwd-relative root derivation
description: ## BLUF**The comment added by #858 points the next reader at two scripts as exemplars of the safe idiom. Both use a strictly worse one.**`no-tracked-credentials.sh:81-82` says:> `bare-path-scripts-executable.sh` and `action-pins-labelled.sh` already derive their root this way and are structurally immune; this is the same idiom.Measured at the merged tip `34347a8fa`:`action-pins-labelled.sh:46          REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"bare-path-scripts-executable.sh:57  REPO_ROOT="$(cd ../.. && pwd)"`That is **cwd-relative**, not script-relative. It depends on the caller's working directory, where the idiom the comment describes (`$(dirname "$0")/../..`) does not. They are not immune, and they are not the same idiom.## Why it mattersThe comment is load-bearing prose: it exists to tell the next person what shape to copy. Pointing at a worse form is how the family spreads.## Fix shapeCorrect the comment to describe the idiom without endorsing those two, and either fix their derivations or reference the audit ticket that covers them.Residue of the #858 tier-2 gate (F-QA-01, Minor). Parent: KS-859, merged at `34347a8fafb5feca69d59dcee12b8aca9ce4a69d`.

title: KS-869's COALESCE backfill has an EMPTY window — the 39 pre-existing keys never backfill, so the KS-843 cutover flip still has no usable evidence
description:
## BLUF

**KS-869 does not fix the KS-843 cutover's evidence problem for keys that already exist.** The `COALESCE(EXCLUDED.connector_id, svc_api_keys.connector_id)` backfill I described as filling pre-fix rows "for free" **has no window in which to fire**. Found by the KS-869 tier-1 gate; **correcting my own claim** in that PR body.

## Why the window is empty

`connectorId` enters an `ApiKey` object in exactly two places:

* at **mint** (`services/security/src/index.ts:1004`), or
* from the **row** (`:345`, `rowToApiKey`)

`memApiKeys` is warmed **only from the database at boot** (`:376-381`). The deploy restarts the service, so every pre-fix row re-warms with `connectorId` **undefined**; every later save therefore passes NULL; and `COALESCE` correctly declines to overwrite with NULL. **"The next save backfills it for free" is true only for keys minted after this deploys.**

## The consequence, and it lands on KS-843

Kam's 2026-09-06 13:59 logged-grace ruling flips `SUBJECTS_ERASE_SCOPE_ENFORCED` **once the log shows Platform S on the new key**. After KS-869 merges and deploys, the `[KS-843]` grace log will **still record** `connectorId: null` **for every EXISTING Platform S key**. The flip's evidence is not restored by KS-869 alone.

## FIRST ITEM — the measurement that decides the fix

**Does anything on the row determine the connector?** Check `key_prefix`, `organization_id`, `name` (the mint sets `name` to `Platform S connector — <org|externalRef>`) against the 39 existing rows (measured 2026-09-06; this ticket originally said 43). If one of them does, a one-off backfill is possible. If none does, **the answer is a re-mint of Platform S's keys** — which is Stuart's window and therefore Kam's call, and it merges with the KS-577 rotation conversation rather than being a separate ask.

## Acceptance

Either the 43 rows carry a correct `connector_id` (backfilled from a source named in the measurement above), or a ruling is recorded that Platform S's keys will be re-minted, with the flip explicitly waiting on it. **KS-843's cutover comment must be updated either way** — today it says KS-869 is the prerequisite; if that is not sufficient, it should say so.

title: Every ADMITTED erasure authenticates twice — the door's chain and the catch-all both run authenticateToken, doubling a remote key validation on a partner path
description:
## BLUF

On the erasure path an **admitted** request authenticates **twice**; a refused one authenticates once. Measured fresh by the round-3 gate across 14 shapes × 2 modes: **refused = 1, admitted = 2**.

Carried out of KS-861 when #845 merged, per the ruling that F-11 is a follow-up and not a gate item. **Not a live defect — a cost defect on a partner-facing path.**

## Mechanism

`services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts`:

* `:677` — the erasure door's chain carries `authenticateToken(true)`
* `:696` — the catch-all `router.use('/api/gdpr', authenticateToken(true), proxy('originate', …))` carries it again

An admitted request passes through the door, `next()`s, and hits the catch-all's copy. A refused one is stopped by the responding handler, so the second never runs — the correct direction, and why this is a cost issue rather than a correctness one.

## Why it matters

In production `authenticateToken` validates an `sk_` key **over HTTP** to the security service — `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:257` → `validateApiKey:209` → `POST /api/keys/validate`. So every admitted erasure doubles a remote call on a partner-facing path. It surfaces as latency, not as an error, which is why nothing has flagged it.

## Fix shape (from the round-2 tester)

Either the door's chain omits `authenticateToken` and relies on the catch-all's, or `authenticateToken` short-circuits when `req.user` is already set. **The second touches shared auth middleware and therefore every route** — it wants its own measurement rather than being folded in as an obvious win.

## Note on the round-3 fix

The F-9 fix (an inner express `Router`) was checked against this and **does not** close it for free — that was the stated condition for folding it into round 3, and it was not met.

## Acceptance

An admitted erasure invokes `authenticateToken` **once**, driven by counting invocations of an injected factory (the harness in `ks843-erasure-path-bypass.test.ts` already injects one); a refused erasure still invokes it once; guardrail behaviour and the 403/200 outcomes across the 14 shapes are unchanged.

title: Merge protocol: the server-side `sha=` pin protects the PR head, not the base — a 9-second race merged onto an unapproved parent and invalidated the gate's predicted tree oid
description:
## BLUF

**The merge protocol we were running could not enforce its own central assertion.** "Sha-asserted against a tip re-read in the same minutes" was executed via `PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/merge -f sha=…` — and **that** `sha` **pins the pull request's HEAD. There is no base parameter on that endpoint.** So the base could move between the assertion and GitHub executing the merge, and the merge would silently succeed onto a parent nobody had approved.

Measured, not theorised. This ticket is the record for the next reader; the fix is already ruled and in force.

## What happened (PR #852, 2026-09-06)

| time | event |
| -- | -- |
| 04:27:09Z | asserted `develop` = `81bf7b078`, exactly as the GO named |
| 04:27:18Z | **#848 (the other seat) merged** → `606aa385b` |
| 04:27:20Z | #852 merged onto `606aa385b`, **not** `81bf7b078` |

A **nine-second** window, with the protocol followed exactly.

## What it cost

**Nothing in content.** #848 touched only `.githooks/pre-push`; #852 touched only four `deployment/azure` files; `git diff --name-only 81bf7b078 af078257` returns all five, so both landed and the sets are disjoint.

**Something in evidence.** The gate's predicted merge-tree oid `82acc2da…` was computed against `81bf7b078` and is **not** the tree that exists — the real tree is `39acb349…`. A reviewer checking the merge against the predicted oid finds a mismatch and is right to stop. That is the actual damage: a correct merge that cannot be checked against its own gate's prediction.

## The ruling now in force (both seats)

1. Merge from **your own checkout**: `git ls-remote origin develop` → `git fetch origin develop` → `git merge --no-ff --no-edit <pr-head-sha>` onto `origin/develop` as read → `git push origin HEAD:develop`.
2. **No** `--force`**, no** `--force-with-lease`**.** A plain push already refuses a non-fast-forward, so **a base that moved turns a silent wrong merge into a refused push** — which is exactly the property wanted. On refusal: re-read, re-merge onto the new tip, push again, and **the receipt names both attempts**.
3. **Every receipt carries the base line:** `first parent = <sha>` beside `asserted = <sha>`. Equal → "base held". Different → name what landed, whether the file sets are disjoint (measured with `diff --name-only`), and that the gate's predicted tree does not apply.
4. A gate's predicted merge-tree oid is carried as **"predicted against base** `<sha>`**"**. A differing first parent invalidates the **prediction**, not the merge — re-derive `merge-tree` against the real first parent and name the new oid.
5. The server-side `PUT … sha=` shape stays acceptable **only for a seat merging alone**, which with two parallel seats is never.
6. **Serialising the seats was explicitly not ruled** — parallel stays. The mechanism above is what makes a lost race safe.

## Why this is filed rather than just fixed

The mechanism is already in force from the next merge. What a ticket preserves is the *reason*: a future reader seeing `PUT … sha=` in old receipts, or wondering why we push a merge commit by ref instead of using the API, needs the nine-second timeline above — otherwise the API call looks simpler and someone reintroduces it.

## Acceptance

No further build. Closed when the merge shape above appears in `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` alongside the existing merge-flow section, with the timeline as its justification.

title: `@secuura/shared` `main` points at an untracked, never-built `dist/index.js` — anything outside vitest's alias resolves to nothing
description:
**Category 1. Low. AUTHORISED, UNFILED — Linear's free-tier cap is refusing creation.**

## BLUF

`packages/shared/package.json` `main` points at `dist/index.js`. `dist/` **is gitignored, untracked, and no install step builds it.** In a tree that has never run a build, `require.resolve('@secuura/shared')` **throws** `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

Measured 2026-09-06 during the KS-830 cell, in a fresh clone at `904ca6ef2` after a clean `npm ci` (1937 packages, exit 0):

|  | working checkout | fresh clone |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `require.resolve('@secuura/shared')` | `packages/shared/dist/index.js` | **THROWS** `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` |
| entry sha256 | `52ff4828de770b62669e828139c1d03b72834fb82c38f85ab1538fdddd38bce9` | n/a |
| `dist/` present after `npm ci` | YES (built earlier by hand) | **NO** |
| `npm ls @secuura/shared` | `@secuura/shared@0.3.0 -> ./packages/shared` | **identical** |

The workspace symlink is the same in both. The only variable is whether somebody has run a build in that tree.

## Why it is currently invisible

`packages/shared/vitest.config.ts` aliases `@secuura/shared` to `src/index.ts`, and that alias covers the whole of the shared test suite's import graph — so **the suites are green in both trees** and nothing surfaces the gap. The alias's own comment explains it was added for class identity (KS-727), not for resolvability; the resolvability fix is a side effect nobody declared.

## Why it is worth a ticket anyway

Anything in that package that runs **outside** vitest's alias — a script, a tool, a `node -e`, a consumer resolving the workspace package by name without a prior build — resolves to nothing on a fresh checkout. A new developer or a CI job that does not build first gets `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from a package that `npm ls` reports as correctly linked, which is a confusing failure to diagnose.

**Priority Low, deliberately:** nothing is broken today, no suite depends on it, and the alias hides it everywhere it currently matters. This is a trap, not a defect.

## Fix shapes (not chosen — whoever picks this up should)

* Add a `prepare` script so the workspace builds on install; or
* point `main` at `src/index.ts` and let consumers transpile; or
* declare `exports` with a source condition.

Each has consequences for the Docker builds, which is why this is filed rather than fixed in passing.

## Provenance

Found while running the KS-830 `npm ci` cell on Wednesday's ruling of 2026-09-05T23:09:26Z; carried out of KS-830 as its own item on her 23:15:00Z ruling, both SPF + DKIM `header.i=@agentmail.to` + DMARC pass. KS-830 comment `565ea3cc-bc90-47c9-aa72-319bbc397605` holds the full measurement. **It is NOT the cause of KS-830's red** — that was measured and excluded.

---

*Filed by s138 (seat A) 2026-09-06. Text authored by s137 and preserved at* `5_Project_History/unfiled-tickets-s137/unfiled-dist-resolution-trap.md`*; creation was refused by Linear's cap on 2026-09-05T23:33:40Z and retried after Kam upgraded the plan (panel, 09:45).*

title: The OAuth error code travels in error.message and the contract never says so; and authorize refusals answer JSON where RFC 6749 redirects
description:
**From the KS-822 tier-1 gate.** `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s136-ks822-835-pass1-04994288a-tier1/` (QA tree)

Two related contract defects in the OAuth error envelope, both **pre-existing** (KS-804's shape, not KS-822's changes).

**1. The OAuth code travels in the wrong field and the contract never names it.** Every refusal from the authorize and token endpoints answers `{ success: false, error: { code: 'BAD_REQUEST', message: '<oauth_code>', description } }` — so `error.code` is the platform's HTTP-ish code and the **OAuth** code (`invalid_client`, `invalid_grant`, `invalid_scope`, `unsupported_response_type`) is in `error.message`. The published descriptions name those codes but never say which field carries them, so an integrator has to guess or read a response.

**2. RFC 6749 4.1.2.1 delivers authorize errors by REDIRECT, not a JSON 400.** For an authorize request with a *valid* client and redirect URI, the RFC says the server redirects back with `error=...&state=...` rather than answering the user agent with JSON. This platform answers JSON 400 for the whole rule set. That is a design question, not a bug to fix quietly — the deny path already redirects, so the two halves of the same endpoint disagree.

**Done when:** the contract states which field carries the OAuth code; and a decision is recorded on whether authorize refusals should redirect per the RFC, with the deny path's existing behaviour as the reference point.

title: Make the authorize rules DATA the resolver iterates, so the GET/POST agreement guard is structural instead of textual
description:
**From the KS-822 tier-1 gate.** `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-06-s136-ks822-835-pass1-04994288a-tier1/` (QA tree)

`ks804-authorize-get-post-agree-per-rule.test.ts`'s `RULES` table is a hand-maintained literal. Its header once promised that a rule added to one handler and not the other "fails here by construction, because the table below is the list of rules" — corrected in KS-822 F-8, because it is the list of rules *someone wrote down*, not the list the code has.

F-8 enforced the half that could be enforced: the table's `expected` set must equal the refusal-message set `resolveAuthorizeClient` can return. **That guard is TEXTUAL and has three named limits, each measured rather than asserted:**

* a rule that **REUSES** an existing message is invisible to it — F-6 and F-7 both did, and their RULES rows are hand-added, which is the only thing making those rules driven;
* it is a **SOURCE-TEXT** guard: it sees a literal appear or disappear and **cannot see a rule stop working while its literal stays on the page** (a condition-shaped tamper on RULE 5 reds the behaviour cases and leaves the guard green);
* its span is anchored on the function signature as text, so a `return {` + `ok: true,` written with different whitespace ends it early or not at all.

**The real fix the header already names: make the rules DATA the resolver iterates**, so the table is derived rather than maintained and the guard becomes structural instead of textual. That is a route refactor of `resolveAuthorizeClient`, not a change to the suite, which is why it was not taken inside KS-822.

**Done when:** the resolver's app rules are a list it walks; the suite derives its cases from that list; a new rule is driven through both handlers without anyone adding a row; and the three limits above are closed or explicitly re-stated against the new shape.

title: Published prose drifts from the routes it describes and nothing detects it — the phrase check, the marker convention, and the ~306 unswept descriptions
description:
**Ruled lines 1, 2 and 5 of KS-822's five, lifted onto one ticket so they survive that ticket closing.** They are one problem seen three ways: *published prose drifts away from the routes it describes, and nothing detects it.*

The evidence is not hypothetical. `POST /api/oauth/token`'s description was swept **twice** and was wrong in **three** places both times. One wrong sentence about client authentication reached **four** separate places (comment → contract → test header → route), and the fourth landed *inside the commit that corrected the first three*.

---

## Line 1 — targeted contract-source phrase check (~half a day, SIZED)

A retired-phrase registry checked against **contract sources only**: `services/*/src/*.openapi.ts` plus the generated `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`.

* **No marker convention needed to start** — in that surface a quotation carrying a marker is rare to nonexistent.
* Catches the **comment → contract** hop, which is the one that publishes a wrong rule to integrators.
* **The matcher must be wrap-tolerant by construction**: normalise whitespace and comment punctuation across line boundaries before matching. ~15 lines.
* ⚠ **A single-token control is NOT a valid control for a line-wrapping phrase.** That exact mistake made an earlier sweep report **0** where the true count was **4**.
* **Stated limitation, on the line rather than discovered later: this would NOT have caught F-1c.** Test headers are outside the surface and F-1c was a test header. This is the cheap 80%, not the class.

## Line 2 — repo-wide marker convention (UNSIZED, deliberately)

Not sized pending a population measurement, and **measuring the population is most of the work.**

The shape it must survive, from a real specimen produced on `develop`: in `BACKLOG.md` the retired phrase *"deletion only"* appears twice — once as the live claim and once inside a quotation of the old wording. A sweep that cannot tell a quotation from a claim makes a correct commit look like a regression, because the phrase count went **1 → 2** for an entirely correct reason.

## Line 5 — the ~306 unswept published descriptions (UNSIZED)

The other **~306** published operation descriptions have never been swept against their routes. Sizing it means sampling, and sampling is most of the work. **It pairs naturally with line 1**, which runs over the same surface.

---

## Why these are together

Line 1 is the instrument, line 2 is what the instrument needs to avoid false positives at repo scale, and line 5 is the population it would be pointed at. Building line 1 alone is defensible and cheap; building it *without* line 2's distinction is what makes a sweep that cries wolf and gets switched off.

## The standing ruling

**Wednesday priced line 1 and ruled DO NOT BUILD IT NOW** (2026-09-05T15:44:16Z), after it was proposed. That ruling is carried here unchanged — this ticket is the record, not a commission. Anyone picking it up should re-price rather than assume the half-day still holds.

*Source: KS-822 comments* `e38c5f38` *(lines 1 and 2) and* `4f901d71` *(line 5), from PR #831's tier-2 gate.*

title: Publish a `request:` block for POST /api/oauth/token — the endpoint's shape is asserted nowhere, and adding it moves what Schemathesis generates
description:
**Ruled line 3 of KS-822's five, lifted onto its own ticket so it survives that ticket closing.**

`POST /api/oauth/token` publishes **no** `request:` **block**. That is why its description spells the form fields out in prose — `grant_type`, `code`, `code_verifier`, `redirect_uri`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `refresh_token` are described in a sentence rather than declared as a schema an integrator or a tool can read.

## Why it was NOT added in #831, and the reason still holds

Publishing a form-body schema where none exists **changes what Schemathesis generates against a live auth endpoint.** That is not a docs-only change, and #831 was a prose-scoped round. It wants its own change **with the suite actually run** — the point is precisely that the generator's behaviour moves, so a change that does not run the suite has not been tested.

## What it is worth

The token endpoint's published contract has been tightened repeatedly (KS-820 client authentication; KS-822 F-2d bound the status→code split to assertions). All of that is in prose. A `request:` block is the half a machine can check, and its absence is why the endpoint's shape is asserted nowhere in the spec.

## Done when

* A `request:` block declaring the form body, with `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` as the media type the endpoint actually accepts (it is in `FORM_ALLOWED_PATHS` — the only path that is).
* **Schemathesis run before and after**, with the operation's case counts and outcomes compared. A change that moves the generator and reports no delta has not been measured.
* The prose reduced to what the schema cannot say, rather than left to drift beside it.

*Source: KS-822 comment* `e38c5f38` *(line 3), from PR #831's tier-2 gate. Nothing was built for it in KS-822's round.*

title: [Decision] POST /api/certifications/:id/verify has no auth handler — leave it public, or gate it?
description:
**The ask, first:** @kamil.kreiser **— should** `POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` **stay public, or be moved behind auth?** Default if you say nothing: **leave it public**. Nothing changes in code either way until you rule. This is a **product decision recorded, not a defect actioned** (category 2).

## What is measured

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:556`) is mounted with **no authentication handler** — only `mockBodyParser`. A request carrying no `Authorization` header reaches the route handler and gets the handler's own answer.

**At the KS-815 head (recorded during the KS-800 round):** C10 → **200 headerless**, with C11 → **401** as the discriminating control.

**Re-measured live on the local stack today, 2026-09-05T20:02Z, at** `develop` `0b9346f31`**:**

| case | request | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| SUBJECT | `POST /api/certifications/550e8400-…/verify`, **no** `Authorization` | **404** with the handler's own body — `{"verified":false,…,"error":"Certification not found","checks":{"exists":false}}` |
| SUBJECT | same, `id=test-cert-1` | **404**, same shape |
| **CONTROL** | `POST /api/documents`, **no** `Authorization`, same client and shape | **401** |

**Why the 404 is the finding and not a refusal:** an auth-guarded route never reaches its handler headerless — it answers 401 before the handler runs, as `/api/documents` does from the same client in the same second. This route answers *from inside the handler* (`checks.exists` is the handler's own field), so the request got all the way through. The 404 is "that certification does not exist", not "you are not allowed to ask".

## What it does and does not expose

The handler is **read-only** — it calls `checkDocumentExists(id, authHeader)` and returns JSON. It writes nothing. It forwards whatever `Authorization` header it received, so a caller who *has* a token is still scoped downstream; a caller with none is not stopped at the door.

Since the F-03 pen-test fix it can no longer claim `anchored: true`: certifications without real on-chain confirmation return `verified: false` and `confidence: 'pending-onchain'`. So what an unauthenticated caller learns is **existence** plus issuance status for an id they already hold.

## The two readings, so the decision is a decision

* **Leave public (the default).** Verification is the product — a relying party checking a certification they were handed should not need a Secuura account. The route leaks existence for an id you must already possess, and writes nothing.
* **Put it behind auth.** Existence-oracle on guessable or enumerable ids, and it is the only verify-family route on the gateway with no handler; the asymmetry is itself a smell for anyone reading the mount list.

## If the answer is "leave public"

Close this ticket and it becomes the written record that the posture is deliberate — which is the thing that is missing today. A future guard sweep that flags this mount then has an answer to read.

---

*Filed on Wednesday's ruling 2026-09-05T20:00:24Z, on the default carried by Kam's silence past the 06:00 sweep. Raised to Kam 2026-09-05 22:46 and carried in the 05:15 morning brief. Category 2. No code, branch or PR was touched.*

title: Audit gate baseline data model: an unvalidated `scope` lets a GREEN root gate advertise a row leg 7 still needs, and suppression matches by advisory id alone
description:
## BLUF

**Two Minor findings in the audit gate's BASELINE DATA MODEL, both from the #829 fuse gate (tier 2, PASS — merged at** `ec5431f6b`**). Neither blocked the merge. F1 is the one s133 walked into and which cost a refused push; F2 means a baseline row silently covers more than it was written about.** Filed beside KS-763 as the gate ruled. Fix-shapes below are the tester's, quoted as **hypotheses** — run each against the unfixed instrument before building on it.

## F1 (Minor) — a green root gate can advertise a row for deletion that a second gate still needs

`scope: "standalone-locks"` is **optional and unvalidated**: `baseline-contract.mjs:41` REQUIRED_FIELDS is `package` / `reason` / `ticket` only. But the root gate's CLEANUP advice keys on that field (`audit-gate.mjs:203-205`).

So an advisory that lives **only in a standalone lock**, baselined without the marker, is advertised for deletion by a **GREEN** root gate — while leg 7 (`audit:locks`) still needs the row. That is exactly what happened on 2026-09-05: `audit:gate` printed `CLEANUP … remove: GHSA-v422-hmwv-36x6` and the push preflight then refused the deletion, because the root audit reads the **hoisted workspace tree** and cannot see standalone locks. Deleting on the root gate's word would have broken the push gate for every author.

The class is swept clean at head — one such row, and it is marked.

**Fix-shape (hypothesis):** either `validateBaseline` refuses a row that the root audit does not report and that lacks `scope`, or the root gate declines to list for cleanup any row it cannot positively attribute. **Regression:** a locks-only advisory baselined without `scope` must NOT appear in CLEANUP.

## F2 (Minor) — suppression matches by ADVISORY ID ALONE

`baseline[id]` at `audit-locks.mjs:286-289` and `audit-gate.mjs:194-197`. A row written about one version and one path silently covers **every** version and **every** path of that advisory.

Demonstrated by this very PR: the regen added a **vulnerable-range qs instance** (nested `qs` 6.15.3 under body-parser 1.20.6) and **no gate output changed**.

**Fix-shape (hypothesis):** record the measured versions on the row; **warn — not fail** — when a matched instance falls outside them.

## F3 (polish) — a wording fix on the record

"before the regen leg 7 refused" described the **deletion-only attempt**, not the parent SHA. The parent is GREEN 30/30. The refusal is the head-baseline + parent-lock cell, which the tester reproduced exactly. Correct the phrasing wherever it is repeated.

## F4 (polish) — the mysql2 row's clocks disagree

`GHSA-rgwj-5xj2-c3m3` mixes a local date with ISO dates, and its `decidedAt` still reads `2026-09-03` under a **2026-09-04** ruling by Kam. Verified on develop `ec5431f6b`: `decidedAt: "2026-09-03"`, `expires: "2026-09-24"`. Being fixed in the BACKLOG docs commit if it is a one-line change; otherwise it stays here as this ticket's fourth line.

## For the record — the tester's own retraction

qs 6.15.3 was **already** in four locks at the parent (`frontend/issuer`, `services/vc-issuer`, `services/mcp-server`, `packages/shared`::body-parser). The nesting is an existing repo pattern, so the hazard disclosed on #829 is **milder** than first read. The two #801 rows cover the nested instance by id, tamper-proven.

**Not commissioned, said so:** the reachability re-check. The tester checked the mysql2 **row** (id → package by tamper; 3.15.3 in exactly two locks), not the measurement behind it.

## Provenance

Gate mail `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura FUSE #829 PASS 1 @ b7fc43473 (tier 2 narrow)` 2026-09-05T15:18:05Z; routed here by Wednesday's GO 2026-09-05T15:21:12Z. Sits beside KS-763 (the fuse ticket #829 carries on its mysql2 row).

title: Gate integrity: the auth suite's green is not deterministic — three head runs gave 534/0, 534/0, and 534 with 2 FAILED
description:
## BLUF

**A security PR merged on one green run is merged on a sample.** The KS-820+821 gate ran the auth
suite three times at the head and got **534/0, 534/0, and 534 with 2 FAILED** — the failing file
(`ks431-oauth-app-update.test.ts`) is **byte-identical at both SHAs**, failing with
`TypeError: fetch failed` plus a stale 500. The suite's green is a sample, and every gate in this
class currently reads one draw of it as a verdict.

## Mechanism — measured, and the same one twice

**21 of the 40 auth test files open a server per request** (`app.listen(0)`). s132's `BACKLOG.md`
entry — `auth.integration.test.ts` failing 1 run in 3 with a registration helper getting 501 — is
**the same mechanism in another file**, and is carried here **as a hypothesis, not a diagnosis**:
its preconditions are all measured (a server per REQUEST, no agent passed,
`http.globalAgent.keepAlive === true` on node 24, `501` absent from all of `services/auth/src`) but
the link has never been reproduced deterministically.

## Why it is worth its own ticket

The flake and the gate are separate problems. Even once the flake is diagnosed, **a gate that reads**
**a single run cannot tell a real red from a draw** — that is the part that decides whether security
work merges correctly.

## Shapes, neither yet run

* **The flake:** listen once per suite, or pass an agent with `keepAlive: false`.
* **The gate:** run the suite N times, or make the runner report the draw rather than the verdict.
  Whichever is chosen, prove it by reproducing a red first — a fix that cannot be shown to change
  the failure rate has not been shown to do anything.

---

*Filed by s133 from the KS-820+821 tier-1 gate (PASS 1 @* `0e8d3e60a`*, report* `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-05-s132-ks820-821-pass1-0e8d3e60a/report.md` *at the QA tree), on Wednesday's disposition ruling of 2026-09-05T13:01:20Z. Inherited — not introduced by #825.*

title: OAuth app_type: a CASED row is neither normalised by 047 nor refused by its CHECK, and docker/init's unnamed constraint defeats 047's idempotence guard
description:
## BLUF

Two DDL defects left by KS-821's migration 047. **F-2 is the one that matters: a cased row such as**
`'Public'` **is silently and permanently bricked** — it is not normalised and not refused, and the
app's users get the false message *"Invalid or expired authorization code"* forever.

## F-2 (Major) — the case hole survives 047 in both directions

* 047's normalisation predicate is `lower(app_type) NOT IN (...)`, so `'Public'` **does not match**
  and is left untouched.
* The CHECK it adds **permits** `'Public'` as well, so the row is legal forever.
* Every consuming rule is an **exact** match, so `'Public'` is a third string to all of them and
  takes the else-branch — the app can never satisfy the rule it is judged by.

**Fix-shape (the tester's — a HYPOTHESIS until run against the unfixed product):** either normalise
on the exact set and `SET app_type = lower(app_type)`, or fold case at the three exact-match
consumers — `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:276`, `:615`, and
`services/auth/src/services/oauth.ts:209`. Measure which before choosing; a CHECK that permits a
value the code cannot honour is the defect, so the constraint's own predicate is in scope too.

## F-3 (Minor) — a second identical constraint

`docker/init`'s inline CHECK is **UNNAMED**, so Postgres names it `oauth_apps_app_type_check` — the
same name 047's idempotence guard looks for is not the name it looks for. The guard misses it and
adds a **second identical constraint** on a fresh database.

## Scope note

`app_type` is now inside `CreateOAuthAppSchema` case-folded (KS-821), so the **API** can no longer
mint a cased row. This ticket is about rows arriving any other way — a direct DB write, a restore,
a seed, or anything predating 047.

---

*Filed by s133 from the KS-820+821 tier-1 gate (PASS 1 @* `0e8d3e60a`*, report* `projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-05-s132-ks820-821-pass1-0e8d3e60a/report.md` *at the QA tree), on Wednesday's disposition ruling of 2026-09-05T13:01:20Z. Inherited — not introduced by #825.*

title: The control-byte guard cannot see a raw body — findNulBytePath returns null for every Buffer, and the doc claims otherwise
description:
## BLUF

**The control-byte guard cannot see a raw body.** `findNulBytePath` and
`findControlBytePath` both return `null` for **every** `Buffer`, so a request parsed
by `express.raw()` passes the guard whatever bytes it carries. The guard's own doc
comment says every field is covered; that is not true of raw bodies. Nothing is
exploitable on `develop` today — the one live `express.raw` is path-scoped and its
payload is not persisted as text — but the guarantee KS-471/KS-472 states is wider
than the guarantee the code delivers.

**This ticket asks a question rather than answering it: should a webhook payload be**
**scanned at all, or declared out of the class in writing?** Both are defensible. What
is not defensible is the current state, where the doc claims one and the code does
the other.

## Recommendation

Decide first, then implement — the implementation differs completely by answer:

* **(A) Scan raw bodies.** Teach `findControlBytePath` to walk a `Buffer` (a byte
  scan, not `Object.entries`), and mount the guard after `express.raw` on
  `/webhooks`. Cost: a byte walk on every webhook body. Risk: a signed webhook
  payload whose signature covers the raw bytes must not be altered — rejection is
  fine, mutation is not, and the guard only rejects.
* **(B) Declare raw bodies out.** Say so in the guard's doc comment and in
  `mountBodyParsers`'s, and add a leg asserting that no `express.raw`/`express.text`
  mount feeds a handler that persists its body as text. The exclusion becomes a
  **declared set with a reason**, which is the shape the KS-800 gate asked for.

## Detail — measured, not quoted

Against `packages/shared/dist/middleware/index.js` built from this branch's source:

```
Buffer [61 00 62]            findNulBytePath       null
Buffer [61 00 62]            findControlBytePath   null
CONTROL {f: "a"+NUL+"b"}     findNulBytePath       "f"      <- the walker works
CONTROL {a: 0} (a number)    findNulBytePath       null     <- not a numeric artefact
CONTROL {s: buf.toString()}  findNulBytePath       "s"      <- same bytes, as a string
```

Two controls that could have disagreed and did not: the identical bytes presented as
a **string** are found, so the failure is Buffer-specific and not a broken walker;
and a literal number `0` is correctly not a NUL, so the null is not a numeric
artefact either.

**Cause.** The walker recurses with `Object.entries(value)`. On a `Buffer` that
yields numeric indices with **number** values, and no branch of the walker matches a
number — so it returns `null` without ever looking at a byte.

**Every raw/text parser in tracked source** (`git ls-files` over `*.ts`/`*.js`, so
build output cannot inflate it):

| Site | Status |
| -- | -- |
| `services/billing/src/index.ts:50` | **LIVE** — `app.use('/webhooks', express.raw({type:'application/json'}), webhookRoutes)`, path-scoped, mounted **before** the guard |
| `services/billing/src/__tests__/ks488-c4-webhook-idempotency-fail-closed.test.ts:63` | test harness, same shape |
| `packages/shared/src/middleware/request-limits.ts:92` | `express.raw` factory — **shared exports a way to mount one** |
| `packages/shared/src/middleware/request-limits.ts:102` | `express.text` factory, same |

The last two matter beyond this ticket: they are the same two factories recorded as
**KS-800 F-16**. `express.text` sets `req.body` to a **string**, which the guard
*can* walk — so for text bodies ordering is real protection and the KS-802 widening
of `PARSER_CALL` is load-bearing. For `raw` it is not: ordering a raw parser before
the guard buys nothing at all. **Detection is not protection, and the two cases**
**differ.** Whatever is decided here should be written into `PARSER_CALL`'s comment so
the next reader does not infer that a detected raw mount is a guarded one.

## Provenance

* The Buffer behaviour and its two controls: measured in this session against a
  fresh `tsc` build; command and output above.
* The parser-site table: `git ls-files | grep -nE` at `55894a5b5`.
* Raised by the KS-802 gate (report §4, PR #818 @ `8a9fa6bde`) and folded to a ticket
  by Wednesday's ruling 2026-09-05 06:35:12Z. Related: **KS-800** (F-16), **KS-802**.

title: S revokes that emit no lifecycle event, or emit share-permission-change, are indistinguishable on K from a document that was never revoked
description:
## BLUF

**K cannot tell a revoked document from one that was never revoked, when S's revoke path emits no lifecycle event — and cannot tell a revoke from an ordinary permission change when S emits** `share-permission-change` **instead of** `share-revoke`**.** Both are silent on the K side. Raised from Stuart's PS-749 split (PS-764/765/766/767) as the **K-side** question those S-side findings imply; no S-side work is proposed here.

Measured read-only on `develop`, 2026-09-04. Nothing was written.

## The two cases, and what K actually sees

| S behaviour | K row | Can K distinguish it from "never revoked"? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| emits `share-revoke` | `action='share-revoke'` | **Yes** — this is the working path |
| emits `share-permission-change` (two Edit-dropdown paths) | `action='share-permission-change'` + free-form payload | **No** — not without parsing a payload K does not own |
| emits nothing (Outlook add-in revoke, PS-765; and the Share Now **reuse path **`:402-420`, which applies permission and expiry changes and records neither) | **no row at all** | **No — identical by construction** |

## Why K cannot distinguish them — the mechanism, not the symptom

**1. K validates the verb and never the detail. **`migrations/037_document_lifecycle_events.sql:34` states the contract in its own words:

> Verb-specific detail (e.g. rename's new display name, share-revoke's share id). **Free-form by design — the vocabulary owns the verb, S owns the detail.**

So on a `share-permission-change` row, whether the permission moved *to NoAccess* (a revoke) or from view→download (a routine change) lives entirely in a `payload JSONB` K neither schemas, validates nor documents. K has **no basis** to reclassify one as the other.

**2.** `share-revoke` **and** `share-permission-change` **are SEPARATE entries in K's own closed vocabulary** (`services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts:40-41`, `docs/VOCABULARY.md:45`). K already has a verb that means *revoked*. A revoke arriving as `share-permission-change` is therefore not merely under-detailed — it is **mislabelled against K's own contract**, and K's graph will read it as a permission edit forever.

**3. There is no gap detection, so an absent event is undetectable. **`document_lifecycle_events` holds `id, tenant_id, parent_document_id, action, payload, actor_user_id, anchor_id, created_at` — **no sequence number and no previous-event pointer**. Reads are *"events for this document, newest first"*. An event S never sends leaves no hole to notice.

**Worth flagging on its own:** migration 037's header says *"K's lineage view of these events now mirrors S's PreviousChainId chain." ***The schema does not do that.** It attaches events to `parent_document_id`; it stores no chain link between events. The comment claims a property the table cannot provide, and it is the property that would have made an omission detectable.

**4. No reconciliation exists.** The only reconciler in the tree is KS-584's **stuck-anchor** reconciler (`services/anchoring/src/reconciler.ts`) — it reconciles K's own anchor submission state against chain, not S's event stream against K's. Grep for `reconcil` across `Blockchain/Dev/services/` returns that and nothing else.

## Controls

* *The vocabulary grep can find things* — `share-permission-change` returns non-zero across 10 files, against `share-revoke`'s 20.
* *The absence of a sequence column is real, not a missed migration* — `037_…lifecycle_events.sql` is the only lifecycle migration in the tree, and no later migration adds one.
* *The* `PreviousChainId` *mirror does not exist in K* — the only matches in the K tree are the migration comment, the OpenAPI description and the repo/route prose. No column, no code.

## Why this matters

Anchoring is the product claim. A provenance record that reads identically for *"this share was revoked"* and *"this share was never revoked"* is not a weaker record — for that question it is a **wrong** one, and the reader has no way to know. It also means K's own `share-revoke` verb currently under-counts real revokes by an unknown amount, so nobody can measure the size of this from the K side either.

## Done when

1. **Decide the contract**, with S: does a revoke-to-NoAccess emit `share-revoke` (K's own vocabulary), or does `share-permission-change` carry a payload field K agrees to schema and read? Either is defensible; the current state — where it depends on which S UI path the user clicked — is not.
2. **If the payload route is chosen**, K stops treating this one payload as free-form: a declared shape, validated at the route, documented in `VOCABULARY.md`.
3. **Correct migration 037's header** so it stops claiming a `PreviousChainId` mirror the schema does not implement — or implement the chain link, which is what makes an omission detectable at all.
4. **Decide whether K should be able to detect an omission** (a per-document event sequence, or a periodic S↔K reconciliation). This is the bigger of the two and may well be its own ticket; recording the question here so it is not lost.
5. **Measure the current divergence** once the contract is agreed — how many `share-permission-change` rows are in fact revokes.

Nothing here is actionable without S. Filed as a line in the **KS-772** S↔K integration-contract stream.

## Provenance

* The S-side behaviours that raise the question | Stuart's PS-749 review split (PS-764/765/766/767) and his own 2026-09-03T23:33:13Z correction retracting two of four, relayed via Wednesday | not independently verified — S-side, and out of this ticket's scope
* Every K-side statement above | read-only on `origin/develop` at `492152a81`: `migrations/037_document_lifecycle_events.sql`, `services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts`, `services/originate/src/repositories/lifecycleEventRepo.ts`, `docs/VOCABULARY.md` | read 2026-09-04

title: Compose resolves the SHELL over .env while the checker resolves .env over the shell — a green credential check over a stack running the shared literal
description:
## BLUF

`docker compose` resolves the **shell environment over the project** `.env`; `source` resolves the `.env` **over the shell**. The credential checker uses `source`. So in one shell, with one correctly-rotated `.env`, **the checker prints a full green bill of health and** `rc=0` **while compose resolves both datastore passwords to the shared literals from git history.**

This is **F-800-05 reopened by a new route** — a confident green over an exposed stack — and it lands on the surface Stuart and Peter are asked to trust on rotation day (`APP_DB_PASSWORD` rotation 2026-09-05 09:00).

Found by the compose-precedence probe named as the highest-value next step in the 2026-09-04 through-code gate on #800's fix round. **No fix is written.** Filed separately from #800 on Wednesday's ruling: the fix is a behaviour change to the start path, not a change to the checker's parser.

## Recommendation

Fix on its own branch off `develop`, not on #800. Two candidate shapes, neither chosen here:

* **(a)** have `start-environment.sh` source `.env` on the same path, so the shell and compose agree — this also makes FR-1's safety claim true, which is the same defect from the other side; or
* **(b)** have the checker "be the consumer" for real: read the values the way compose does (shell first, `.env` second) rather than the way `source` does.

**(b) is the one that matches what the script claims about itself.** See the claim-defect below.

## Detail

### The measurement, and why the discriminator is the keeper

`${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-secuura_dev_password}` means **the compose default IS the shared literal**. So a naive probe — export the shared literal, see whether compose renders the shared literal — **cannot distinguish "the shell won" from "compose saw nothing and fell back to its default."** It returns the alarming-looking answer for the reassuring reason, or the reassuring answer for no reason at all.

A **three-way sentinel** was used instead:

| rendered value | meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `rotated_probe_pg_A1` (the fixture) | the `.env` won — no inversion |
| `AMBIENT_SHELL_pg_B2` (the sentinel) | **the shell won — inversion real** |
| `secuura_dev_password` (compose default) | neither was seen — the probe did not vary its subject |

Result, `docker compose config` only (render-only; no `-o`, no `--lock-image-digests`, no `up`), fixture supplied via `--env-file` from a scratchpad file:

| run | interp-env PG | interp-env Redis | rendered postgres service |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **CONTROL** — no ambient export | fixture wins | fixture wins | fixture wins |
| **TREATMENT** — shell exports sentinel | **SHELL WINS** | **SHELL WINS** | **SHELL WINS** |

**The control is what makes the treatment readable.** It proves `--env-file` was honoured, that the fixture is genuinely the file compose read, and — since nothing unrecognised appeared — that no real `.env` leaked into the probe. The only thing differing between the two runs is the ambient export.

### The real-world shape, both instruments in one shell

Shell still exports the old shared literals; `.env` correctly rotated:

* **checker** → `✓ POSTGRES_PASSWORD is per-clone`, `✓ REDIS_PASSWORD is per-clone`, `rc=0`
* **compose** → `POSTGRES_PASSWORD=secuura_dev_password`, `REDIS_PASSWORD=secuura_redis_dev`

### The claim in shipped source that this refutes

`check-slot-credentials.sh:96-99` carries the justification for the entire sourcing design:

> *"it cannot drift from the consumer, **because it IS the consumer**."*

It is not the consumer. Compose is, and compose resolves with the opposite precedence. (The sentence itself is being corrected on #800's branch alongside FR-1/FR-6; the behavioural fix is this ticket.)

### Blast radius — bounded, and it lands on FR-1's caller

Measured per caller at `e26cfce2b`, with a bash-semantics control:

* `start-local.sh` — checker L63, `source .env` L103 with **no** `set -a`. A plain assignment to an **already-exported** variable keeps the export attribute and updates the value, so the stale ambient **is overwritten** by the rotated `.env` before compose runs. Control: with the variable not previously exported, a child process sees nothing. **This path is neutralised — by accident. Nothing anywhere records that the L103** `source` **is load-bearing**, so moving or removing it silently opens this hole.
* `start-environment.sh` — checker L91, **no** `source` **anywhere in its 283 lines**, `docker compose up` L135. The stale export survives untouched from the operator's shell into compose. **This is the live path, and it is the same caller QA FR-1 named.**

### The precondition is self-priming

`check-slot-credentials.sh:164`, in the UNREADABLE arm, tells the operator:

> `See the parse error with:  sh -n '<file>'  (or: set -a; . '<file>')`

**Running that second form in an interactive shell is exactly the act that exports these two variables into it.** So the script hands the operator the command that arms the trap — and the operator most likely to type it is the one whose `.env` is malformed, i.e. mid-rotation. (The suggestion is being dropped from that message on #800's branch as part of the upgraded FR-8; that removes one route to the precondition, **not** the precedence defect itself.)

### Not established

Whether `start-environment.sh` runs anywhere but a developer laptop — laptop only, or also the demo/UAT VM. That bounds the severity and it was not settled from the tree.

---

Discovered 2026-09-04 (s122) by the compose-precedence probe. Related: PR #800 (`e26cfce2b`), QA FR-1 (same caller), QA FR-8 (the self-priming message).

title: POST /api/teams/webhook-config fails the Schemathesis pr sweep on every run — including develop — and is tracked by nothing
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/teams/webhook-config` **fails the Schemathesis** `pr` **sweep on every run, on** `develop` **as well as on feature branches, and maps to no open ticket.** Not a regression from any current PR — an unrecorded pre-existing failure, which is the shape that quietly becomes "known noise" and then becomes invisible.

Filed on Wednesday's instruction after it surfaced during #805's contract-gate run. **No fix attempted; not investigated beyond establishing that it is real, stable and unowned.**

## Evidence — three runs, one variable

| run | branch / spec served | tests | failures | this op failed? |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | PR [#805](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/805>) (`Anchor.status` widened) | 316 | 12 | **yes** |
| 2 | `develop` `492152a81` | 316 | 12 | **yes** |
| 3 | #805 again | 316 | 12 | **yes** |

Run validity clean on all three — **0 of 316 operations errored**, 85-91s each, ~1,680 cases per run. Profile `pr`, local gateway, `mode: positive`, checks `not_a_server_error, response_schema_conformance, status_code_conformance, content_type_conformance, response_headers_conformance`.

**It is in the STABLE core, not the flaky slot.** Eleven operations fail in all three runs; a twelfth slot rotates between runs (`referrals/apply` → `security/rate-limit/check` → `gdpr/consent`). `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` is in the stable eleven — so it is deterministic, not noise.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a shrug

Ten of the eleven stable failures are accounted for:

| operations | ticket |
| -- | -- |
| 7 × m365 / onedrive | [KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693) — *"M365 routes answer 503 when ENTRA_* is unconfigured — 9 permanent Schemathesis failures on every run"* |
| `POST /api/wallets/verify` | [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686) — `not_a_server_error` flags the by-design 501 |
| `POST /api/gdpr/erasures`, `GET /api/gdpr/erasures/{externalRef}` | the erasure family — [KS-695](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-695), [KS-754](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-754), [KS-757](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-757), [KS-758](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-758) |
| `POST /api/teams/webhook-config` | **none — this ticket** |

**A failure nobody owns is worse than a failure somebody has deprioritised**, because the first gets absorbed into the expected red and stops being counted.

## ⚠ A count on KS-693 that should be reconciled, not inherited

[KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693)'s title asserts **"9 permanent Schemathesis failures on every run"**. This measurement finds **7** m365/onedrive operations failing, within a stable core of **11** and a total of **12**. The figures may be reconcilable (different profile, different spec revision, or the count included operations since fixed) — but **they should be checked against a run rather than carried forward**, on the same principle that made [KS-763](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-763) assert a case count for equality instead of a floor: a number in a title is a claim, and an unrechecked one drifts.

## What is NOT established here

* **Why** it fails. The failing check(s) were not isolated — the run records them, but this ticket deliberately reports the observation rather than a half-diagnosis.
* Whether it shares KS-693's cause (an unconfigured integration answering 503) or is a distinct defect. `teams` is a different integration from `m365`, so it should not be assumed.
* Whether it is by design, like [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686)'s 501 — which would make this a spec-declaration fix rather than a code fix.

## Reproduce

```
cd systemTest/schemathesis
./venv/bin/python3 scripts/run.py pr --base-url http://localhost:6882
```

Failures are in `output/reports/latest/schemathesis-output.xml` (JUnit; one `<testcase>` per operation).

## Related

[KS-693](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-693) (the other permanent integration failures, and the count above) · [KS-686](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-686) (a by-design status flagged by a check) · [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) (173 routed endpoints absent from the spec) · surfaced during [#805](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/805>)'s contract-gate run

title: A platform admin who loses their TOTP device has no self-service recovery — TOTP-only branch, no backup codes
description:
## BLUF

**A platform admin who loses their TOTP device has no self-service recovery.** The platform-admin login branch accepts TOTP only — there is no backup-code path, and no alternative second factor. Recovery today means someone with database access editing `platform_admins`.

Surfaced while correcting a comment on [#804](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/804>) (KS-737). **The wording was the trivial half; this is the half that matters**, filed rather than left in a PR comment — a gap recorded only in a comment is a claim that outlives every tracker it names.

## The asymmetry, and note it runs the SAFE direction

|  | second factors accepted |
| -- | -- |
| regular user (`auth.ts:501-531`) | TOTP **or** a backup code (`verifyBackupCode`, `auth.ts:507-514`) |
| **platform admin** | **TOTP only** |

`#804`'s code comment describes the platform-admin branch as "shaped exactly like the regular-user branch below". It is not — and the difference makes the privileged path **stricter**, which is the right direction and the opposite of the defect KS-737 closed. Nothing here is a security regression.

**The problem is availability, not authorisation.** The strictest possible second factor with no recovery path is a lockout waiting for a lost or wiped phone, on precisely the accounts whose lockout is most expensive. And it interacts badly with two things already on the board:

* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) — per-person platform-admin identities. Today the seeded admin is shared; once identities are per-person, one person's lost device locks **that person** out with no path back, and there is no second admin who can help them without DB access.
* [KS-171](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-171) — `platform_admins.mfa_secret` handling. Any recovery mechanism has to not undo that work.

## Options, none chosen

1. **Backup codes for platform admins**, matching the user branch. Simplest, reuses `verifyBackupCode` and its KS-622 factor-1 proof. But it widens the privileged surface, and KS-622 exists because that path was got wrong once.
2. **A second platform admin can re-enrol the first.** Better separation, needs per-person identities ([KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)) and an audit trail to be meaningful.
3. **A documented, audited break-glass** — explicitly operator-run against the database, with the audit row as the deliverable. Honest about what happens today rather than pretending a product path exists.

**(2) is the right long-term shape and (3) is what should exist tonight**, because (3) is a runbook rather than code and the current answer is "someone edits the table and nobody records it". But that is a call for @kamil.kreiser, not an implementer's choice.

## Done when

* A platform admin who has lost their TOTP device has a defined, **audited** path back that does not require ad-hoc database editing.
* Whatever ships, the `auth.ts` comment stops claiming the two branches are identically shaped — that wording is what hid this.

## Related

[KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) (#804, where this surfaced) · [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579) (per-person platform-admin identities) · [KS-622](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-622) (backup codes needing factor-1 proof) · [KS-171](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-171) (platform-admin MFA secret storage) · [KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781) (the other doors that skip MFA entirely)

title: [Decision] OAuth consent: a proper two-step MFA challenge on /api/oauth/authorize (the design half of KS-781)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/oauth/authorize` **should challenge for the second factor as a proper two-step consent flow, rather than accepting** `mfaCode` **in the same body as the password.** This is the **product-design** half of [KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781); that ticket carries the **security** half.

**Filed deliberately before KS-781 closes.** Wednesday's ruling (2026-09-03): *"a deferral that lives only in a PR comment is a claim that outlives every tracker it names."* This exists so the design question survives the fix.

## The split, and why it is this way round

KS-781 closes a live hole: that route is a second, password-only login with no MFA, no lockout and no status check. **The ruled fix there is minimal — accept** `mfaCode` **in the authorize body, mirroring** `/api/auth/login`**.** Two reasons, both worth preserving here:

1. A security defect must not wait on a design decision.
2. **Mirroring** `login` **keeps ONE MFA semantics across both login routes.** Two different MFA shapes on two login routes would recreate the very class that produced [KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) — paths that must agree, drifting because nothing compares them — while closing a single instance of it.

So the minimal fix is not a stopgap that this ticket replaces in shame; it is the correct first move. This ticket is the upgrade.

## What a proper flow looks like

`POST /api/oauth/authorize` currently does password verification and code issuance in one request, then 302s. A second-factor challenge needs an intermediate state:

1. credentials verified → if `user.mfaEnabled`, **do not** mint an authorization code; return/redirect to an MFA challenge bearing a short-lived, single-use challenge token bound to (user, client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, scope, state);
2. the challenge is satisfied (TOTP, or backup code, matching `login`'s semantics);
3. only then mint the authorization code and 302.

**Open questions this ticket exists to answer** — none of them decided:

* Does the challenge render server-side, or does the OAuth client host it? The latter needs the challenge token to be safe to hand to a client.
* **Where does the challenge state live?** Redis with a TTL is the obvious answer and matches the lockout store; it is also a new short-lived-secret surface.
* How does this interact with PKCE (`code_challenge` / `code_challenge_method`) — the challenge token must not become a way to bypass or re-bind PKCE parameters.
* Backup codes: `login` accepts them ([`auth.ts:507-514`](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura>)). Consent should too, or the asymmetry needs stating.
* Rate limiting on the challenge step. [KS-733](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-733) already records that `/api/users/me/mfa/*` is unthrottled and ~450x more attackable than `/api/auth/login` — a new TOTP-accepting surface must not repeat that.

## A coverage note that matters for whatever ships here

[KS-548](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-548) measured why the current defect went unseen: `POST /api/oauth/authorize` declares `security: []`, is one of only **2 operations of 318** declaring a 3xx, and **its 302 path is never exercised** — generated `client_id`/`redirect_uri` values reference no registered client, so it 400s per RFC 6749 first, and Schemathesis has no per-operation don't-follow-redirects switch.

**So this route is structurally invisible to the sweep, and a redirect-based challenge flow adds MORE redirect surface to a route the fuzzers already cannot reach.** Whatever ships here needs its own tests; it will not be caught by the platform suites.

## Not in scope

The three checks themselves (MFA gate, lockout, status refusal) and the shared `assertLoginAllowed` extraction — those are KS-781's.

## Related

[KS-781](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-781) (the security half — the minimal `mfaCode` fix; **this ticket must not block it**) · [KS-737](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-737) (the class: two paths that must agree) · [KS-548](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-548) (why the sweep cannot reach this route) · [KS-733](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-733) (unthrottled TOTP surface) · [KS-722](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-722) (other shapes on the social handler)

title: Review stream: S<->K integration contract
description:

title: Review stream: API contract and the four platform suites
description:
**Review stream for Peter — one review, one test pass, 19 tickets.**

## The one test pass

1. Regenerate the OpenAPI spec, then **restart** the api-gateway container. The yaml is bind-mounted, so a restart publishes it and a rebuild does not.
2. `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py pre-merge --base-url http://localhost:6882` — **13.4 min measured** (~2,016 cases over 318 operations). Report **the failing SET of operation ids and its diff against the develop baseline set**, never a bare count.
3. `node scripts/preflight/spec-auth-conformance.mjs --base http://localhost:6882` (seconds) — every bearer-authed operation must reject unauthenticated.
4. `cd systemTest/playwright && npm run quality:static && npm run test:unit && npm run test:e2e` — **3.8 s measured**, all three must pass.
5. `cd systemTest/performance && npm run test:smoke` — **53 s measured**. Read **the printed** `Status:` **line, not the exit code**, which is 0 either way.

## Two traps that make this run lie

* **A second back-to-back Schemathesis run fails at *setup* with 401**, not on a finding: the fuzz tiers change the test persona's password. `docker restart secuura-auth` re-seeds it. The `Run validity: OK` line does not catch this — it counts schemathesis operations, not pytest setup errors.
* **A partial stack produces a confident FALSE RED. **`docker-compose.local.yml` defines 38 services; when some are down the gateway answers `502 BAD_GATEWAY` and the suites score it as a defect indistinguishable from a real one. Run `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml ps` first and confirm every service is up.

Commands and wall-clocks are quoted from `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` section *Manual CI-gate equivalents*.

title: audit-locks scans 35 of 45 lockfiles — 3 vulnerable locks have coverage from neither gate
description:
## BLUF

`audit-locks.mjs` **scans 35 of the repo's 45 lockfiles, and three of the ten it cannot see carry a vulnerable package right now** — with coverage from neither gate. The script prints "35 standalone lockfiles" as its headline, which reads like a total; it is a *surface*, and the surface is ten locks short of the repo.

## Measured

`findStandaloneLocks()` (`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs:77-88`) is hardcoded to:

```js
for (const top of ['services', 'packages', 'frontend', 'scripts']) {
```

— one level deep, four top-level directories, all under `Blockchain/Dev`. Everything else is invisible to it.

Locks outside the scan, at `develop` `e02e15811` (all 45 locks parsed from the git blobs):

| lock | vulnerable content | covered by anything? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/connectors/whatsapp-bot` | **qs@6.14.2** | **NO** — `connectors/` is simply not in the list |
| `systemTest/akto` | **fast-uri@3.1.5** | **NO** — repo root, outside `devRoot` entirely |
| `systemTest/api-explorer` | **fast-uri@3.1.5** | **NO** — same |
| `Blockchain/Dev/package-lock.json` | fast-uri@3.1.5, qs@6.15.3 | yes — audit-gate's hoisted root scan |
| `Blockchain/Dev/mobile/secuura-app` | — | no |
| `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e`, `tests/e2e-v2` | — | no |
| `observability` | — | no |
| `systemTest/performance`, `systemTest/playwright` | — | no |

`qs@6.14.2` is inside both GHSA-4mjr-xmp4-gh2g and GHSA-x5fp-wj9c-mxmx. `fast-uri@3.1.5` is inside all four of the HIGH fast-uri advisories (GHSA-5jgf / GHSA-f65p / GHSA-fph4 / GHSA-jqff — SSRF and host confusion).

## The consequence that has already bitten us

**#794's fast-uri baseline row says the advisory is present in FIVE locks. It is present in SEVEN.** The row was written from what the gate can see, and the gate cannot see `systemTest/akto` or `systemTest/api-explorer`. Applying that five-file list as a fix set would have left two locks on `fast-uri@3.1.5`, kept the advisory live, and made a correct fix look like it had failed.

The same blind spot means `connectors/whatsapp-bot`'s `qs@6.14.2` has never appeared in any gate output, in either direction — it is not baselined and not reported.

## The ask

Widen the discovery so the gate's count is the repo's count, or state the exclusions deliberately. Both are defensible; what is not defensible is a hardcoded four-directory list that silently decides the scope. Two shapes worth considering:

1. **Discover, don't enumerate** — walk for `package-lock.json` from the repo root, excluding `node_modules`, and let an explicit deny-list carry any genuine exclusions with a reason each.
2. **Keep the list, print the gap** — if `systemTest/` and `connectors/` are deliberately out of scope, the script should say so in its output and name what it skipped, so "35 lockfiles" is never read as "all of them".

`lockfile-cleanroom.sh` has the same four-directory shape (`find services packages frontend scripts`) and would need the same treatment to stay consistent.

## Done when

Every `package-lock.json` in the repo is either scanned, or excluded by a named rule with a recorded reason; and the script's summary line states its surface rather than implying a total. `connectors/whatsapp-bot`'s qs and the two `systemTest` fast-uri pins are triaged either way.

## Not in scope

Fixing the three vulnerable locks. The `fast-uri` overrides for `systemTest/akto` and `systemTest/api-explorer` are already applied on `feature/ks-763-fast-uri-overrides` `7b40543a3` (KS-763); `connectors/whatsapp-bot`'s qs is blocked by tilde parents like the other 27 (see KS-763's measurement comment).

Filed from session 113 — found while red-proving the KS-763 gate hardening: the gate's own scan output disagreed with my lockfile parse, and the gate was the one that was short.

title: Decide the 17 baseline entries that carry no `expires` — permanent acceptance, or dated exception?
description:
## BLUF

**17 of the 35 baseline entries carry no** `expires`**, and each one is a decision nobody has made explicitly.** They predate the expiry requirement and read as permanent acceptances — unreachable code paths, build-tree-only dependencies — which is why they were written without a date. Since KS-763 they are enumerated in `GRANDFATHERED_NO_EXPIRY` (`scripts/audit/baseline-contract.mjs`) rather than admitted by a missing-field check, so the set is now **countable and closed**: any *new* entry without `expires` fails the gate. This ticket is the decision on the 17 themselves.

## The ask

For each entry: does it stay a permanent acceptance, or does it become a dated exception with a review date? A permanent acceptance is a legitimate answer — it just has to be an answer, rather than a field nobody filled in.

## The set

Predicate: every key in `accepted` with no `expires`, at `develop` `e02e15811`. Count re-derived, not copied.

| GHSA | package | deciding ticket |
| -- | -- | -- |
| GHSA-2mjp-6q6p-2qxm | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-35p6-xmwp-9g52 | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-4992-7rv2-5pvq | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-5qjj-4xww-7phc | valibot | KS-493 |
| GHSA-848j-6mx2-7j84 | elliptic | KS-470 |
| GHSA-8xcm-r25x-g524 | undici | KS-559 |
| GHSA-92pp-h63x-v22m | @hono/node-server | KS-470 |
| GHSA-g8m3-5g58-fq7m | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-g9mf-h72j-4rw9 | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-m8rv-5g2x-5cg5 | undici | KS-559 |
| GHSA-p88m-4jfj-68fv | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-v2v4-37r5-5v8g | ip-address | KS-470 |
| GHSA-v3r7-h72x-cjcm | undici | KS-559 |
| GHSA-v9p9-hfj2-hcw8 | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-vrm6-8vpv-qv8q | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-vxpw-j846-p89q | undici | KS-470 |
| GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq | uuid | KS-470 |

**13 of the 17 are** `undici`, all resting on the same acceptance (the issuer build tree; no backend service pulls it), re-verified 2026-08-12 against all 27 backend standalone locks. If that reasoning still holds, those 13 are one decision, not thirteen.

## Why it matters

The baseline's own `$comment` says entries with `expires` are temporary exceptions pending a fix — which implies entries *without* one are permanent. Nothing in the file states that, and until KS-763 nothing enforced it either. Someone reading a bare entry cannot tell "we decided this is permanently fine" from "we forgot the date".

## Done when

Each of the 17 either (a) carries an `expires` and leaves `GRANDFATHERED_NO_EXPIRY`, or (b) carries an explicit note in its `reason` saying it is a permanent acceptance and why re-review is not needed. The set shrinks to what was consciously chosen.

## Not in scope

Changing any acceptance. Nothing here says the 17 are wrong — only that their permanence is currently implicit.

title: Merge helper must refuse a non-read SHA and have no fallback that re-derives its own expectation — the #774 gate could not fail
description:
## BLUF

**A merge gate that asserts the head SHA can be made unable to fail, and it was, tonight, on PR #774.** Two defects combined; the second is the dangerous one and it is mechanically preventable.

## What happened (s112, 2026-09-03)

The merge helper takes an *expected* head SHA and refuses to PUT if the PR's actual head differs.
