1. **The expected SHA was fabricated.** It was produced by extending a 9-character prefix (`21ba93b49`, copied from a boot report table) into a full 40-character string — 31 invented hex characters. `git cat-file -t` on it returns *"fatal: could not get object info"*; on the real head, `commit`. It was never a repo object. This is the second instance of the standing line *"a SHA is READ or it is not used — never extended from a prefix"* in two sessions.
2. **The recovery deleted the assertion.** The call was written as:

   ```
   merge_helper 774 <fabricated> || merge_helper 774 "$(gh api …/pulls/774 --jq .head.sha)"
   ```

   The fallback **re-reads the head from the API and passes it back as the EXPECTED value**, so `expected == actual` by construction. That gate cannot fail. #774 was merged behind a head-check that proved nothing.

The merge itself was correct — the reviews check is an independent gate, ran against the real head, and the PUT carried that same read SHA — but one gate of six was self-confirming and nothing in the tooling said so.

## The standing line this produced

> **A fallback that re-reads the value it is asserting has deleted the assertion — a retry may change the ACTION but never the EXPECTATION.**

Adopted fleet-wide. This ticket is the mechanical half, in this repo.

## Done means

A committed merge helper (`scripts/` — replacing the ad-hoc per-session one) that:

1. **Refuses an expected SHA that is not exactly 40 hex characters.** A prefix is a hard error with a message naming the rule, not a silent widening.
2. **Reads the expected SHA itself**, in the same invocation, from `git ls-remote refs/pull/<n>/head` or the pulls API — and takes the *comparison* value from a second, independent read, so the two can disagree.
3. **Has no fallback path that re-derives the expectation.** A STOP is terminal. A retry may re-read the *actual*, never the *expected*.
4. **Verifies the approval independently** — `commit_id == head.sha` on `/pulls/{n}/reviews` — and requires `mergeable_state == clean`, so no single gate carries the decision alone.
5. Ships with a **self-test** proving each refusal fires: a short SHA rejected, a mismatched SHA rejected, a stale approval rejected, and a valid case allowed. The self-test is the control — a gate whose refusals are never exercised is a gate nobody knows works.

## Why it is worth committing rather than remembering

Every session so far has re-written this helper inline, which is why the same class recurs. The rule is cheap to encode and expensive to re-learn: the last two sessions each lost a round to a SHA that was not read.

title: similarity-undiscriminating FP entries have no staleness detection — a tolerance can outlive its premise and keep hiding a real finding
description:
## BLUF

`similarity-undiscriminating` **false-positive entries have no staleness detection, so a tolerance can outlive the condition that justified it and silently keep hiding a real finding.** Raised by @peter in his systemTest review of [PR #783](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/783>) (2026-09-02 14:25Z). Not a blocker for that PR — a decision in its own right.

## The asymmetry

The endpoint-scoped false-positive table has two kinds, and they are guarded very differently:

| kind | offline spec check | live probe that goes red when stale |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `public-by-design` | yes | **yes** — `publicEndpointGuard.ts` fires an unauthenticated request at each entry; a 401/403 means the endpoint now enforces auth, so the suppression is stale |
| `similarity-undiscriminating` | yes | **no** — nothing ever re-measures the null attack |

Measured on the local stack 2026-09-02 while confirming #783: the guard probes **3 **`public-by-design` entries (all 200 = `public`, 0 stale) and skips all **5** similarity entries — and the control run shows each of those five returns **401**, which the classifier would call `stale`. So the kind gate is correct and necessary; it also means the similarity arm has no live evidence rule at all.

## Why it matters

The five entries carry measured `percentageMatch` figures — 35.9%, 37.5%, **0%**, 12.32%, 16.67% — and every one is **a snapshot of one day's data volatility**. The tolerance is justified by "this endpoint's body changes under the scan's own traffic, so the similarity template cannot discriminate here". That premise can stop being true without anything changing in this repo: if `/api/status` stabilises, the template would discriminate fine, and the entry keeps suppressing it. A suppression whose premise has expired is indistinguishable from a suppression that is still earned.

## The decision (Peter's two options, with his lean)

1. `expires` **per entry**, checked by the existing offline guard.
2. **A nightly null-attack re-measurement** that goes red when a figure moves above a threshold. ← **Peter's lean, and the recommendation**

His reasoning, which I would not improve on: *"an expiry only tells you time has passed, a re-measurement tells you the premise changed."*

Option 2 costs a scheduled job and a threshold nobody has picked yet; option 1 is nearly free but only ever produces a prompt to re-measure by hand — which is the work option 2 automates.

## Done when

* A decision is recorded between (1) and (2), by @kam or @peter.
* The chosen mechanism is implemented and has a red-proof: an entry whose premise has expired must make the gate go red, with a control proving the mechanism does not simply red everything.
* The `similarity-undiscriminating` kind has a stated evidence rule in the same place `public-by-design`'s live probe is documented, so the asymmetry cannot silently return.

## Context

Filed from session 111 under Peter's review of #783. Both the design (`kind` split, bound to `SIMILARITY_TEMPLATE_IDS`, now a compiler-enforced union) and the decision to list only `ADD_USER_ID` were endorsed in that review; this is the one piece he left open.

title: The GitHub integration walks Linear tickets on branch names and PR bodies — 4 unrequested state changes in one night, all reverted by hand
description:
## BLUF

**The GitHub↔Linear integration moves tickets nobody asked it to move, and the board has been silently wrong between each walk and the next manual revert.** Four measured walks in one night, on three different tickets, all with `actor = automation`. Every one had to be reverted by hand, and one ticket was walked twice.

## Measured (2026-09-02, all times UTC)

| time | ticket | walk | trigger |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| ~13:1x | KS-229 | `Backlog → In Review` | #789's body cites KS-229 |
| 14:32 | KS-365 | `Tested Not Deployed → In Progress` | #793 opened |
| 14:33 | KS-365 | `In Progress → In Review` | #793 opened |
| 14:44 | KS-229 | `Backlog → In Review` | #785 pushed; branch `docs/ks-229-encryptedfield-header` |

The trigger is an identifier appearing in a **branch name or PR body**. That is not a statement about the ticket's state, and the integration treats it as one.

## Why it is worse than cosmetic

* **A tracker ticket walked to In Review implies its whole finding set is with a reviewer.** KS-229 is the 2026-06-10 assurance-review tracker; #785 closes one Low finding under it. The board said the tracker was in review; it was not.
* **It walks tickets OUT of terminal states.** KS-365 was walked off `Tested Not Deployed`, which is part of a census Kam asked to keep visible. A state Kam is reading as a count can be changed by opening an unrelated follow-up PR.
* **It can move someone else's ticket.** An identifier in a branch name transitions that ticket regardless of who owns it — already recorded as a known trap on this board.
* The walks are only ever caught because a human or agent happens to be watching the history API. Between the walk and the revert, the board is wrong and nobody is told.

## Done when

1. The integration's state mapping is either **disabled** for automatic transitions, or narrowed to a signal that actually means something (a merged PR that *closes* the ticket via a `Closes #`-style link, not a branch-name substring).
2. A stated rule for what an automated transition is allowed to do, written where the board rules live.
3. Until (1), the standing practice is recorded: **any automated transition on a tracker ticket is noise — walk it back with a one-line comment naming the PR.**

## Notes

Filed from session 111 after the second KS-229 revert of the night. Not urgent — it is board hygiene, not a platform defect — but it is a recurring manual tax and it makes the board unreliable as a record precisely when several PRs are moving at once.

Searched before filing: no existing ticket covers this (`title contains "auto-transition"` → 0, `"walk"` → 1 unrelated, `"integration"` → 12 all unrelated; control `"erasure"` → 3, so the query discriminates).

title: Connector erasure re-drive is unbounded against concurrency — and all three prescribed fixes are blocked (QA F-6)
description:
**BLUF — QA F-6. The connector erasure re-drive SELECT is unbounded against concurrency, and all THREE of the fixes prescribed for it are blocked by something measurable. Filing rather than half-building one, because each of the three fails in a way that is worse than the defect.**

The race (`services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts`, `executeErasureByExternalRef`): the re-drive read

```sql
SELECT id FROM data_subject_requests
WHERE user_id = $1::uuid AND type = 'erasure'
  AND status NOT IN ('completed', 'denied')
ORDER BY requested_at ASC LIMIT 1
```

takes no lock. Platform S retries **without bound**, so two retries that overlap either both select the same DSR and both drive `executeErasureImpl` against it, or both miss and both file one — the orphan accumulation the re-drive was added to prevent.

### The three prescribed fixes, each measured

**1. Partial unique index — cannot be built on existing data.**

```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX … ON data_subject_requests (user_id)
  WHERE type = 'erasure' AND status NOT IN ('completed','denied');
```

Measured on the local database: **4 users already hold more than one non-terminal erasure DSR.** The index would fail to build. (Control: the same GROUP BY … HAVING count(*) > 1 without the type/status predicate returns **12**, so the query discriminates and the 4 is not a false zero.) This needs a data-reconciliation migration first — deciding which duplicate survives is a GDPR-records question, not an index.

**2.** `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` **— wrong for this shape.** If the row is locked by a concurrent attempt, SKIP LOCKED returns nothing, so the second caller falls through to the `else` branch and **files a new DSR**. That is precisely the accumulation the re-drive block exists to prevent, and the comment above it says so. Plain blocking `FOR UPDATE` is the right semantic, but it is inert outside an explicit transaction — a single `$queryRaw` commits immediately and drops the lock.

**3.** `prisma.$transaction` **+** `pg_advisory_xact_lock` **— deadlocks on the connection pool.** Transaction-scoped is the correct lock kind here (`pgbouncer.ini:54` is `pool_mode = transaction`, so a session-scoped advisory lock would leak onto whichever client next receives the server connection). But the block it would have to wrap calls `createDSR`, and `createDSR` issues its INSERT on the **module-level** `prisma` (`gdprService.ts:289`), not on the `tx` handle. So the inner write runs on a *different* connection, outside the transaction — losing the atomicity the lock was for — and worse, the outer transaction holds one pooled server connection while the inner call waits for another from the same pool. Under load that is a self-deadlock.

### What a real fix needs

Any of these, and each is its own piece of work:

* Thread a transaction client through `createDSR` (and `writePii`, which it awaits) so the claim and the INSERT share one connection — then the advisory lock works as intended; **or**
* an optimistic claim using the status vocabulary that already exists: a single atomic `UPDATE … SET status='processing' WHERE … AND status='pending' RETURNING id`, where losing the claim means another attempt is in flight. This needs a staleness timeout, or a crashed attempt strands the DSR in `processing` forever; **or**
* reconcile the 4 duplicate rows, then add the partial unique index and have the caller catch `23505` and re-read.

### Scope note

Not shipped in #790. That PR closes QA F-1 (denied DSRs re-driven) and F-5 (a test asserting its own fixture), both Majors, and adding a half-bounded lock would have made the concurrency story *look* handled while leaving the deadlock in. The re-drive block itself is not a regression from #790 — it was added in that PR's earlier revision and the unboundedness is inherent to the shape, not to the KS-695 change.

### Provenance

Measured 2026-09-02 (session 110) against branch `feature/ks-695-ask1-erasure-by-external-ref` at `b8d658d2a`, `develop` at `0e67228df`. Duplicate counts and the control read from the local Postgres read-only; `pool_mode` read from `docker/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini:54` and confirmed inside the running `secuura-pgbouncer` container. No writes.

title: Wire up the opaque refresh token that createSession already mints — one write site, zero read sites (KS-329 ruling (a) prerequisite)
description:
**BLUF —** `createSession` **has minted an opaque refresh token on every session since the session service was written, and nothing has ever read it. One write site, zero read sites, measured with a control. Wiring it up is the prerequisite Kam's KS-329 ruling (a) actually names, it is not PQC work, and it can ship without committing to ML-DSA at all.**

**Recommendation:** do this first, on its own; leave KS-329 to be the algorithm swap, which gets materially smaller once the refresh path carries no signature.

### The measurement

`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:143`:

```
refreshToken: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex'),
```

* Write sites for `session.refreshToken`: **1** — `session.ts:289`, inside `rotateSessionRefreshToken`.
* Read / compare sites across all of `services/`: **0**. The only other occurrence of the identifier anywhere is a comment at `routes/auth.ts:635`.
* **Control:** the same grep against `session.isActive` — a field that genuinely is compared — returns **6** read sites (`session.ts:265, 304, 346, 357, 363`, `oauth.ts:391`). The search can find comparisons; the zero is real.
* `session.token` (`session.ts:142`, same `randomBytes(32)` shape) has **zero** read sites too.

The code already says it. `routes/auth.ts:634-635`:

> `// The session-record rotation alone is not enough — nothing in the`
> `// /refresh path compared the incoming JWT against session.refreshToken.`

The other half of the ruling is already live: `POST /api/auth/refresh` does a server-side session lookup at `routes/auth.ts:606-607` (`verifyRefreshToken` → `getSession(payload.sessionId)`). Both halves exist. What is missing is the wire between them — the cookie carries the JWT, the lookup keys off a claim *inside* that JWT, and the opaque handle sits in Redis unread.

### Why it stands on its own merits, independent of PQC

* **It removes a signature from a path that does not need one.** The refresh token is presented to exactly one endpoint, which already loads server-side state. A signed 942–1071 B JWT is doing work a 64 B handle does better.
* **It makes the size ceiling disappear permanently.** Measured on develop `8c9559cfd`: an ML-DSA-65 refresh token signs to **5018–5147 B** on real payloads against **3976 B** of usable cookie value (RFC 6265 §6.1 counts name + attributes; the exact options at `auth.ts:644-650` cost 120 B). Over by 1042–1171 B. ML-DSA-44 fits by **14 bytes** on the widest real profile — a coincidence, not a design. A 64 B handle leaves 3912 B spare for any future algorithm.
* **It simplifies reuse detection.** Today's A-05 control is sound — `denylistRefreshJti` throws rather than skips when Redis is down (`refreshDenylist.ts:30-35`), and the TTL matches the token's own remaining life — but a handle compared against the session record gives the same guarantee by construction, with no `jti`, no denylist and no TTL arithmetic.

### Scope

1. Redis reverse index `refresh:<handle> → sessionId`. Sessions are keyed `sess:<id>` and `user_sessions:<userId>` — there is currently no way to find a session *by* refresh token.
2. `POST /api/auth/refresh` — look up by handle, compare against `session.refreshToken`, rotate; drop `verifyRefreshToken` from the path.
3. The three cookie-set sites carry the handle instead of the JWT: `routes/auth.ts:394` (register), `:565` (login), `:644` (refresh).
4. `routes/oauth.ts` — `:242` and `:289` emit `refresh_token` in the body, and `:254-271` runs its **own** refresh path with its own `verifyRefreshToken` + denylist check. It moves in the same change or it becomes the bypass.
5. `shouldEmitRefreshTokenInBody` (`auth.ts:100-102`) — native/api clients take the token in the body and are not cookie-capped, but they should carry the handle too rather than leaving two token formats to verify forever.
6. **Transition, and this is the decision worth making explicitly rather than discovering:** live cookies hold JWTs. Either accept both formats for one refresh lifetime (7 days) then drop the JWT branch, or accept a single forced re-login across the estate.
7. `generateRefreshToken` / `verifyRefreshToken` / `generateTokenPair` shrink or go.

### Sizing

**1–2 days**, dominated by item 6 (the transition window) and item 4 (oauth's parallel path), not by the handle itself. Failing-test-first; the reverse index and the both-formats window each want their own test with a negative control.

### Provenance

Measured 2026-09-02 (session 110) against develop `8c9559cfd` — a read of the working tree plus local signing runs with the tree's own `jose` 6.2.3 on Node v24.7.0. No code changed, no platform writes. Full numbers, the per-profile size table and the nginx buffer check are in the KS-329 design note (comment `a9c84d3b`).

Prerequisite for KS-329. Ruling: Kam, 2026-09-02 19:35 AEST, decision card `secuura-ks329-refresh-token-size` (KS-329 comment `f62f6761`).

title: Schemathesis baseline gate is unreachable: run.py skips it whenever the sweep fails — i.e. on every run it exists to triage
description:
## BLUF

**The Schemathesis baseline gate added by KS-256 (PR #782) ships inert: it is skipped on exactly the runs it exists to triage.** Not a regression — `develop` has no baseline gate at all — but the feature does not do what its own header claims until this is fixed.

## Mechanism

`systemTest/schemathesis/scripts/run.py:533`:

```python
if not success:
    Logger.warning("SKIPPED - upstream gate failed: report reconciliation and the "
                   "schemathesis baseline gate were not evaluated for this run.")
else:
    success = evaluate_report_reconciliation(OUTPUT_DIR)
    if success:
        success = evaluate_schemathesis_baseline(...)
```

`success` already carries the sweep's own outcome. So:

* sweep **fails** -> `success` False -> **baseline gate skipped** — but a failing sweep is the only thing the baseline has to triage;
* sweep **passes** -> gate runs -> nothing to triage.

The gate is unreachable in its own use case. The 97 accepted `check::operation` pairs in `config/schemathesis-baseline.json` therefore gate nothing as shipped.

## Measured

Run `pr-2026-09-02T07-06-54Z` against `custody/568-rebase` @ `8d7109411`: 10 failing operations, `Run validity: OK - 0 of 314 operations errored`, and then `SKIPPED - upstream gate failed`. The triage that would have classified all 10 as known never ran.

## Relationship to KS-256 QA F-5

F-5 (fixed in s105) made this skip **speak** — before it, the `and` short-circuit meant the gate silently never ran, which read exactly like a pass. That fix is why this is visible at all. It did not make the gate **reachable**.

## Fix

Evaluate report reconciliation and the baseline **eagerly** rather than behind `success`, and combine the verdicts afterwards. The existing code comment already names this as the tidier shape and records why it was deferred: *"a gate that fires on an INVALID run may not have the artefacts it reads, so that swap needs an invalid-run rehearsal this change does not have."*

So the work is: the eager swap **plus** an invalid-run rehearsal proving the baseline gate degrades safely when the artefacts it reads are absent or partial.

## Acceptance

A run with a failing sweep whose failures are all in the baseline must print the baseline gate's verdict, and a failing pair **absent** from the baseline must still fail the run — with a control proving the gate can fail (deliberately remove one accepted pair and confirm the run goes red).

Found in s106 while running the four suites for PR #782. Peter's triage input wanted on priority.

title: svc_api_keys.organization_id is not a tenancy boundary and nothing keeps it coherent with tenant_id — an incoherent pair is storable
description:
## BLUF

`svc_api_keys.organization_id` **is not a tenancy boundary and nothing keeps it coherent with** `tenant_id`**.** An incoherent pair — an org belonging to tenant B stored against `tenant_id` = tenant A — **is storable**, and RLS then resolves the row entirely in favour of `tenant_id`, because the policy never consults `organization_id`.

**Not a live escalation.** Post-KS-742 the application enforces tenancy on both `GET` and `POST /api/keys`, and DB-layer isolation is working as designed (measured below). This is an **integrity gap**: future code that treats `organization_id` as implying a tenant would be wrong, and nothing in the schema would stop it.

Raised by Peter on the KS-742 thread ("the org/tenant pair can be made incoherent … bounded, and unmeasured by me"). This is the measurement.

## Measured on LOCAL

**Constraints — read, not inherited. **`svc_api_keys` has exactly **one** constraint:

```
svc_api_keys_pkey | p
```

No foreign keys, no check constraint tying `organization_id` to `tenant_id`. `018_svc_api_keys_reconcile.sql` was read in full: it does ADD COLUMN, a backfill (`organization_id` → `organizations.tenant_id`), NOT NULL, an index and RLS — and **adds no constraint of any kind**. The backfill sets the pair coherently *once*; nothing holds it that way afterwards.

**Storability — proven, nothing persisted.** An INSERT of `{organization_id: <an org owned by tenant fd4254fd…>, tenant_id: a0000000-…-0001}` was **accepted** (`INSERT 0 1`) inside a transaction that then **ROLLED BACK**. Post-rollback control: rows matching the probe id = **0**. I used a rollback rather than a persisted write because it answers the same question and leaves no credential behind.

**What the GUC then shows.** The `tenant_isolation` policy keys on `tenant_id` alone:

```
(current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true) IS NOT NULL
 AND current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true) <> ''
 AND tenant_id::text = current_setting('app.current_tenant_id', true))
OR current_setting('app.tenant_scope_bypass', true) = 'platform_admin'
```

So an incoherent row is visible to **tenant A's** admins (its `tenant_id`) and invisible to **tenant B's** (its org's real owner). `organization_id` plays no part.

## ⚠ Two corrections to my own reading, recorded because they nearly became findings

**1. A** `qual=true` **policy that looked like a hole is not one. **`svc_api_keys` carries a second policy, `svc_api_keys_auth_lookup`, PERMISSIVE / SELECT / `qual=true`. Permissive policies are OR'd, so at first read that appeared to defeat tenant isolation for every reader. **It does not** — it is scoped to `roles={secuura_auth_lookup}`, a dedicated role, while `tenant_isolation` applies to `{public}`. Same pattern on `users` and `oauth_apps`. It is a correctly-scoped carve-out for the credential-lookup path, which must find a key by hash *before* a tenant context exists. **Recording it positively so nobody "fixes" it later.**

**2. My first RLS measurement was worthless.** I connected as `secuura` — `super=true bypassrls=true` — so RLS never applied and every count came back unfiltered. The control that caught it: `documents` (a single fail-closed policy, no auth-lookup policy) returned the same 95,015 with and without a dead tenant GUC, which is impossible if the GUC were filtering.

**Re-measured as** `secuura_app` (`super=false bypassrls=false`), with controls that fire in both directions:

| session | rows |
| -- | -- |
| no GUC | **0** |
| GUC = a nonexistent tenant | **0** |
| GUC = the default tenant | **480** |
| `app.tenant_scope_bypass = platform_admin` | **1165** |
| as `secuura_auth_lookup`, no GUC | **1165** (its policy, as intended) |

So the fail-closed policy is genuinely fail-closed for the runtime role, and the instrument can return non-zero — the 0s mean something.

## Fix shape (not done here)

Either a `FOREIGN KEY (organization_id) REFERENCES organizations(id)` plus a trigger or check asserting `tenant_id` matches that org's tenant, **or** an explicit decision that `organization_id` is descriptive metadata and never a boundary — written down where the next reader will find it. The second is cheaper and may be the right answer; what should not persist is the current state, where the field *looks* like a boundary and is not.

⚠ Adding an FK is not free: `organization_id` is NULL-able by design (018 §2, so the originate admin path can issue tenant-scoped keys with no org), and the s99 record notes demo held a synthetic org with no `organizations` row. Any FK needs that data cleaned first.

Filed session 100, KS-742 follow-up 6(b). No fix this session by instruction.

title: Security events carry no tenant at all — KS-743 had to gate them platform-only, which is a workaround for the data model
description:
## BLUF

**Security events are authorised platform-only because they carry no tenant — not because platform-only is the right long-term answer.** KS-743 gated `GET /api/events` and `PATCH /api/events/:id/resolve` to platform roles. That is the only authorisation that is *true* of the surface today, and it is a workaround for a data-model gap.

## The gap, measured

* `SecurityEvent` (`services/security/src/index.ts:95-107`) has **no tenant field**: `id, eventType, severity, source, userId?, ipAddress?, details, resolved, resolvedAt?, resolvedBy?, createdAt`.
* `svc_security_events` (`migrations/002_verification-tiers.sql:536`) has **no tenant column**.
* `dbSaveSecurityEvent` (`index.ts:181`) INSERTs **eleven** columns — `id, event_type, severity, source, user_id, ip_address, details, resolved, resolved_at, resolved_by, created_at`. None is a tenant or an organisation.

So there is no `targetTenantId` to hand `decideTenantAccess`, which is exactly why the read could return the whole cross-tenant corpus to an ordinary tenant admin (measured before the fix on the local published gateway: **200,** `total: 651`).

## Consequence of the interim gate

A tenant admin can no longer see security events **for their own tenant either** — because there is no such thing as "their own" yet. That is a real capability loss, accepted deliberately over leaking every tenant's events. It is also invisible today: a sweep of `frontend/` found **zero** references to `/api/security/events` (control: **3** for `/api/security/audit`, which the admin dashboard does use), so nothing in the product currently asks for it.

## What the fix would involve

1. `tenant_id` on `svc_security_events` + a migration, with a decision on what to backfill existing rows to — they have no recoverable tenant, so a NULL/`unknown` sentinel and a policy for reading those.
2. `tenantId` on `SecurityEvent`, derived from the verified JWT at `POST /api/events` (the same server-derived shape `POST /api/audit` already uses at `index.ts:556-561`, deliberately never from the body).
3. Swap `requirePlatformOperator` for `decideTenantAccess` on the two read/write routes, keeping platform cross-tenant reach.
4. Producers: every internal caller of `POST /api/events` needs to be carrying a tenant-bearing token, or the sentinel path has to be defined for them. **Not enumerated here** — that sweep is part of the work, not of this description.

## Status of this description

Points 1-3 are a **design sketch, not an agreed plan**. Point 4 in particular is unmeasured. Whether events should be tenant-scoped at all, rather than remaining a platform-operations surface with a proper operator console, is the actual product question and is **open** — this ticket exists so that question is asked deliberately rather than inherited from a gate I added under time pressure.

Follow-up to KS-743 (PR #778). Filed session 100.

title: Verify results show the user nothing about what was registered — a renamed file confirms green with no explanation (PS-723)
description:
## BLUF

**A verify result shows the user nothing about what was registered, so a renamed file confirms green with no way to notice the rename.** Stuart hit this on PS-723 and ruled the direction: *"it should be explained to the user, otherwise confusion will result… b should also have the note to the user that the filename has changed."*

The API is not the problem — it already returns the registered `title`, `issuer` and `certifiedAt`. **The portal never displays them**, because it reads a nested shape the backend does not emit. And the portal already sends the presented filename, which the backend silently discards. So both halves of the comparison exist today and nothing joins them.

## RECOMMENDATION

Render the registered metadata beside the confirmation, plus a plain-language line that verification is **content-based** — a rename neither breaks nor fakes it. Where the presented filename differs from the registered title, say so explicitly rather than leaving the user to spot it.

One decision is **not mine and should be made before any code**: the flat-vs-nested contract question in §2. That is Peter's call.

## 1. What the verify response actually returns

Measured live, `POST /api/verification/verify` with `contentHash` — the path a renamed-file verify takes:

```
verified: true
title: "E2E Test Certificate"     <- the REGISTERED title
issuer: "demo"
documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt
certification: { certifiedAt, certifiedBy, certifierOrganizationId }
checks: { documentExists, hashValid, integrityVerified, ... }
```

So the metadata Stuart wants shown is already on the wire.

⚠ **The OpenAPI schema understates this. **`VerifyResponse` declares 20 properties and **none** is `title` / `originalFilename` / `registeredAt` / `registrant`; the live response carries `title` and `issuer` anyway. Same declared-vs-actual family as **KS-712** — worth fixing in the same pass so the contract stops lying about this endpoint.

## 2. Why nothing renders — the mechanism

`frontend/verifier/src/components/ResultPage.tsx:423` guards the entire "Document Details" card:

```tsx
{result.verified && result.document && ( ...Title... Issuer... )}
```

* The API returns `title` and `issuer` **at the top level** and emits **no** `document` **object** (measured top-level keys: `verified, documentId, title, documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt, issuer, blockchain, certification, checks, verifiedAt`).
* `result.document` is therefore undefined, the guard is falsy, and **the card never renders**.
* The portal references `result.document.*` **5** times and `result.title` **0** times. Control: `result.verified` matches **14** times, so the grep discriminates.
* The data is **not** lost in parsing — `VerifyResponseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so the top-level `title` survives into the parsed object and is simply never read.
* The schema *does* declare `document: DocumentSummarySchema.nullable().optional()` carrying `title` + `issuer`. **The frontend was written against a nested shape the backend does not produce** — one side moved and the other did not.
* Confirmed on the path in use: all three verifier call sites hit **v1 **`/verification/verify`. v2 is a different shape entirely (`count, hash, matches, verifiedAt`) and the portal does not use it.

### The contract question — Peter's call, not to be decided in the fix

Either the **frontend reads the flat fields**, or the **backend nests them** under `document` to match the schema the client already expects. Both work; they differ in blast radius (the backend shape is consumed by the Outlook add-in and issuer too). Naming it rather than picking it.

## 3. `fileName` is already sent, and silently discarded

`frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx:127` sends `{ contentHash, fileName: file.name }` and `:138` threads `fileName` into the result object. So the **client already holds both halves** of the comparison — presented name and registered title — and needs no new input to detect a mismatch.

Server-side, however:

* `VerifyRequest` declares only `documentId, hash, title, contentHash` — `fileName` **is not in the contract.**
* **No backend route handler reads it**: 0 files under `services/*/src/routes/` reference `fileName`, against a control of **8** referencing `contentHash`.

So the field is sent on every verify and thrown away. Either consume it (and declare it) or stop sending it — the current state is a silent no-op.

## 4. Scope — three surfaces, per Stuart, not just the verifier portal

His comment names them: *"This affects Outlook plug ins, and Verify functionality in 'Views' and directly from the menu."* Verify call sites in the tree:

| app | file |
| -- | -- |
| verifier portal | `frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx`, `ResultPage.tsx` |
| **Outlook add-in** | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/utils/api.ts` |
| issuer portal | `frontend/issuer/src/services/api.ts`, `components/admin/ConnectorsPage.tsx` |

Whatever wording is agreed should land on all of them, or the same confusion simply moves to whichever surface is left out.

## 5. Design constraint — the KS-695 erasure interplay

**KS-695 item 2 brings** `documents.title` **INTO erasure coverage**, because S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`). For S-originated documents that field **is** the original filename — exactly what this ticket wants displayed. Item 3 goes further: connector-scoped dissolution blanks all connector documents' titles.

So the two pull opposite ways: PS-723 wants the registered name shown; KS-695 makes that same field erasable PII that can legitimately be blank. Both are correct on their own terms.

**This must be specified, not discovered:** decide what a verify result shows for a document whose title has been erased — a blank, or an explicit *"registered name erased"* state. Rendering empty silently would recreate today's confusion in a new form.

## Not in scope here

No fix in this ticket — it is the specification and the evidence. No change to PS-723, which is Stuart's.

## Related

* **PS-723** — *Verify still confirms if filename has changed* (Stuart, 2026-09-01). The originating report and his ruling.
* **KS-712** — the declared-vs-actual spec gap this endpoint also exhibits.
* **KS-695** — `documents.title` erasure coverage; the design constraint in §5.

title: test:pr never re-imports the OpenAPI spec, so Akto scans a collection that has drifted from it — a declared operation is not a scanned one
description:
> **Origin.** Parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comment `718362a9` (2026-08-28T22:30:04Z) under "Related, found today and unfiled for the same reason" — `issueCreate` was refusing workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket**; the numbers are the ones recorded on 2026-08-28 against PR [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>).

## BLUF

**Declaring an operation in the OpenAPI spec does not put it in Akto's scan collection. **`test:pr` does **not** re-import the spec — only `test:pre-merge` runs `feed-har` — so the collection Akto scans drifts away from the spec silently, and a PR that adds operations gets an Akto result that never touched them.

This is the [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) premise reaching one step further than that ticket states it. KS-712 says: an operation absent from the spec is invisible to both tools. This says: an operation **present** in the spec can still be invisible to Akto.

## Measured

On PR #762, which declares four operations (`GET`/`PUT` on `/api/privacy/settings` and `/api/settings/notifications`):

| operation | occurrences in the Akto report |
| -- | -- |
| the two endpoints #762 declares | **0** |
| control endpoint A | 105 |
| control endpoint B | 7 |

The two controls are what make the zero readable: the report was produced, it was parsed, and it does contain occurrence counts — the declared endpoints simply are not in it. Without the controls, `0` and "the grep could not have matched" are the same reading.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a note

The failure is **silent and it points the wrong way**. An author who declares a new operation, runs `test:pr`, and sees no Akto finding on it will reasonably conclude the operation was scanned and is clean. Under the current wiring that conclusion is unsupported: the operation was never in the collection. Every "Akto clean" claim in a Test Evidence block on a spec-adding PR carries this caveat, whether or not the author knows it.

This sits directly against the merge flow adopted 2026-08-25, where the **Test Evidence block carries the testing claim**. A block that says "Akto FAIL 3, none on a touched route" is true and still misleading if the touched routes could not have been scanned.

## Not fixed, and why

Re-importing the spec into Akto **mutates harness state** — the collection is shared, and @PeterObeden has live work on it ([KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717)). Doing it unilaterally mid-review would corrupt someone else's measurements to fix a reporting gap. It belongs with the harness owner, alongside [KS-716](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716).

## Possible shapes (for whoever owns it — not a design commitment)

1. Have `test:pr` re-import when the spec's hash has changed since the last import — cheap, and the common case is no change.
2. Fail `test:pr` loudly when an operation touched by the diff is absent from the collection, rather than reporting a clean scan of it. This is the honesty-guard shape already used elsewhere in the harness.
3. Leave `test:pr` alone and have the Test Evidence template require the author to state Akto collection coverage explicitly, so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

Option 2 is the one that fails closed, but it is the harness owner's call.

title: The whole super-admin surface is silently unscanned — no system_admin block means the HAR replay fallback never fires (0 of 16 endpoints, incl. KS-694's GDPR routes)
description:
## BLUF

Every **super-admin-only** endpoint is invisible to Akto on a stock local checkout, and nothing says so. `config/secrets.yml` carries no `system_admin` block — `config/secrets.example.yml` documents one — so `resolveReplayTokens()` returns `adminToken: null`, the issuer→admin fallback never fires, and each endpoint `ISSUER_ADMIN` cannot get a 2xx from stays a spec-imported placeholder (`responseCode: -1`) that `api_selection_filters` excludes from **every** BOLA/BFLA/authz template.

The bias is the problem: the endpoints that are hardest to authenticate to are the privileged ones, so the harness systematically skips the surface where an authz defect matters most — and reports green.

## Measured — 2026-08-29, local slot-1 stack, Akto 2.22.2

```
collection 56068490 "OpenAPI Secuura API": 323 endpoints
  absolute (scannable)  : 307
  relative (unscannable):  16

endpoints scanned, BOLA run:
  relative : 0 / 16
  absolute : 46 / 80 sampled     <-- discriminating control
```

The 16 that never get scanned:

```
/api/admin/audit/export      /api/analytics/activity        /api/analytics/certifications
/api/analytics/governance    /api/analytics/overview        /api/analytics/revenue
/api/analytics/users         /api/analytics/verifications   /api/audit-log
/api/billing/customers/by-email  /api/gdpr/consent/check    /api/gdpr/deletion-log
/api/m365/callback           /api/oauth/authorize           /api/onedrive/files
/api/system-errors
```

The 7 `analytics` paths are excluded on purpose (`VOLATILE_PATH_RE`, KS-357). **The other 9 are not excluded by anything — they are simply unreachable by the replay persona.** They include `/api/gdpr/deletion-log`, `/api/gdpr/consent/check` and `/api/system-errors` — the exact routes **KS-694 (Urgent)** just put a role gate on, and `/api/oauth/authorize`.

Note the tell: an unscannable entry is stored as a bare path (`/api/audit-log` — the tenant-provisioning upstream path) while a scanned one is a full gateway URL (`http://localhost:6882/api/documents`). That difference is a cheap, reliable detector.

## Proof of causation

Adding the documented `system_admin` block to local `secrets.yml` (gitignored; seeded `admin@secuura.com`, per `secrets.example.yml`):

```
captured 2xx samples : 71 → 79
audit-log in api_info: /api/audit-log  →  http://localhost:6882/api/platform/audit-log
ADD_USER_ID on it    : 0 rows → 1 row
```

That change is what made **KS-708** reproducible at all. Before it, `ADD_USER_ID` reported *"188 tested, 0 vulnerable"* while never touching the endpoint under investigation.

## The documentation understates it

`secrets.example.yml:30-34` says `system_admin` is *"optional. Only needed to seed the locked-account test-role… Absent ⇒ that one role is skipped (best-effort), and* `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE` *keeps skipping honestly."*

That is not the whole consequence. Absent, it also removes the entire super-admin surface from HAR replay, and therefore from every similarity-based authz template. Nobody reading that comment would expect it.

## Suggested shape

1. **Warn loudly when** `adminToken` **is null** — name the count of endpoints that will consequently have no 2xx sample. Silence is the actual defect; a skipped endpoint should never be indistinguishable from a clean one (the KS-700 / KS-709 principle, applied to coverage rather than results).
2. Correct the `secrets.example.yml` comment to state the coverage consequence.
3. Consider failing `test:setup` when the block is absent, or defaulting it to the seeded local admin.

## Done means

1. A run without a system-admin token says so, with the affected endpoint count.
2. `secrets.example.yml` states the real consequence.
3. The relative-vs-absolute URL split is asserted somewhere, so this cannot silently regress.

title: Akto reports a PASS for a test that executed NOTHING — 'clean 0 / not-applicable 969 ✓' is a second false-zero axis that richCaptureFailed does not catch
description:
## BLUF

**KS-700 closes one false-zero axis and this is the other one.** On @PeterObeden's 2026-08-28 review run, `analytics: code injection` returned **clean 0 · not-applicable 969** and reported **✓**. The capture *succeeded* — so `richCaptureFailed` is correctly false — and the scan still measured nothing that actually executed. A green tick on zero executed requests.

⚠ **Provenance: Peter's measurement from his** `test:security` **run, not independently reproduced here.** Filed so the class is tracked rather than living in a PR thread.

## ✅ Done so far — PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1336](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1286-akto-2356-honest-coverage-paced-tiers-stall-stop-and-slot-safe-cba284970402) ([KS-1286](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1286/akto-image-2222-2356-latest-paired-local-pair-verified-2026-09-28-and)), merged 2026-09-28

These sections are delivered; the ticket stays open for criteria 1 and 3 below.

* ✅ **A 429 result is no longer scored as a pass** — its own `rateLimited` bucket (it was 79% of a full scan's "passes"); COVERAGE DEGRADED when refusals outnumber what executed.
* ✅ **A zero-run report says NO COVERAGE** instead of "0 vulnerable" (the `-t` filter case in Kamil's comment).
* ✅ **Pacing** so the platform's limiter no longer decides coverage — 0 of 50,306 full-scan results refused (open decision on the platform side: [KS-1374](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1374/akto-scans-are-now-paced-to-fit-the-platforms-rate-limit-test-times)).

## Why KS-700's fix does not cover it

KS-700 distinguishes *"asked Mongo and got nothing"* (`richCaptureFailed`) from *"never asked"*. Both are about the **capture**. This is a third state the capture cannot see: **the capture worked, and what it faithfully reports is that nothing ran.** `clean 0` with `not-applicable 969` means every candidate was filtered out before a request was sent — so the ✓ attests to an empty set, not to a clean one.

Read the way a reader naturally reads it, *"analytics: code injection ✓"* means the endpoints were tested and were fine. It means neither.

`DEV-PROCESS.md` already says an Akto PASS should be read as *"nothing was reported"*, not *"nothing is there"* — this is the sharpest instance of why.

## Suggested shape

Treat **executed == 0 with a non-zero candidate count** as its own verdict, the way `richCaptureFailed` is — not PASS. Something like `NO COVERAGE — 969 candidates, 0 executed`, failing or warning per tier. The count is already computed: `executedResultCount(breakdown)` in `src/scan/runTiming.ts`, and `clean + vulnerable` is the executed figure.

Note the same shape appears in the aggregate: this session's `test:pr` runs report `not-applicable 3281` and `not-on-stack 360` against `clean ~803` — so roughly 80% of every run is filtered before a request is sent. That is not necessarily wrong, but nothing currently asserts a floor on it.

## Done means

1. A scan where a whole test category executes nothing does **not** report ✓.
2. ✅ **Done** — a control: a category that genuinely executes and is clean still passes (so the fix is not "fail everything"). Shown live on slot 2, 2026-09-28: `clean 140 · rate-limited 0` reported PASS three times in the same run.
3. Reproduced from a real run, not only a unit test — the [KS-700](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-700/akto-harness-prints-a-false-zero-when-its-mongo-capture-fails-no) review's own standard.

title: No table references `users`: 0 of the database's 29 foreign keys point at it, across 52 user-reference columns — KS-697 was this hole being exercised
description:
## BLUF

**No table in the platform database has a foreign key to** `users`**.** Not one — across **52** columns named `%user_id` / `%holder_id` / `%_by_id`. The schema *does* use foreign keys (**29** of them), which is what makes this a gap rather than a deliberate house style.

Every one of those 52 columns can therefore hold a uuid that references nobody, and nothing in the database will object.

## Measured — live local DB, `develop cc65abad5`

| measure | value |
| -- | -- |
| foreign keys in the database | **29** |
| of those, pointing at `users` | **0** |
| columns named like a user reference | **52** |
| FKs on `shares` (any) | **0** |
| FKs on `custody_events` | **1** — `document_id` only |

The `custody_events` row is the tell: that table *does* carry an FK, on `document_id`, and `to_holder_id` sits beside it without one.

## Why this is being filed now

[KS-697](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-697) was exactly this hole being exercised: `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` accepted an invented `newHolderId`, returned 201, and **minted an anchor** for a custody chain pointing at a user that has never existed. That route is fixed in application code ([PR #751](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/751>)) — but the fix is one handler, and the underlying condition covers 51 other columns.

Known second instance, unfixed: `POST /api/documents/{id}/share` format-checks `recipients[].userId` (KS-536) but **never checks it exists** — `shares.recipient_user_id` is cast to `::uuid` and inserted with no FK behind it. Lower blast radius than custody (no ownership flip, no anchor), but the same class.

## Not a "just add the FKs" ticket

Recording the reasons up front so whoever picks this up does not discover them the hard way:

1. `users` **is** `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` **fail-closed** (migration 039). FK validation runs as the referencing statement's role, so adding FKs to an RLS-forced table needs thought about which role validates the reference and whether the tenant GUC is set at that moment. This is the KS-458 surface.
2. **Multi-tenancy may put** `users` **in a different database** from the referencing table under the per-tenant-DB model — a cross-database FK is not expressible. That has to be established per table before anything is added.
3. **Existing rows may already violate** what a new FK would assert. KS-697 alone wrote several on local. Any `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT` needs a survey first, and `NOT VALID` + a later `VALIDATE` is probably the shape.
4. **A count guard will lie here. **`users` under FORCE RLS returns 0 rows to a non-superuser without the tenant GUC — an "are there orphans?" query can read clean on a table full of them. Set `app.tenant_scope_bypass` before counting.

## Suggested first step

Not a migration. An **inventory**: for each of the 52 columns, which are genuinely user references, which live in the same database as `users`, and how many current rows are already orphaned. That survey decides whether this is one migration, several, or an application-layer rule instead.

Found during KS-697, 2026-08-27. Filed separately so it does not die when that ticket closes.

title: Akto pr-scan is non-deterministic — three runs on near-identical code gave 1 HIGH / 1 HIGH (different endpoint) / 0 HIGH
description:
## BLUF

**Three Akto** `test:pr` **runs tonight, same harness, same command, gave three different answers — and none of the three carried a captured request or response.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot be read either way: its PASS is not evidence of absence, and its FAIL is not evidence of a defect until re-derived by hand.

## Measured — 2026-08-27, all three within ~20 minutes

| run | target | HIGH |
| -- | -- | -- |
| baseline (s76) | `develop ca5b643e0` | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on a **GDPR** route |
| KS-694 fix branch | `develop` + the KS-694 role-gate fix (touches `gdpr.ts` + `systemErrors.ts` only) | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on `GET /api/documents` |
| 17-PR integration stack | `develop cc65abad5` + 17 open PRs | **0** — `verdict: PASS`, 804 clean, 2 known-FP |

The middle run is the one that rules out "the code changed": that branch touches two route files and cannot have introduced or removed a finding on `/api/documents`.

## The `/api/documents` finding does not reproduce

Derived by hand rather than trusted:

* `?userId=` **injection changes nothing.** The identical document set comes back with no `userId`, with another user's, and with a third user's.
* **Cross-tenant isolation holds.** A default-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 18 documents, an oxford-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 70, **full-id overlap 0**. (An earlier probe of my own appeared to show a shared document — that was an 8-character id truncation in my script, not a leak. Recording the false alarm so nobody re-derives it.)

## Why this matters now

Since 2026-08-27 the four local suites are the **only** merge gate (Kam: *"billing will not be fixed"*). Akto is one of the four. **Two of tonight's three runs would have produced a different merge decision on the same code.** That is the same failure mode `KS-519` names for permanently-red checks, arriving from the other direction.

## Related, already known

`KS-694` came out of the first of these runs — the finding was real but its **label** (`BOLA / ADD_USER_ID`) was wrong, and re-deriving it produced a more precise and more serious defect. Same pattern: the scanner points at something; the label and the endpoint are both unreliable.

## Suggested next step

Establish whether the variance is in the scan (endpoint sampling / timing / auth state) or the reporting, by running `test:pr` N times against a frozen commit with the stack untouched between runs, and recording the HIGH set each time. **Not started** — filed so tonight's measurement is not lost.

title: Anchor-status standoff: a consumer repolls anchors K reports as terminally failed — K's labelling is already honest (KS-587), so the fix is terminal-state handling, not a new K signal
description:
## BLUF

**The standoff is real, but its stated mechanism is wrong — and measuring demo inverted the ownership.** The premise going in was *"K reports simulated anchors as* `confirmed`*; Platform S's honesty rule refuses a* `mock_tx_` *hash; S repolls forever."* Measured on demo tonight, **K does not report them as confirmed.** All 83 simulated anchors on demo are flagged `simulated = true`, `status = failed`, carrying the explicit error `KS-587: simulated placeholder — never on chain; marked …`. **Zero rows on demo are** `simulated = true` **and** `confirmed`**.** K already fixed this — that is what **KS-520 → KS-522 → KS-587** were.

So the accurate statement is: **a consumer is polling anchors that K reports as terminally** `failed`**, forever.** That is not a labelling defect on our side. It is a missing terminal-state rule on the consumer side.

## Recommendation

1. **Layer 1 — the actual fix, PS-side (Stuart's):** treat `status: failed` as **terminal** and stop polling. No new K signal is required; the one already published is sufficient and has been since KS-587 deployed.
2. **Layer 2 — K exposes** `simulated` **machine-readably: ALREADY DONE. This is a no-op, closed here, and no work should be raised for it.** Verified in the **shipped** demo image, not just the source tree.
3. **Layer 3 — env hygiene (Stuart's call):** whatever is polling demo from `52.74.18.212` should not be pointed at demo at all.
4. **Layer 4 — per-environment Blockfrost keys:** still open, still pending the credential question below.

## Detail — what was measured, on demo, read-only

**Demo is not simulating.** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is **absent** from the anchoring container's environment (0 matches against a 22-line env, so the read itself is proven). Boot logs: `Cardano integration active — real blockchain anchoring enabled`, `cardanoMode: "REAL (Blockfrost)"`, network `preview`.

`anchor_store` **composition — 285 rows total:**

| shape | `simulated` | `status` | n | first | last |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| real 64-hex | false | **confirmed** | **194** | 2026-07-08 | 2026-08-14 |
| `mock_tx_*` | **true** | **failed** | **83** | 2026-07-31 | 2026-08-01 |
| NULL | false | failed | 6 | 2026-07-11 | 2026-08-05 |
| real 64-hex | false | failed | 2 | 2026-08-04 | 2026-08-10 |

Crosstab, stated plainly because it is the whole argument: `simulated = true` appears **only** with `status = failed`. **There is no (**`simulated = true`**,** `confirmed`**) row on demo.** Controls: `simulated` is never NULL (0 of 285); totals reconcile 194 + 83 + 6 + 2 = 285.

**The loop's corpus is fully resident on demo — the cross-instance hypothesis is dead.** All **71** distinct anchor ids the loop requests are present in demo's `anchor_store`: **71 present / 0 absent**. Controls both fired: a fabricated id `anchor_0000…0000` matched **0**, a known-real id matched **1**. So these anchors were minted **on demo**; they were not minted on a simulated instance elsewhere and verified here.

**And every one of them is a failed anchor:**

|  | n |
| -- | -- |
| `simulated = true`, `failed`, mock hash | **68** |
| `simulated = false`, `failed`, NULL hash | **3** |
| **confirmed** | **0** |

That is the finding. The loop is polling **71 anchors that can never succeed**, 68 of which K has explicitly labelled as simulated placeholders that were never on chain.

**The** `simulated` **flag is machine-readable, and it ships.** In the **running** demo image (`/app/dist/index.js`, and `docker inspect` shows **no bind-mounts**, so the image *is* what serves):

* `...(simulated ? { simulated: true, simulatedTxRef: rawTxHash } : {})` — 3 emit sites
* `verified: !txView.simulated && anchor.status === 'confirmed'`
* a placeholder hash is moved to `simulatedTxRef` and `transactionHash` is set to **null**, so a mock hash is never presented as a transaction hash

Control: a nonsense token grepped for in the same file returned 0. Source agrees (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts` `honestTxView`, `anchoring.openapi.ts` `simulated: z.boolean().optional()` + `simulatedTxRef`).

**The Blockfrost split — both "zero Blockfrost calls" and "quota exhausted" are true at once.** They describe **different routes**:

| route | behaviour | last 60 min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/anchors/{id}` | **pure DB read**, ~1 ms, no Blockfrost | **1,970 × 200** |
| `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` | **live Blockfrost** | **608 × 200 · 460 × 500** |

**457** of those 500s carry Blockfrost's own string `"Usage is over limit."` (against 3,935 total anchoring log lines). So Stuart's agent's *"zero Blockfrost calls in two hours"* is **correct for status GETs** — that is exactly what they observed, and it is a real property of the code. Our *"quota exhausted"* is **correct for verify-by-hash**. Neither observation refutes the other; the earlier reconciliation hypothesis (creation-simulated / verify-live) was the right shape but the wrong axis — it is **status-read vs verify-by-hash**, not creation vs verification.

**Traffic, for scale.** Last 6 h at demo's edge: **23,515 requests from** `52.74.18.212`**, of 23,515 total — 100.0%** of demo's inbound. Split: `POST /api/verification/verify` 11,620 · `GET /api/anchors/{id}` 9,704 · `GET /api/documents/{id}` 2,190 — **all 200 at the gateway.** ~3,919/hr, consistent with the ~3,850/hr measured on KS-670 across 08-14 → 08-21.

## Attribution, corrected gently

Stuart's agent read the honesty rule as **S's**. The record says the honest-labelling rule was implemented **in K**: **KS-520** (Urgent, Done) — anchoring fabricated a `tx_sim_` hash and marked the document anchored under `SIMULATE_ANCHORING`; **KS-522** (High, Done) — a simulated anchor presented as genuinely verified, no honest-labelling signal; **KS-587** (High, Deployed to UAT) — *"84 demo anchors carry* `mock_tx_` *hashes but are flagged* `simulated=false` *+ confirmed"*. KS-587 is the direct ancestor of this ticket: it found **84** mis-flagged rows and remediated them. Tonight demo holds **83** rows carrying its remediation message. **The defect Stuart's agent describes is one K already found and fixed** — which is worth saying clearly, because it means no K change is needed and the polling behaviour is unaffected by anything we ship.

Credit where due: their diagnosis of the *mechanism* — a consumer refusing a mock hash and retrying forever — is correct and is what made this tractable. Only the direction of the labelling defect was off, and their own caveat (which K instance they queried was unstated) is what prompted the measurement that found it.

## What their numbers describe

Their **1,638 anchors, all simulated** is **not demo** — demo has **285** anchors, of which 83 are simulated. Since all 71 polled ids resolve on demo, the polling target is demo; the 1,638-row instance they inspected is a different K (most likely one of the local development stacks). **Not asserted, and it does not change the finding:** the fix is terminal-state handling regardless of which K holds the larger simulated corpus.

## Still open

* **The credential question, unanswered since 2026-08-20:** does the local K stack hold **demo's** Blockfrost key or its own? If demo's, per-environment key scoping becomes the durable fix, and Kintsugi (its own free-tier project per environment) is the working precedent.
* **The Blockfrost allowance *period* is still unverified** — nothing here should be sized on a 50k/day assumption.

## Provenance

* Demo measurements | read-only SSH to `secuura02-demo-vm`, 2026-08-21 10:26–10:40Z | container env, `docker logs`, `psql` SELECTs, and one `docker inspect`. **No writes, no config change, no key action, no restarts.** Two scratch files created under the VM's `/tmp` during extraction were removed in the same command.
* Loop corpus | demo nginx gateway logs, 6 h window | two of my own extraction patterns were wrong on the first pass (`doc_` vs `doc-`, and verify hashes ride in the POST body rather than the URL); both corrected before any figure here was written down.
* KS-520 / KS-522 / KS-587 / PS-522 | live Linear reads, 2026-08-21 | `PS-522` returns nothing; `KS-999` used as a not-found control.

title: #568 publishes 17 URLs on secuura.io — an unresolving, seemingly unowned domain (KS-669 class; no guard rule covers URLs)
description:
## BLUF

**#568 publishes 17 URLs on** `secuura.io` **— a domain that does not resolve and that we do not appear to own.** This is the same class as [[KS-669]] (`exports.secuura.com`, an unowned for-sale domain in the published spec), three weeks on, and it is back because **no guard rule covers URLs** — E1 splits on `@` and only sees email addresses.

Filed separately from KS-669 rather than as a comment on it, deliberately: KS-669 is In Progress with its own scope (17 of its 18 URLs are still open work) and its operative defect is that it is **unassigned**. Folding a second, differently-sourced class into it makes it bigger, not more actionable. Cross-linked both ways.

**Stated fairly in both directions: #568 is a net improvement here.** It *removes* all **3** `demo@secuura.io` addresses that `develop` publishes today — E1 doing exactly its job. The URL class is the part nothing checks.

---

## Evidence

**DNS, with a control set** (2026-08-21):

| Domain | rcode | NS | SOA |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura.io` | **NXDOMAIN** | none | none |
| `secuura.ai` | NOERROR | `dns2.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.net` | NOERROR | `dns1.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.com` | NOERROR | `ns4.afternic.com.` | present |

The three controls resolve, so the resolver works and the NXDOMAIN discriminates.

⚠ **A limit on this evidence, stated rather than glossed:** `whois secuura.io` falls through to IANA and returns the `.io` **TLD** record, so its `status: ACTIVE` describes the TLD, not the domain. **I am reporting DNS only — NXDOMAIN with no NS and no SOA. I am not claiming a registration status.** Someone with registrar access should confirm ownership before this is closed either way.

**Occurrences in the published spec** (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`):

| Pattern | `c114ceddd` (#568) | `origin/develop` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `example.secuura.io` | **17** | **0** |
| `demo@secuura.io` | **0** | **3** |

Repo-wide on #568 the string appears **35** times across 7 files — the 17 published ones plus 18 in the generating sources (`auth`, `billing`, `m365-integration`, `originate`, `prism` `.openapi.ts`, and `synthesize.ts`). Fixing the source fixes both.

**The 17, by field** — these are not all cosmetic:

* `redirectUri` ×1 · `webhookUrl` ×1 · `successUrl` ×2 · `cancelUrl` ×2 · `siteUrl` ×1
* `serviceEndpoint` ×5 · `url` ×3 · bare array items ×2

`redirectUri`, `webhookUrl`, `successUrl`/`cancelUrl` and `serviceEndpoint` are all fields an integrator may copy into a working configuration. A published spec that points them at an unregistered domain is a domain anyone can register.

**Source** — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/synthesize.ts:203`:

```ts
case 'uri':
case 'url':
    return 'https://example.secuura.io/resource';
```

Every `format: uri` / `format: url` field gets this one literal.

---

## Fix direction

Use a domain reserved for the purpose. `example.com` **is reserved by RFC 2606 / RFC 6761** and can never be registered by anyone — which is the same guarantee the email side already relies on (E1 permits `example.com` addresses). `https://example.com/resource` is a one-line change at `synthesize.ts:203`, plus a regeneration.

**Then close the hole that let it back in:** add a URL rule to the guard — an example whose value parses as a URL must have a host in the reserved set (`example.com`/`.org`/`.net`, `localhost`), or be allowlisted with a reason. Without it this class returns a third time. That rule belongs with the guard-coverage work in the sibling ticket.

---

## Calls needed from @PeterD

1. **Do we own** `secuura.io`**?** If we do, this drops to "point it somewhere real or use `example.com` anyway". If we don't, it should not be in a published spec at all.
2. Is `example.com` acceptable as the synthesised URL host, or do you want a real owned host (e.g. under `secuura.ai`)?

---

**Verified by:** @kamil.kreiser, 2026-08-21 — DNS with control set, occurrence counts on both refs, source line read. Working tree untouched. Related: KS-669 (same class, `exports.secuura.com`), KS-256/#568, KS-665.

title: Compose seeds published *123 credentials by default, and the 11 rotation vars never reach the auth container from .env — every compose deploy (local, demo VM, Kintsugi)
description:
## BLUF

**Any compose deploy of this platform comes up seeding the published** `*123` **credentials, and the documented way to rotate them silently does nothing unless you happen to put them in the one undocumented file.** Two halves of the same asymmetry in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

* the single variable that **enables** published default passwords is interpolated from `.env` and **defaults to** `true`;
* the eleven variables that **replace** those passwords are not interpolated at all, and reach the container only via `.env.local` — which no example file and no doc mentions.

So the natural path (`.env`, which is what `env.example` and the deploy docs use) gives you: seeding **on**, published credentials **live**, and your rotation **ignored** — while the seeder logs that it updated the accounts.

Blast radius is **every compose deploy**: local, the demo VM, and Kintsugi. `docker-compose.local.yml` `include:`s `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`, so the canonical local stack inherits it, and the demo VM + Kintsugi run that file directly.

## Recommendation

Two small changes, both in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

1. Flip the default: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-false}`, and set it explicitly to `true` in the local-dev path that actually wants it. Opting in should be an act, not an omission.
2. Interpolate the eleven rotation variables in the `auth` service's `environment:` block the same way every other secret is (`- DEMO_USER_PASSWORD=${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD:-}` …), so `.env` — the file everyone edits — is a working channel. Then document them in `env.example`.

Neither is a code change to the auth service; the seeder's logic (`userRepo.ts:965-995`) is correct as written.

## A — the gate defaults to ON, and its stated premise is dead

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:626`

```yaml
- ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-true}
```

The pen-test **F-05** fix gated the demo seeder on this variable. The auth service states the premise the gate rests on, at `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:987-991`:

> *"The hardcoded fallbacks remain only because the seeder itself is now gated on* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` *(above) — i.e. **a deploy that doesn't explicitly opt in never sees these strings**."*

That premise is false for every compose deploy, because the compose file opts in on your behalf.

The justification for the default is at `:623-625`:

> *"Defaults to true here ONLY because docker-compose.yml is the local-dev compose; production is on Container Apps where this env var is unset and the gate stays closed."*

**That reasoning died with the KS-414 VM pivot (2026-07-08).** The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31. Since the pivot, `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` is not "the local-dev compose" — it is *the* deployment artefact for the demo VM and now for Kintsugi as well. The comment describes an architecture the project no longer has.

Measured on the running local stack:

```
$ docker exec secuura-auth sh -c 'echo $ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS'
true
```

## B — the eleven rotation variables never reach the container from `.env`

Derived from source rather than from any prior write-up — every `seedPw()` call site in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`:

`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_APEX_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_BUPA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_DELTA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_GREENFIELD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_OXFORD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD`

| check | result | control |
| -- | -- | -- |
| occurrences of each of the 11 in `docker-compose.yml` | **0 / 11** | `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` → **1** |
| present in the running `secuura-auth` container | **0 / 11** | gate present, value `true`; 95 env vars total |

Both zero-results carry a control that fires independently, so they are real absences and not a grep that could never match.

The code's own rotation instruction (`userRepo.ts:992-993`) is:

> *"For per-tenant rotation, set* `DEMO_<TENANT>_PASSWORD` *env vars in Azure Key Vault and **surface them to the auth container**."*

"Surface them to the auth container" is the whole problem — it names no channel, and only one of the two obvious ones works.

## The correction — this is NOT "rotation is impossible"

An earlier write-up of this (KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a`) concluded the documented rotation *cannot work*. **That over-claims, and the correction matters because it changes the fix.** The `auth` service does declare an env_file:

```yaml
env_file:
  - path: .env.local
    required: false
```

Tested rather than assumed: of the **66** variables declared in `.env.local`, **66** are present in the running container. `.env.local` is a fully working injection channel.

So the accurate finding is an **asymmetry of channel**, which is worse than a flat "it doesn't work" because it fails silently in exactly one direction:

| variable | channel | reaches container from `.env`? | effect |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` | `${…:-true}` interpolation | **yes**, and defaults **true** | published `*123` credentials get seeded |
| the 11 `*_PASSWORD` vars | `.env.local` env_file only | **no** | rotation silently ignored |

`.env` is the file `env.example` is copied to, the file the setup instructions name, and the file compose reads for `${…}` interpolation — but it is *not* an env_file for `auth`, so values placed there are invisible to the seeder. Neither `env.example` nor `.env.local.example` mentions any of the eleven, or the gate.

## Why it fails convincingly

Recorded on Kintsugi during the KS-601 Stage C build (2026-08-20) — **this half is that session's on-box measurement; I have not re-run it here**, because reproducing it locally means changing `demo@`'s password and breaking the preflight persona:

Setting the eleven in `.env` and recreating the auth container printed `Demo user updated to match seed config` account after account — on a code path that genuinely does execute an `UPDATE … password_hash`. **The old password still authenticated.** Only a negative control (attempting a login with the *old* credential and expecting it to fail) caught it. Fixed on that box with a compose override making all 11 visible, then verified both directions: old `demo123` → **401**, new credential → **200**.

That is the part worth carrying: the failure produces success-shaped log output, so anyone rotating credentials and checking the logs will believe they succeeded.

## Scope note

Not in scope here: whether the demo VM *should* keep its seeded public credentials. Those are deliberate, documented sample logins for public demos (project `CLAUDE.md`). This ticket is about a deploy coming up more permissive than its operator intended, and a rotation that reports success without doing anything.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:570-666` — `auth` service; `:626` the gate; `:623-625` the dead premise; `env_file` at `:576-578`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:965-995` — the F-05 gate, the `seedPw()` helper and its rotation instruction.
* `docker-compose.local.yml:33-35` — `include:` of `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/env.example`, `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` — neither names the eleven or the gate.
* KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a` — the Kintsugi on-box record (superseded on the "cannot work" point by the correction above).

## Suggested owner

Unassigned deliberately. Compose/deploy topology rather than service logic — @peter or @stuart to route; happy to take it myself if neither has context loaded.

title: The demo VM runs every service as NODE_ENV=development while the code names "demo" as prod-like — ~6 production guards are silently inert, and the public API-docs exposure is one symptom
description:
## BLUF

**The live demo runs all 27 Node services with** `NODE_ENV=development`**.** The codebase explicitly
treats `demo` as a prod-like environment (`services/auth/src/index.ts:220`:
`IS_PROD_LIKE = ['production','staging','demo'].includes(NODE_ENV)`), so a set of guards written to
protect prod-like deployments do not fire on the demo. **Found 2026-08-17 (session 44) as a control**,
while disproving an unrelated claim about KS-656 — nobody was looking for it.

**Filed, deliberately not fixed.** Changing what the demo is counts as demo-affecting config and is
Kam's call. There is also a **live disagreement between three artefacts** about what the demo is
supposed to be, and flipping anything now would destroy the evidence that the question was ever open.

## The disagreement — three artefacts, three answers

| Artefact | Says the demo should be |
| -- | -- |
| `services/auth/src/index.ts:220` | `demo` — an explicit prod-like value |
| `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:578-582` (comment) + `deployment/azure/services.bicep:626` | prod-like: public API docs "never in demo/prod", bicep sets the flag `true` only for `dev` |
| `docker-compose.yml` (the file the VM actually runs) + the VM's `.env:165` | `development` |

**Someone may have set this deliberately** — Stuart or Peter driving Swagger against the demo is
entirely plausible, and it has probably been this way a long time. **Establish which artefact is****
****authoritative before reconciling any of it.**

## Measured on the live demo VM (read-only; values never printed)

```
docker exec <svc> printenv NODE_ENV   -> development     (26 of 26 Node services; 5 infra containers unset)
/home/secuura/secuura/Dev/.env:165    -> NODE_ENV=development
```

**The fix is not a one-line env change**, which is the part worth knowing up front:

```
docker-compose.yml:  "- NODE_ENV=development"           -> 26 occurrences  (hardcoded)
docker-compose.yml:  "- NODE_ENV=${NODE_ENV:-development}" ->  1 occurrence  (api-gateway, :319)
```

So setting `NODE_ENV=demo` in the VM's `.env` would move **exactly one service** and leave the other
26 on `development` — a change that would look applied and mostly not be.

## What is actually inert as a result — argued, and bounded

**Real:**

1. **Full API surface published unauthenticated at the internet edge.** `apiDocsGuard`
   (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:584`) is opt-in via `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS`; the VM's `.env:217` sets it
   `true`, and `docker-compose.yml:327` defaults it `false`, so the VM is overriding the default. Both
   spec routes serve real content (verified by content-type; an invented sibling path returns the
   Swagger HTML catch-all, which is the control that makes those 200s evidence). The guard's own
   comment calls this "a free attack-surface map for anyone (audit F-04)". **342 endpoints, every****
****parameter and every auth mechanism — no credentials in it.**
2. **5xx responses return the raw internal error message to the caller.**
   `api-gateway/src/index.ts:1031` masks to "An unexpected error occurred" only when
   `NODE_ENV === 'production'`; `:1038` adds `details.details = err.message` whenever it is not.
   Live example of the class from the local stack, same code path:
   `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml'` — an internal
   filesystem path in a client-visible body. (`err.stack` goes to the **logger** only, not the response.)
3. **Session/auth and CSRF cookies are not marked** `Secure` — `secure: NODE_ENV === 'production'` at
   `auth/src/routes/auth.ts:369,536,615` and `api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts:60`, on an origin that
   is HTTPS-only via Caddy. ⚠ **Code-level only — deliberately NOT runtime-verified**, because
   confirming it means authenticating against the demo and minting a session.
4. **The** `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` **fail-fast cannot fire.** `auth/src/index.ts:225-227` exits 1 when the key
   is missing *in a prod-like env* — protecting PII **and** MFA TOTP secrets (KS-158). On the demo it
   degrades to a warning. **Latent, not live: the key IS set (measured present, 64 chars).** So this is
   a guard that cannot fire, not exposed PII.
5. **Password-reset and email-verification links are logged in full when SMTP send fails**
   (`auth/src/routes/auth.ts:230,686`, both gated `NODE_ENV !== 'production'`). Tokens reach the VM's
   container logs. Relevant next to KS-488 C-5, which turned the SMTP transport off by default.

**Checked and NOT true — recorded so nobody re-derives it:**

* **Mock endpoints are OFF.** `ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` measured literal `false` on the gateway; the gate
  at `:752` needs `NODE_ENV !== 'production' && ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS === 'true'`, so only one half is open.
* `CSRF_SECRET` **is set** on the gateway (36 chars), so the `:50`/`:276` production-only requirement
  not firing costs nothing today.
* **No PII is exposed** — see 4.
* Demo seeding being enabled is plausibly intentional for a demo, not counted as a defect here.

## Severity — argued as Medium, and explicitly not inflated

Every individual inert guard is either backed by a secret that is actually present (4), mitigated by
the HTTPS-only edge (3), or off on its second condition (mocks). Nothing here is exploitable for
credentials or PII as it stands. **What makes it worth fixing is that it is a class, not an item:** one
env value silently disables roughly six independent protections at once on the only internet-facing
Secuura deployment, and the artefacts disagree about whether that is intended.

**What would raise this to High:** `PII_ENCRYPTION_KEY` going missing (4 becomes live and silent), or
`ENABLE_MOCK_ENDPOINTS` being flipped (2 of 2 conditions open). Both are one env edit away, and today
nothing would fail loudly to tell you.

## Tracked nowhere until now

Searched the board three ways before filing — `ENABLE_PUBLIC_API_DOCS`, `public API docs`, `F-04`.
No result covers this. F-04 lives in **KS-491 (Review F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation)**, which
records the docs-exposure *finding* against the code but not the *live demo state*.

## Proposed disposition (needs Kam)

1. **Decide what the demo is** — prod-like (`demo`) or a dev sandbox that happens to face the internet.
   That single ruling resolves all six items.
2. If prod-like: the compose `NODE_ENV` hardcoding (26 sites) has to be parameterised first, or the
   change is cosmetic.
3. If it stays a sandbox: say so in the compose file and retire the "never in demo/prod" comment at
   `api-gateway/src/index.ts:578-582`, so the artefacts stop contradicting each other.

**No change has been made to the VM, its** `.env`**, or the repo.**
