title: Bulk re-key: one admin-authorised rotate across a named set of externalRefs
description:
## BLUF

@peter asked for **one** admin-authorised action that re-keys a named set of Organisations by `externalRef`, instead of N separate `register-connector` calls during an incident. The loop itself is **1–2 days**.

**It must not ship before** [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) **(revoke-on-rotate).** Built on today's additive rotate, a bulk re-key would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and *look* like recovery.

## Detail

Today's single-org path is `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` with `rotate: true` — `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:476-729`:

* platform-admin only; guardrail 1 refuses a connector-authorised rotate with 403 (`:499-509`)
* resolves the org by `metadata->>'externalRef'` under platform scope (`:590-593`)
* mints a fresh `sk_` key via the security service (`:674-686` → `services/security/src/index.ts:800`)
* plaintext key returned exactly once (`:719-720`)

`runWithPlatformScope` (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:102`) already handles the cross-tenant access, so multi-tenancy is **not** the hard part here.

**Scope**

* Extract `platform.ts:476-729` into a reusable per-org function; add a bulk route taking a list of `externalRef`s.
* Return a **per-ref result array** — partial success must be explicit. An incident operator has to know which refs failed and why.
* OpenAPI entry + `generate-openapi` regen + api-gateway rebuild (the gateway bakes the spec) + KS-380 preflight.

**Explicitly out of scope:** delivery of the key material for N keys. One response body carrying N live secrets is not the answer; that needs its own design and a security review (see the KS-480 sizing table).

**Cheaper alternative on the record** (raised because @peter asked not to have the manual path assumed away): a scripted loop over the existing admin endpoint gives one *operator action* today at near-zero build cost. It does not give one *authorisation*, which is the part actually being asked for.

**Done when:** an admin can re-key a named set of refs in one authorised call, each prior key is revoked per the [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) semantics, per-ref outcomes are explicit, and the [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) rehearsal passes all four steps.

---

Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: Sweeps 2026-08-05: untracked failures across 10 ops — response-schema recurrence (KS-498 residual), 3 genuine 500s, non-envelope 5xx on by-design-503 ops, undocumented status
description:
Findings from two runs on the same code, 2026-08-05: `full-2026-08-05T08-44-00Z` and `pre-merge-2026-08-05T09-18-45Z` (Schemathesis 4.24.3, 316/318 operations, 316/317 past auth, no health-check suppression, untruncated messages). Everything else in those runs maps to [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) / [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) / [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code). The operations below map to **no ticket**.

> **Read the counts as a FLOOR, not a total.** The two runs agreed on the failing *classes* but not the failing *operations* — five ops failed in pre-merge that were absent from the full sweep. Property-based generation samples; it does not enumerate. Verify a specific operation with a targeted probe, never by its absence from one run.

## 1. response_schema_conformance recurs on 4 NEW ops ([KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) residual)

[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) is **Done** — closed 2026-07-29 having verified the class down to 2 ops, both [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) family. **None of these four are those two**, so this is a recurrence on different operations, not unfinished work. Filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

| Operation | full | pre-merge |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/complete` | 14 | yes |
| `POST /api/presentations/verify` | 13 | yes |
| `POST /api/wallets/verify` | 4 | yes |
| `PATCH /api/security/events/{id}/resolve` | 4 | yes |
| `POST /api/oauth/apps/{id}/rotate-secret` — **added 2026-09-10** from `pr-ks-971-2026-09-10T16-31-45Z-slot1` (Schemathesis 4.25.x, `pr` profile, slot 1, develop at `688f4dded` + the [KS-971 (2/2): slot-isolate the k6 performance harness, and prove it by fault injection](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-971-22-slot-isolate-the-k6-performance-harness-and-prove-it-by-34bc0f07c5ba) systemTest branch). Runtime answers `200 {"success":true,"clientSecret":"scs_…","warning":"Store the new client_secret securely — it cannot be retrieved later."}`; the declared 200 schema requires `id`. Handler `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1079`; the route reached develop between the 2026-08-05 sweeps and 2026-08-28 ([KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) oauth-apps work), which is why it is absent above. The 2026-08-19 baseline already lists its `positive_data_acceptance` pair ([KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks)) but NOT `response_schema_conformance`, so this pair fails the gate until fixed or baselined. | — | pr: yes |
| `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/session/{sessionId}` — **added 2026-10-22** ([KS-1511](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1511/audit-log-limit-follow-up-retire-the-stale-accepted-baseline-entry) control sweep `pre-merge-2026-10-22T11-15-40Z-slot1`, platform-k slot 1 on Peter's Mac, develop `f75b52721`, `pre-merge --seed 1511`). ST108 ×1: `"sessionId" is a required property` against the declared 200 schema (requires `sessionId`, `status`, `createdAt`). Same message as the sibling `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/result/{sessionId}`, already baselined under this ticket; whether both share one handler defect in `services/kyc/src/routes/microsoft-verification.ts` is not established. Not baselined, so it fails the triaged-baseline gate whenever drawn; seen intermittently before (before-only pair in a version-bump comparison, `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` \~line 1099). | — | pre-merge: yes |

Three of the four **also** fail `negative_data_rejection` — likely one root cause ("nothing validated, so nothing shaped correctly"), not four independent drifts. Worth confirming before treating them as separate work. Fix per [KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444): runtime is truth, reconcile the declared response schema, regenerate with `npm run generate-openapi`, rebuild api-gateway on both targets (it bundles the spec).

## 2. Three genuine 500s on schema-compliant input

| Operation | Site | Mechanism |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/users/admin/create` | `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:177` | `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard — a non-string `email` (e.g. `{}`) raises `TypeError` → 500 instead of a typed 4xx |
| `GET /api/users/admin/list` | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:344` **and** `:398` | `parseInt(req.query.offset as string) || 0` — `-1` is truthy so it passes through; Postgres rejects it (`OFFSET must not be negative`) → 500. The `|| 0` fallback only catches `NaN` |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` | not yet traced | 500 in the pre-merge run; absent from the full sweep |

**The negative-offset pattern is SIX sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reached:

* `auth/src/routes/users.ts:344`, `:398`
* `originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1006`, `:1166` — raw `LIMIT ${limit} OFFSET ${offset}`, x4 queries
* `tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:556`
* `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:374` — `Math.min` caps the upper bound only, no negative guard

**Not an injection risk** — the raw-SQL cases use Prisma `$queryRaw` tagged templates (parameterised) and `parseInt(...) || 0` always yields a number. The defect is the unvalidated negative reaching Postgres as a 500. A fix touching only `users.ts:344` leaves five siblings exposed. Suggested fix: `.int().min(0)` on `offset` at handler entry.

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

## 3. `integration_5xx_guard` fires on by-design-503 ops — non-envelope 5xx

| Operation | full | pre-merge |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/timestamps` | 4 | yes |
| `POST /api/credentials` | 1 | yes |

Both are on `_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS` in `systemTest/schemathesis/config/checks.py` (blanket `not_a_server_error` disabled because they 503 by design when their provider is unconfigured). The [KS-268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-268/localdev-coverage-for-503-by-design-integration-endpoints-billing)/[KS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-499/unconfigured-provider-503s-on-7-write-ops-beyond-ks-268s-3-exclusions) guard replaces it and **passes** a clean declared-503 envelope — so a failure here means a 5xx that is **not** a proper 503 envelope, i.e. a genuine server error the exception list is demonstrably not hiding. Worth confirming whether it is a raw 500 or a malformed 503 body.

## 4. Undocumented status — `POST /api/referrals/apply` (6)

`status_code_conformance` fails: the operation returns a status not in its declared response set. Distinct from [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) (`GET /api/documents/{id}/sig-json`, still open) — same class, different operation. Fix per [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code): either stop returning the undeclared status, or declare it — whichever reflects intended behaviour, per the "spec is the contract" rule.

## Not included here

* `POST /api/presentations` failing `not_a_server_error` — **already fixed** under [KS-544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-544/schemathesis-4242-4243-adopt-full-cli-parameter-surface-always) by adding it to `_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS`; live-verified it 503s by design (`VC_SIGNING_KEY is required to sign a presentation. Refusing to emit an HMAC-signed presentation falsely labelled Ed25519`) when `holderDID` is present.
* New `negative_data_rejection` ops (`POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector`, `POST /api/users/admin/create`) and the still-failing status-list trio — registered on [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data), whose register is live and In Progress.

## Please run the full sweep before closing

The fast PR gate covers none of these classes — it does not validate response bodies, does not generate negative bodies, and does not fuzz these write paths:

```bash
cd systemTest/schemathesis
python3 scripts/run.py full        # local stack on :6882
```

Full artefacts under `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/` for both run directories — NDJSON event stream (authoritative for check totals), VCR cassette, HAR, per-call metrics, replayable crash files.

## Related

[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) / [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) (response schema) · [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) (negative data) · [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) (undocumented status) · [KS-268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-268/localdev-coverage-for-503-by-design-integration-endpoints-billing) / [KS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-499/unconfigured-provider-503s-on-7-write-ops-beyond-ks-268s-3-exclusions) (the 5xx guard) · [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) (stateful links — the majority class; 0 declared transitions with 104 producers available explains \~78% of the full sweep's failures) · [KS-544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-544/schemathesis-4242-4243-adopt-full-cli-parameter-surface-always) (the sweep that found these).

*Found by the* [KS-544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-544/schemathesis-4242-4243-adopt-full-cli-parameter-surface-always) *sweeps, 2026-08-05. systemTest rule: refs as KS-NNN text, repro via local stack.*

title: anchoring threadTokenMint test fails only under root-visible npm install layout — nested @lucid-evolution/plutus duplicate-instance (pre-existing, layout-dependent; KS-559 A/B-cleared)
description:
**Found during KS-559 validation (2026-08-04, Agent Teams pilot) — pre-existing, NOT caused by the dep sweep (controlled A/B in two independent environments: identical failure with pre-KS-559 and post-KS-559 locks).**

`services/anchoring` test `threadTokenMint.test.ts › parameterises mint + spend with a deterministic per-seed policyId` fails with `Could not serialize the data: Error: Unsupported type` in `applyParamsToScript` — the classic **duplicate-instance** signature: the test's `Constr` comes from the top-level `@lucid-evolution/plutus@0.1.31` while `@lucid-evolution/utils@0.1.70` serializes against its own nested `plutus@0.1.33` copy, and the cross-copy instanceof check fails.

**It is INSTALL-LAYOUT-DEPENDENT, which is why it looks flaky across setups:**

* `npm ci` in a **parentless standalone** copy of services/anchoring (= what the Dockerfile does) → **110/110 pass**. Verified on macOS host for both develop and KS-559 locks.
* `npm ci --workspaces=false` with the **monorepo root visible** as a parent dir (worktree, full-repo container mount) → **109/110, this test fails**. Verified on macOS host AND in node:24-alpine, again for both locks.

Same lock file both ways (`packages` dict byte-identical to develop) — npm physically lays the tree out differently when it can see a parent workspace root, and one layout resolves the utils→plutus import to the nested copy.

**Why it matters:** (1) any dev running anchoring tests inside the monorepo checkout with a standalone install hits a phantom red; (2) the nested plutus duplication itself (0.1.31 vs 0.1.33) is fragile — a future hoist change could flip the shipped image's behaviour. Fix options: dedupe/pin `@lucid-evolution/plutus` so one copy exists; or make the test/lib resolution layout-proof; or document the supported install layout for the suite.

Evidence + repro commands in the KS-559 PR thread and session history 2026-08-04. Credit: caught by the KS-559 deps teammate's controlled A/B refusing to accept an unqualified 110/110.

title: KMS: move platform wallet mnemonic to Key Vault (KS-326 follow-up)
description:
**Follow-up carved out of** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms)**.** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) (Phase 0 — crypto-agility + KMS) was closed as Done, but only the **JWT signing key** half of its KMS item actually shipped (PR #361/#362 — JWT private key now loads from Azure Key Vault with an env fallback). The **platform wallet mnemonic** was left behind and is still loaded from an env var.

**Current state (verified in code):**

* `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` is read from `process.env` in `services/anchoring` (e.g. `services/anchoring/src/index.ts:850`), then passed to `initWallet(mnemonic, network)` in `services/anchoring/src/cardano/wallet.ts` to derive the BIP-39 → BIP-32 → Ed25519 signing key.
* The JWT-key KMS plumbing already exists to reuse: `packages/shared/src/vault/key-vault.ts` (Key Vault `getSecret` with env fallback).

**Ask:**

- [ ] Load `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` from Azure Key Vault via the existing `key-vault.ts` helper, with an always-on env fallback (mirror the JWT-key pattern, so local/dev with no Key Vault still works).
- [ ] Support rotation (versioned secret) — note a mnemonic rotation also rotates the derived wallet address, so document the operational impact.
- [ ] Keep behaviour-preserving defaults: no Key Vault configured → falls back to `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` env, identical to today.

**Why it matters:** the mnemonic is the platform wallet's root secret; leaving it in env is a wider blast radius than the JWT key that already moved. Not urgent (env is the current accepted posture), but it closes the gap [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) implied was done.

**Refs:** [KS-326](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-326/phase-0-crypto-agility-foundation-kms) (parent, closed), PR #361/#362 (JWT-key KMS pattern to follow), `docs/security/POST-QUANTUM-CRYPTO-MIGRATION-PLAN.md` §5 Phase 0 / §7.

Add it to Phase 0 and to `tests-unit/exchange-recorder.test.ts` |

### What needs doing, in order

1. **Decide D1, D2 and D3** (R9, R10).
2. **Phase 0** — the checklist below, minus the CI items (R4), with the oxlint rule (R7) and always-on masking (R12).
3. **Phase 0b** — recount against the current spec and re-home all 346 operations into the flow catalogue (R1). Raise `COVERAGE_FLOOR` towards the new total.
4. **Spine** (F3 → F4 → F5), then the **F10 pilot**, reviewed before the remaining plans are written.
5. **The 22 remaining child plans** and their implementation.
6. **Triage** the `no-documented-flow` residuals.

---

## Summary

`systemTest/playwright/` covers **8 of 310** published API operations (2.6 %) and issues **no writes at all** — so no complete business flow exists anywhere in the suite. This ticket takes Playwright to full coverage of the published contract, driven by the documented product flows, reusing the personas the platform already seeds.

## Current state (measured 2026-07-24 — see R1–R3 for today)

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Published contract | `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — 278 paths / **310 operations** / 42 tags |
| Playwright today | 3 clients, 3 spec files, 11 tests, **8 operations** |
| Writes today | **zero** — read-only plus two unauthenticated 401/403 checks |
| Zero-coverage domains | Billing 21, M365 22, Governance 18, NFT 18, KYC 16, GDPR 15, Analytics 12, Staking 12, VC/VP/StatusList/DID 24, Webhooks 7, Tenants 6, Timestamps 6, API Keys 4, Sessions 2 |

Covered today: `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `GET /users/me`, `GET /documents`, `GET /documents/{id}`, `POST /verification/verify`, plus unauth-only checks on `POST /documents/{id}/verify` and `POST /notifications`.

> **Design verified against the Playwright docs for the pinned** `@playwright/test` **1.61.1** (2026-07-24). *Pin is now 1.64.1 — re-check per R6.* Every design decision cites its source in **Playwright references** at the end.

## Implementation principle — use Playwright's own primitives

**Never implement something ourselves if Playwright already provides it.** Anything the framework ships — polling, stepping, retries, parallelism, artifact attachment, context isolation — is used as-is. Our code exists only to express *Secuura's* domain (personas, flows, coverage classes) or to fill a capability the framework genuinely does not have. A hand-rolled equivalent of a framework feature is a review rejection.

| Need | Mechanism | Ours or Playwright's? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Wait for an async outcome | `expect.poll` (`{ timeout, intervals, message }`) | **Playwright's.** `helpers/settle.ts` is a thin wrapper supplying the project deadlines **\[ref 8\]** |
| Ordered, named stages in a flow | `test.step()` | **Playwright's** |
| Per-persona session isolation | `playwright.request.newContext()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 2\]** |
| Persist an artifact + surface it in the report | `testInfo.outputPath()` + `testInfo.attach({ path })` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 6\]** |
| Parallelism, retries, sharding, reporters, tagging | runner config | **Playwright's** |
| Setup/teardown lifecycle | fixtures with `use()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 7\]** |
| **Capturing API exchanges as a durable artefact** | `helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` | **Ours — the framework has no equivalent** (upstream request closed unimplemented, **\[ref 5\]**). Built *on* `testInfo.attach`/`outputPath` |
| CSRF double-submit echo | `helpers/csrf.ts` | **Ours** — application-protocol concern |
| Coverage classification vs the OpenAPI spec | `coverage/*` | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |
| Persona catalogue, flow definitions | `config/`, `helpers/flow.ts`, specs | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |

## Stack isolation — Playwright runs on its own Docker instance

* ~~**CI**~~ *(moot — GitHub Actions retired 2026-08-27, see R4/R5)* — the `playwright` job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` boots via `boot-platform-stack` with `stack_prefix: pr-playwright`, gateway **6982**, postgres 6532, redis 6479, pgbouncer 6533; pointed at by `API_BASE_URL: http://localhost:6982/api`. Distinct `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` / `STACK_PREFIX` → separate containers, volumes, networks. Siblings sit on 6882 / 7082 / 7182.
* **Local** — the suite does not start or stop a server (`playwright.config.ts`); it attaches to whatever `API_BASE_URL` points at. Use its own instance for destructive flows (F14 erasure, F5 revoke).

Any environment posture we choose applies to Playwright alone. The only shared thing is the composite action's *source file*.

## Scope boundary

Playwright asserts **business outcomes of documented flows**. It does not re-test what the sibling suites own — see `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html` §2–3 and the Coverage & Scenario Matrix in `QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`.

| Excluded from Playwright | Owner |
| -- | -- |
| Boundary values, negative **data**, fuzzing | Schemathesis |
| Status/header compliance, undeclared verbs, redirects, rate-limit headers, 429 | Schemathesis |
| RBAC matrices, cross-tenant, IDOR/BOLA | Schemathesis (+ Akto) |
| Unauthenticated 401/403 sweeps | Schemathesis + the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight |
| OWASP API Top 10, injection, SSRF, BFLA | Akto |
| Throughput, latency, saturation | Performance (k6) |
| Real Cardano chain integrity / anchor-vs-chain | anchoring Integration suite ([KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489/review-d-blockchain-anchoring-smart-contract-integrity)-D) — see Risk 3 |

**A distinction that matters, because it looks like the excluded category but is not:** a *documented business outcome that is not success* — a verification returning **Expired**, a tampered document returning **Failed**, a certifier **Rejecting** a request — is in scope. Those are product states the stakeholder guides describe, reached with valid inputs. What is excluded is malformed **data** (missing fields, oversize values, type confusion). F6 and F7 exist precisely to cover the former.

Consistent with Playwright's Best Practices — *"Only test what you control."* — which is why provider-gated paths (Stripe, M365) record a by-design 503 rather than reaching for the third party. **\[ref 1\]**

**Two existing specs are duplicates and are retired in Phase 0**: `notifications.spec.ts` (both tests assert unauth → 401/403, already swept for every bearer op by the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight) and the invalid-credentials / missing-email cases in `login.spec.ts` (negative data, owned by Schemathesis `test_authentication.py`).

## Persona policy

**Use the existing** `default`**-tenant personas first.** The seeder (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` → `demoAccounts`) provides 17 accounts across 7 tenants. A new persona is created **only where an existing one provably cannot serve**. Permissions on seeded accounts are **not** changed. Non-default tenants are not used.

### Existing personas — the working set (`default` tenant)

| Email | Role | Verification | Password env (fallback) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `issuer@secuura.com` | ISSUER_ADMIN | ENHANCED | `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` (`issuer123`) |
| `admin@secuura.com` | SYSTEM_ADMIN | HIGH | `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` (`admin123`) |
| `demo@secuura.io` | OWNER | ENHANCED | `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` (`demo123`) |
| `holder@secuura.com` | OWNER | BASIC | `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` (`holder123`) |
| `verifier@secuura.com` | VERIFIER | STANDARD | `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD` (`verifier123`) |

Seeding is gated on `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true`; the `config/environment.ts` getters must read the **same env names** with these fallbacks. `kam@secuura.ai` is a real person's account — **do not use**.

### Additions — three, each with a blocking justification

Created at runtime by F2 via `POST /api/users/admin/create` as `admin@secuura.com`. Confirmed viable: the handler assigns `role` from the body, and admin-created users are `emailVerified: true` / `status: ACTIVE`.

| Proposed name | Role / level | Flow | Why no existing persona works |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `pw-approver-<run>@secuura-test.invalid` | ISSUER_APPROVER / ENHANCED | F3, F7 | **Role gap.** `ISSUER_APPROVER` is in the `UserRole` union (`services/auth/src/types/index.ts:8`) but no seeded account holds it |
| `pw-gdpr-subject-<run>@…` | OWNER / BASIC | F14 | **Erasure is irreversible.** Running it on `holder@secuura.com` destroys a persona F9 and F20 depend on |
| `pw-kyc-subject-<run>@…` | OWNER / **NONE** | F15 | **KYC state is one-way.** A reused persona is already-verified on re-run, breaking determinism |

Plus one **non-user identity**: the platform API key (`SECUURA_PLATFORM_API_KEY`, already used by Akto) for **F8**'s machine path. Not an account; no new seed data.

### Deliberately not added

| Considered | Why not |
| -- | -- |
| Default-tenant ORG_ADMIN | `admin@secuura.com` performs the org/tenant operations; ORG_ADMIN-vs-SYSTEM_ADMIN is RBAC → Schemathesis |
| Second rights holder for F9 | Two OWNERs already exist in `default`: `demo@secuura.io` → `holder@secuura.com` |
| Two governance participants for F20 | The same two OWNERs serve; re-registration conflict handled as a valid state |
| Dedicated billing customer | Billing customer creation is 503-by-design locally; `demo@secuura.io` suffices |
| Any non-default-tenant account | Cross-tenant behaviour belongs to Schemathesis |

## ⚠ Two platform capabilities we do not have — needed by F6 and F13

Two flows assert a documented product state that **cannot currently be reached on demand**. Neither blocks Phase 0, but both block their own flow's plan from being finalised. Raised with @kamil.kreiser and @stuart.jamieson in the comments — **and probed ourselves first** (see Risk mitigation), because the capability may already exist.

| Need | Flow | Why it is needed | What "available" looks like |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **Induce an expired certification** | **F6** | The Verifier guide documents **Expired** as one of five verification result states. Verifying it requires a certification that is *already* past its expiry. If expiry is purely wall-clock with no way to set a past date, F6's expired leg is unreachable and the state stays permanently untested | Either an issuance parameter accepting a past `expiresAt` (non-prod only), or a supported way to age an existing certification. A test must be able to produce one deterministically, in-run, without clock manipulation on the host |
| **Raise a system error on demand** | **F13** | F13's only real journey is *error → resolve*. Asserting it requires a system error to exist first. Provoking one by genuinely breaking a service is not acceptable in a shared or CI stack | A non-prod-only way to emit a synthetic entry into the system-errors surface with a known signature, so the test can find it, resolve it, and assert it reflects as resolved |

**If either already exists**, this is a documentation gap rather than a build ask. **If neither is feasible**, the affected leg is recorded as a documented coverage gap rather than quietly dropped: F6 keeps its tampered + not-found legs, F13 falls back to `positive-path` for the whole read surface.

## Flow catalogue

**Restructured 2026-07-24** and now supersedes the earlier 14-entry list. ### Acceptance criterion per flow

Each flow is accepted on **one stated business outcome**, not a set of status codes. These are what the child plans must satisfy.

* **F1** — a token issued at login authenticates `GET /users/me` as the expected persona for all five accounts; a refreshed token works, and the pre-logout token stops working.
* **F2** — a document type created by admin is returned by the subsequent list, and each of the three new personas can log in at its intended role.
* **F3** — a document created by `issuer@secuura.com` is retrievable by id and its certification appears in the certification list. **The anchor leg is blocked on D1.**
* **F4** — verifying the spine document's content hash returns `verified: true` and identifies the issuing party.
* **F5** — after revoke, the same verify call that previously returned verified now reports **revoked**, and the status list reflects it.
* **F6** — a **tampered** payload verifies as failed, and an unknown hash returns `verified: false` without an error. The **expired** leg — an expired certification verifying as expired, not as valid or missing — requires the capability gap above to be closed; until then it is a documented gap, not a silent omission.
* **F7** — a rejected certification request ends in a rejected state, the requester can see the rejection, and the document is **not** certified.
* **F8** — a document certified with `x-api-key` (no bearer, no cookies) is retrievable and verifies identically to one certified by a browser persona. Proves the partner path end-to-end.
* **F9** — custody transfers from `demo@secuura.io` to `holder@secuura.com`: the recipient is notified (`expect.poll` **— delivery is async**), and the prior owner can no longer mutate the document.
* **F10** — a registered webhook's test delivery appears in its delivery list (`expect.poll` **— delivery is async**); rotating the secret changes the signing secret without dropping the registration.
* **F11** — a credential issued for a document verifies as a presentation and its DID resolves — **or** the by-design 503 on `POST /api/credentials` is the recorded outcome.
* **F12** — an async export reaches a downloadable state within `EXPORT_SETTLE_TIMEOUT` and the downloaded artefact contains the requesting tenant's data.
* **F13** — the audit trail contains the lifecycle events of a document **this flow created itself**. The *error → resolve* journey requires the capability gap above; until then the whole read surface is asserted as `positive-path` and **declared as such**.
* **F14** — the subject's export contains their record; after erasure the same export no longer returns personal data and the deletion log records the event.
* **F15** — a KYC session initiated at verification level `NONE` reaches a terminal reviewed state and the subject's verification level changes.
* **F16** — a wallet challenge is issued and the account reflects the linked wallet address. **Stops short of asserting signature validity** — `POST /api/wallets/verify` returns `verified:true` for any signature and is an open Known Failure ([KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet)-C).
* **F17** — an authorised app receives a token that can call an in-scope operation, and revoking the grant stops it working.
* **F18** — a connector reaches a connected state and a sync lists at least one document — **or** the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome.
* **F19** — a customer's purchase appears in their purchase list and their credit balance reflects it — **or** the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome.
* **F20** — a proposal created by `demo@secuura.io` receives a vote from `holder@secuura.com` and reaches a terminal state — **or** the documented precondition refusal ([KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)) is recorded.
* **F21** — a stake is recorded and the resulting reward balance reflects it — **or** the documented precondition refusal is recorded.
* **F22** — a referral code applied by a second user is attributed to the referrer and moves a milestone — **or** the documented precondition refusal is recorded.
* **F23** — a minted NFT certificate is retrievable and its asset verifies — **or** the chain/IPFS-dependent outcome is recorded as such.

### Notes for whoever writes the child plans

* **The spine (F3 → F4 → F5) is one spec, one test.** F6, F7 and F8 sit outside it and create their own prerequisites.
* **A flow whose dominant class is not** `flow-verified` **must say so up front** (F13, F18, F19).
* **Flows marked "Setup"** (F6, F7, F14, F15) create a disposable persona or artefact first; that setup is plumbing and does not count toward `COVERAGE_FLOOR`.
* **F6 and F13 have an open platform dependency** — plan the unblocked legs; record the blocked ones as documented gaps.
* **Every flow declares its own teardown** — fixture-scoped, so it runs on failure too.
* **Each flow plan carries its own estimate** — the programme total is the sum, which is how this work gets scheduled.
* **F10 is written first as the pilot** (see Risk mitigation) — later plans should follow whatever shape F10 proves out.

## Driving the flows — per-flow contexts and in-test persona switching

Each flow runs with its own isolated client session, and a single test can act as several personas in sequence so cross-persona interaction is directly observable.

Both are straightforward **because the suite has no browser**. The API analogue of a private window is `playwright.request.newContext()`, and the docs confirm the isolation property: *"If you don't want APIRequestContext to use and update cookies from the browser context, you can manually create a new instance of APIRequestContext which will have its own isolated cookies."* **\[ref 2\]**

| Isolated per flow / persona | Shared across all flows |
| -- | -- |
| Cookie jar, `XSRF-TOKEN`, storage state, `Authorization` bearer | Documents, users, anchors, webhooks — the platform's own state |

**Not hypothetical — the suite already has the bug isolation prevents.** `notifications.spec.ts` documents unauthenticated POSTs returning 403 instead of 401 because a server-set `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie rode along on the *shared* unauth context, making the outcome order-dependent.

### Switching persona inside one test

Every client takes `(api, token)` in its constructor, so the same class bound to different contexts yields `documentsAsDemo`, `documentsAsHolder`, `documentsAsVerifier`. F9's criterion is then close to verbatim:

```ts
test('custody transfers from demo to holder', async ({
    documentsAsDemo, documentsAsHolder, notificationsAsHolder,
}) => {
    const { body: doc } = await documentsAsDemo.create(buildDocumentPayload('f9'));
    await documentsAsDemo.transferCustody(doc.id, holderUserId);

    const received = await documentsAsHolder.get(doc.id);   // recipient can now read
    expect(received.status).toBe(200);

    const stale = await documentsAsDemo.revoke(doc.id);      // prior owner cannot mutate
    expect(stale.status).toBe(403);
});
```

**Calls are always asynchronous** — Playwright has no sync API. Stages within a flow are strictly sequential (each depends on prior state); independent reads may be batched with `Promise.all`, bounded by the \~2000/60s platform limit. Because batched calls complete out of order, **the exchange recorder stamps its sequence at request start** and carries a duration.

### The F3 → F4 → F5 spine is ONE test with steps — not `describe.serial`

F4 verifies *F3's* document and F5 revokes *that same* document, so the chain needs shared state. A `test.describe.serial` block is the wrong instrument **\[ref 3\]**:

* *"If one of the serial tests fails, all subsequent tests are skipped."* — downstream stages would report as **skips**, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` is explicit that a skip is neither red nor green and proves nothing.
* *"All tests in a group are retried together."* — serial buys no retry granularity over a single test.
* *"Using serial is not recommended."* — and Best Practices: *"Each test should be completely isolated from another test…"* **\[ref 1\]**

**Resolution:** `tests/spine/document-lifecycle.spec.ts` holds the chain as **one test** whose stages are `test.step()` calls sharing one document. Tagged `@smoke`. `describe.serial` is not used anywhere.

### Evidence capture — we must build our own

**Both** `video` **and** `trace` **are inert for this suite.**

* **Video** records a browser-context viewport; there is no page here. `playwright.config.ts:54-59` already says so and the docs confirm: *"Videos are saved upon browser context closure."* **\[ref 4\]**
* **Trace** is a `browserContext.tracing` facility and does not capture a standalone `APIRequestContext` created via `playwright.request.newContext()`. **\[ref 5\]**

**The upstream request was closed unimplemented — settled, not pending.** microsoft/playwright#18891 was closed by a maintainer on 30 Jun 2023: *"This issue was closed due to limited engagement (upvotes/activity), lack of recent activity, and insufficient actionability."* GitHub renders the state as "closed as completed", which is misleading — the comment is explicit that it was a housekeeping closure, **not** a shipped feature.

Per the **Implementation principle**, we build our substitute *on* Playwright's own primitives **\[ref 6\]**: `testInfo.attach(name, { path, contentType })` and `testInfo.outputPath()`.

### The exchange recorder — design and tidy-up

Today `helpers/api-report.ts` → `recordApiExchange` attaches **three entries per call**. A 40-call flow produces 120 attachments and none of it is machine-readable as a whole. Split into two modules:

`helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` **— collect + persist (new)**

* Ordered typed record per call: sequence **stamped at request start**, acting persona, enclosing `test.step()` name, method, URL, headers, bodies, status, duration, repro curl. Reuses `format.ts`'s `RequestParts` / `ResponseParts`.
* At test end (fixture teardown) writes **one** file — `testInfo.outputPath('api-exchanges.json')` — attached once with `contentType: 'application/json'`.

`helpers/api-report.ts` **— render (existing, slimmed)**

* One human-readable markdown attachment per call; cookies and curl fold into the JSON record.
* ~~Redaction unchanged: masked when ~~`~~getRedactSecrets()~~`~~ is on (default in CI, off locally).~~ *Superseded (R12):* GDPR personal data, access tokens and secret/API keys are masked in every run.

**Hard review rule, now enforced by lint (see Risk mitigation):** all transport goes through `performApiCall`.

### Constraints

* **Switching identity never means logging in again** — contexts are built from `.auth/token-<persona>.json`.
* **Context isolation does not solve data races** — hence the per-flow data strategy.
* **Teardown must be fixture-scoped, not trailing statements.** *(The docs never explicitly address the failure case — so we prove it with the mid-flow failure check.)* **\[ref 7\]**
* *(Cost note:* `RECORD_HAR=true` *sources the context from real chromium —* `fixtures/api.fixture.ts:116-128`*. Opt-in, never in the PR gate.)*

## Coverage is classified, not just counted

| Class | Meaning |
| -- | -- |
| `flow-verified` | Exercised inside a flow whose business-outcome criterion passes — the strongest class |
| `positive-path` | A single valid authenticated call asserting the documented success response; no flow reaches it |
| `503-tolerated` | Provider unconfigured locally; the by-design 503 is the recorded outcome (`_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS`) |
| `precondition-refused` | Precondition unmeetable locally; the enveloped business 4xx is the recorded outcome ([KS-478](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful)) |
| `no-documented-flow` | Reached by no product-documented flow — a finding in its own right, triaged at the end |

The catalogue's **Expected dominant class** column is the planning-time prediction; the matrix records what actually happened. A flow landing materially weaker than predicted is a finding, not a silent downgrade.

## Toggles — two of them, and they work differently

### 1. CSRF hardening — test-side, ON by default

The gateway mounts a double-submit guard (`api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts`, mounted `index.ts:370-371` inside `if (NODE_ENV !== 'test')`): the server mints an HMAC-signed token, sets the readable `XSRF-TOKEN` cookie and mirrors it in the `X-CSRF-Token` **response** header; a client echoes it back as `X-XSRF-TOKEN`.

The [KS-428](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and) rewrite short-circuits `protectMiddleware` for any request carrying `Authorization: Bearer …` or `x-api-key`, so authenticated writes are **not expected to need the token today**. **We send it anyway** — the suite behaves like a correct client and keeps passing if that bypass is narrowed.

* **Local:** `getCsrfEnabled()` in `config/environment.ts`, default `true`: `readEnv('CSRF_ENABLED', 'true') !== 'false'`. Commented override in `.env.example`.
* ~~**CI:**~~ *(moot — R4)* `CSRF_ENABLED: ${{ vars.PLAYWRIGHT_CSRF_ENABLED || 'true' }}` on the `playwright` job only.

### 2. Login rate limiter (`LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED`) — platform-side, read at gateway boot

**A test cannot flip this at runtime.** `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:858` passes it into `shouldSkipLoginLimiter({ nodeEnv, disableEnv })`; `middleware/rateLimitSkip.ts:68-69` honours it **only** when the value is `'true'` **and** `NODE_ENV` is in the non-prod allow-list. Never honoured in production ([KS-191](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-191/schemathesis-gate-rank-2-disable-login-limiter-in-cilocal-to-stop)).

| Where | Today | Effect |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Local | `docker-compose.yml:368` → `${LOCAL_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED:-false}` | **ACTIVE** unless exported before `docker compose up -d`. *(Verified 2026-07-24: the running developer stack has it* `true` *— something in the boot path exported it. Don't infer the default from a running container.)* |
| CI | `boot-platform-stack/action.yml:123` → hardcoded `"true"` | **DISABLED** for every suite's stack, with no way to change it |

What this ticket adds: a documented local runbook line; a `getLoginLimiterDisabled()` accessor so `auth.setup.ts` can annotate the report and decide whether a login 429 gets bounded backoff; and a `login-limiter-disabled` **input** on the composite (**default** `"true"`, additive) fed by `${{ vars.PLAYWRIGHT_LOGIN_LIMITER_DISABLED || 'true' }}` from the Playwright caller only. The design rule that makes the toggle optional: **one login per persona per run**.

*Setting either repo Variable is a human action in repo settings —* `gh variable set` *is a GitHub API call, barred for systemTest work.*

## Definition of done

1. **All published operations classified** (346 on 2026-10-26, R1), none unaccounted for.
2. **Class distribution meets its floors** — no downgrade out of `flow-verified` without a recorded reason.
3. **Every flow passes its stated acceptance criterion**, or records a documented gap where a platform capability is missing (F6 expired, F13 error → resolve).
4. **No residue** — two consecutive full runs leave identical record counts outside the documented append-only exclusion list.
5. **Residual triage complete.**
6. All four suites' `quality` gates green; both QA HTML docs synced.

## Risk mitigation

Most of the risks below are removable — not by being careful, but by deciding, probing, or automating a detector. What remains is labelled honestly rather than managed.

### 1. Prove the pattern once before repeating it 22 times

Do **Phase 0 + Phase 0b + the spine + F10** as a complete vertical slice, and only then write the remaining plans. F10 is deliberately the pilot: 7 operations, self-contained, `Own` data, and it exercises an async boundary — so it stresses every enabler without being large.

Every shared mechanism (CSRF, personas, per-persona contexts, the exchange recorder, `expect.poll` settle, fixture teardown, the coverage matrix) gets validated against the real stack **once**. If an assumption is wrong it is wrong in one flow, not twenty-three. **Reduces Risks 1, 8, 9, 11, 12** — all of which are "does the shared plumbing actually work" in disguise.

### 2. Four probes that turn a risk into a fact (each under an hour, all in Phase 0)

| Probe | Question it answers | Kills |
| -- | -- | -- |
| **A** — authenticated `POST /api/documents` with `CSRF_ENABLED=false` | Does the [KS-428](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and) Bearer bypass actually hold? | Risk 1 |
| **B** — force a mid-flow failure, check cleanup ran | Does fixture teardown run on failure? | the ref-7 doc gap |
| **C** — create a certification with a past `expiresAt` | Can we reach the Expired state ourselves? | Risk 14 |
| **D** — POST a synthetic entry to system-errors | Can we raise an error on demand? | Risk 15 |

**Run C and D before waiting on a reply** — the capability may already exist, in which case the ask resolves itself and both flow plans proceed unchanged.

### 3. Three risks need a decision, not work

**D1, D2 and D3 at the top of this ticket.** They cost nothing to settle and currently block F3/the spine, the tier split, and the child-plan layout respectively. **Deciding them is the cheapest risk reduction available.**

### 4. Turn conventions into gates

A rule enforced only at review will eventually be broken. Three become automated:

| Was | Becomes | Kills |
| -- | -- | -- |
| "All transport goes through `performApiCall`" (review rule) | **oxlint rule** *(R7)* forbidding `api.fetch(` / direct `request.` outside `helpers/api-call.ts` — the repo already uses `no-restricted-properties` this way to keep `process.env` inside the config module | Risk 12 |
| "A change to `/api/users/admin/*` breaks Phase 0 silently" | **Guard assertion** that the endpoint still assigns the role it is given — fails loudly and immediately | Risk 2 |
| ~~"The composite action is shared source"~~ *(moot — R4)* | **Cross-suite diff** — after the change, run one job from each of the other three suites and compare boot output | Risk 7 |

Plus the guards already planned: the residue check (Risk 8), the order-independence check (Risk 9), and the per-class floors in `coverage.test.ts` (Risk 4).

### 5. What is irreducible — and what we do instead

Risks **5, 6, 13** and the provider-gated parts of **4** cannot be engineered away: they are properties of the local environment, the platform's state machines, and an open defect ([KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet)-C). The mitigation is **honest labelling** — the verification classes and the per-flow *Expected dominant class* column make each one visible in the matrix rather than hidden inside a green run. A risk that shows up in the report is not a risk; it is a documented limitation.

## Risks

 1. **CSRF** — hardened by default; expected to be a non-issue because of the [KS-428](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-428/api-gateway-csrf-guard-is-inverted-it-exempts-cookie-only-requests-and>) Bearer bypass. *Mitigated by Probe A.*
 2. **Persona setup depends on an unpublished endpoint** — `/api/users/admin/*` is live but absent from the spec. Must not count toward `COVERAGE_FLOOR`. *Mitigated by the guard assertion.*
 3. **⚠ No Cardano backend on either stack — F3's anchor leg is not satisfiable as written.** Verified 2026-07-24: `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` unset on `secuura-anchoring`/`secuura-originate` (code tests `=== 'true'`, `services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:459`); `CARDANO_NODE_URL=http://cardano-devnet:8090`, empty `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY`; `cardano-devnet` is behind the compose profile `devnet` and no such container exists; the CI composite's service list (`boot-platform-stack/action.yml:124-129`) excludes it. *This is **D1** — needs a decision, not work.*
 4. `503-tolerated` **and** `precondition-refused` **are weak classes** — F11, F18, F19 and F20–F23 carry most of them. *Mitigated by per-class floors + the predicted-class column.*
 5. **State-machine operations legitimately 4xx** ([KS-478](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-478/ks-466-11-state-machineprecondition-400s-resolve-via-ks-188-stateful>)) — F20/F21/F22 must reach a satisfiable state or record the refusal. *Irreducible; labelled.*
 6. **Rate limits** — \~2000/60s; login 10/hour/IP without the override. One login per persona. *Irreducible; designed around.*
 7. ~~**The composite action is shared source, even though the stacks are not.**~~ *Moot — GitHub Actions retired (R4).*
 8. **Test-data accumulation** — 23 flows creating fixture data per run. *Mitigated by fixture-scoped teardown + the residue check.*
 9. **Data races between parallel flows** — isolation separates sessions, not platform state. *Mitigated by the per-flow data strategy + the order-independence check.*
10. **F10's webhook URL must pass the SSRF guard** ([KS-487](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487/review-b-input-validation-injection-upload-xssssrf-and-crypto>)-B). *Settled in Phase 0 by the URL convention.*
11. **Four async boundaries** — anchoring, export, notification delivery (F9), webhook delivery (F10). All four use `expect.poll`. *Mitigated by the pilot exercising one of them.*
12. **The exchange recorder is the only evidence.** *Mitigated by the oxlint rule (R7).*
13. **F16 must not encode a known bug as expected behaviour** — `POST /api/wallets/verify` returns `verified:true` for any signature ([KS-488](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488/review-c-sk-channel-paymentswebhooks-and-integrations-m365-kyc-wallet>)-C). F16 stops at wallet linkage. *Irreducible; labelled. Schemathesis's xfail will xpass loudly when the fix lands, prompting a revisit.*
14. **F6's expired leg depends on a platform capability we do not have.** *Probe C first; then the ask to* @kamil.kreiser */* @stuart.jamieson\*; else a documented gap.\*
15. **F13's only journey depends on a platform capability we do not have.** *Probe D first; same escalation; else F13 is labelled a read surface.*

## Playwright references

Grounded in the docs for the pinned **1.61.1**. Checked 2026-07-24.

| \# | Source | What it establishes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 1 | [Best Practices](<https://playwright.dev/docs/best-practices>) | *"Each test should be completely isolated from another test and should run independently with its own local storage, session storage, data, cookies etc."* · *"Only test what you control."* → per-flow data ownership; provider-gated paths record a by-design 503 |
| 2 | [API testing](<https://playwright.dev/docs/api-testing>) | *"…you can manually create a new instance of APIRequestContext which will have its own isolated cookies."* → the per-persona / per-flow context model |
| 3 | [Parallelism](<https://playwright.dev/docs/test-parallel>) | *"If one of the serial tests fails, all subsequent tests are skipped."* · *"All tests in a group are retried together."* · *"Using serial is not recommended."* → the spine is one stepped test |
| 4 | [Videos](<https://playwright.dev/docs/videos>) | *"Videos are saved upon browser context closure at the end of a test."* → video cannot capture an API-only test |
| 5 | [Trace viewer](<https://playwright.dev/docs/trace-viewer>) + [microsoft/playwright#18891](<https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/18891>) + [microsoft/playwright-pytest#137](<https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-pytest/issues/137>) | Tracing is started via `browserContext.tracing`; no documented path records a standalone `APIRequestContext`. **#18891 closed 30 Jun 2023 as stale** — *"limited engagement… insufficient actionability"* — **not** implemented, despite the "closed as completed" label |
| 6 | [TestInfo](<https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-testinfo>) | `attach()`: *"Either path or body must be specified, but not both"*; *"automatically takes care of copying attached files to a location that is accessible to reporters."* · `outputPath()`: *"a path inside the testInfo.outputDir where the test can safely put a temporary file"* |
| 7 | [Fixtures](<https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures>) | *"…teardown is executed when the fixture is no longer being used by the test/hook."* — the failure case is **not** explicitly covered, hence Probe B |
| 8 | [Assertions](<https://playwright.dev/docs/test-assertions>) | *"You can convert any synchronous expect to an asynchronous polling one using expect.poll"*, with `{ timeout, intervals, message }` and a documented API-polling example |

## Related

A **High**-severity privilege-escalation finding was surfaced while verifying whether this work could provision an `ISSUER_APPROVER` persona at runtime, filed as a comment on [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor) (Review A): a case-sensitive platform-role denylist combined with case-normalising persistence lets a tenant-scoped `ORG_ADMIN` mint a platform `SYSTEM_ADMIN` via `role: "Super_Admin"`. Not in scope here. Its systemTest regression belongs to [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-security-regression-coverage) (Review G) once the fix lands.

## ⚠ New gap found 2026-08-14 — anti-automation has ZERO coverage

Found during the [KS-441](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-441/akto-ci-scan-throughput-21-s-local-vs-10-min-in-the-isolated-pr-akto) Akto throughput investigation (**report attached above**, §7). Two independent measurements, both pointing the same way:

* The **login brute-force limiter is disabled in CI *and* on the VM**, so nothing exercises it.
* Akto's rate-limiting family produces **969 results, 100% not-applicable, zero executed** — which renders in the report as "0 vulnerable", indistinguishable from a pass.

**A regression removing brute-force protection would ship green today.** This is exactly the MUST #13 rule-6 shape: a check whose input is missing scoring as clean rather than red.

A regression test has been added and **proven red** (`tests/test_login_rate_limit.py` + the pure helper `tests/support/login_rate_limit.py`, offline-unit-tested). **Green is blocked** by a harness gap, not a platform one: `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` never passes `LOGIN_RATE_LIMIT` through to the gateway, so the limiter cannot be turned on for the test. Fixing that passthrough is the next step and is the only thing standing between this row and ✅.

Also relevant to how this register should be read: **Akto verdicts are non-deterministic** (same template/endpoint/session returned clean, clean, HIGH, clean, HIGH; three scans with identical 1,615-result coverage returned `vulnerable` 1, 0, 0). Treat Akto as discovery, not acceptance — a green Akto row is not evidence a finding is fixed.

That is **backend work owned by Kamil** under the Platform K review work-streams — tracked in his tickets, not here; the flip lands as a separate backend PR, at which point G un-marks the `xfail`/`skip`.

Cross-tenant mutate/transfer-custody, cross-owner read/revoke within a tenant, forged `x-tenant-id`, and api-key isolation all landed as passing regressions. (Backend owner-scoping/header-trust remediation is Review A — [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486/review-a-authn-authz-tenancy-and-idor), Kamil — not tracked here.)
4. **Other harnesses under G** — Akto OWASP re-baseline ([KS-395](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-395/validate-weekend-platform-fixes-akto-owasp-security-scan) pattern) and Playwright UI-level auth/admin-gating/XSS: **not started**.

[KS-533](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-533/sk-security-register-data-loss-unrecoverability-scenarios-code) was closed 2026-09-14 with every row dispositioned (K-side residue [KS-532](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-532/sk-dr-k-side-key-store-restore-path-joint-restore-point-coverage-demo) / [KS-581](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-581/register-connector-volume-alerting-rate-limit-and-correlation-of), Kam); these two are Peter's and are **blocked on** [KS-516](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-516/schemathesis-systemtest-seed-a-real-sk-api-key-documentswrite-so-the) seeding two real `sk_` keys (provisioning + operational). For each confirmed finding: (1) write a test that **reproduces** it pre-fix (red), (2) land it alongside the remediation so it goes green, (3) keep it in the pre-merge tier so regressions fail fast. **Acceptance:** each A–F remediation ships with a linked regression here; the security-relevant checks run in the pre-merge suites (schemathesis pre-merge + Akto). The "Still to fix" list above is the live checklist.

title: Review F — Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation
description:
> ## ✅ F-9 RESOLVED — added 2026-08-17. **The row is FALSE at the live edge: all three portals already serve their own CSP. Do NOT add one at the gateway — it would break them.**
>
> **F-9 is closed on this ticket. KS-491 itself stays OPEN** for the two rows that are still live: the **strategic WAF gap** and the **absent Caddyfile**.
>
> ### 1. The claim, tested at the internet-facing edge
>
> Three read-only GETs against `https://secuura02-demo.southeastasia.cloudapp.azure.com`:
>
> | Path | CSP served? | Distinguishing directive |
> | -- | -- | -- |
> | `/` (issuer) | **yes** | `script-src … 'unsafe-eval'` — issuer only |
> | `/admin/` | **yes** | `connect-src … wss://*.secuura.io` — admin only |
> | `/verify/` | **yes** | `frame-ancestors 'self' https://*.secuura.io https://secuura.io` |
>
> **They differ from one another, and that difference is the discriminator.** A single `add_header` at the gateway would make all three byte-identical. Control: `/api/health` returns a **fourth, different** CSP from the API service — so a CSP on this host is not a gateway-wide artefact.
>
> Source side agrees: **8** `Content-Security-Policy` occurrences across `frontend/{issuer,verifier,admin,outlook-addin}/nginx.conf`, and the gateway does **not** `proxy_hide_header Content-Security-Policy`, so downstream policies pass through untouched. It *does* hide-and-re-add `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy` and HSTS — which is why those five are gateway-owned and CSP is not. The file is internally consistent.
>
> ### 2. The gateway's abstention is a decision, and it is NEWER than this row
>
> `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf:240-245`, immediately above the live header block:
>
> > *"CSP is DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE. It is app-specific — issuer, admin and verifier each ship their own — and a single generic policy at the gateway would either be too loose to be worth having or would break a portal. Owning it here would also silently override a tighter downstream policy. That stays with the apps; tracked as its own decision, not smuggled in."*
>
> `git log -S"DELIBERATELY NOT SET HERE"` attributes it to exactly one commit — `045c658ec`**, 2026-08-13, "KS-613/KS-615: harden the live gateway edge…" (#678)** — the same hardening pass that fixed F-2, F-6 and F-7. Sentinel control returns empty. **The missing gateway CSP is not an oversight this review caught; it is a decision the F-remediation took afterwards, in writing.**
>
> ### 3. Why "just add one" is actively harmful, not merely redundant
>
> Two `Content-Security-Policy` headers are **not merged**. Each policy is enforced independently, so a resource must satisfy **both** — the effective policy is the **intersection**. Intersecting the commented-out `:595` policy against what admin actually serves:
>
> | directive | `:595` policy | admin's live policy | effective | consequence |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `connect-src` | `'self' https://*.blockfrost.io` | `'self' http://localhost:* https://*.secuura.io wss://*.secuura.io` | `'self'` | **admin's XHR/WebSocket blocked** |
> | `script-src` | `'self' 'unsafe-inline'` | `'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'` | `'self'` | **wasm blocked, all three portals** |
> | `img-src` | `'self' data: https:` | `'self' data: https: blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob images blocked** |
> | `worker-src` | absent → falls back to `script-src` | `'self' blob:` | loses `blob:` | **blob workers blocked** |
>
> That is the portal-breaking outcome the in-file comment predicts, arrived at independently.
>
> ### 4. Recorded so it is not re-derived
>
> Two things stated explicitly because a later reader will otherwise repeat the work:
>
> * `frame-ancestors` **is NOT part of the breakage.** It does not fall back to `default-src`, so an unspecified `frame-ancestors` in a gateway policy leaves each portal's own value governing. An earlier note of mine claimed otherwise; it was wrong and the four rows above stand without it.
> * `outlook-addin` **is not routed through this gateway** (0 matches for `outlook` in `nginx-demo.conf`), so its policy is unaffected either way.
>
> ### 5. The real question this surfaced → **KS-648**
>
> The policies exist and are well-formed, but two directives are weak: `'unsafe-eval'` **on the issuer alone** (the other two manage on `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`) and `'unsafe-inline'` **styles on all three**. That is an app-level quality question, exactly as the in-file comment says — filed as [KS-648](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-648), Low, in the Security Review project. **Not** part of F-9.
>
> *Established read-only: three GETs,* `git log -S`*, and greps over the tree. No code changed, nothing deployed, no probe whose success path writes. F-9's deploy authorisation was retired rather than released.*

---

> ## ⚠️ STATUS BANNER — added 2026-08-16. **The table below says "0** `limit_req`**, 0** `client_max_body_size`**". That is now FALSE, and the fix is CONFIRMED LIVE ON THE VM.**
>
> **This resolves the open question of whether F's edge hardening was merged-but-undeployed. It is deployed.** Established read-only, with no rate-limit or body-cap probe against the live demo.
>
> ### F-2 / F-7 — fixed in code **and live**
>
> | Measure | Register says | Repo today | **Running container** |
> | -- | -- | -- | -- |
> | `limit_req` | **0** | **9** | **9** |
> | `limit_conn` | 0 | **4** | — |
> | `client_max_body_size` | **0** | **12m** (`:215`) | — |
>
> **The proof that it is live, rather than merely merged:**
>
> * `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` on the VM is **byte-identical to the repo copy** — md5 `8be17f5b075d51a170269cd404dc6a87` on both.
> * The **running** `secuura-nginx-gateway` **container** serves `/etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf` at the **same md5**, so this is the config nginx actually loaded, not just a file sitting on the host disk.
> * Ordering closes it: conf mtime `2026-08-13T00:09:07Z`, container start `2026-08-14T05:06:57Z` — **the container started after the file's last modification**, so it cannot be serving an older copy. `nginx -t` passes.
>
> This matters because **the conf is bind-mounted, not baked into the image** — an image rebuild proves nothing about it either way, which is exactly why the merge alone was not evidence. Shipped by KS-613/#678 and KS-616/#679.
>
> ### Why the earlier "unestablished" reading was right at the time
>
> A single GET returns HSTS, CSP and `X-Frame-Options`, and **none of those discriminate**: the CSP cannot come from this conf (its own is commented out — see below), and Caddy terminates TLS in front, making HSTS unattributable. **Reading the mounted file was the check that discriminates**; the header response was not.
>
> ### Still open
>
> * **F-9 partial — CSP is still commented out at** `nginx-demo.conf:595`**.** `X-Frame-Options` and HSTS are active; the CSP line is inert. Verified today.
> * The **strategic Crit row (no WAF anywhere)** stands unchanged — it is a greenfield gap, not a stale row.
> * **Caddyfile still absent from the repo**, so the TLS edge remains unversioned.
>
> *Banner added during the session-38 closure sweep. Ticket left **open** for F-9's CSP, the WAF row, and the Caddyfile.*

---

Work-stream **F** of the [Platform K security review](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-485>). Forward-looking edge & resilience posture for a millions-of-users, continuously-attacked target. Largely a **gap analysis** — what's ABSENT matters as much as what's present. Recon complete on `develop` @ `fcf2d878c`.

**Scope / checklist**

* WAF: is any WAF present (nginx ModSecurity / Front Door / App Gateway WAF / Cloudflare)? Where would it integrate? (Product owner explicitly wants WAF.)
* Edge config: nginx gateway + Caddy — security headers, request-size limits, timeouts, TLS.
* Rate limiting / DDoS: edge + app tier; connection/request caps; Slowloris/large-body.
* Bot / anti-automation: CAPTCHA on signup/login/verify.
* Secret manager (runtime) & observability/alerting; network segmentation of infra services.

## Findings / recommendations (develop @ fcf2d878c)

| Sev | Evidence | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Crit (strategic) | repo-wide absent; `deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md:50` | **No WAF** anywhere — no ModSecurity, no Front Door/App Gateway WAF; Cloudflare is DNS-only (grey-cloud), so no Cloudflare WAF. Greenfield. Integration point: in front of Caddy (Front Door WAF) or a ModSecurity sidecar at the gateway. |
| High | `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx-demo.conf` (0 `limit_req`, 0 `client_max_body_size`) | The **live** gateway conf has no edge rate-limit and no request-body cap. The hardened `nginx-production.conf:21-22,216` (10r/s, 2r/s auth, `client_max_body_size 10m`) is for the **decommissioned** Container Apps path only — never runs today. Port these to the live conf. |
| High | Caddyfile absent from repo | The actual TLS edge (Caddy on the VM) is **not version-controlled** → TLS ciphers/protocols, HSTS, timeouts, body limits unauditable and drift-prone. Commit the Caddyfile. |
| High | `docker-compose.yml:63-64` (`6432:5432`), `:118-119` (`6379:6379`) | Postgres + Redis publish to host `0.0.0.0` ("remove in production" comments, but active). On the VM these are internet-reachable unless the NSG/ufw blocks them — relies on an external firewall, not config. Bind to the internal network. |
| High | repo-wide absent | **No** CAPTCHA/reCAPTCHA/hCaptcha/Turnstile on signup, login, or public verify. Only IP/velocity limits stand between a botnet and account/verify abuse. |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/middleware/rateLimitEnforce.ts:135-137` | App-tier limiters fail **open** on error; if Redis is down the per-client counter degrades to per-replica in-memory (inflated ceiling — [KS-170](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-170/enforceclientratelimit-runs-in-memory-per-replica-wire-the-redis)). |
| Med | `nginx-demo.conf` (no `limit_conn`/`client_body_timeout`/`client_header_timeout`) | No Slowloris/large-body/slow-request protection at the live edge. |
| Low | `nginx-demo.conf` (no active HSTS/CSP `add_header`) | Gateway emits no security headers of its own; relies wholly on downstream helmet + Caddy. Single point of omission if a service skips helmet. |

**GREEN (verified):** app-tier defence is real and layered — `express-rate-limit` global limiter (`api-gateway/src/index.ts:448`, 300/min prod), per-route login (15/15min, `:849`), register (`:861`), verification (`:469`) limiters; per-API-key distributed Redis limiter (`rateLimitEnforce.ts`); **application-level account lockout** on login (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:285-303`). Helmet provides per-service CSP + HSTS + nosniff. A standalone `observability/` module exists. The pen-tested `nginx-production.conf` is a strong hardening template — it just isn't the config in production.

**Acceptance:** WAF introduced at the edge; live gateway/Caddy config carries rate-limits/body-caps/headers; pg/redis bound internal; bot protection on public auth/verify; each with a verification test where feasible (Review G). Several items here are **new-build recommendations**, not code defects — track as remediation issues with owners.

title: Security review — plan, methodology & handover (Platform K)
description:
> **This issue is the coordination hub and living plan for the Platform K security review.** It holds the scope, threat model, methodology, the index of review work-streams, the evidence-cited findings register, remediation sequencing, and full handover context so anyone can pick this up cold. Modelled on the Platform S plan [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175).
>
> **v1 — grounded 2026-07-21 against** `develop` **@** `fcf2d878c` (161 commits since 2026-07-01). Register built from a 6-stream parallel recon (A–F); each finding cites `file:line` under `Blockchain/Dev/` on develop.

## 1. Target & threat context

* **System:** platform-k = the Secuura Cardano/blockchain anchoring platform. Node.js microservices monorepo (28 backend services: api-gateway, auth, originate, anchoring, timestamping, kyc, billing, analytics, m365-integration, tenant-provisioning, wallet-connector, nft-certificate, vc-issuer, security, governance, guardian, etc.), PostgreSQL/Prisma + RLS, Redis, Aiken smart contracts on Cardano, three React frontends (Issuer/Verifier/Admin) + Outlook/Gmail add-ins.
* **Code:** `Distributed_Secuura`, remote `github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura.git`, branch `develop`. Platform under `Blockchain/Dev/`.
* **Live env (2026-07-08,** [KS-414](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-414/demo-env-cost-pivot-replace-container-apps-with-a-single-vm-running)): single Azure VM — Caddy auto-TLS → compose nginx gateway (`nginx-demo.conf`) at `https://demo-pk.secuura.net`. The Container Apps template + hardened `nginx-production.conf` are **decommissioned/unused**. **⚠ v1 claimed** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING=true` **in the demo. That is FALSE (corrected 2026-08-13).** The demo does **real** Cardano `preview`-testnet anchoring: `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is unset, `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` is set, anchoring boots `cardanoMode: REAL (Blockfrost)`, and a funded **platform wallet mnemonic is present on the VM**. Treat the anchoring path on the live target as a live chain-submission path with key material, not a simulation — see the re-grounding comment (2026-08-13) and KS-535 / KS-607.
* **Integrations:** platform-s (SSD document platform, the S↔K channel — K is the server), Stripe (billing), Microsoft 365 / Entra Verified-ID (KYC/IDV), M365 Graph (Outlook/Gmail add-ins), Cardano (Blockfrost).
* **Protects:** legally-significant artefacts (on-chain anchors, timestamps, VCs/NFTs, document hashes), PII, org/tenant data, payment flows, per-tenant connector credentials.
* **Threat assumptions:** millions of users, high public profile, under continuous attack. Treat availability, tenant isolation, and **anchor/signature integrity** as first-order.

## 2. Objectives

1. Evidence-cited findings register (`file:line`, severity) across the whole attack surface — kept current with develop.
2. Prioritised, **sequenced** remediation issues with owners and acceptance criteria (see §5).
3. Strategic hardening for scale — WAF, bot/anti-automation, edge rate-limits/body-caps, secret manager at runtime, DDoS protection, observability/alerting.
4. Repeatable security gates (make the report-only CI scans blocking; keep the [KS-470](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-470/npm-audit-25-transitive-advisories-on-the-develop-lockfile) audit-gate + lockfile clean-room green) so posture doesn't regress.
5. A **security regression test** for every confirmed finding, in the right harness (systemTest — schemathesis / Akto / cross-tenant-isolation / Playwright).

## 3. Scope & review work-streams

Recon streams A–F are **complete** (this v1 pass). Work-stream owners: **Kamil** for A–F + H; **Peter** for G (systemTest).

> **Table amended 2026-08-13** — the v1 table showed six streams all reading "Recon done", which had drifted from the board in both directions and **omitted Review H entirely** (created by comment on 2026-07-21, closed 2026-08-02). A wrong index costs every future reader. `Status` below is the live Linear state; `Recon` records whether the v1 recon pass covered it.

| \# | Work-stream | Issue | Owner | Recon | Status (live 2026-08-13) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| A | AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR | [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486) | Kamil | done | **In Review** |
| B | Input validation, injection, upload, XSS/SSRF & crypto | [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| C | S↔K channel, payments/webhooks & integrations (M365 / KYC / wallet / email) | [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| D | Blockchain / anchoring / smart-contract integrity | [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489) | Kamil | done | **In Review** |
| E | Deployment, containers & CI/CD supply chain | [KS-490](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-490) | Kamil | done | Todo |
| F | Edge, WAF, DDoS & anti-automation | [KS-491](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-491) | Kamil | done | **Todo — IN PROGRESS 2026-08-13** (untouched 07-21 → 08-13) |
| **G** | **systemTest security regression coverage** | [KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492) | **Peter** | n/a | Standing (Todo) |
| **H** | **Dependency currency & known-vuln package upgrades** | [KS-493](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-493) | Kamil | done (pass-2) | ✅ **Done 2026-08-02** |

**Deferred as its own sequenced pass:** re-recon of streams A–F against the 168 commits / 202 changed files landed since v1's baseline `fcf2d878c`. Tracked as [KS-612](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-612) (child of this issue) — this re-grounding refreshed the *plan*, not the findings.

## 4. Methodology

Recon → findings register (severity-rated, evidence-cited, mapped loosely to OWASP ASVS / Top 10) → triage (severity × exploitability × blast-radius-at-scale) → sequenced remediation issues with acceptance criteria → verification (reproduce pre-fix, confirm blocked post-fix, add a systemTest regression). **Re-ground the register against develop whenever the branch has materially moved** (the [PS-175](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-175/security-review-plan-methodology-and-handover-platform-s) v2 pass is the template).

## 5. Findings register + remediation sequencing

**Legend:** Sev = severity as found on develop @ `fcf2d878c`. All rows cite `Blockchain/Dev/…`. Full evidence + GREEN notes live on each work-stream issue.

### A — AuthN / AuthZ / tenancy & IDOR — [KS-486](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-486)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Med | `services/api-gateway/src/routes/notifications.ts:242-272` | `POST /api/notifications` takes `userId` from body, no self/admin check → spoofed `security`/`system` notifications w/ `actionUrl` to anyone (in-app phishing / BOLA). |
| Med | `services/originate/src/repositories/documentRepo.ts:173-205`; transfer `routes/documents.ts:1318` | Documents scoped by `tenant_id` only, never `owner_user_id` — any user in a tenant can read/mutate/transfer another user's doc. Confirm intended tenant==org boundary. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/index.ts:220-227`; `routes/documents.ts:131-133` | Tenant scope derived from inbound `x-tenant-id`; originate JWT has no `tenantId` to cross-check → pure header trust. Safe only via gateway strip + RLS; header-forwarding/SSRF re-opens [KS-4](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-4/critical-cross-tenant-document-leak-via-x-tenant-override-bug)-class cross-tenant read. |
| Low | `services/auth/src/routes/mfa.ts:225-236` | `mfa/verify` validates TOTP with no proof factor-1 passed (standalone TOTP oracle; issues no tokens). |
| Low | gateway `middleware/auth.ts:106-150` vs auth `middleware/authenticate.ts:19-65` | `test_token_*` backdoor guarded asymmetrically — one mis-set env = role/tenant spoof. |

### B — Input validation, injection, upload, XSS/SSRF & crypto — [KS-487](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-487)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:1072,1202` | Teams `webhookUrl` validated only by `z.string().url()` — no SSRF guard; `fetch()` to `169.254.169.254`/RFC1918/localhost. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/routes/webhooks.ts:153-205,455-490` | `validateWebhookUrl` blocks only IP literals (no DNS resolution → DNS-rebind) and only at registration, not send time. |
| Med | `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1769-1773` (+`:36`) | `POST /api/admin/seed-demo-users` mints ORG_ADMIN/OWNER w/ hardcoded `admin123`; no `NODE_ENV`/`ENABLE_DEMO_SEED` gate. |
| Med | `services/kyc/src/index.ts:251` | ID images stored from caller-supplied `mimeType`, no magic-byte verification. |
| Low | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/taskpane/index.tsx:60` | `el.innerHTML` interpolates `${e.message}` — unescaped sink (error path). |

### C — S↔K channel, payments/webhooks & integrations — [KS-488](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-488)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
| High | `services/kyc/src/routes/microsoft-verification.ts:201` | Callback authed by static `api-key` w/ hardcoded default `'secuura-kyc-callback'` → forge Entra Verified-ID results. |
| High | `services/wallet-connector/src/server.ts:246-259` | `POST /api/wallets/verify` is a stub — always `verified:true`. Wallet-ownership proof fully bypassable. |
| Med | `services/m365-integration/src/index.ts:138-161,235-243` | Graph access+refresh tokens persisted to Postgres in plaintext. |
| Med | `services/billing/src/routes/webhooks.ts:34-37` | `isEventProcessed` fails **open** on DB-unavailable → redelivered Stripe event re-adds credits. |
| Low | `services/auth/src/services/email.ts:40-45,148-149` | No CRLF sanitisation on `documentTitle`→`subject`; no recipient-domain allow-list. |
| Low | `frontend/gmail-addon/Code.gs:17-18` | Hardcoded to decommissioned Container Apps URLs (stale). |

### D — Blockchain / anchoring / smart-contract integrity — [KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489)

| Sev | file:line | Finding |
| -- | -- | -- |
